We'll have a single `number` transform that handles both.\n\nToday is the last day for clarification questions, so if you haven't emailed hiring@activv.money about password handling and scanned PDFs, do it now.\n\n---\n\n# Part 0: Project setup\n\n## Step 1: Check Python\n\n```bash\npython --version\n```\n\nYou need **3.10 or higher**. If not, install Python 3.11 or 3.12 from python.org.\n\n## Step 2: Create the project folder and Git repo\n\n**Mac/Linux:**\n```bash\nmkdir statement-parser && cd statement-parser\ngit init\nmkdir app samples configs tests docs\ntouch app/__init__.py\n```\n\n**Windows (PowerShell):**\n```powershell\nmkdir statement-parser; cd statement-parser\ngit init\nmkdir app, samples, configs, tests, docs\nNew-Item app/__init__.py -ItemType File\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create a virtual environment\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\n```\n\nActivate it:\n- Mac/Linux: `source .venv/bin/activate`\n- Windows: `.venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1`\n\nYour terminal prompt should now start with `(.venv)`.\n\n## Step 4: Create `requirements.txt`\n\n```text\npydantic>=2.5\npytest>=8.0\npdfplumber>=0.11\npikepdf>=9.0\nreportlab>=4.0\nopenpyxl>=3.1\npython-dotenv>=1.0\nfastapi>=0.110\nuvicorn>=0.29\n```\n\nInstall:\n```bash\npip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\nWe won't use all of these yet, but installing now avoids interruptions later.\n\n## Step 5: Create `.gitignore`\n\nThe brief says to never commit passwords, API keys or personal details.\n\n```text\n.venv/\n__pycache__/\n*.pyc\n.pytest_cache/\n.env\n*.db\n*.sqlite3\ncredentials.json\ntoken.json\n.DS_Store\n.idea/\n.vscode/\n```\n\n## Step 6: Create `.env.example`\n\nReal secrets go in `.env`, which is ignored. This file only shows which variables exist:\n\n```text\nGMAIL_ADDRESS=your-test-account@gmail.com\nGMAIL_APP_PASSWORD=\nLLM_API_KEY=\nLLM_PROVIDER=\n```\n\n## Step 7: Create `pytest.ini`\n\nThis lets tests import from `app`:\n\n```ini\n[pytest]\npythonpath = .\ntestpaths = tests\n```\n\n## Step 8: First commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Project setup\"\n```\n\nThen create an empty repo on GitHub and push:\n```bash\ngit remote add origin <your-repo-url>\ngit branch -M main\ngit push -u origin main\n```\n\nPart 0 is done.\n\n---\n\n# Part 1: Schema and transforms\n\n## What we're building and why\n\n- **`schema.py`**: the standard shape every statement ends up in, whatever the provider.\n- **`transforms.py`**: the whitelist of trusted functions that turn raw text like `\"(1,234.00)\"` into `Decimal(\"-1234.00\")`.\n\nThree design decisions to remember for the interview:\n\n1. **`Decimal`, never `float`.** `0.1 + 0.2` in float is `0.30000000000000004`. For money that's unacceptable.\n2. **Most fields are `Optional`.** An AIF has no holdings table, and a PMS has no NAV per unit. One schema must fit both.\n3. **The schema is lenient about suspicious data and strict about impossible data.** A malformed ISIN shouldn't crash the parse. It should be *flagged* in Part 6. But a period that ends before it starts is structurally impossible, so the schema rejects it.\n\n## Step 1: Create `app/schema.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Standard output structure. Every provider's statement is converted into this.\"\"\"\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom decimal import Decimal\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator\n\n\nclass StatementType(str, Enum):\n    PMS = \"pms\"\n    AIF = \"aif\"\n\n\nclass TransactionType(str, Enum):\n    BUY = \"buy\"\n    SELL = \"sell\"\n    DIVIDEND = \"dividend\"\n    FEE = \"fee\"\n    INFLOW = \"inflow\"\n    OUTFLOW = \"outflow\"\n    OTHER = \"other\"  # unrecognised label; validation (Part 6) will flag these\n\n\nclass Holding(BaseModel):\n    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)\n\n    security_name: str = Field(min_length=1)\n    isin: Optional[str] = None\n    quantity: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    cost: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    market_price: Optional[Decimal] = None  # used later for qty x price check\n    market_value: Decimal\n    weight_pct: Optional[Decimal] = None  # 12.5 means 12.5%\n\n    @field_validator(\"isin\", mode=\"before\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _normalise_isin(cls, v):\n        # Only normalise here. Format and checksum are checked in validation (Part 6),\n        # so a bad ISIN gets flagged instead of crashing the whole parse.\n        if v is None:\n            return None\n        v = str(v).replace(\" \", \"\").upper()\n        return v or None\n\n\nclass Transaction(BaseModel):\n    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)\n\n    date: date\n    type: TransactionType\n    security_name: Optional[str] = None  # fees and inflows may have no security\n    quantity: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    amount: Decimal\n\n\nclass Summary(BaseModel):\n    opening_value: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    closing_value: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    cash_balance: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    fees_charged: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    nav_per_unit: Optional[Decimal] = None   # AIF\n    units_held: Optional[Decimal] = None     # AIF\n    # Optional extras, used by the reconciliation check in Part 6:\n    capital_inflows: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    capital_outflows: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    net_gain: Optional[Decimal] = None\n\n\nclass Statement(BaseModel):\n    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)\n\n    statement_type: StatementType\n    provider: str = Field(min_length=1)\n    strategy_name: Optional[str] = None\n    client_id: str = Field(min_length=1)\n    period_start: date\n    period_end: date\n    currency: str = \"INR\"\n\n    summary: Summary = Field(default_factory=Summary)\n    holdings: list[Holding] = Field(default_factory=list)\n    transactions: list[Transaction] = Field(default_factory=list)\n\n    source_file_hash: Optional[str] = None  # filled by the pipeline later\n\n    @field_validator(\"currency\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _upper_currency(cls, v: str) -> str:\n        return v.upper()\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def _check_period(self):\n        if self.period_end < self.period_start:\n            raise ValueError(\"period_end is before period_start\")\n        return self\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `app/transforms.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Whitelist of trusted value-parsing functions.\n\nThe LLM may only *name* these in a config. It can never add new ones.\nEvery transform takes a raw string and returns a clean value, or None if the\ncell is empty. If the text can't be understood, it raises TransformError\n(loud failure, never a silent wrong number).\n\"\"\"\nimport re\nfrom datetime import date, datetime\nfrom decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation\nfrom typing import Any, Callable, Optional\n\nfrom app.schema import TransactionType\n\n\nclass TransformError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"The raw text could not be interpreted by this transform.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownTransformError(KeyError):\n    \"\"\"A config named a transform that is not in the registry.\"\"\"\n\n\n_EMPTY_MARKERS = {\"\", \"-\", \"--\", \"\u2014\", \"\u2013\", \"nil\", \"n/a\", \"na\"}\n_CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r\"(\u20b9|rs\\.?|inr)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n_PLAIN_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r\"^(\\d+(\\.\\d*)?|\\.\\d+)$\")\n\n\ndef _is_empty(raw: Optional[str]) -> bool:\n    return raw is None or str(raw).strip().lower() in _EMPTY_MARKERS\n\n\n# ---------- numbers ----------\n\ndef _to_decimal(raw: Optional[str], *, drcr: bool = False, eu: bool = False) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n\n    s = _CURRENCY_RE.sub(\"\", str(raw)).strip()\n    negative = False\n\n    # Trailing Dr/Cr, only when this transform explicitly allows it\n    if drcr:\n        m = re.search(r\"(dr|cr)\\.?$\", s, re.IGNORECASE)\n        if m:\n            negative = m.group(1).lower() == \"dr\"\n            s = s[: m.start()].strip()\n\n    # Brackets mean negative: (1,234.00)\n    if s.startswith(\"(\") and s.endswith(\")\"):\n        negative = True\n        s = s[1:-1].strip()\n\n    # Leading or trailing minus (including the unicode minus sign)\n    if s and s[0] in \"-\u2212\":\n        negative = True\n        s = s[1:].strip()\n    elif s and s[-1] in \"-\u2212\":\n        negative = True\n        s = s[:-1].strip()\n\n    s = s.replace(\" \", \"\")\n    # Removing commas handles both 3,45,000 (Indian) and 345,000 (international).\n    if eu:\n        s = s.replace(\".\", \"\").replace(\",\", \".\")\n    else:\n        s = s.replace(\",\", \"\")\n\n    if not _PLAIN_NUMBER_RE.match(s):\n        raise TransformError(f\"Cannot read {raw!r} as a number\")\n\n    try:\n        value = Decimal(s)\n    except InvalidOperation as e:\n        raise TransformError(f\"Cannot read {raw!r} as a number\") from e\n    return -value if negative else value\n\n\ndef number(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"1,23,456.78 | 123,456.78 | (1,234) | -1,234 | 1,234- | Rs. 500\"\"\"\n    return _to_decimal(raw)\n\n\ndef number_drcr(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"Like number, but a trailing Dr means negative and Cr means positive.\"\"\"\n    return _to_decimal(raw, drcr=True)\n\n\ndef number_eu(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"European style: 1.234,56\"\"\"\n    return _to_decimal(raw, eu=True)\n\n\ndef percent(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"12.5% -> Decimal('12.5')  (kept as a percentage, not 0.125)\"\"\"\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n    return _to_decimal(str(raw).replace(\"%\", \"\"))\n\n\n# ---------- dates ----------\n\ndef _make_date_parser(fmt: str) -> Callable[[Optional[str]], Optional[date]]:\n    def parse(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[date]:\n        if _is_empty(raw):\n            return None\n        cleaned = \" \".join(str(raw).split())\n        try:\n            return datetime.strptime(cleaned, fmt).date()\n        except ValueError as e:\n            raise TransformError(f\"Cannot read {raw!r} as a date ({fmt})\") from e\n\n    return parse\n\n\n# ---------- text ----------\n\ndef text(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n    return \" \".join(str(raw).split())\n\n\ndef isin(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n    return str(raw).replace(\" \", \"\").upper()\n\n\n_TXN_KEYWORDS = [  # order matters: first match wins\n    (TransactionType.DIVIDEND, [\"dividend\"]),\n    (TransactionType.FEE, [\"fee\", \"charge\", \"brokerage\"]),\n    (TransactionType.BUY, [\"buy\", \"purchase\", \"bought\"]),\n    (TransactionType.SELL, [\"sell\", \"sale\", \"sold\"]),\n    (TransactionType.INFLOW, [\"inflow\", \"deposit\", \"contribution\", \"capital call\",\n                              \"subscription\", \"funds added\"]),\n    (TransactionType.OUTFLOW, [\"outflow\", \"withdraw\", \"redemption\", \"distribution\"]),\n]\n\n\ndef transaction_type(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[TransactionType]:\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n    label = str(raw).lower()\n    for txn_type, keywords in _TXN_KEYWORDS:\n        if any(k in label for k in keywords):\n            return txn_type\n    return TransactionType.OTHER  # Part 6 will flag statements containing OTHER\n\n\n# ---------- the registry ----------\n\nTRANSFORMS: dict[str, Callable[[Optional[str]], Any]] = {\n    \"text\": text,\n    \"isin\": isin,\n    \"number\": number,\n    \"number_drcr\": number_drcr,\n    \"number_eu\": number_eu,\n    \"percent\": percent,\n    \"txn_type\": transaction_type,\n    \"date_dd_mon_yyyy\": _make_date_parser(\"%d-%b-%Y\"),       # 01-Apr-2026\n    \"date_dd_mm_yyyy\": _make_date_parser(\"%d/%m/%Y\"),        # 01/04/2026\n    \"date_dd_mm_yyyy_dash\": _make_date_parser(\"%d-%m-%Y\"),   # 01-04-2026\n    \"date_iso\": _make_date_parser(\"%Y-%m-%d\"),               # 2026-04-01\n    \"date_dd_month_yyyy\": _make_date_parser(\"%d %B %Y\"),     # 1 April 2026\n    \"date_month_dd_yyyy\": _make_date_parser(\"%B %d, %Y\"),    # April 1, 2026\n}\n\n\ndef apply_transform(name: str, raw: Optional[str]) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"The only way the engine runs a transform. Unknown names are rejected.\"\"\"\n    if name not in TRANSFORMS:\n        raise UnknownTransformError(f\"Transform {name!r} is not in the registry\")\n    return TRANSFORMS[name](raw)\n\n\ndef is_known_transform(name: str) -> bool:\n    return name in TRANSFORMS\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create `tests/test_transforms.py`\n\n```python\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.schema import TransactionType\nfrom app.transforms import (\n    TransformError, UnknownTransformError, apply_transform, is_known_transform,\n)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw, expected\", [\n    (\"3,45,000.00\", Decimal(\"345000.00\")),   # Indian grouping\n    (\"345,000.00\", Decimal(\"345000.00\")),    # international grouping\n    (\"(1,234.00)\", Decimal(\"-1234.00\")),     # brackets\n    (\"-1,234.50\", Decimal(\"-1234.50\")),      # leading minus\n    (\"1,234.50-\", Decimal(\"-1234.50\")),      # trailing minus\n    (\"\u20b9 1,00,000\", Decimal(\"100000\")),\n    (\"Rs. 5,000.50\", Decimal(\"5000.50\")),\n    (\"  120  \", Decimal(\"120\")),\n    (\"-\", None),\n    (\"\", None),\n    (None, None),\n])\ndef test_number(raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(\"number\", raw) == expected\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw\", [\"abc\", \"12.5.3\", \"1,2x4\", \"Dr 500\"])\ndef test_number_rejects_garbage(raw):\n    with pytest.raises(TransformError):\n        apply_transform(\"number\", raw)\n\n\ndef test_number_does_not_silently_accept_drcr():\n    # Dr/Cr must be opted into via number_drcr. Otherwise it fails loudly.\n    with pytest.raises(TransformError):\n        apply_transform(\"number\", \"1,234.00 Dr\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw, expected\", [\n    (\"1,234.00 Dr\", Decimal(\"-1234.00\")),\n    (\"1,234.00 Cr\", Decimal(\"1234.00\")),\n    (\"500 CR\", Decimal(\"500\")),\n    (\"500\", Decimal(\"500\")),\n])\ndef test_number_drcr(raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_drcr\", raw) == expected\n\n\ndef test_number_eu():\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_eu\", \"1.234,56\") == Decimal(\"1234.56\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw, expected\", [\n    (\"12.5%\", Decimal(\"12.5\")),\n    (\"12.5 %\", Decimal(\"12.5\")),\n    (\"(2.5)%\", Decimal(\"-2.5\")),\n    (\"-\", None),\n])\ndef test_percent(raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(\"percent\", raw) == expected\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name, raw, expected\", [\n    (\"date_dd_mon_yyyy\", \"01-Apr-2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_dd_mon_yyyy\", \"01-APR-2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_dd_mm_yyyy\", \"01/04/2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_dd_mm_yyyy_dash\", \"01-04-2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_iso\", \"2026-04-01\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_dd_month_yyyy\", \"1 April 2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_month_dd_yyyy\", \"April 1, 2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_iso\", \"\", None),\n])\ndef test_dates(name, raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(name, raw) == expected\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name, raw\", [\n    (\"date_dd_mm_yyyy\", \"31/02/2026\"),   # impossible date\n    (\"date_dd_mm_yyyy\", \"2026-04-01\"),   # wrong style for this transform\n    (\"date_dd_mon_yyyy\", \"hello\"),\n])\ndef test_dates_reject_bad_input(name, raw):\n    with pytest.raises(TransformError):\n        apply_transform(name, raw)\n\n\ndef test_dd_mm_is_not_mm_dd():\n    # 04/05/2026 is 4 May under dd/mm. The config must pick the right one.\n    assert apply_transform(\"date_dd_mm_yyyy\", \"04/05/2026\") == date(2026, 5, 4)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw, expected\", [\n    (\"Purchase\", TransactionType.BUY),\n    (\"SALE\", TransactionType.SELL),\n    (\"Dividend Received\", TransactionType.DIVIDEND),\n    (\"Management Fee\", TransactionType.FEE),\n    (\"Capital Call\", TransactionType.INFLOW),\n    (\"Withdrawal\", TransactionType.OUTFLOW),\n    (\"something weird\", TransactionType.OTHER),\n])\ndef test_txn_type(raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(\"txn_type\", raw) == expected\n\n\ndef test_isin_and_text():\n    assert apply_transform(\"isin\", \"ine002a01018 \") == \"INE002A01018\"\n    assert apply_transform(\"text\", \"  Reliance   Industries \") == \"Reliance Industries\"\n\n\ndef test_unknown_transform_is_rejected():\n    assert not is_known_transform(\"do_something_clever\")\n    with pytest.raises(UnknownTransformError):\n        apply_transform(\"do_something_clever\", \"x\")\n```\n\n## Step 4: Create `tests/test_schema.py`\n\n```python\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nimport pytest\nfrom pydantic import ValidationError\n\nfrom app.schema import Holding, Statement, StatementType, Summary\n\n\ndef make_statement(**overrides):\n    data = dict(\n        statement_type=StatementType.PMS,\n        provider=\"ABC Portfolio Managers\",\n        client_id=\"AB1234\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 4, 1),\n        period_end=date(2026, 4, 30),\n    )\n    data.update(overrides)\n    return Statement(**data)\n\n\ndef test_minimal_pms_statement():\n    s = make_statement(holdings=[\n        Holding(security_name=\"Reliance Industries\", isin=\"ine002a01018\",\n                quantity=Decimal(\"120\"), market_value=Decimal(\"345000.00\")),\n    ])\n    assert s.currency == \"INR\"\n    assert s.holdings[0].isin == \"INE002A01018\"       # normalised\n    assert s.summary.nav_per_unit is None             # PMS has no NAV\n\n\ndef test_aif_statement_without_holdings():\n    s = make_statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.AIF,\n        summary=Summary(nav_per_unit=Decimal(\"1234.5678\"), units_held=Decimal(\"1000\")),\n    )\n    assert s.holdings == []\n    assert s.summary.nav_per_unit == Decimal(\"1234.5678\")\n\n\ndef test_period_end_before_start_is_rejected():\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        make_statement(period_start=date(2026, 5, 1), period_end=date(2026, 4, 1))\n\n\ndef test_missing_client_id_is_rejected():\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        make_statement(client_id=\"\")\n\n\ndef test_bad_isin_is_kept_not_rejected():\n    # Flagging bad ISINs is validation's job (Part 6), not the schema's.\n    h = Holding(security_name=\"X\", isin=\"NOTANISIN\", market_value=Decimal(\"1\"))\n    assert h.isin == \"NOTANISIN\"\n\n\ndef test_decimal_survives_json_round_trip():\n    s = make_statement(summary=Summary(closing_value=Decimal(\"655000.10\")))\n    restored = Statement.model_validate_json(s.model_dump_json())\n    assert restored.summary.closing_value == Decimal(\"655000.10\")\n```\n\n## Step 5: Run the tests\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -v\n```\n\nYou should see all tests pass. If any fail, paste the error and I'll help you debug it.\n\n## Step 6: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 1: schema and transform registry with tests\"\ngit push\n```\n\n---\n\n## Things to be able to explain after this part\n\n1. Why `Decimal` and not `float`?\n2. Why are most `Summary` and `Holding` fields `Optional`?\n3. Why does `number` reject `\"1,234.00 Dr\"` instead of guessing? (Silent wrong answers are worse than loud failures.)\n4. Why does the schema accept a malformed ISIN but reject an end date before the start date?\n5. What stops the LLM from inventing a transform? (`apply_transform` checks the registry, and Part 7 will check configs against `is_known_transform` before storing them.)\n\nWhen your tests pass, tell me and we'll start **Part 2: generating the sample statements**. That's the most creative part: we'll make 3 or 4 fake statements with different layouts, including a password-protected one.", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-10T08:20:53.194590Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-10T08:21:41.479760Z", "flags": null, "type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "summaries": [{"summary": "Building the initial setup and schema with tests."}, {"summary": "Designing data models for holdings, transactions, and summaries."}, {"summary": "Building number and date parsing transforms for messy inputs."}, {"summary": "Mapping transaction types and currency formats to decimal values."}, {"summary": "Normalizing sign conventions for negatives and amount notations."}, {"summary": "Defining matching rules for transaction type keywords."}, {"summary": "Finalizing data model fields and setup instructions for both platforms."}, {"summary": "Verifying parsing cases for amounts, dates, and sign formats."}], "cut_off": false, "truncated": true, "hidden": false, "thinking_hidden": true, "alternative_display_type": null, "signature": null}, {"start_timestamp": "2026-10-10T08:21:41.479799Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-10T08:22:23.061259Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "# Part 0 and Part 1: Setup, Schema and Transforms\n\nOne correction to my earlier example first. `3,45,000.00` (Indian grouping) and `345,000.00` (international grouping) are the same thing once you remove the commas, so we don't need separate transforms for them. We'll have a single `number` transform that handles both.\n\nToday is the last day for clarification questions, so if you haven't emailed hiring@activv.money about password handling and scanned PDFs, do it now.\n\n---\n\n# Part 0: Project setup\n\n## Step 1: Check Python\n\n```bash\npython --version\n```\n\nYou need **3.10 or higher**. If not, install Python 3.11 or 3.12 from python.org.\n\n## Step 2: Create the project folder and Git repo\n\n**Mac/Linux:**\n```bash\nmkdir statement-parser && cd statement-parser\ngit init\nmkdir app samples configs tests docs\ntouch app/__init__.py\n```\n\n**Windows (PowerShell):**\n```powershell\nmkdir statement-parser; cd statement-parser\ngit init\nmkdir app, samples, configs, tests, docs\nNew-Item app/__init__.py -ItemType File\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create a virtual environment\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\n```\n\nActivate it:\n- Mac/Linux: `source .venv/bin/activate`\n- Windows: `.venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1`\n\nYour terminal prompt should now start with `(.venv)`.\n\n## Step 4: Create `requirements.txt`\n\n```text\npydantic>=2.5\npytest>=8.0\npdfplumber>=0.11\npikepdf>=9.0\nreportlab>=4.0\nopenpyxl>=3.1\npython-dotenv>=1.0\nfastapi>=0.110\nuvicorn>=0.29\n```\n\nInstall:\n```bash\npip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\nWe won't use all of these yet, but installing now avoids interruptions later.\n\n## Step 5: Create `.gitignore`\n\nThe brief says to never commit passwords, API keys or personal details.\n\n```text\n.venv/\n__pycache__/\n*.pyc\n.pytest_cache/\n.env\n*.db\n*.sqlite3\ncredentials.json\ntoken.json\n.DS_Store\n.idea/\n.vscode/\n```\n\n## Step 6: Create `.env.example`\n\nReal secrets go in `.env`, which is ignored. This file only shows which variables exist:\n\n```text\nGMAIL_ADDRESS=your-test-account@gmail.com\nGMAIL_APP_PASSWORD=\nLLM_API_KEY=\nLLM_PROVIDER=\n```\n\n## Step 7: Create `pytest.ini`\n\nThis lets tests import from `app`:\n\n```ini\n[pytest]\npythonpath = .\ntestpaths = tests\n```\n\n## Step 8: First commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Project setup\"\n```\n\nThen create an empty repo on GitHub and push:\n```bash\ngit remote add origin <your-repo-url>\ngit branch -M main\ngit push -u origin main\n```\n\nPart 0 is done.\n\n---\n\n# Part 1: Schema and transforms\n\n## What we're building and why\n\n- **`schema.py`**: the standard shape every statement ends up in, whatever the provider.\n- **`transforms.py`**: the whitelist of trusted functions that turn raw text like `\"(1,234.00)\"` into `Decimal(\"-1234.00\")`.\n\nThree design decisions to remember for the interview:\n\n1. **`Decimal`, never `float`.** `0.1 + 0.2` in float is `0.30000000000000004`. For money that's unacceptable.\n2. **Most fields are `Optional`.** An AIF has no holdings table, and a PMS has no NAV per unit. One schema must fit both.\n3. **The schema is lenient about suspicious data and strict about impossible data.** A malformed ISIN shouldn't crash the parse. It should be *flagged* in Part 6. But a period that ends before it starts is structurally impossible, so the schema rejects it.\n\n## Step 1: Create `app/schema.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Standard output structure. Every provider's statement is converted into this.\"\"\"\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom decimal import Decimal\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator\n\n\nclass StatementType(str, Enum):\n    PMS = \"pms\"\n    AIF = \"aif\"\n\n\nclass TransactionType(str, Enum):\n    BUY = \"buy\"\n    SELL = \"sell\"\n    DIVIDEND = \"dividend\"\n    FEE = \"fee\"\n    INFLOW = \"inflow\"\n    OUTFLOW = \"outflow\"\n    OTHER = \"other\"  # unrecognised label; validation (Part 6) will flag these\n\n\nclass Holding(BaseModel):\n    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)\n\n    security_name: str = Field(min_length=1)\n    isin: Optional[str] = None\n    quantity: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    cost: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    market_price: Optional[Decimal] = None  # used later for qty x price check\n    market_value: Decimal\n    weight_pct: Optional[Decimal] = None  # 12.5 means 12.5%\n\n    @field_validator(\"isin\", mode=\"before\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _normalise_isin(cls, v):\n        # Only normalise here. Format and checksum are checked in validation (Part 6),\n        # so a bad ISIN gets flagged instead of crashing the whole parse.\n        if v is None:\n            return None\n        v = str(v).replace(\" \", \"\").upper()\n        return v or None\n\n\nclass Transaction(BaseModel):\n    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)\n\n    date: date\n    type: TransactionType\n    security_name: Optional[str] = None  # fees and inflows may have no security\n    quantity: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    amount: Decimal\n\n\nclass Summary(BaseModel):\n    opening_value: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    closing_value: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    cash_balance: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    fees_charged: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    nav_per_unit: Optional[Decimal] = None   # AIF\n    units_held: Optional[Decimal] = None     # AIF\n    # Optional extras, used by the reconciliation check in Part 6:\n    capital_inflows: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    capital_outflows: Optional[Decimal] = None\n    net_gain: Optional[Decimal] = None\n\n\nclass Statement(BaseModel):\n    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)\n\n    statement_type: StatementType\n    provider: str = Field(min_length=1)\n    strategy_name: Optional[str] = None\n    client_id: str = Field(min_length=1)\n    period_start: date\n    period_end: date\n    currency: str = \"INR\"\n\n    summary: Summary = Field(default_factory=Summary)\n    holdings: list[Holding] = Field(default_factory=list)\n    transactions: list[Transaction] = Field(default_factory=list)\n\n    source_file_hash: Optional[str] = None  # filled by the pipeline later\n\n    @field_validator(\"currency\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _upper_currency(cls, v: str) -> str:\n        return v.upper()\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def _check_period(self):\n        if self.period_end < self.period_start:\n            raise ValueError(\"period_end is before period_start\")\n        return self\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `app/transforms.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Whitelist of trusted value-parsing functions.\n\nThe LLM may only *name* these in a config. It can never add new ones.\nEvery transform takes a raw string and returns a clean value, or None if the\ncell is empty. If the text can't be understood, it raises TransformError\n(loud failure, never a silent wrong number).\n\"\"\"\nimport re\nfrom datetime import date, datetime\nfrom decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation\nfrom typing import Any, Callable, Optional\n\nfrom app.schema import TransactionType\n\n\nclass TransformError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"The raw text could not be interpreted by this transform.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownTransformError(KeyError):\n    \"\"\"A config named a transform that is not in the registry.\"\"\"\n\n\n_EMPTY_MARKERS = {\"\", \"-\", \"--\", \"\u2014\", \"\u2013\", \"nil\", \"n/a\", \"na\"}\n_CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r\"(\u20b9|rs\\.?|inr)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n_PLAIN_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r\"^(\\d+(\\.\\d*)?|\\.\\d+)$\")\n\n\ndef _is_empty(raw: Optional[str]) -> bool:\n    return raw is None or str(raw).strip().lower() in _EMPTY_MARKERS\n\n\n# ---------- numbers ----------\n\ndef _to_decimal(raw: Optional[str], *, drcr: bool = False, eu: bool = False) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n\n    s = _CURRENCY_RE.sub(\"\", str(raw)).strip()\n    negative = False\n\n    # Trailing Dr/Cr, only when this transform explicitly allows it\n    if drcr:\n        m = re.search(r\"(dr|cr)\\.?$\", s, re.IGNORECASE)\n        if m:\n            negative = m.group(1).lower() == \"dr\"\n            s = s[: m.start()].strip()\n\n    # Brackets mean negative: (1,234.00)\n    if s.startswith(\"(\") and s.endswith(\")\"):\n        negative = True\n        s = s[1:-1].strip()\n\n    # Leading or trailing minus (including the unicode minus sign)\n    if s and s[0] in \"-\u2212\":\n        negative = True\n        s = s[1:].strip()\n    elif s and s[-1] in \"-\u2212\":\n        negative = True\n        s = s[:-1].strip()\n\n    s = s.replace(\" \", \"\")\n    # Removing commas handles both 3,45,000 (Indian) and 345,000 (international).\n    if eu:\n        s = s.replace(\".\", \"\").replace(\",\", \".\")\n    else:\n        s = s.replace(\",\", \"\")\n\n    if not _PLAIN_NUMBER_RE.match(s):\n        raise TransformError(f\"Cannot read {raw!r} as a number\")\n\n    try:\n        value = Decimal(s)\n    except InvalidOperation as e:\n        raise TransformError(f\"Cannot read {raw!r} as a number\") from e\n    return -value if negative else value\n\n\ndef number(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"1,23,456.78 | 123,456.78 | (1,234) | -1,234 | 1,234- | Rs. 500\"\"\"\n    return _to_decimal(raw)\n\n\ndef number_drcr(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"Like number, but a trailing Dr means negative and Cr means positive.\"\"\"\n    return _to_decimal(raw, drcr=True)\n\n\ndef number_eu(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"European style: 1.234,56\"\"\"\n    return _to_decimal(raw, eu=True)\n\n\ndef percent(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"12.5% -> Decimal('12.5')  (kept as a percentage, not 0.125)\"\"\"\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n    return _to_decimal(str(raw).replace(\"%\", \"\"))\n\n\n# ---------- dates ----------\n\ndef _make_date_parser(fmt: str) -> Callable[[Optional[str]], Optional[date]]:\n    def parse(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[date]:\n        if _is_empty(raw):\n            return None\n        cleaned = \" \".join(str(raw).split())\n        try:\n            return datetime.strptime(cleaned, fmt).date()\n        except ValueError as e:\n            raise TransformError(f\"Cannot read {raw!r} as a date ({fmt})\") from e\n\n    return parse\n\n\n# ---------- text ----------\n\ndef text(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n    return \" \".join(str(raw).split())\n\n\ndef isin(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n    return str(raw).replace(\" \", \"\").upper()\n\n\n_TXN_KEYWORDS = [  # order matters: first match wins\n    (TransactionType.DIVIDEND, [\"dividend\"]),\n    (TransactionType.FEE, [\"fee\", \"charge\", \"brokerage\"]),\n    (TransactionType.BUY, [\"buy\", \"purchase\", \"bought\"]),\n    (TransactionType.SELL, [\"sell\", \"sale\", \"sold\"]),\n    (TransactionType.INFLOW, [\"inflow\", \"deposit\", \"contribution\", \"capital call\",\n                              \"subscription\", \"funds added\"]),\n    (TransactionType.OUTFLOW, [\"outflow\", \"withdraw\", \"redemption\", \"distribution\"]),\n]\n\n\ndef transaction_type(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[TransactionType]:\n    if _is_empty(raw):\n        return None\n    label = str(raw).lower()\n    for txn_type, keywords in _TXN_KEYWORDS:\n        if any(k in label for k in keywords):\n            return txn_type\n    return TransactionType.OTHER  # Part 6 will flag statements containing OTHER\n\n\n# ---------- the registry ----------\n\nTRANSFORMS: dict[str, Callable[[Optional[str]], Any]] = {\n    \"text\": text,\n    \"isin\": isin,\n    \"number\": number,\n    \"number_drcr\": number_drcr,\n    \"number_eu\": number_eu,\n    \"percent\": percent,\n    \"txn_type\": transaction_type,\n    \"date_dd_mon_yyyy\": _make_date_parser(\"%d-%b-%Y\"),       # 01-Apr-2026\n    \"date_dd_mm_yyyy\": _make_date_parser(\"%d/%m/%Y\"),        # 01/04/2026\n    \"date_dd_mm_yyyy_dash\": _make_date_parser(\"%d-%m-%Y\"),   # 01-04-2026\n    \"date_iso\": _make_date_parser(\"%Y-%m-%d\"),               # 2026-04-01\n    \"date_dd_month_yyyy\": _make_date_parser(\"%d %B %Y\"),     # 1 April 2026\n    \"date_month_dd_yyyy\": _make_date_parser(\"%B %d, %Y\"),    # April 1, 2026\n}\n\n\ndef apply_transform(name: str, raw: Optional[str]) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"The only way the engine runs a transform. Unknown names are rejected.\"\"\"\n    if name not in TRANSFORMS:\n        raise UnknownTransformError(f\"Transform {name!r} is not in the registry\")\n    return TRANSFORMS[name](raw)\n\n\ndef is_known_transform(name: str) -> bool:\n    return name in TRANSFORMS\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create `tests/test_transforms.py`\n\n```python\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.schema import TransactionType\nfrom app.transforms import (\n    TransformError, UnknownTransformError, apply_transform, is_known_transform,\n)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw, expected\", [\n    (\"3,45,000.00\", Decimal(\"345000.00\")),   # Indian grouping\n    (\"345,000.00\", Decimal(\"345000.00\")),    # international grouping\n    (\"(1,234.00)\", Decimal(\"-1234.00\")),     # brackets\n    (\"-1,234.50\", Decimal(\"-1234.50\")),      # leading minus\n    (\"1,234.50-\", Decimal(\"-1234.50\")),      # trailing minus\n    (\"\u20b9 1,00,000\", Decimal(\"100000\")),\n    (\"Rs. 5,000.50\", Decimal(\"5000.50\")),\n    (\"  120  \", Decimal(\"120\")),\n    (\"-\", None),\n    (\"\", None),\n    (None, None),\n])\ndef test_number(raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(\"number\", raw) == expected\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw\", [\"abc\", \"12.5.3\", \"1,2x4\", \"Dr 500\"])\ndef test_number_rejects_garbage(raw):\n    with pytest.raises(TransformError):\n        apply_transform(\"number\", raw)\n\n\ndef test_number_does_not_silently_accept_drcr():\n    # Dr/Cr must be opted into via number_drcr. Otherwise it fails loudly.\n    with pytest.raises(TransformError):\n        apply_transform(\"number\", \"1,234.00 Dr\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw, expected\", [\n    (\"1,234.00 Dr\", Decimal(\"-1234.00\")),\n    (\"1,234.00 Cr\", Decimal(\"1234.00\")),\n    (\"500 CR\", Decimal(\"500\")),\n    (\"500\", Decimal(\"500\")),\n])\ndef test_number_drcr(raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_drcr\", raw) == expected\n\n\ndef test_number_eu():\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_eu\", \"1.234,56\") == Decimal(\"1234.56\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw, expected\", [\n    (\"12.5%\", Decimal(\"12.5\")),\n    (\"12.5 %\", Decimal(\"12.5\")),\n    (\"(2.5)%\", Decimal(\"-2.5\")),\n    (\"-\", None),\n])\ndef test_percent(raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(\"percent\", raw) == expected\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name, raw, expected\", [\n    (\"date_dd_mon_yyyy\", \"01-Apr-2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_dd_mon_yyyy\", \"01-APR-2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_dd_mm_yyyy\", \"01/04/2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_dd_mm_yyyy_dash\", \"01-04-2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_iso\", \"2026-04-01\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_dd_month_yyyy\", \"1 April 2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_month_dd_yyyy\", \"April 1, 2026\", date(2026, 4, 1)),\n    (\"date_iso\", \"\", None),\n])\ndef test_dates(name, raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(name, raw) == expected\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name, raw\", [\n    (\"date_dd_mm_yyyy\", \"31/02/2026\"),   # impossible date\n    (\"date_dd_mm_yyyy\", \"2026-04-01\"),   # wrong style for this transform\n    (\"date_dd_mon_yyyy\", \"hello\"),\n])\ndef test_dates_reject_bad_input(name, raw):\n    with pytest.raises(TransformError):\n        apply_transform(name, raw)\n\n\ndef test_dd_mm_is_not_mm_dd():\n    # 04/05/2026 is 4 May under dd/mm. The config must pick the right one.\n    assert apply_transform(\"date_dd_mm_yyyy\", \"04/05/2026\") == date(2026, 5, 4)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"raw, expected\", [\n    (\"Purchase\", TransactionType.BUY),\n    (\"SALE\", TransactionType.SELL),\n    (\"Dividend Received\", TransactionType.DIVIDEND),\n    (\"Management Fee\", TransactionType.FEE),\n    (\"Capital Call\", TransactionType.INFLOW),\n    (\"Withdrawal\", TransactionType.OUTFLOW),\n    (\"something weird\", TransactionType.OTHER),\n])\ndef test_txn_type(raw, expected):\n    assert apply_transform(\"txn_type\", raw) == expected\n\n\ndef test_isin_and_text():\n    assert apply_transform(\"isin\", \"ine002a01018 \") == \"INE002A01018\"\n    assert apply_transform(\"text\", \"  Reliance   Industries \") == \"Reliance Industries\"\n\n\ndef test_unknown_transform_is_rejected():\n    assert not is_known_transform(\"do_something_clever\")\n    with pytest.raises(UnknownTransformError):\n        apply_transform(\"do_something_clever\", \"x\")\n```\n\n## Step 4: Create `tests/test_schema.py`\n\n```python\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nimport pytest\nfrom pydantic import ValidationError\n\nfrom app.schema import Holding, Statement, StatementType, Summary\n\n\ndef make_statement(**overrides):\n    data = dict(\n        statement_type=StatementType.PMS,\n        provider=\"ABC Portfolio Managers\",\n        client_id=\"AB1234\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 4, 1),\n        period_end=date(2026, 4, 30),\n    )\n    data.update(overrides)\n    return Statement(**data)\n\n\ndef test_minimal_pms_statement():\n    s = make_statement(holdings=[\n        Holding(security_name=\"Reliance Industries\", isin=\"ine002a01018\",\n                quantity=Decimal(\"120\"), market_value=Decimal(\"345000.00\")),\n    ])\n    assert s.currency == \"INR\"\n    assert s.holdings[0].isin == \"INE002A01018\"       # normalised\n    assert s.summary.nav_per_unit is None             # PMS has no NAV\n\n\ndef test_aif_statement_without_holdings():\n    s = make_statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.AIF,\n        summary=Summary(nav_per_unit=Decimal(\"1234.5678\"), units_held=Decimal(\"1000\")),\n    )\n    assert s.holdings == []\n    assert s.summary.nav_per_unit == Decimal(\"1234.5678\")\n\n\ndef test_period_end_before_start_is_rejected():\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        make_statement(period_start=date(2026, 5, 1), period_end=date(2026, 4, 1))\n\n\ndef test_missing_client_id_is_rejected():\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        make_statement(client_id=\"\")\n\n\ndef test_bad_isin_is_kept_not_rejected():\n    # Flagging bad ISINs is validation's job (Part 6), not the schema's.\n    h = Holding(security_name=\"X\", isin=\"NOTANISIN\", market_value=Decimal(\"1\"))\n    assert h.isin == \"NOTANISIN\"\n\n\ndef test_decimal_survives_json_round_trip():\n    s = make_statement(summary=Summary(closing_value=Decimal(\"655000.10\")))\n    restored = Statement.model_validate_json(s.model_dump_json())\n    assert restored.summary.closing_value == Decimal(\"655000.10\")\n```\n\n## Step 5: Run the tests\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -v\n```\n\nYou should see all tests pass. If any fail, paste the error and I'll help you debug it.\n\n## Step 6: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 1: schema and transform registry with tests\"\ngit push\n```\n\n---\n\n## Things to be able to explain after this part\n\n1. Why `Decimal` and not `float`?\n2. Why are most `Summary` and `Holding` fields `Optional`?\n3. Why does `number` reject `\"1,234.00 Dr\"` instead of guessing? (Silent wrong answers are worse than loud failures.)\n4. Why does the schema accept a malformed ISIN but reject an end date before the start date?\n5. What stops the LLM from inventing a transform? (`apply_transform` checks the registry, and Part 7 will check configs against `is_known_transform` before storing them.)\n\nWhen your tests pass, tell me and we'll start **Part 2: generating the sample statements**. That's the most creative part: we'll make 3 or 4 fake statements with different layouts, including a password-protected one.", "citations": []}], "sender": "assistant", "created_at": "2026-10-10T08:22:23.132791Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-10T08:22:23.132791Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a124e6-8c0d-7bc8-a9fb-697fb2ba6155"}, {"uuid": "01a124ff-ad06-7978-a53b-f4ae479f85e9", "text": "can you just tell me this instead of commiting after every step should i just commit after finishing the project or not", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-10T08:48:19.620155Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-10T08:48:19.620155Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "can you just tell me this instead of commiting after every step should i just commit after finishing the project or not", "citations": []}], "sender": "human", "created_at": "2026-10-10T08:48:19.620404Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-10T08:48:19.620404Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a124e6-8c0d-7e4b-ab67-cc5bd309e421"}, {"uuid": "01a124ff-ad06-7f84-8269-32dff844b0d6", "text": "Don't wait until the end. If your laptop dies on 15 Oct, you still have everything on GitHub.\n\n**Why not after every tiny step**\n- It's noise, and it's slow. I'd avoid putting \"Activv\" or \"internship assignment\" in the name, since the repo is public (or at least visible to the reviewers) and a neutral, descriptive name looks more professional.\n\n**Description** (the one-liner under the name):\n\n```\nSelf-learning parser for PMS/AIF statements: an LLM learns each new format once, then a deterministic engine parses it with no AI.\n```\n\n## Creating it on GitHub\n\n1. Go to github.com, click **+** (top right), then **New repository**.\n2. Enter the name and description above.\n3. Choose **Public** or **Private**. Either works, but if Private, you must give the reviewers access before they ask for it. The brief says the repo must stay accessible until the discussion is complete.\n4. **Important:** leave **all three boxes unchecked**: no README, no .gitignore, no license. You already have local files, and adding them on GitHub creates a conflict on your first push.\n5. Click **Create repository**.\n\nGitHub then shows a page with commands. You only need the repository URL, which looks like:\n\n```\nhttps://github.com/<your-username>/self-learning-statement-parser.git\n```\n\n## Connecting your local project and pushing\n\nRun these inside your `statement-parser` folder (with Part 0 already committed):\n\n```bash\ngit remote add origin https://github.com/<your-username>/self-learning-statement-parser.git\ngit branch -M main\ngit push -u origin main\n```\n\nIf you haven't committed yet, do that first:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Project setup\"\n```\n\nAfter the push, refresh the GitHub page and you should see your files.\n\n## Authentication problem you may hit\n\nGitHub no longer accepts your account password when pushing over HTTPS. If it asks for a password and rejects it:\n\n- **Easiest:** install **GitHub CLI** (`gh`) and run `gh auth login`, then push again.\n- **Or:** create a **Personal Access Token** (GitHub \u2192 Settings \u2192 Developer settings \u2192 Personal access tokens \u2192 Tokens (classic) \u2192 give it the `repo` scope) and paste it as the password.\n- **Or:** use **GitHub Desktop**, which handles login for you.\n\n## Committing from now on\n\nEvery time you finish something:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 1: schema and transform registry with tests\"\ngit push\n```\n\nBefore `git add .`, a quick habit worth building:\n\n```bash\ngit status\n```\n\nCheck that no `.env`, no `.db` file and no real PDFs with personal data are listed. Your `.gitignore` covers `.env` and `.db`, but it's good to look.\n\n## Commit message style\n\nShort, in the present tense, saying what changed:\n\n- `Part 1: schema and transform registry with tests`\n- `Add PDF reader with password support`\n- `Fix Dr/Cr handling in number transform`\n\nAvoid messages like `update` or `changes`. Reviewers may read your history to see how the project evolved.\n\n## README heading\n\nYou'll write the full README at the end (Part 11), but for now you can create a placeholder `README.md`:\n\n```markdown\n# Self-Learning PMS/AIF Statement Parser\n\nAn LLM learns each new statement format once. Every later statement in that format is parsed deterministically, with no AI call.\n\n> Work in progress.\n```\n\nCommit it with:\n\n```bash\ngit add README.md\ngit commit -m \"Add README placeholder\"\ngit push\n```\n\nOnce the push works and your tests pass, tell me and we'll move on to **Part 2: generating the sample statements**.", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-10T09:20:31.457251Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-10T09:20:40.131774Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "# Creating the GitHub repo and connecting your local project\n\n## Repo name and description\n\n**Repository name** (lowercase, hyphens, no spaces):\n\n```\nself-learning-statement-parser\n```\n\nOther fine options: `pms-aif-statement-parser`, `activv-statement-parser`. You already have local files, and adding them on GitHub creates a conflict on your first push.\n5. Click **Create repository**.\n\nGitHub then shows a page with commands. You only need the repository URL, which looks like:\n\n```\nhttps://github.com/<your-username>/self-learning-statement-parser.git\n```\n\n## Connecting your local project and pushing\n\nRun these inside your `statement-parser` folder (with Part 0 already committed):\n\n```bash\ngit remote add origin https://github.com/<your-username>/self-learning-statement-parser.git\ngit branch -M main\ngit push -u origin main\n```\n\nIf you haven't committed yet, do that first:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Project setup\"\n```\n\nAfter the push, refresh the GitHub page and you should see your files.\n\n## Authentication problem you may hit\n\nGitHub no longer accepts your account password when pushing over HTTPS. If it asks for a password and rejects it:\n\n- **Easiest:** install **GitHub CLI** (`gh`) and run `gh auth login`, then push again.\n- **Or:** create a **Personal Access Token** (GitHub \u2192 Settings \u2192 Developer settings \u2192 Personal access tokens \u2192 Tokens (classic) \u2192 give it the `repo` scope) and paste it as the password.\n- **Or:** use **GitHub Desktop**, which handles login for you.\n\n## Committing from now on\n\nEvery time you finish something:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 1: schema and transform registry with tests\"\ngit push\n```\n\nBefore `git add .`, a quick habit worth building:\n\n```bash\ngit status\n```\n\nCheck that no `.env`, no `.db` file and no real PDFs with personal data are listed. Your `.gitignore` covers `.env` and `.db`, but it's good to look.\n\n## Commit message style\n\nShort, in the present tense, saying what changed:\n\n- `Part 1: schema and transform registry with tests`\n- `Add PDF reader with password support`\n- `Fix Dr/Cr handling in number transform`\n\nAvoid messages like `update` or `changes`. Reviewers may read your history to see how the project evolved.\n\n## README heading\n\nYou'll write the full README at the end (Part 11), but for now you can create a placeholder `README.md`:\n\n```markdown\n# Self-Learning PMS/AIF Statement Parser\n\nAn LLM learns each new statement format once. Every later statement in that format is parsed deterministically, with no AI call.\n\n> Work in progress.\n```\n\nCommit it with:\n\n```bash\ngit add README.md\ngit commit -m \"Add README placeholder\"\ngit push\n```\n\nOnce the push works and your tests pass, tell me and we'll move on to **Part 2: generating the sample statements**.", "citations": []}], "sender": "assistant", \"pydantic could not be resolved\"\n\nYour install worked (the log ends with `Successfully installed ... pydantic-2.14.0`). The warning is almost certainly **your editor** (VS Code with Pylance) looking at a different Python than the one in your `.venv`. Nothing is wrong with the code or the install.\n\nYour prompt shows `(.venv) (base)`, meaning conda's `base` is also active. That makes it easy for the editor to pick the wrong interpreter.\n\n## Step 1: Confirm the install works in the terminal\n\n```bash\npython -c \"import pydantic; print(pydantic.__version__)\"\n```\n\nIf it prints `2.14.0`, the install is fine and only the editor is confused.\n\nIf you want to be sure which Python is being used:\n\n```bash\nwhich python\n```\n\nIt should end in `.../internship project/.venv/bin/python`. If it points to conda's `base`, run `conda deactivate` once, then re-activate the venv:\n\n```bash\nconda deactivate\nsource .venv/bin/activate\n```\n\n## Step 2: Tell the editor to use the `.venv`\n\nIn VS Code:\n\n1. Press `Cmd + Shift + P`\n2. Type **Python: Select Interpreter** and press Enter\n3. Choose the one that shows `.venv` (path like `./.venv/bin/python`)\n   - If it isn't listed, choose **Enter interpreter path...** \u2192 **Find...** and select `.venv/bin/python` inside your project folder\n\nThen reload the window: `Cmd + Shift + P` \u2192 **Developer: Reload Window**. The yellow squiggle under `pydantic` should disappear.\n\n(If you're using PyCharm or another editor, the equivalent is setting the project interpreter to the `.venv` one.)\n\n## Step 3: The real test, run the tests\n\nThe editor warning doesn't matter if the tests pass. Make sure you've created the files from Part 1 (`app/schema.py`, `app/transforms.py`, `tests/test_transforms.py`, `tests/test_schema.py`), then run:\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -v\n```\n\nIf these pass, everything is fine regardless of what the editor shows.\n\n## Two small notes\n\n- **Folder name has spaces** (`internship project`). It works, but quote the path if you ever use it in a command, e.g. `cd \"internship project\"`.\n- You can ignore the `pip` upgrade notice. If you want to silence it: `pip install --upgrade pip`.\n\nIf the tests fail or `import pydantic` fails in the terminal, paste the exact error and I'll debug it. "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a12529-9026-7b76-8e9f-8059d7f4acc5"}, {"uuid": "01a12533-8a09-7e21-8004-73c2501fddd0", "text": "# Part 1 is done: all 52 tests pass\n\nCommit it:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 1: schema and transform registry with tests\"\ngit push\n```\n\nThe editor warning was just the interpreter mismatch. Your tests run against the right Python (`.venv/bin/python`, 3.13), so you can ignore it or fix it later with **Python: Select Interpreter**.\n\n---\n\n# Part 2: Synthetic sample statements\n\n## What we're building and why\n\nThe system needs statements to learn from and be tested on. Real client data is forbidden by the brief, so we generate our own. We'll create **4 formats**, deliberately different from each other:\n\n| # | Provider (fictional) | Type | Layout style | Special feature |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | ABC Portfolio Managers | PMS | Plain text table, Indian numbers, `01-Apr-2026` dates | Baseline |\n| 2 | XYZ Wealth | PMS | Different words, column order, `01/04/2026` dates, brackets for negatives | Password-protected |\n| 3 | Sterling Growth Fund | AIF | Capital account statement, no holdings table | NAV per unit, units |\n| 4 | Meridian Capital | PMS | Summary box on top, `Dr/Cr` amounts | Extra messy layout |\n\nEach sample gets **two files**:\n- the PDF (what the system reads)\n- an `expected.json` (the correct answer, written by the generator from the same data)\n\nThe `expected.json` is your answer key. Later, the test is: *does the engine's output equal the expected file?*\n\n## Design decisions to remember\n\n1. **One data source, two outputs.** The generator holds the real numbers in Python, draws the PDF from them, and writes `expected.json` from the same numbers. So the PDF and the answer key can never disagree.\n2. **The numbers are internally consistent.** Holdings sum to closing value, opening plus flows plus gains minus fees equals closing, weights sum to about 100%. This lets Part 6 validation pass on clean samples.\n3. **Seeded values.** Everything is fixed, not random, so the output is reproducible.\n4. **Fake data only.** Fictional providers, fake client codes, ISINs that pass the checksum.\n\n## Step 1: ISIN checksum helper\n\nCreate `app/isin_util.py`. We need it now to generate valid ISINs, and again in Part 6 to validate them.\n\n```python\n\"\"\"ISIN check-digit logic (Luhn algorithm applied to the letters-as-numbers form).\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _expand(body: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Letters become two-digit numbers (A=10 ... Z=35); digits stay as they are.\"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(str(int(c, 36)) for c in body)\n\n\ndef _luhn_check_digit(digits: str) -> int:\n    total = 0\n    # Walk right to left. The check digit will sit to the right of this string,\n    # so the rightmost digit of `digits` is doubled.\n    for i, ch in enumerate(reversed(digits)):\n        d = int(ch)\n        if i % 2 == 0:\n            d *= 2\n            if d > 9:\n                d -= 9\n        total += d\n    return (10 - total % 10) % 10\n\n\ndef compute_check_digit(first_11: str) -> str:\n    return str(_luhn_check_digit(_expand(first_11.upper())))\n\n\ndef make_isin(first_11: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Build a valid ISIN from its first 11 characters.\"\"\"\n    return first_11.upper() + compute_check_digit(first_11)\n\n\ndef is_valid_isin(isin: str) -> bool:\n    isin = isin.strip().upper()\n    if len(isin) != 12 or not isin.isalnum() or not isin[:2].isalpha():\n        return False\n    if not isin[-1].isdigit():\n        return False\n    return compute_check_digit(isin[:11]) == isin[-1]\n```\n\n## Step 2: Test it against known real ISINs\n\nCreate `tests/test_isin.py`. These are well-known public ISINs, not client data:\n\n```python\nimport pytest\nfrom app.isin_util import is_valid_isin, make_isin\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"isin\", [\n    \"INE002A01018\",  # Reliance Industries\n    \"INE040A01034\",  # HDFC Bank\n    \"INE009A01021\",  # Infosys\n    \"US0378331005\",  # Apple\n])\ndef test_known_real_isins_are_valid(isin):\n    assert is_valid_isin(isin)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"isin\", [\n    \"INE002A01019\",   # wrong check digit\n    \"INE002A0101\",    # too short\n    \"12E002A01018\",   # country code must be letters\n    \"\",\n])\ndef test_bad_isins_are_rejected(isin):\n    assert not is_valid_isin(isin)\n\n\ndef test_make_isin_round_trip():\n    assert make_isin(\"INE002A0101\") == \"INE002A01018\"\n    assert is_valid_isin(make_isin(\"INE123A0100\"))\n```\n\nRun it:\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_isin.py -v\n```\n\nAll should pass. If one of the real ISINs fails, tell me. It would mean my algorithm has a bug and we fix it before going on.\n\n## Step 3: The sample data (single source of truth)\n\nCreate `samples/sample_data.py`. This holds the numbers for all four statements.\n\nI'm computing values from quantity and price so everything reconciles. Prices are fictional.\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Fictional statement data. The PDFs and expected.json are both generated from this.\"\"\"\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom decimal import Decimal as D\n\nfrom app.isin_util import make_isin\nfrom app.schema import (\n    Holding, Statement, StatementType, Summary, Transaction, TransactionType,\n)\n\nT = TransactionType\n\n\ndef _holdings(rows, total_value):\n    \"\"\"rows: (name, isin_first_11, qty, price, cost). Weight is computed from value.\"\"\"\n    out = []\n    for name, isin11, qty, price, cost in rows:\n        value = (D(qty) * D(price)).quantize(D(\"0.01\"))\n        out.append(Holding(\n            security_name=name,\n            isin=make_isin(isin11),\n            quantity=D(qty),\n            cost=D(cost),\n            market_price=D(price),\n            market_value=value,\n            weight_pct=(value / total_value * 100).quantize(D(\"0.01\")),\n        ))\n    return out\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. ABC (PMS)\ndef abc_pms() -> Statement:\n    rows = [\n        (\"Reliance Industries\", \"INE002A0101\", 120, \"2875.00\", \"310000.00\"),\n        (\"HDFC Bank\", \"INE040A0103\", 200, \"1550.00\", \"290000.00\"),\n        (\"Infosys\", \"INE009A0102\", 150, \"1480.00\", \"205000.00\"),\n        (\"Tata Consultancy Services\", \"INE467B0102\", 40, \"3950.00\", \"140000.00\"),\n        (\"ITC\", \"INE154A0102\", 500, \"420.00\", \"190000.00\"),\n    ]\n    equity = sum(D(q) * D(p) for _, _, q, p, _ in rows)      # 1,215,000\n    cash = D(\"85000.00\")\n    closing = equity + cash                                   # 1,300,000\n    hold = _holdings(rows, closing)\n    return Statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.PMS,\n        provider=\"ABC Portfolio Managers\",\n        strategy_name=\"ABC Large Cap Growth\",\n        client_id=\"AB1234\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 4, 1), period_end=date(2026, 4, 30),\n        holdings=hold,\n        transactions=[\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 6), type=T.BUY, security_name=\"Infosys\",\n                        quantity=D(\"50\"), amount=D(\"72000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 15), type=T.SELL, security_name=\"ITC\",\n                        quantity=D(\"100\"), amount=D(\"41000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 22), type=T.DIVIDEND, security_name=\"HDFC Bank\",\n                        amount=D(\"3000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 30), type=T.FEE,\n                        security_name=\"Management fee\", amount=D(\"8000.00\")),\n        ],\n        summary=Summary(\n            opening_value=D(\"1200000.00\"),\n            closing_value=closing,\n            cash_balance=cash,\n            fees_charged=D(\"8000.00\"),\n            capital_inflows=D(\"50000.00\"),\n            capital_outflows=D(\"0.00\"),\n            net_gain=closing - D(\"1200000.00\") - D(\"50000.00\") + D(\"8000.00\"),  # 58,000\n        ),\n    )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. XYZ (PMS)\ndef xyz_wealth() -> Statement:\n    rows = [\n        (\"Bajaj Finance\", \"INE296A0102\", 60, \"7100.00\", \"390000.00\"),\n        (\"Larsen & Toubro\", \"INE018A0103\", 90, \"3600.00\", \"270000.00\"),\n        (\"Asian Paints\", \"INE021A0102\", 70, \"2400.00\", \"150000.00\"),\n        (\"Maruti Suzuki India\", \"INE585B0101\", 25, \"12500.00\", \"280000.00\"),\n    ]\n    equity = sum(D(q) * D(p) for _, _, q, p, _ in rows)      # 1,375,000\n    cash = D(\"125000.00\")\n    closing = equity + cash                                   # 1,500,000\n    hold = _holdings(rows, closing)\n    return Statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.PMS,\n        provider=\"XYZ Wealth\",\n        strategy_name=\"XYZ Multicap Opportunities\",\n        client_id=\"98765\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 4, 1), period_end=date(2026, 4, 30),\n        holdings=hold,\n        transactions=[\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 3), type=T.INFLOW,\n                        security_name=\"Funds added\", amount=D(\"100000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 9), type=T.BUY, security_name=\"Asian Paints\",\n                        quantity=D(\"20\"), amount=D(\"47000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 17), type=T.OUTFLOW,\n                        security_name=\"Withdrawal\", amount=D(\"-30000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 30), type=T.FEE,\n                        security_name=\"Management fee\", amount=D(\"-12000.00\")),\n        ],\n        summary=Summary(\n            opening_value=D(\"1350000.00\"),\n            closing_value=closing,\n            cash_balance=cash,\n            fees_charged=D(\"12000.00\"),\n            capital_inflows=D(\"100000.00\"),\n            capital_outflows=D(\"30000.00\"),\n            net_gain=closing - D(\"1350000.00\") - D(\"100000.00\") + D(\"30000.00\") + D(\"12000.00\"),  # 92,000\n        ),\n    )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. Sterling (AIF)\ndef sterling_aif() -> Statement:\n    units = D(\"1000.0000\")\n    nav = D(\"1285.4300\")\n    closing = (units * nav).quantize(D(\"0.01\"))               # 1,285,430.00\n    opening = D(\"1100000.00\")\n    called = D(\"100000.00\")\n    distributed = D(\"0.00\")\n    fees = D(\"5000.00\")\n    gain = closing - opening - called + distributed + fees    # 90,430\n    return Statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.AIF,\n        provider=\"Sterling Growth Fund\",\n        strategy_name=\"Sterling Growth Fund - Category II\",\n        client_id=\"SGF-00457\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 1, 1), period_end=date(2026, 3, 31),\n        transactions=[\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 2, 10), type=T.INFLOW,\n                        security_name=\"Capital call - 3rd drawdown\", amount=called),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 3, 31), type=T.FEE,\n                        security_name=\"Management fee\", amount=fees),\n        ],\n        summary=Summary(\n            opening_value=opening,\n            closing_value=closing,\n            nav_per_unit=nav,\n            units_held=units,\n            fees_charged=fees,\n            capital_inflows=called,\n            capital_outflows=distributed,\n            net_gain=gain,\n        ),\n    )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. Meridian (PMS)\ndef meridian_capital() -> Statement:\n    rows = [\n        (\"Sun Pharmaceutical Industries\", \"INE044A0103\", 180, \"1650.00\", \"240000.00\"),\n        (\"Titan Company\", \"INE280A0102\", 60, \"3400.00\", \"175000.00\"),\n        (\"Axis Bank\", \"INE238A0103\", 250, \"1180.00\", \"260000.00\"),\n    ]\n    equity = sum(D(q) * D(p) for _, _, q, p, _ in rows)      # 797,000\n    cash = D(\"203000.00\")\n    closing = equity + cash                                   # 1,000,000\n    hold = _holdings(rows, closing)\n    return Statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.PMS,\n        provider=\"Meridian Capital\",\n        strategy_name=\"Meridian Value Equity\",\n        client_id=\"MC/2291/B\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 4, 1), period_end=date(2026, 4, 30),\n        holdings=hold,\n        transactions=[\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 2), type=T.BUY, security_name=\"Axis Bank\",\n                        quantity=D(\"50\"), amount=D(\"-57500.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 14), type=T.DIVIDEND, security_name=\"Sun Pharmaceutical Industries\",\n                        amount=D(\"4500.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 28), type=T.SELL, security_name=\"Titan Company\",\n                        quantity=D(\"20\"), amount=D(\"67000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 30), type=T.FEE,\n                        security_name=\"Performance fee\", amount=D(\"-6000.00\")),\n        ],\n        summary=Summary(\n            opening_value=D(\"950000.00\"),\n            closing_value=closing,\n            cash_balance=cash,\n            fees_charged=D(\"6000.00\"),\n            capital_inflows=D(\"0.00\"),\n            capital_outflows=D(\"0.00\"),\n            net_gain=closing - D(\"950000.00\") + D(\"6000.00\"),  # 56,000\n        ),\n    )\n\n\nALL_SAMPLES = {\n    \"abc_pms\": abc_pms,\n    \"xyz_wealth\": xyz_wealth,\n    \"sterling_aif\": sterling_aif,\n    \"meridian_capital\": meridian_capital,\n}\n\n# Passwords are fake, for demo only. Real ones would never be committed.\nPASSWORDS = {\"xyz_wealth\": \"demo1234\"}\n```\n\n**Note on the transaction signs.** I deliberately made sign conventions differ per provider (ABC shows fees as positive, XYZ as negative). That's realistic and it's something the validation in Part 6 must tolerate. The `expected.json` records what the PDF actually shows.\n\n## Step 4: Quick sanity test of the data\n\nCreate `tests/test_sample_data.py`:\n\n```python\nfrom decimal import Decimal as D\n\nfrom app.isin_util import is_valid_isin\nfrom samples.sample_data import ALL_SAMPLES\n\n\ndef test_all_isins_valid():\n    for name, build in ALL_SAMPLES.items():\n        for h in build().holdings:\n            assert is_valid_isin(h.isin), f\"{name}: {h.security_name} has bad ISIN {h.isin}\"\n\n\ndef test_holdings_plus_cash_equal_closing():\n    for name, build in ALL_SAMPLES.items():\n        s = build()\n        if not s.holdings:\n            continue\n        total = sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings) + s.summary.cash_balance\n        assert total == s.summary.closing_value, name\n\n\ndef test_weights_sum_close_to_equity_share():\n    for name, build in ALL_SAMPLES.items():\n        s = build()\n        if not s.holdings:\n            continue\n        equity_pct = sum(h.weight_pct for h in s.holdings)\n        expected = sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings) / s.summary.closing_value * 100\n        assert abs(equity_pct - expected) < D(\"0.1\"), name\n\n\ndef test_aif_closing_is_units_times_nav():\n    s = ALL_SAMPLES[\"sterling_aif\"]()\n    assert s.summary.units_held * s.summary.nav_per_unit == s.summary.closing_value\n```\n\nYou also need `samples/__init__.py`, an empty file, so Python can import from it:\n\n```bash\ntouch samples/__init__.py\n```\n\nRun everything:\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -v\n```\n\n## Step 5: Commit this checkpoint\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 2a: ISIN utility and sample data definitions\"\ngit push\n```\n\n---\n\n## Where we are, and what's next\n\nPart 2 has two halves. You've now done the **data** half. The **PDF drawing** half is next: `samples/generate.py`, which draws four differently laid-out PDFs with reportlab, encrypts the XYZ one, and writes each `expected.json`. I'm splitting it out because the layout code is long and I want you to run the data tests first.\n\nRun the tests above and tell me the result:\n- If all pass, I'll give you the PDF generator.\n- If any fail, paste the error. Something may be off in my numbers, and I'd rather catch it now.\n\nTwo things to be ready to explain:\n1. **Why generate `expected.json` from the same Python data as the PDF?** (So the answer key can't drift from the document, and tests stay trustworthy.)\n2. **Why make the sample numbers reconcile exactly?** (So clean samples pass validation, and we can then corrupt them on purpose to prove validation catches errors.)", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-10T09:44:58.344446Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-10T09:45:33.551405Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "# Part 1 is done: all 52 tests pass\n\nCommit it:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 1: schema and transform registry with tests\"\ngit push\n```\n\nThe editor warning was just the interpreter mismatch.
