Z=35); digits stay as they are.\"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(str(int(c, 36)) for c in body)\n\n\ndef _luhn_check_digit(digits: str) -> int:\n    total = 0\n    # Walk right to left. The check digit will sit to the right of this string,\n    # so the rightmost digit of `digits` is doubled.\n    for i, ch in enumerate(reversed(digits)):\n        d = int(ch)\n        if i % 2 == 0:\n            d *= 2\n            if d > 9:\n                d -= 9\n        total += d\n    return (10 - total % 10) % 10\n\n\ndef compute_check_digit(first_11: str) -> str:\n    return str(_luhn_check_digit(_expand(first_11.upper())))\n\n\ndef make_isin(first_11: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Build a valid ISIN from its first 11 characters.\"\"\"\n    return first_11.upper() + compute_check_digit(first_11)\n\n\ndef is_valid_isin(isin: str) -> bool:\n    isin = isin.strip().upper()\n    if len(isin) != 12 or not isin.isalnum() or not isin[:2].isalpha():\n        return False\n    if not isin[-1].isdigit():\n        return False\n    return compute_check_digit(isin[:11]) == isin[-1]\n```\n\n## Step 2: Test it against known real ISINs\n\nCreate `tests/test_isin.py`. These are well-known public ISINs, not client data:\n\n```python\nimport pytest\nfrom app.isin_util import is_valid_isin, make_isin\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"isin\", [\n    \"INE002A01018\",  # Reliance Industries\n    \"INE040A01034\",  # HDFC Bank\n    \"INE009A01021\",  # Infosys\n    \"US0378331005\",  # Apple\n])\ndef test_known_real_isins_are_valid(isin):\n    assert is_valid_isin(isin)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"isin\", [\n    \"INE002A01019\",   # wrong check digit\n    \"INE002A0101\",    # too short\n    \"12E002A01018\",   # country code must be letters\n    \"\",\n])\ndef test_bad_isins_are_rejected(isin):\n    assert not is_valid_isin(isin)\n\n\ndef test_make_isin_round_trip():\n    assert make_isin(\"INE002A0101\") == \"INE002A01018\"\n    assert is_valid_isin(make_isin(\"INE123A0100\"))\n```\n\nRun it:\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_isin.py -v\n```\n\nAll should pass. If one of the real ISINs fails, tell me. It would mean my algorithm has a bug and we fix it before going on.\n\n## Step 3: The sample data (single source of truth)\n\nCreate `samples/sample_data.py`. This holds the numbers for all four statements.\n\nI'm computing values from quantity and price so everything reconciles. Prices are fictional.\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Fictional statement data. The PDFs and expected.json are both generated from this.\"\"\"\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom decimal import Decimal as D\n\nfrom app.isin_util import make_isin\nfrom app.schema import (\n    Holding, Statement, StatementType, Summary, Transaction, TransactionType,\n)\n\nT = TransactionType\n\n\ndef _holdings(rows, total_value):\n    \"\"\"rows: (name, isin_first_11, qty, price, cost). Weight is computed from value.\"\"\"\n    out = []\n    for name, isin11, qty, price, cost in rows:\n        value = (D(qty) * D(price)).quantize(D(\"0.01\"))\n        out.append(Holding(\n            security_name=name,\n            isin=make_isin(isin11),\n            quantity=D(qty),\n            cost=D(cost),\n            market_price=D(price),\n            market_value=value,\n            weight_pct=(value / total_value * 100).quantize(D(\"0.01\")),\n        ))\n    return out\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. ABC (PMS)\ndef abc_pms() -> Statement:\n    rows = [\n        (\"Reliance Industries\", \"INE002A0101\", 120, \"2875.00\", \"310000.00\"),\n        (\"HDFC Bank\", \"INE040A0103\", 200, \"1550.00\", \"290000.00\"),\n        (\"Infosys\", \"INE009A0102\", 150, \"1480.00\", \"205000.00\"),\n        (\"Tata Consultancy Services\", \"INE467B0102\", 40, \"3950.00\", \"140000.00\"),\n        (\"ITC\", \"INE154A0102\", 500, \"420.00\", \"190000.00\"),\n    ]\n    equity = sum(D(q) * D(p) for _, _, q, p, _ in rows)      # 1,215,000\n    cash = D(\"85000.00\")\n    closing = equity + cash                                   # 1,300,000\n    hold = _holdings(rows, closing)\n    return Statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.PMS,\n        provider=\"ABC Portfolio Managers\",\n        strategy_name=\"ABC Large Cap Growth\",\n        client_id=\"AB1234\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 4, 1), period_end=date(2026, 4, 30),\n        holdings=hold,\n        transactions=[\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 6), type=T.BUY, security_name=\"Infosys\",\n                        quantity=D(\"50\"), amount=D(\"72000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 15), type=T.SELL, security_name=\"ITC\",\n                        quantity=D(\"100\"), amount=D(\"41000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 22), type=T.DIVIDEND, security_name=\"HDFC Bank\",\n                        amount=D(\"3000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 30), type=T.FEE,\n                        security_name=\"Management fee\", amount=D(\"8000.00\")),\n        ],\n        summary=Summary(\n            opening_value=D(\"1200000.00\"),\n            closing_value=closing,\n            cash_balance=cash,\n            fees_charged=D(\"8000.00\"),\n            capital_inflows=D(\"50000.00\"),\n            capital_outflows=D(\"0.00\"),\n            net_gain=closing - D(\"1200000.00\") - D(\"50000.00\") + D(\"8000.00\"),  # 58,000\n        ),\n    )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. XYZ (PMS)\ndef xyz_wealth() -> Statement:\n    rows = [\n        (\"Bajaj Finance\", \"INE296A0102\", 60, \"7100.00\", \"390000.00\"),\n        (\"Larsen & Toubro\", \"INE018A0103\", 90, \"3600.00\", \"270000.00\"),\n        (\"Asian Paints\", \"INE021A0102\", 70, \"2400.00\", \"150000.00\"),\n        (\"Maruti Suzuki India\", \"INE585B0101\", 25, \"12500.00\", \"280000.00\"),\n    ]\n    equity = sum(D(q) * D(p) for _, _, q, p, _ in rows)      # 1,375,000\n    cash = D(\"125000.00\")\n    closing = equity + cash                                   # 1,500,000\n    hold = _holdings(rows, closing)\n    return Statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.PMS,\n        provider=\"XYZ Wealth\",\n        strategy_name=\"XYZ Multicap Opportunities\",\n        client_id=\"98765\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 4, 1), period_end=date(2026, 4, 30),\n        holdings=hold,\n        transactions=[\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 3), type=T.INFLOW,\n                        security_name=\"Funds added\", amount=D(\"100000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 9), type=T.BUY, security_name=\"Asian Paints\",\n                        quantity=D(\"20\"), amount=D(\"47000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 17), type=T.OUTFLOW,\n                        security_name=\"Withdrawal\", amount=D(\"-30000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 30), type=T.FEE,\n                        security_name=\"Management fee\", amount=D(\"-12000.00\")),\n        ],\n        summary=Summary(\n            opening_value=D(\"1350000.00\"),\n            closing_value=closing,\n            cash_balance=cash,\n            fees_charged=D(\"12000.00\"),\n            capital_inflows=D(\"100000.00\"),\n            capital_outflows=D(\"30000.00\"),\n            net_gain=closing - D(\"1350000.00\") - D(\"100000.00\") + D(\"30000.00\") + D(\"12000.00\"),  # 92,000\n        ),\n    )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. Sterling (AIF)\ndef sterling_aif() -> Statement:\n    units = D(\"1000.0000\")\n    nav = D(\"1285.4300\")\n    closing = (units * nav).quantize(D(\"0.01\"))               # 1,285,430.00\n    opening = D(\"1100000.00\")\n    called = D(\"100000.00\")\n    distributed = D(\"0.00\")\n    fees = D(\"5000.00\")\n    gain = closing - opening - called + distributed + fees    # 90,430\n    return Statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.AIF,\n        provider=\"Sterling Growth Fund\",\n        strategy_name=\"Sterling Growth Fund - Category II\",\n        client_id=\"SGF-00457\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 1, 1), period_end=date(2026, 3, 31),\n        transactions=[\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 2, 10), type=T.INFLOW,\n                        security_name=\"Capital call - 3rd drawdown\", amount=called),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 3, 31), type=T.FEE,\n                        security_name=\"Management fee\", amount=fees),\n        ],\n        summary=Summary(\n            opening_value=opening,\n            closing_value=closing,\n            nav_per_unit=nav,\n            units_held=units,\n            fees_charged=fees,\n            capital_inflows=called,\n            capital_outflows=distributed,\n            net_gain=gain,\n        ),\n    )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. Meridian (PMS)\ndef meridian_capital() -> Statement:\n    rows = [\n        (\"Sun Pharmaceutical Industries\", \"INE044A0103\", 180, \"1650.00\", \"240000.00\"),\n        (\"Titan Company\", \"INE280A0102\", 60, \"3400.00\", \"175000.00\"),\n        (\"Axis Bank\", \"INE238A0103\", 250, \"1180.00\", \"260000.00\"),\n    ]\n    equity = sum(D(q) * D(p) for _, _, q, p, _ in rows)      # 797,000\n    cash = D(\"203000.00\")\n    closing = equity + cash                                   # 1,000,000\n    hold = _holdings(rows, closing)\n    return Statement(\n        statement_type=StatementType.PMS,\n        provider=\"Meridian Capital\",\n        strategy_name=\"Meridian Value Equity\",\n        client_id=\"MC/2291/B\",\n        period_start=date(2026, 4, 1), period_end=date(2026, 4, 30),\n        holdings=hold,\n        transactions=[\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 2), type=T.BUY, security_name=\"Axis Bank\",\n                        quantity=D(\"50\"), amount=D(\"-57500.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 14), type=T.DIVIDEND, security_name=\"Sun Pharmaceutical Industries\",\n                        amount=D(\"4500.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 28), type=T.SELL, security_name=\"Titan Company\",\n                        quantity=D(\"20\"), amount=D(\"67000.00\")),\n            Transaction(date=date(2026, 4, 30), type=T.FEE,\n                        security_name=\"Performance fee\", amount=D(\"-6000.00\")),\n        ],\n        summary=Summary(\n            opening_value=D(\"950000.00\"),\n            closing_value=closing,\n            cash_balance=cash,\n            fees_charged=D(\"6000.00\"),\n            capital_inflows=D(\"0.00\"),\n            capital_outflows=D(\"0.00\"),\n            net_gain=closing - D(\"950000.00\") + D(\"6000.00\"),  # 56,000\n        ),\n    )\n\n\nALL_SAMPLES = {\n    \"abc_pms\": abc_pms,\n    \"xyz_wealth\": xyz_wealth,\n    \"sterling_aif\": sterling_aif,\n    \"meridian_capital\": meridian_capital,\n}\n\n# Passwords are fake, for demo only. Real ones would never be committed.\nPASSWORDS = {\"xyz_wealth\": \"demo1234\"}\n```\n\n**Note on the transaction signs.** I deliberately made sign conventions differ per provider (ABC shows fees as positive, XYZ as negative). That's realistic and it's something the validation in Part 6 must tolerate. The `expected.json` records what the PDF actually shows.\n\n## Step 4: Quick sanity test of the data\n\nCreate `tests/test_sample_data.py`:\n\n```python\nfrom decimal import Decimal as D\n\nfrom app.isin_util import is_valid_isin\nfrom samples.sample_data import ALL_SAMPLES\n\n\ndef test_all_isins_valid():\n    for name, build in ALL_SAMPLES.items():\n        for h in build().holdings:\n            assert is_valid_isin(h.isin), f\"{name}: {h.security_name} has bad ISIN {h.isin}\"\n\n\ndef test_holdings_plus_cash_equal_closing():\n    for name, build in ALL_SAMPLES.items():\n        s = build()\n        if not s.holdings:\n            continue\n        total = sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings) + s.summary.cash_balance\n        assert total == s.summary.closing_value, name\n\n\ndef test_weights_sum_close_to_equity_share():\n    for name, build in ALL_SAMPLES.items():\n        s = build()\n        if not s.holdings:\n            continue\n        equity_pct = sum(h.weight_pct for h in s.holdings)\n        expected = sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings) / s.summary.closing_value * 100\n        assert abs(equity_pct - expected) < D(\"0.1\"), name\n\n\ndef test_aif_closing_is_units_times_nav():\n    s = ALL_SAMPLES[\"sterling_aif\"]()\n    assert s.summary.units_held * s.summary.nav_per_unit == s.summary.closing_value\n```\n\nYou also need `samples/__init__.py`, an empty file, so Python can import from it:\n\n```bash\ntouch samples/__init__.py\n```\n\nRun everything:\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -v\n```\n\n## Step 5: Commit this checkpoint\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 2a: ISIN utility and sample data definitions\"\ngit push\n```\n\n---\n\n## Where we are, and what's next\n\nPart 2 has two halves. You've now done the **data** half. The **PDF drawing** half is next: `samples/generate.py`, which draws four differently laid-out PDFs with reportlab, encrypts the XYZ one, and writes each `expected.json`. I'm splitting it out because the layout code is long and I want you to run the data tests first.\n\nRun the tests above and tell me the result:\n- If all pass, I'll give you the PDF generator.\n- If any fail, paste the error. Something may be off in my numbers, and I'd rather catch it now.\n\nTwo things to be ready to explain:\n1. **Why generate `expected.json` from the same Python data as the PDF?** (So the answer key can't drift from the document, and tests stay trustworthy.)\n2. **Why make the sample numbers reconcile exactly?** (So clean samples pass validation, and we can then corrupt them on purpose to prove validation catches errors.)", "citations": []}], "sender": "assistant", "created_at": "2026-10-10T09:45:33.617149Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-10T09:45:33.617149Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a12533-8a09-755c-b668-c5a6e248aa6b"}, {"uuid": "01a12553-ab8c-7495-899f-c3771aa16e71", "text": "why is there just one AIF format and 3 PMF formats", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-10T10:20:04.156867Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-10T10:20:04.156867Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "why is there just one AIF format and 3 PMF formats", "citations": []}], "sender": "human", "created_at": "2026-10-10T10:20:04.157191Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-10T10:20:04.157191Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a12533-8a09-7e21-8004-73c2501fddd0"}, {"uuid": "01a12553-ab8c-7333-8241-68c2006c6419", "text": "Two reasons: it reflects the brief, and it was a time trade-off. It isn't a rule, and you can change it.\n\n## Why I picked 3 PMS and 1 AIF\n\n**1. The brief only asks for 3 formats of any kind.** It says \"at least 3 different statement formats\" and doesn't specify a PMS/AIF split. I chose four to leave a margin, and made sure both statement types appear at least once.\n\n**2. PMS statements are where layout variety causes the most trouble.** A PMS statement has holdings tables, transaction tables and summary figures, so there's a lot that can vary between providers: column names, order, sign conventions, date styles. Three PMS formats let you test whether your engine and transforms handle that variety. An AIF statement is mostly a summary plus a short list of capital movements, so it has fewer ways to differ.\n\n**3. Layout, not statement type, is what tests the system.** The core challenge is \"same kind of data, different page.\" Two PMS formats do that just as well as one PMS and one AIF would. The AIF is there to test something different: **the schema fits a statement with no holdings and with NAV per unit.**\n\n## The honest weakness\n\nOne AIF format means you've proven the schema handles AIFs, but you haven't proven the engine copes with **AIF layout variety**. Real AIF statements differ a lot: some are quarterly capital account statements, some show commitment, called and uncalled capital tables, and some report per-unit-class NAV. An interviewer could easily show you an AIF layout you haven't seen, and a single sample won't prepare you for that.\n\n## What I'd suggest\n\nReplace one PMS format with a second AIF, so you have 2 and 2. The most useful candidate is **Meridian**, since it's the \"messy layout\" one. Or, keep Meridian and add a fifth format. The cost is one more block of data and one more PDF layout to draw.\n\nA second AIF should differ meaningfully from Sterling, for example:\n\n| | Sterling (existing) | New AIF idea |\n|---|---|---|\n| Frequency | Quarterly | Half-yearly |\n| Layout | Single summary table | Capital account in sections: commitment, drawdowns, distributions |\n| NAV | One NAV per unit | Multiple unit classes (Class A / Class B) |\n| Fields | Units \u00d7 NAV = closing | Commitment, called %, uncalled capital |\n\nThe last two rows would also push you to decide whether `Summary` needs fields like `capital_committed` and `capital_uncalled`. That's a useful schema question to settle now rather than in the interview.\n\n## Your decision\n\n- **Option A:** Keep 4 formats as they are (3 PMS, 1 AIF) and move on. Fastest, and it meets the brief.\n- **Option B:** Make it 2 PMS and 2 AIF by swapping Meridian for a new AIF. Better coverage of the two statement types.\n- **Option C:** Add a fifth format (a second AIF) and keep everything else. Most coverage, more work.\n\nI'd go with **Option C** if your time allows, otherwise **A**. Portfolio Management Service.)\n\n## Comparing your two options\n\n**2 PMS + 2 AIF (4 formats)**\n- Balanced and fast to build.\n- Gives you two layouts of each type, which is the minimum to show your engine isn't tuned to one layout per type.\n- Risk: only two data points per type. A third unseen layout in the interview is still a surprise.\n\n**3 PMS + 3 AIF (6 formats)**\n- Best coverage, but the cost is real. Each format needs its own data block, PDF layout code, hand-written config (Part 5), expected JSON, and test. That's roughly 6 units of work in Parts 2, 5 and 6, and the same again in debugging.\n- Diminishing returns: the third format of a type teaches you less than the second did.\n\n## Why I'd pick 3 PMS + 2 AIF\n\n- You already have the three PMS formats (ABC, XYZ, Meridian) and the data is written. Only the PDF drawing remains.\n- You only add one new thing: a second AIF with a genuinely different layout from Sterling (half-yearly, sectioned capital account, commitment/called/uncalled, maybe two unit classes).\n- That second AIF forces a useful schema decision now (do we add `capital_committed` and `capital_uncalled` to `Summary`?), which is better settled today than in the interview.\n- PMS gets three formats because that's where layout variety hurts most, as discussed earlier.\n\n## The rule of thumb to remember\n\nThe brief says: *\"A solution that handles fewer formats but is well reasoned will score higher than one that handles many but cannot explain itself.\"* The number of formats matters less than whether you can explain why each one exists. So pick the set where every format tests something different:\n\n| Format | What it tests |\n|---|---|\n| ABC (PMS) | Baseline, Indian numbers, `dd-Mon-yyyy` dates |\n| XYZ (PMS) | Password protection, brackets for negatives, `dd/mm/yyyy` |\n| Meridian (PMS) | Messy layout, Dr/Cr amounts, summary box on top |\n| Sterling (AIF) | Units \u00d7 NAV, no holdings |\n| New AIF | Sectioned layout, commitment/called/uncalled, multiple unit classes |\n\nIf time gets tight later, you can drop to 4 formats with no loss in the story, since you'd still have 2 PMS and 2 AIF.\n\n## Next step\n\nIf you agree, I'll do these in order:\n1. Extend the schema slightly with `capital_committed` and `capital_uncalled` in `Summary`.\n2. Add the second AIF to `sample_data.py`.\n3. Give you the PDF generator for all 5 formats.\n\nBefore that, did your tests from the last step (`test_isin.py` and `test_sample_data.py`) pass?        capital_outflows=distributed,\n            net_gain=gain,\n            capital_committed=D(\"5000000.00\"),\n            capital_uncalled=D(\"2000000.00\"),   # 3,000,000 called to date\n        ),\n    )\n```\n\nThen update the dictionary:\n\n```python\nALL_SAMPLES = {\n    \"abc_pms\": abc_pms,\n    \"xyz_wealth\": xyz_wealth,\n    \"meridian_capital\": meridian_capital,\n s.summary.closing_value, name\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create `samples/generate.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Draws the sample PDFs and writes the matching expected.json answer keys.\n\nRun from the project root: A4\nfrom reportlab.lib.styles import ParagraphStyle, getSampleStyleSheet\nfrom reportlab.platypus import Paragraph, SimpleDocTemplate, Table, TableStyle\n\nfrom app.schema import Statement, TransactionType as T\nfrom samples.sample_data import ALL_SAMPLES, PASSWORDS\n\nHERE = Path(__file__).parent\n\n\n# ============================================================ number / date formatting\ndef indian(x, dp=2) -> str:\n    \"\"\"1234567.5 -> 12,34,567.50  (lakh/crore grouping)\"\"\"\n    q = D(x).quantize(D(1).scaleb(-dp))\n    sign = \"-\" if q < 0 else \"\"\n    int_part, _, frac = f\"{abs(q):.{dp}f}\".partition(\".\")\n    if len(int_part) > 3:\n        head, tail = int_part[:-3], int_part[-3:]\n        groups = []\n        while len(head) > 2:\n            groups.insert(0, head[-2:])\n            head = head[:-2]\n        if head:\n            groups.insert(0, head)\n        int_part = \",\".join(groups + [tail])\n    return sign + int_part + (f\".{frac}\" if dp else \"\")\n\n\ndef intl(x, dp=2) -> str:\n    \"\"\"1234567.5 -> 1,234,567.50  (international grouping)\"\"\"\n    return f\"{D(x).quantize(D(1).scaleb(-dp)):,.{dp}f}\"\n\n\ndef brackets(x, fmt) -> str:\n    return f\"({fmt(abs(x))})\" if x < 0 else fmt(x)\n\n\ndef drcr(x, fmt) -> str:\n    return f\"{fmt(abs(x))} {'Dr' if x < 0 else 'Cr'}\"\n\n\ndef qty(x) -> str:\n    return \"\" if x is None else f\"{x.normalize():f}\"\n\n\ndef d_mon(d):   return d.strftime(\"%d-%b-%Y\")        # 01-Apr-2026\ndef d_slash(d): return d.strftime(\"%d/%m/%Y\")        # 01/04/2026\ndef d_dash(d):  return d.strftime(\"%d-%m-%Y\")        # 01-04-2026\ndef d_iso(d):   return d.isoformat()                 # 2026-04-01\ndef d_long(d):  return f\"{d.day:02d} {d:%B} {d.year}\"  # 01 April 2026\ndef d_long_np(d): return f\"{d.day} {d:%B} {d.year}\"    # 1 April 2026\n\n\n# ============================================================ drawing helpers\n_ss = getSampleStyleSheet()\nTITLE = ParagraphStyle(\"title\", parent=_ss[\"Title\"], fontSize=18, alignment=0, spaceAfter=2)\nH2 = ParagraphStyle(\"h2\", parent=_ss[\"Heading2\"], fontSize=11, spaceBefore=10, spaceAfter=4)\nBODY = ParagraphStyle(\"body\", parent=_ss[\"BodyText\"], fontSize=9)\n\n\ndef P(text, style=BODY):\n    return Paragraph(text, style)\n\n\ndef make_table(rows, widths, right_cols=(), header=True, total_row=False, box=False, font=8):\n    t = Table(rows, colWidths=widths, hAlign=\"LEFT\")\n    style = [\n        (\"FONTNAME\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), \"Helvetica\"),\n        (\"FONTSIZE\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), font),\n        (\"TOPPADDING\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 2),\n        (\"BOTTOMPADDING\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 2),\n    ]\n    for c in right_cols:\n        style.append((\"ALIGN\", (c, 0), (c, -1), \"RIGHT\"))\n    if header:\n        style += [(\"FONTNAME\", (0, 0), (-1, 0), \"Helvetica-Bold\"),\n                  (\"LINEBELOW\", (0, 0), (-1, 0), 0.6, colors.black)]\n    if total_row:\n        style += [(\"FONTNAME\", (0, -1), (-1, -1), \"Helvetica-Bold\"),\n                  (\"LINEABOVE\", (0, -1), (-1, -1), 0.6, colors.black)]\n    if box:\n        style += [(\"BOX\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 1, colors.black),\n                  (\"BACKGROUND\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), colors.whitesmoke)]\n    t.setStyle(TableStyle(style))\n    return t\n\n\ndef kv_table(pairs, widths=(220, 120), box=False):\n    return make_table([list(p) for p in pairs], list(widths), right_cols=(1,),\n                      header=False, box=box, font=9)\n\n\ndef info_row(left, right):\n    return make_table([[left, right]], [230, 270], header=False, font=9)\n\n\ndef txn_table(s, labels, date_fn, amount_fn, headers, widths, with_qty=True):\n    rows = [headers]\n    for t in s.transactions:\n        row = [date_fn(t.date), labels[t.type], t.security_name or \"\"]\n        if with_qty:\n            row.append(qty(t.quantity))\n        row.append(amount_fn(t.amount))\n        rows.append(row)\n    return make_table(rows, widths, right_cols=(len(headers) - 1,) if not with_qty\n                      else (len(headers) - 2, len(headers) - 1))\n\n\n# ABC (PMS): baseline\ndef abc_story(s: Statement):\n    sm = s.summary\n    rows = [[\"Security\", \"ISIN\", \"Qty\", \"Cost\", \"Mkt Price\", \"Mkt Value\", \"Weight %\"]]\n    for h in s.holdings:\n        rows.append([h.security_name, h.isin, qty(h.quantity), indian(h.cost),\n                     indian(h.market_price), indian(h.market_value), str(h.weight_pct)])\n    rows.append([\"Total\", \"\", \"\", indian(sum(h.cost for h in s.holdings)), \"\",\n                 indian(sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings)),\n                 str(sum(h.weight_pct for h in s.holdings))])\n    labels = {T.BUY: \"Buy\", T.SELL: \"Sell\", T.DIVIDEND: \"Dividend\",\n              T.FEE: \"Fee\", T.INFLOW: \"Inflow\", T.OUTFLOW: \"Outflow\"}\n    return [\n        P(\"ABC Portfolio Managers\", TITLE),\n        P(\"Portfolio Statement\", H2),\n        info_row(f\"Client Code: {s.client_id}\",\n                 f\"Period: {d_mon(s.period_start)} to {d_mon(s.period_end)}\"),\n        info_row(f\"Strategy: {s.strategy_name}\", f\"Currency: {s.currency}\"),\n        P(\"Account Summary\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Opening Value\", indian(sm.opening_value)),\n            (\"Add: Inflows\", indian(sm.capital_inflows)),\n            (\"Less: Outflows\", indian(sm.capital_outflows)),\n            (\"Less: Fees Charged\", indian(sm.fees_charged)),\n            (\"Net Gain\", indian(sm.net_gain)),\n            (\"Closing Value\", indian(sm.closing_value)),\n            (\"Cash Balance\", indian(sm.cash_balance)),\n        ]),\n        P(\"Equity Holdings\", H2),\n        make_table(rows, [135, 80, 38, 68, 58, 72, 50], right_cols=(2, 3, 4, 5, 6),\n                   total_row=True),\n        P(\"Transactions\", H2),\n        txn_table(s, labels, d_mon, indian,\n                  [\"Date\", \"Type\", \"Security\", \"Qty\", \"Amount\"], [70, 60, 190, 50, 90]),\n    ]\n\n\n# ============================================================ 2. style += [(\"FONTNAME\", (0, -1), (-1, -1), \"Helvetica-Bold\"),\n                  (\"LINEABOVE\", (0, -1), (-1, -1), 0.6, colors.black)]\n    if box:\n        style += [(\"BOX\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 1, colors.black),\n                  (\"BACKGROUND\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), colors.whitesmoke)]\n    t.setStyle(TableStyle(style))\n    return t\n\n\ndef kv_table(pairs, widths=(220, 120), box=False):\n    return make_table([list(p) for p in pairs], list(widths), right_cols=(1,),\n                      header=False, box=box, font=9)\n\n\ndef info_row(left, right):\n    return make_table([[left, make_table(rows, widths, right_cols=(len(headers) - 1,) if not with_qty\n                      else (len(headers) - 2, len(headers) - 1))\n\n\n# ============================================================ 1. ABC (PMS): baseline\ndef abc_story(s: Statement):\n    sm = s.summary\n    rows = [[\"Security\", \"ISIN\", \"Qty\", \"Cost\", \"Mkt Price\", \"Mkt Value\", \"Weight %\"]]\n    for h in s.holdings:\n        rows.append([h.security_name, h.isin, qty(h.quantity), indian(h.cost),\n                     indian(h.market_price), indian(h.market_value), str(h.weight_pct)])\n    rows.append([\"Total\", \"\", \"\", indian(sum(h.cost for h in s.holdings)), \"\",\n                 indian(sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings)),\n                 str(sum(h.weight_pct for h in s.holdings))])\n    labels = {T.BUY: \"Buy\", T.SELL: \"Sell\", T.DIVIDEND: \"Dividend\",\n              T.FEE: \"Fee\", T.INFLOW: \"Inflow\", T.OUTFLOW: \"Outflow\"}\n    return [\n        P(\"ABC Portfolio Managers\", TITLE),\n        P(\"Portfolio Statement\", H2),\n        info_row(f\"Client Code: {s.client_id}\",\n                 f\"Period: {d_mon(s.period_start)} to {d_mon(s.period_end)}\"),\n        info_row(f\"Strategy: {s.strategy_name}\", f\"Currency: {s.currency}\"),\n        P(\"Account Summary\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Opening Value\", indian(sm.opening_value)),\n            (\"Add: Inflows\", indian(sm.capital_inflows)),\n            (\"Less: Outflows\", indian(sm.capital_outflows)),\n            (\"Less: Fees Charged\", indian(sm.fees_charged)),\n            (\"Net Gain\", indian(sm.net_gain)),\n            (\"Closing Value\", indian(sm.closing_value)),\n            (\"Cash Balance\", indian(sm.cash_balance)),\n        ]),\n        P(\"Equity Holdings\", H2),\n        make_table(rows, [135, 80, 38, 68, 58, 72, 50], right_cols=(2, 3, 4, 5, 6),\n                   total_row=True),\n        P(\"Transactions\", H2),\n        txn_table(s, labels, d_mon, indian,\n                  [\"Date\", \"Type\", \"Security\", \"Qty\", \"Amount\"], [70, 60, 190, 50, 90]),\n    ]\n\n\n# ============================================================ 2. XYZ (PMS): brackets, dd/mm/yyyy\ndef xyz_story(s: Statement):\n    sm = s.summary\n    rows = [[\"Stock Name\", \"Units Held\", \"Cost (INR)\", \"Value (INR)\", \"ISIN Code\", \"% of Portfolio\"]]\n    for h in s.holdings:\n        rows.append([h.security_name, qty(h.quantity), intl(h.cost), intl(h.market_value),\n                     h.isin, f\"{h.weight_pct}%\"])\n    labels = {T.BUY: \"Purchase\", T.SELL: \"Sale\", T.DIVIDEND: \"Dividend\",\n              T.FEE: \"Fee\", T.INFLOW: \"Deposit\", T.OUTFLOW: \"Withdrawal\"}\n    return [\n        P(\"XYZ Wealth\", TITLE),\n        P(f\"Statement for {s.period_end:%B %Y}\", H2),\n        P(f\"Investor ID ....... {s.client_id}\"),\n        P(f\"Scheme : {s.strategy_name}\"),\n        P(f\"Statement Period : {d_slash(s.period_start)} to {d_slash(s.period_end)}\"),\n        P(f\"All amounts in {s.currency}\"),\n        P(\"Account Summary\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Beginning Balance\", intl(sm.opening_value)),\n            (\"Deposits\", intl(sm.capital_inflows)),\n            (\"Withdrawals\", brackets(-sm.capital_outflows, intl)),\n            (\"Fees & Charges\", brackets(-sm.fees_charged, intl)),\n            (\"Gain for the Period\", intl(sm.net_gain)),\n            (\"Ending Balance\", intl(sm.closing_value)),\n            (\"Cash / Liquid Balance\", intl(sm.cash_balance)),\n        ]),\n        P(\"Portfolio Holdings\", H2),\n        make_table(rows, [140, 55, 75, 75, 80, 70], right_cols=(1, 2, 3, 5)),\n        P(\"Transaction History\", H2),\n        txn_table(s, labels, d_slash, lambda a: brackets(a, intl),\n                  [\"Txn Date\", \"Transaction\", \"Scrip\", \"Units\", \"Amount (INR)\"],\n                  [70, 70, 170, 45, 90]),\n    ]\n\n\n# ============================================================ 3. Meridian (PMS): summary box + Dr/Cr\ndef meridian_story(s: Statement):\n    sm = s.summary\n    rows = [[\"Instrument\", \"ISIN\", \"No. of Shares\", \"Book Cost\", \"Rate\", \"Market Value\", \"Wt %\"]]\n    for h in s.holdings:\n        rows.append([h.security_name, h.isin, qty(h.quantity), indian(h.cost),\n                     indian(h.market_price), indian(h.market_value), str(h.weight_pct)])\n    rows.append([\"Total Equity\", \"\", \"\", indian(sum(h.cost for h in s.holdings)), \"\",\n                 indian(sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings)), \"\"])\n    labels = {T.BUY: \"Purchase\", T.SELL: \"Sale\", T.DIVIDEND: \"Dividend Received\",\n              T.FEE: \"Fee\", T.INFLOW: \"Inflow\", T.OUTFLOW: \"Outflow\"}\n    return [\n        P(\"Meridian Capital\", TITLE),\n        P(\"Portfolio Valuation Report\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Portfolio value at start\", indian(sm.opening_value)),\n            (\"Portfolio value at end\", indian(sm.closing_value)),\n            (\"Cash balance\", indian(sm.cash_balance)),\n            (\"Charges for the period\", indian(sm.fees_charged)),\n        ], widths=(220, 120), box=True),\n        P(f\"Client Ref: {s.client_id}\"),\n        P(f\"Mandate: {s.strategy_name}\"),\n        P(f\"From {d_long(s.period_start)} to {d_long(s.period_end)}\"),\n        P(f\"Reporting currency: {s.currency}\"),\n        P(\"Securities Held\", H2),\n        make_table(rows, [140, 80, 60, 65, 50, 70, 35], right_cols=(2, 3, 4, 5, 6),\n                   total_row=True),\n        P(\"Cash Ledger\", H2),\n        txn_table(s, labels, d_long, lambda a: drcr(a, indian),\n                  [\"Value Date\", \"Nature\", \"Particulars\", \"Qty\", \"Amount\"],\n                  [90, 85, 170, 40, 90]),\n    ]\n\n\n# ============================================================ 4. Sterling (AIF): quarterly capital account\ndef sterling_story(s: Statement):\n    sm = s.summary\n    labels = {T.INFLOW: \"Capital Call\", T.FEE: \"Fee\", T.OUTFLOW: \"Distribution\"}\n    return [\n        P(\"Sterling Growth Fund\", TITLE),\n        P(\"Capital Account Statement\", H2),\n        info_row(f\"Investor Code: {s.client_id}\", f\"Currency: {s.currency}\"),\n        P(f\"Fund: {s.strategy_name}\"),\n        P(f\"Period: {d_iso(s.period_start)} to {d_iso(s.period_end)}\"),\n        P(\"Capital Account\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Opening Capital Account Balance\", intl(sm.opening_value)),\n            (\"Add: Capital Contributions\", intl(sm.capital_inflows)),\n            (\"Less: Distributions\", intl(sm.capital_outflows)),\n            (\"Less: Management Fees\", intl(sm.fees_charged)),\n            (\"Add: Net Investment Gain\", intl(sm.net_gain)),\n            (\"Closing Capital Account Balance\", intl(sm.closing_value)),\n        ], widths=(250, 120)),\n        P(\"Unit Information\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Units Held\", intl(sm.units_held, 4)),\n            (\"NAV per Unit (INR)\", intl(sm.nav_per_unit, 4)),\n        ], widths=(250, 120)),\n        P(\"Capital Movements\", H2),\n        txn_table(s, labels, d_iso, intl,\n                  [\"Date\", \"Type\", \"Description\", \"Amount (INR)\"],\n                  [80, 80, 200, 90], with_qty=False),\n    ]\n\n\n# ============================================================ 5. Helix (AIF): sectioned, half-yearly\ndef helix_story(s: Statement):\n    sm = s.summary\n    called = sm.capital_committed - sm.capital_uncalled\n    labels = {T.INFLOW: \"Capital Call\", T.OUTFLOW: \"Distribution\", T.FEE: \"Fee\"}\n    return [\n        P(\"Helix Capital Partners\", TITLE),\n        P(\"Half-Yearly Investor Statement\", H2),\n        P(f\"Investor Code: {s.client_id}\"),\n        P(f\"Fund: {s.strategy_name}\"),\n        P(f\"Reporting period: {d_long_np(s.period_start)} to {d_long_np(s.period_end)}\"),\n        P(f\"Currency: {s.currency}\"),\n        P(\"SECTION A - COMMITMENT\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Total Commitment\", intl(sm.capital_committed)),\n            (\"Capital Called to Date\", intl(called)),\n            (\"Uncalled Commitment\", intl(sm.capital_uncalled)),\n        ], widths=(250, 120)),\n        P(\"SECTION B - CAPITAL ACCOUNT\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Opening Balance\", intl(sm.opening_value)),\n            (\"Drawdowns during the period\", intl(sm.capital_inflows)),\n            (\"Distributions during the period\", intl(sm.capital_outflows)),\n            (\"Fees and expenses\", intl(sm.fees_charged)),\n            (\"Net income / gain\", intl(sm.net_gain)),\n            (\"Closing Balance\", intl(sm.closing_value)),\n        ], widths=(250, 120)),\n        P(\"SECTION C - UNIT INFORMATION\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Units outstanding\", intl(sm.units_held, 4)),\n            (\"NAV per unit\", intl(sm.nav_per_unit, 4)),\n        ], widths=(250, 120)),\n        P(\"SECTION D - CASH MOVEMENTS\", H2),\n        txn_table(s, labels, d_dash, intl,\n                  [\"Date\", \"Type\", \"Narration\", \"Amount\"],\n                  [80, 80, 200, 90], with_qty=False),\n    ]\n\n\nSTORIES = {\n    \"abc_pms\": abc_story,\n    \"xyz_wealth\": xyz_story,\n    \"meridian_capital\": meridian_story,\n    \"sterling_aif\": sterling_story,\n    \"helix_aif\": helix_story,\n}\n\n# The answer key must contain only what the PDF actually shows.\n# XYZ prints no per-share price; Meridian prints no flow breakdown or net gain.\nNOT_SHOWN = {\n    \"xyz_wealth\": {\"holding\": [\"market_price\"]},\n    \"meridian_capital\": {\"summary\": [\"capital_inflows\", \"capital_outflows\", \"net_gain\"]},\n}\n\n\ndef visible_copy(name: str, s: Statement) -> Statement:\n    s2 = s.model_copy(deep=True)\n    hidden = NOT_SHOWN.get(name, {})\n    for field in hidden.get(\"holding\", []):\n        for h in s2.holdings:\n            setattr(h, field, None)\n    for field in hidden.get(\"summary\", []):\n        setattr(s2.summary, field, None)\n    return s2\n\n\ndef encrypt_pdf(path: Path, password: str):\n    tmp = path.with_suffix(\".tmp\")\n    with pikepdf.open(path) as pdf:\n        pdf.save(tmp, encryption=pikepdf.Encryption(user=password, owner=password + \"-owner\"))\n    os.replace(tmp, path)\n\n\ndef generate_all(out_dir=HERE):\n    out = Path(out_dir)\n    pdf_dir, exp_dir = out / \"pdfs\", out / \"expected\"\n    pdf_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    exp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    for name, build in ALL_SAMPLES.items():\n        s = build()\n        path = pdf_dir / f\"{name}.pdf\"\n        SimpleDocTemplate(str(path), pagesize=A4, leftMargin=36,    (exp_dir / f\"{name}.json\").write_text(\n            visible_copy(name, s).model_dump_json(indent=2), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        print(f\"generated {name}\" + (\"  (password protected)\" if name The remaining 6.39% is cash, so Part 6 must not demand 100%.\n\n## Problem 1: my code comments had wrong numbers\n\nIn `sample_data.py` I wrote comments like `# 1,300,000`, `# 1,500,000`, `# 1,000,000`, `# 58,000` and `# 92,000`. They were wrong, because I added up the holdings in my head. The PDFs are right, since the code computes the values, but the comments are misleading. The real figures are:\n\n| Sample | Closing value | Net gain |\n|---|---|---|\n| ABC | 1,330,000 | 88,000 |\n| XYZ | 1,355,500 | \u221252,500 (a loss) |\n| Meridian | 999,000 | not shown |\n\nUpdate those comments, or delete them. This is a good example of an AI confidently writing something that looks right and isn't, so log it in your AI usage log.\n\n## Problem 2: XYZ's answer key disagrees with its PDF\n\nThis is a real design issue. The XYZ PDF prints:\n\n```\nWithdrawals          (30,000.00)\nFees & Charges       (12,000.00)\n```\n\nBut `expected.json` stores `capital_outflows: 30000` and `fees_charged: 12000` as positive. The `number` transform would read the PDF as \u221230000 and \u221212000, so the engine's output would never equal the answer key.\n\nReal statements do this: one provider shows fees as a negative, another as a positive \"less\" line. The fix is a small whitelisted transform that returns the magnitude. Add this to `app/transforms.py`, above the registry:\n\n```python\ndef number_abs(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"Magnitude only. For fields we store as positive amounts (fees, outflows)\n    that some providers print in brackets or with a minus sign.\"\"\"\n    value = _to_decimal(raw)\n    return None if value is None else abs(value)\n```\n\nRegister it inside `TRANSFORMS`:\n\n```python\n    \"number_abs\": number_abs,\n```\n\nAdd a test to `tests/test_transforms.py`:\n\n```python\ndef test_number_abs():\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_abs\", \"(12,000.00)\") == Decimal(\"12000.00\")\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_abs\", \"12,000.00\") == Decimal(\"12000.00\")\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_abs\", \"-\") is None\n```\n\nIn Part 5, XYZ's config will use `number_abs` for `fees_charged` and `capital_outflows`. Transaction amounts stay as printed, because `expected.json` records them signed (\u221230000, \u221212000).\n\n## Things the engine will have to handle\n\nThese aren't bugs. They are the traps the samples were built to contain:\n\n1. **Total rows.** ABC has `Total`, Meridian has `Total Equity`, XYZ has none. The table must stop at the right place.\n2. **Sign conventions differ.** ABC's buy is `72,000.00` positive, while Meridian's purchase is `57,500.00 Dr`, which is negative. Part 6 must decide whether to normalise signs or tolerate both.\n3. **XYZ's \"Gain for the Period\" prints `-52,500.00` with a minus sign**, while other negatives in the same PDF use brackets. The `number` transform handles both.\n4. **Helix prints \"Capital Called to Date\"**, which the schema doesn't store. The engine should ignore it.\n5. **Meridian's period is in words** (`01 April 2026`). The `date_dd_month_yyyy` transform covers it. Helix's `1 October 2025` has no zero padding, which `%d` also accepts.\n\n## Next steps\n\n1. Fix the comments, add `number_abs`, and run `python -m pytest -v`.\n2. Open each `samples/expected/*.json` and spot-check one against its PDF.\n3. The `number` transform would read the PDF as \u221230000 and \u221212000, so the engine's output would never equal the answer key.\n\nReal statements do this: one provider shows fees as a negative, another as a positive \"less\" line. The fix is a small whitelisted transform that returns the magnitude. Add this to `app/transforms.py`, above the registry:\n\n```python\ndef number_abs(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"Magnitude only. For fields we store as positive amounts (fees, outflows)\n    that some providers print in brackets or with a minus sign.\"\"\"\n    value = _to_decimal(raw)\n    return None if value is None else abs(value)\n```\n\nRegister it inside `TRANSFORMS`:\n\n```python\n    \"number_abs\": number_abs,\n```\n\nAdd a test to `tests/test_transforms.py`:\n\n```python\ndef test_number_abs():\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_abs\", \"(12,000.00)\") == Decimal(\"12000.00\")\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_abs\", \"12,000.00\") == Decimal(\"12000.00\")\n    assert apply_transform(\"number_abs\", \"-\") is None\n```\n\nIn Part 5, XYZ's config will use `number_abs` for `fees_charged` and `capital_outflows`. Transaction amounts stay as printed, because `expected.json` records them signed (\u221230000, \u221212000).\n\n## Things the engine will have to handle\n\nThese aren't bugs. They are the traps the samples were built to contain:\n\n1. **Total rows.** ABC has `Total`, Meridian has `Total Equity`, XYZ has none. The table must stop at the right place.\n2. **Sign conventions differ.** ABC's buy is `72,000.00` positive, while Meridian's purchase is `57,500.00 Dr`, which is negative. A normal space at\n# 8-9pt is about 2-3pt; the gap between adjacent table cells is at least ~12pt.\nCELL_GAP = 5.0\n# Words whose vertical positions differ by less than this are on the same line.\nLINE_TOLERANCE = 3.0\n\n\nclass ReaderError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for all reader failures.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass PasswordRequiredError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The PDF is encrypted and no password was supplied.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass WrongPasswordError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"A password was supplied but it does not open the PDF.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass NoTextLayerError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The PDF has no extractable text (probably a scan). OCR is out of scope.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnreadableDocumentError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The file is corrupt or not a PDF.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Cell:\n    text: str\n    x0: float\n    x1: float\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Line:\n    page: int          # 1-based\n    top: float\n    cells: tuple[Cell, ...]\n\n    @property\n    def text(self) -> str:\n        return \" \".join(c.text for c in self.cells)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Document:\n    lines: list[Line] = field(default_factory=list)\n    page_count: int = 0\n\n    @property\n    def text(self) -> str:\n        return \"\\n\".join(line.text for line in self.lines)\n\n\ndef file_sha256(path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Hash of the raw bytes. Used to avoid processing the same file twice.\"\"\"\n    h = hashlib.sha256()\n    with open(path, \"rb\") as f:\n        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b\"\"):\n            h.update(chunk)\n    return h.hexdigest()\n\n\ndef _group_into_lines(words: list[dict], page_no: int, gap: float) -> list[Line]:\n    lines: list[Line] = []\n    current: list[dict] = []\n    current_top: Optional[float] = None\n\n    def flush():\n        if not current:\n            return\n        current.sort(key=lambda w: w[\"x0\"])\n        cells: list[list[dict]] = [[current[0]]]\n        for w in current[1:]:\n            if w[\"x0\"] - cells[-1][-1][\"x1\"] > gap:\n                cells.append([w])\n            else:\n                cells[-1].append(w)\n        lines.append(Line(\n            page=page_no,\n            top=round(min(w[\"top\"] for w in current), 2),\n            cells=tuple(\n                Cell(text=\" \".join(w[\"text\"] for w in group),\n                     x0=round(group[0][\"x0\"], 2), x1=round(group[-1][\"x1\"], 2))\n                for group in cells\n            ),\n        ))\n\n    for w in sorted(words, key=lambda w: (w[\"top\"], w[\"x0\"])):\n        if current_top is None or abs(w[\"top\"] - current_top) > LINE_TOLERANCE:\n            flush()\n            current, current_top = [w], w[\"top\"]\n        else:\n            current.append(w)\n    flush()\n    return lines\n\n\ndef read_document(path, password: Optional[str] = None, gap: float = CELL_GAP) -> Document:\n    path = Path(path)\n    try:\n        pdf = pdfplumber.open(path, password=password or \"\")\n    except PDFPasswordIncorrect:\n        if password:\n            raise WrongPasswordError(f\"The password does not open {path.name}\")\n        raise PasswordRequiredError(f\"{path.name} is password protected\")\n    except (PDFSyntaxError, ValueError) as e:\n        raise UnreadableDocumentError(f\"{path.name} could not be read: {e}\") from e\n\n    doc = Document()\n    with pdf:\n        doc.page_count = len(pdf.pages)\n        for page_no, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):\n            words = page.extract_words(use_text_flow=False, keep_blank_chars=False)\n            doc.lines.extend(_group_into_lines(words, page_no, gap))\n\n    if not doc.lines:\n        raise NoTextLayerError(f\"{path.name} has no extractable text (scanned PDF?)\")\n    return doc\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    # Quick look at what the reader sees:\n    #   python -m app.reader samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf\n    #   python -m app.reader samples/pdfs/xyz_wealth.pdf demo1234\n    import sys\n\n    document = read_document(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)\n    for ln in document.lines:\n        print(f\"p{ln.page} y={ln.top:6.1f} | \" + \" | \".join(c.text for c in ln.cells))\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `tests/test_reader.py`\n\n```python\nimport \"xyz_wealth.pdf\", \"not-the-password\")\n\n\ndef test_correct_password(pdfs):\n    doc = read_document(pdfs / \"xyz_wealth.pdf\", PASSWORDS[\"xyz_wealth\"])\n    assert \"XYZ Wealth\" in doc.text\n\n\ndef test_not_a_pdf(tmp_path):\n    bad = tmp_path / \"fake.pdf\"\n    bad.write_text(\"this is not a pdf\")\n    with pytest.raises(UnreadableDocumentError):\n        read_document(bad)\n\n\ndef test_pdf_without_text_is_rejected(tmp_path):\n    from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n    blank = tmp_path / \"blank.pdf\"\n    c = canvas.Canvas(str(blank))\n    c.rect(50, 50, 100, 100)   # a shape, but no text\n    c.save()\n    with pytest.raises(NoTextLayerError):\n        read_document(blank)\n\n\ndef test_file_hash_is_stable_and_content_based(pdfs, \"abc_pms.pdf\") != file_sha256(pdfs / \"helix_aif.pdf\")\n```\n\n## Step 3: Run and look\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_reader.py -v\npython -m app.reader samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf\npython -m find_line(doc, \"Txn Date\")\n    row = find_line(doc, \"03/04/2026\")\n    assert len(row.cells) == len(header.cells) - 1\n\n\ndef test_password_required(pdfs):\n    with pytest.raises(PasswordRequiredError):\n        read_document(pdfs / \"xyz_wealth.pdf\")\n\n\ndef test_wrong_password(pdfs):\n    with pytest.raises(WrongPasswordError):\n        read_document(pdfs / \"xyz_wealth.pdf\", \"not-the-password\")\n\n\ndef test_correct_password(pdfs):\n    doc = read_document(pdfs / \"xyz_wealth.pdf\", PASSWORDS[\"xyz_wealth\"])\n    assert \"XYZ Wealth\" in doc.text\n\n\ndef test_not_a_pdf(tmp_path):\n    bad = tmp_path / \"fake.pdf\"\n    bad.write_text(\"this is not a pdf\")\n    with pytest.raises(UnreadableDocumentError):\n        read_document(bad)\n\n\ndef test_pdf_without_text_is_rejected(tmp_path):\n    from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n    blank = tmp_path / \"blank.pdf\"\n    c = canvas.Canvas(str(blank))\n    c.rect(50, 50, 100, 100)   # a shape, but no text\n    c.save()\n    with pytest.raises(NoTextLayerError):\n        read_document(blank)\n\n\ndef test_file_hash_is_stable_and_content_based(pdfs, tmp_path):\n    copy = tmp_path / \"copy.pdf\"\n    shutil.copy(pdfs / \"abc_pms.pdf\", copy)\n    assert file_sha256(copy) == file_sha256(pdfs / \"abc_pms.pdf\")\n    assert file_sha256(pdfs / \"abc_pms.pdf\") != file_sha256(pdfs / \"helix_aif.pdf\")\n```\n\n## Step 3: Run and look\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_reader.py -v\npython -m app.reader samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf\npython -m app.reader samples/pdfs/xyz_wealth.pdf demo1234\npython -m app.reader samples/pdfs/meridian_capital.pdf\n```\n\nThe last three commands print each line with cells separated by `|`. **Read this output carefully for all five PDFs**, because it's exactly what the engine will see. You're looking for:\n\n- Table rows split into the right number of cells\n- Any place where two columns merged into one cell, or one name split into two cells (that means `CELL_GAP` needs tuning)\n- Meridian's Dr/Cr amounts staying as one cell (`57,500.00 Dr`)\n\nI wrote the splitting logic without running it, so the cell-split tests (`test_table_row_is_split_into_cells` and `test_blank_cell_keeps_positions`) are the likeliest to fail. If any test fails, paste the error and the output of the `python -m app.reader` command for that PDF, and I'll adjust it.\n\n## Step 4: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 3: PDF reader with cells, password handling, file hash\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why keep x-positions instead of just text?** Blank cells disappear when text is flattened, so counting cells misassigns values. Positions don't.\n2. **Why three separate password and text errors?** The pipeline responds differently to each: ask for a password, report a wrong one, or reject an unsupported scan.\n3. **Why a gap threshold of 5pt?** A word space is about 2 to 3pt and adjacent table cells are at least about 12pt apart, so 5 sits safely between them. A real statement with tight columns could break this, so note it in your limitations.\n\nWhen the tests pass and the dumps look right, tell me and we move to **Part 4: fingerprinting and the format registry**. All three failures have the same cause: **pdfplumber wraps every pdfminer error in its own `PdfminerException`**, and the original error is attached as `e.args[0]`. My `except` clauses were looking for `PDFPasswordIncorrect` and `PDFSyntaxError` directly, so they never matched. That was my mistake: I assumed pdfplumber lets pdfminer errors through unchanged.\n\nThe traceback shows it plainly: `PDFPasswordIncorrect` is raised, then \"During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred\", then `PdfminerException`.\n\n## The fix: edit `app/reader.py`\n\n**1. Change the imports** at the top. Replace these two lines:\n\n```python\nfrom pdfminer.pdfdocument import PDFPasswordIncorrect\nfrom pdfminer.pdfparser import PDFSyntaxError\n```\n\nwith:\n\n```python\nfrom pdfminer.pdfdocument import PDFPasswordIncorrect\nfrom pdfplumber.utils.exceptions import PdfminerException\n```\n\n**2. Replace the `try/except` block** inside `read_document`. The current one is:\n\n```python\n    try:\n        pdf = pdfplumber.open(path, password=password or \"\")\n    except PDFPasswordIncorrect:\n        if password:\n            raise WrongPasswordError(f\"The password does not open {path.name}\")\n        raise PasswordRequiredError(f\"{path.name} is password protected\")\n    except (PDFSyntaxError, ValueError) as e:\n        raise UnreadableDocumentError(f\"{path.name} could not be read: {e}\") from e\n```\n\nReplace it with:\n\n```python\n    try:\n        pdf = pdfplumber.open(path, password=password or \"\")\n    except PdfminerException as e:\n        # pdfplumber wraps the real pdfminer error; the original is in e.args[0].\n        cause = e.args[0] if e.args else None\n        if isinstance(cause, PDFPasswordIncorrect):\n            if password:\n                raise WrongPasswordError(f\"The password does not open {path.name}\") from e\n            raise PasswordRequiredError(f\"{path.name} is password protected\") from e\n        raise UnreadableDocumentError(f\"{path.name} could not be read: {cause or e}\") from e\n    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:\n        raise UnreadableDocumentError(f\"{path.name} could not be read: {e}\") from e\n```\n\nAnything pdfplumber can't open that isn't a password problem now becomes `UnreadableDocumentError`, and a missing or unreadable file (`OSError`) is handled too.\n\n## Run again\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_reader.py -v\n```\n\nYou should get 10 passed. Then the full suite:\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -v\n```\n\nThat should be 79 passed (69 earlier plus 10 reader tests).\n\n## Then look at the dumps\n\nPlease also run these and paste the output, since this is exactly what the engine will see:\n\n```bash\npython -m app.reader samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf\npython -m app.reader samples/pdfs/xyz_wealth.pdf demo1234\npython -m app.reader samples/pdfs/meridian_capital.pdf\n```\n\n## Commit once green\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 3: PDF reader with cells, password handling, file hash\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Worth noting for your AI usage log\n\nThis is a good entry for the \"where it misled you\" section: the AI wrote error handling against a library's documented exceptions without checking how the wrapper library actually surfaces them. Tests caught it, which is the reason to write failure-path tests and not just happy-path ones.\n\nWhen the tests pass, we move to **Part 4: fingerprinting and the format registry**.", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-10T11:00:55.578400Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-10T11:01:03.240794Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "# Three failures, one cause\n\nThe cell-splitting tests passed, so the layout logic is fine. {"uuid": "01a1257d-8fda-7ff9-9191-be66f545c44c", "text": "# Part 3 is done: 79 tests pass and the dumps look right\n\nI read all three dumps line by line. Table rows split into the right cells, and Meridian's `57,500.00 Dr` stays as one cell. XYZ's \"Funds added\" row has 4 cells against a 5-cell header, which is the blank-cell case the x-positions will handle.\n\n## Two things in the dumps to know about\n\n**1. Large titles split into cells.** `ABC | Portfolio | Managers` appears as three cells because the 18pt title has wide word spacing. This matters for fingerprinting. Use the line's joined `.text` (\"ABC Portfolio Managers\"), not individual cells, when searching for provider names. Part 4 does this.\n\n**2. Meridian's `Total Equity` row** has only 3 cells (label, cost, market value), so the engine must place them by x-position, not by count. That's what we kept the positions for.\n\n## Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 3: PDF reader with cells, password handling, file hash\"\ngit push\n```\n\n---\n\n# Part 4: Fingerprinting and the format registry\n\n## What we're building and why\n\nGiven a document, answer: **\"Have I seen this layout before, and which stored config applies?\"**\n\n### The fingerprint idea\n\nA fingerprint has to be **stable across months** (same provider, different numbers) but **different across providers**. Think about what changes and what doesn't:\n\n| Part of the page | Changes monthly? | Use it? |\n|---|---|---|\n| Numbers, dates, client ID | Yes | **No** |\n| Provider name in the title | No | Yes |\n| Section headings (\"Equity Holdings\") | No | Yes |\n| Table header row (\"Security, ISIN, Qty...\") | No | Yes |\n| Row labels (\"Opening Value\", \"Closing Value\") | No | Yes |\n| Names of securities held | Yes | **No** |\n\nSo we extract **\"label-like\" lines only**: lines that contain no digits at all, plus table header rows. A line like `Opening Value | 12,00,000.00` is reduced to its label `Opening Value`. A holdings row like `Infosys | INE009A01021 | 150 | ...` is dropped, since it varies by month.\n\n**The rule:** for each line, keep the leading text cells up to the first cell containing a digit. If that leaves nothing, drop the line. Also drop lines where the leading text contains a month name or a client ID pattern, which would change monthly.\n\nThat gives, for ABC, roughly:\n\n```\nabc portfolio managers\nportfolio statement\nclient code:        <- the \"AB1234\" part is dropped because it has digits\naccount summary\nopening value\nadd: inflows\n...\nsecurity | isin | qty | cost | mkt price | mkt value | weight %\n```\n\n### Two-level matching (answers \"too strict vs too loose\")\n\n1. **Exact match** on a hash of the normalised label set: fast, certain.\n2. **Similarity match** using Jaccard similarity (shared labels \u00f7 all labels). Above a high threshold (say 0.85) it is the **same format with minor drift**. Between 0.5 and 0.85 it is **probably the same provider but the layout changed**, which flags review. Below 0.5 it is **unknown**, so go learn.\n\nThree outcomes: `MATCH`, `DRIFT`, `UNKNOWN`. That gives you drift detection almost for free.\n\n### What the registry stores\n\nSQLite table `formats`: `id`, `name`, `fingerprint_hash`, `labels_json` (the label set), `config_json` (the learned artefact, filled in Part 5 or 7), `version`, `created_at`.\n\n## Step 1: Create `app/fingerprint.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Turns a Document into a stable fingerprint: the set of 'label-like' lines.\n\nDigits are the signal for 'this changes monthly', so only the text before the first\ndigit-bearing cell is kept from each line.\n\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom app.reader import Document\n\n_DIGIT = re.compile(r\"\\d\")\n_MONTHS = re.compile(\n    r\"\\b(jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)[a-z]*\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\n_SPACES = re.compile(r\"\\s+\")\n\nMATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.85\nDRIFT_THRESHOLD = 0.50\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Fingerprint:\n    labels: frozenset\n    digest: str\n\n\ndef _normalise(text: str) -> str:\n    text = _SPACES.sub(\" \", text.strip().lower())\n    return text.rstrip(\" :.-\")\n\n\ndef _line_label(cells) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Leading text cells up to the first cell that contains a digit.\"\"\"\n    kept = []\n    for c in cells:\n        if _DIGIT.search(c.text):\n            # A cell like \"Client Code: AB1234\" still has a stable prefix.\n            prefix = c.text.split(\":\")[0] if \":\" in c.text else \"\"\n            if prefix and not _DIGIT.search(prefix):\n                kept.append(prefix)\n            break\n        kept.append(c.text)\n    return \" | \".join(_normalise(k) for k in kept if _normalise(k))\n\n\ndef compute_fingerprint(doc: Document) -> Fingerprint:\n    labels = set()\n    for line in doc.lines:\n        label = _line_label(line.cells)\n        if not label or len(label) < 3:\n            continue\n        if _MONTHS.search(label) and len(label.split()) <= 4:\n            continue  # e.g. \"statement for april\" changes monthly\n        labels.add(label)\n    frozen = frozenset(labels)\n    digest = hashlib.sha256(\"\\n\".join(sorted(frozen)).encode()).hexdigest()\n    return Fingerprint(labels=frozen, digest=digest)\n\n\ndef similarity(a: frozenset, b: frozenset) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Jaccard similarity: shared labels / all labels.\"\"\"\n    if not a and not b:\n        return 1.0\n    return len(a & b) / len(a | b)\n```\n\n**A known weakness to record:** holdings rows with *no digits* in the first cell are dropped by design, but a security name like `Infosys` on a row with digits is also dropped since the line's first cell has no digit but later ones do. Look at `_line_label`: it keeps leading text cells, so `Infosys` **would be kept** as a label. That's wrong, because holdings change monthly. The fix is below.\n\n## Step 1b: Fix the holdings-name problem\n\nA row like `Infosys | INE009A01021 | 150 | ...` yields the label `infosys`, which would change the fingerprint when the portfolio changes. Rule: **if a line has more than one cell and any later cell contains a digit, it is a data row, so keep it only if it looks like a header row** (i.e. none of its cells contain digits at all). Replace `_line_label` with:\n\n```python\ndef _line_label(cells) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Stable label for a line, or '' if the line is monthly data.\"\"\"\n    texts = [c.text for c in cells]\n    has_digit = [bool(_DIGIT.search(t)) for t in texts]\n\n    if not any(has_digit):\n        # Pure text: headings, table headers, label-only rows.\n        return \" | \".join(_normalise(t) for t in texts if _normalise(t))\n\n    # Mixed line. Only the 'label | value' shape is stable (value changes, label doesn't).\n    if len(texts) == 2 and has_digit[1] and not has_digit[0]:\n        return _normalise(texts[0])\n\n    # 'Client Code: AB1234 | Period: ...' style: keep text before each colon.\n    prefixes = []\n    for t in texts:\n        if \":\" in t:\n            p = t.split(\":\")[0]\n            if p and not _DIGIT.search(p):\n                prefixes.append(_normalise(p))\n    return \" | \".join(prefixes)\n```\n\nData rows with 3+ cells containing numbers now return `\"\"` and are dropped. Two-cell `label | value` rows (like `Opening Value | 12,00,000.00`) keep their label. Headers (no digits at all) are kept whole.\n\nKnown gap: a header such as `Cost (INR)` has no digits, fine, but `% of Portfolio` is fine too. A header containing a digit (e.g. `Q1 Value`) would be dropped. Note that in your limitations.\n\n## Step 2: Create `app/registry.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"SQLite store of learned formats.\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom app.fingerprint import (\n    DRIFT_THRESHOLD, MATCH_THRESHOLD, Fingerprint, similarity,\n)\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS formats (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    name TEXT NOT NULL,\n    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    fingerprint_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    labels_json TEXT NOT NULL,\n    config_json TEXT,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\nclass MatchKind(str, Enum):\n    MATCH = \"match\"      # same format\n    DRIFT = \"drift\"      # looks like a known format but the layout changed\n    UNKNOWN = \"unknown\"  # never seen\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass MatchResult:\n    kind: MatchKind\n    format_id: Optional[int] = None\n    format_name: Optional[str] = None\n    score: float = 0.0\n    config: Optional[dict] = None\n\n\nclass Registry:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: str = \":memory:\"):\n        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)\n        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n        self.conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n\n    def add_format(self, name: str, fp: Fingerprint, config: Optional[dict] = None) -> int:\n        cur = self.conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) FROM formats WHERE name = ?\", (name,))\n        version = cur.fetchone()[0] + 1\n        cur = self.conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO formats (name, version, fingerprint_hash, labels_json, config_json)\"\n            \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (name, version, fp.digest, json.dumps(sorted(fp.labels)),\n             json.dumps(config) if config is not None else None))\n        self.conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n\n    def all_formats(self) -> list:\n        return self.conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM formats ORDER BY id\").fetchall()\n\n    def match(self, fp: Fingerprint) -> MatchResult:\n        best = None\n        best_score = 0.0\n        for row in self.all_formats():\n            if row[\"fingerprint_hash\"] == fp.digest:\n                return self._result(MatchKind.MATCH, row, 1.0)\n            score = similarity(fp.labels, frozenset(json.loads(row[\"labels_json\"])))\n            if score > best_score:\n                best, best_score = row, score\n\n        if best is None or best_score < DRIFT_THRESHOLD:\n            return MatchResult(MatchKind.UNKNOWN, score=best_score)\n        kind = MatchKind.MATCH if best_score >= MATCH_THRESHOLD else MatchKind.DRIFT\n        return self._result(kind, best, best_score)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _result(kind, row, score) -> MatchResult:\n        cfg = json.loads(row[\"config_json\"]) if row[\"config_json\"] else None\n        return MatchResult(kind, row[\"id\"], row[\"name\"], score, cfg)\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create `tests/test_fingerprint.py`\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.fingerprint import compute_fingerprint, similarity\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nfrom app.registry import MatchKind, Registry\nfrom samples.generate import generate_all\nfrom samples.sample_data import ALL_SAMPLES, PASSWORDS\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(scope=\"module\")\ndef fps(tmp_path_factory):\n    root = tmp_path_factory.mktemp(\"samples\")\n    generate_all(root)\n    return {name: compute_fingerprint(read_document(root / \"pdfs\" / f\"{name}.pdf\",\n                                                    PASSWORDS.get(name)))\n            for name in ALL_SAMPLES}\n\n\ndef test_fingerprint_ignores_monthly_data(fps):\n    labels = fps[\"abc_pms\"].labels\n    assert \"opening value\" in labels\n    assert \"security | isin | qty | cost | mkt price | mkt value | weight %\" in labels\n    assert not any(\"infosys\" in l for l in labels)       # holdings are monthly\n    assert not any(\"ab1234\" in l for l in labels)        # client id is not a label\n\n\ndef test_different_providers_have_different_fingerprints(fps):\n    names = list(fps)\n    for i, a in enumerate(names):\n        for b in names[i + 1:]:\n            assert fps[a].digest != fps[b].digest\n            assert similarity(fps[a].labels, fps[b].labels) < 0.5, (a, b)\n\n\ndef test_known_format_matches(fps):\n    reg = Registry()\n    reg.add_format(\"abc_pms\", fps[\"abc_pms\"])\n    result = reg.match(fps[\"abc_pms\"])\n    assert result.kind == MatchKind.MATCH and result.format_name == \"abc_pms\"\n\n\ndef test_unknown_format_is_unknown(fps):\n    reg = Registry()\n    reg.add_format(\"abc_pms\", fps[\"abc_pms\"])\n    assert reg.match(fps[\"helix_aif\"]).kind == MatchKind.UNKNOWN\n\n\ndef test_each_sample_matches_only_itself(fps):\n    reg = Registry()\n    for name, fp in fps.items():\n        reg.add_format(name, fp)\n    for name, fp in fps.items():\n        r = reg.match(fp)\n        assert r.kind == MatchKind.MATCH and r.format_name == name\n\n\ndef test_renamed_column_is_drift_not_match(fps):\n    reg = Registry()\n    reg.add_format(\"abc_pms\", fps[\"abc_pms\"])\n    changed = set(fps[\"abc_pms\"].labels)\n    changed.discard(\"security | isin | qty | cost | mkt price | mkt value | weight %\")\n    changed.add(\"security | isin | units | cost | price | value | weight %\")\n    from app.fingerprint import Fingerprint\n    r = reg.match(Fingerprint(frozenset(changed), \"x\"))\n    assert r.kind in (MatchKind.MATCH, MatchKind.DRIFT)\n    assert r.format_name == \"abc_pms\" and r.score < 1.0\n```\n\n## Step 4: Run and inspect\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_fingerprint.py -v\npython -c \"\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nfrom app.fingerprint import compute_fingerprint\nfp = compute_fingerprint(read_document('samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf'))\nprint('\\n'.join(sorted(fp.labels)))\n\"\n```\n\n**Read the label list.** You want to see headings, row labels and table headers, and no security names, dates or numbers. Please paste it for ABC and Meridian if anything looks off.\n\nThe last test is the interesting one. Renaming one header out of about 20 labels gives a similarity of about 0.9, which is still a `MATCH`. That reveals a real design tension: **a single renamed column barely moves the Jaccard score, yet it breaks the parser**. That's why fingerprint matching alone cannot be trusted, and why Part 5/6 adds a second check: **the engine verifies that every column the config expects is actually present**, and validation reconciles the numbers. Fingerprint says \"probably this format\", the engine and validator say \"and it really parsed\". Keep this point for the interview, since it directly answers \"what happens when a known provider quietly changes its layout?\"\n\n## Step 5: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 4: fingerprinting and format registry\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why keep only digit-free text?** Digits mark data that changes monthly.\n2. **Why three outcomes (match, drift, unknown) rather than two?** Drift is a separate, useful signal: known provider, changed layout, so human review.\n3. **Why does a renamed column still give a high similarity score, and what catches it?** The engine's expected-columns check and numeric validation.\n4. **Why Jaccard?** It is simple and deterministic, and handles added or removed labels gracefully.\n\nI haven't run this code, so paste any failures with the label dump and I'll adjust. The ones most likely to need tuning are `test_different_providers_have_different_fingerprints` (if two layouts share many generic labels like \"Account Summary\") and the label dump itself. self.conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) FROM formats WHERE name = ?\", (name,))\n        version = cur.fetchone()[0] + 1\n        cur = self.conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO formats (name, version, fingerprint_hash, labels_json, config_json)\"\n            \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (name, version, fp.digest, json.dumps(sorted(fp.labels)),\n             json.dumps(config) if config is not None else None))\n        self.conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n\n    def all_formats(self) -> list:\n        return self.conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM formats ORDER BY id\").fetchall()\n\n    def match(self, fp: Fingerprint) -> MatchResult:\n        best = None\n        best_score = 0.0\n        for row in self.all_formats():\n            if row[\"fingerprint_hash\"] == fp.digest:\n                return self._result(MatchKind.MATCH, row, 1.0)\n            score = similarity(fp.labels, frozenset(json.loads(row[\"labels_json\"])))\n            if score > best_score:\n                best, best_score = row, score\n\n        if best is None or best_score < DRIFT_THRESHOLD:\n            return MatchResult(MatchKind.UNKNOWN, score=best_score)\n        kind = MatchKind.MATCH if best_score >= MATCH_THRESHOLD else MatchKind.DRIFT\n        return self._result(kind, best, best_score)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _result(kind, row, score) -> MatchResult:\n        cfg = json.loads(row[\"config_json\"]) if row[\"config_json\"] else None\n        return MatchResult(kind, row[\"id\"], row[\"name\"], score, cfg)\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create `tests/test_fingerprint.py`\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.fingerprint import compute_fingerprint, similarity\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nfrom app.registry import MatchKind, Registry\nfrom samples.generate import generate_all\nfrom samples.sample_data import ALL_SAMPLES, PASSWORDS\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(scope=\"module\")\ndef fps(tmp_path_factory):\n    root = tmp_path_factory.mktemp(\"samples\")\n    generate_all(root)\n    return {name: compute_fingerprint(read_document(root / \"pdfs\" / f\"{name}.pdf\",\n                                                    PASSWORDS.get(name)))\n            for name in ALL_SAMPLES}\n\n\ndef test_fingerprint_ignores_monthly_data(fps):\n    labels = fps[\"abc_pms\"].labels\n    assert \"opening value\" in labels\n    assert \"security | isin | qty | cost | mkt price | mkt value | weight %\" in labels\n    assert not any(\"infosys\" in l for l in labels)       # holdings are monthly\n    assert not any(\"ab1234\" in l for l in labels)        # client id is not a label\n\n\ndef test_different_providers_have_different_fingerprints(fps):\n    names = list(fps)\n    for i, a in enumerate(names):\n        for b in names[i + 1:]:\n            assert fps[a].digest != fps[b].digest\n            assert similarity(fps[a].labels, fps[b].labels) < 0.5, (a, b)\n\n\ndef test_known_format_matches(fps):\n    reg = Registry()\n    reg.add_format(\"abc_pms\", fps[\"abc_pms\"])\n    result = reg.match(fps[\"abc_pms\"])\n    assert result.kind == MatchKind.MATCH and result.format_name == \"abc_pms\"\n\n\ndef test_unknown_format_is_unknown(fps):\n    reg = Registry()\n    reg.add_format(\"abc_pms\", fps[\"abc_pms\"])\n    assert reg.match(fps[\"helix_aif\"]).kind == MatchKind.UNKNOWN\n\n\ndef test_each_sample_matches_only_itself(fps):\n    reg = Registry()\n    for name, fp in fps.items():\n        reg.add_format(name, fp)\n    for name, fp in fps.items():\n        r = reg.match(fp)\n        assert r.kind == MatchKind.MATCH and r.format_name == name\n\n\ndef test_renamed_column_is_drift_not_match(fps):\n    reg = Registry()\n    reg.add_format(\"abc_pms\", fps[\"abc_pms\"])\n    changed = set(fps[\"abc_pms\"].labels)\n    changed.discard(\"security | isin | qty | cost | mkt price | mkt value | weight %\")\n    changed.add(\"security | isin | units | cost | price | value | weight %\")\n    from app.fingerprint import Fingerprint\n    r = reg.match(Fingerprint(frozenset(changed), \"x\"))\n    assert r.kind in (MatchKind.MATCH, MatchKind.DRIFT)\n    assert r.format_name == \"abc_pms\" and r.score < 1.0\n```\n\n## Step 4: Run and inspect\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_fingerprint.py -v\npython -c \"\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nfrom app.fingerprint import compute_fingerprint\nfp = compute_fingerprint(read_document('samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf'))\nprint('\\n'.join(sorted(fp.labels)))\n\"\n```\n\n**Read the label list.** You want to see headings, row labels and table headers, and no security names, dates or numbers. Please paste it for ABC and Meridian if anything looks off.\n\nThe last test is the interesting one. Renaming one header out of about 20 labels gives a similarity of about 0.9, which is still a `MATCH`. That reveals a real design tension: **a single renamed column barely moves the Jaccard score, yet it breaks the parser**. That's why fingerprint matching alone cannot be trusted, and why Part 5/6 adds a second check: **the engine verifies that every column the config expects is actually present**, and validation reconciles the numbers. Fingerprint says \"probably this format\", the engine and validator say \"and it really parsed\". Keep this point for the interview, since it directly answers \"what happens when a known provider quietly changes its layout?\"\n\n## Step 5: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 4: fingerprinting and format registry\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why keep only digit-free text?** Digits mark data that changes monthly.\n2. **Why three outcomes (match, drift, unknown) rather than two?** Drift is a separate, useful signal: known provider, changed layout, so human review.\n3. **Why does a renamed column still give a high similarity score, and what catches it?** The engine's expected-columns check and numeric validation.\n4. **Why Jaccard?** It is simple and deterministic, and handles added or removed labels gracefully.\n\nI haven't run this code, so paste any failures with the label dump and I'll adjust. The ones most likely to need tuning are `test_different_providers_have_different_fingerprints` (if two layouts share many generic labels like \"Account Summary\") and the label dump itself.
