{"uuid": "01a12583-a05c-7b7f-bbe7-6fc32e617601", "text": "# Part 4 passes, but the label dump shows two real flaws\n\nAll 6 tests pass. Reading the ABC label list, two things are wrong:\n\n1. **`abc | portfolio | managers`**: the title is split into three cells, so the provider name is stored as `abc | portfolio | managers` rather than `abc portfolio managers`. It still works as a fingerprint, but it's fragile. If the title font size changed, the cell split could change and the label would no longer match.\n2. **`strategy: abc large cap growth | currency: inr`**: this line has no digits, so it was kept whole. But the strategy name is data, not a label. If the same provider launches another strategy, the fingerprint changes for no good reason. The same line type will also leak the client's currency.\n\n(`client code | period` is fine: the digits were dropped and only the prefixes were kept.)\n\n## Fix 1: normalise label text by joining cells for pure-text lines\n\nIn `app/fingerprint.py`, change the pure-text branch of `_line_label`. Large headings should be joined with spaces. A table header should stay as `a | b | c`. The difference is that table header cells are far apart and heading words are not, but we've lost that at the cell level. A simpler rule: **a pure-text line with 1 to 3 cells whose combined length is under 40 characters and which has no colon is a heading, so join with spaces**.\n\nReplace the first branch of `_line_label` with:\n\n```python\n    if not any(has_digit):\n        joined = \" \".join(t for t in texts)\n        if \":\" in joined:\n            # 'Strategy: ABC Large Cap Growth | Currency: INR' -> keep only the keys\n            keys = [t.split(\":\")[0] for t in texts if \":\" in t]\n            return \" | \".join(_normalise(k) for k in keys if _normalise(k))\n        if len(texts) <= 3 and len(joined) < 40:\n            return _normalise(joined)          # heading, e.g. \"ABC Portfolio Managers\"\n        return \" | \".join(_normalise(t) for t in texts if _normalise(t))\n```\n\nTwo caveats to be honest about:\n\n- A 3-column table header with short names (for example `Date | Type | Amount`) would now be joined into `date type amount`. That is still stable and still unique, so it works, but it's a heuristic, not a principle. Record it in your limitations.\n- The line `Period: 01-Apr-2026 to ...` and the line `Fund: Sterling Growth Fund - Category II` take the colon branch only when they have no digits. `Fund: ...` becomes the label `fund`, which is correct.\n\n## Fix 2: update the tests that assert on the old labels\n\nIn `tests/test_fingerprint.py`, add:\n\n```python\ndef test_provider_title_is_one_label(fps):\n    assert \"abc portfolio managers\" in fps[\"abc_pms\"].labels\n\n\ndef test_strategy_name_is_not_in_fingerprint(fps):\n    assert not any(\"large cap\" in l for l in fps[\"abc_pms\"].labels)\n```\n\nThe existing `test_renamed_column_is_drift_not_match` uses the long ABC header string, which is unchanged (it has 7 cells, so it keeps `|` separators), so it should still pass.\n\n## Re-run\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -v\npython -c \"\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nfrom app.fingerprint import compute_fingerprint\nfor f, pw in [('abc_pms', None), ('meridian_capital', None), ('sterling_aif', None)]:\n    fp = compute_fingerprint(read_document(f'samples/pdfs/{f}.pdf', pw))\n    print('==', f); print('\\n'.join(sorted(fp.labels)))\n\"\n```\n\nYou should see `abc portfolio managers`, `strategy | currency`, and no strategy name or currency value anywhere. Paste the output if anything still looks off. I haven't run this change, so the label dump is the real test.\n\n## Commit and move on\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 4: fingerprinting and format registry\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n- **Why the dump mattered more than the green tests:** the tests passed while the fingerprint contained monthly-changing data (the strategy name). All provider knowledge lives in the config.\n\n## Step 5a: The config models\n\nCreate `app/config_spec.py`:\n\n```python\n\"\"\"The shape of a learned format config. The LLM (Part 7) must produce exactly this.\n\nEverything here is data. There is no code, so nothing in a config can execute.\n\"\"\"\nfrom typing import Literal, Optional\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator\n\nfrom app.transforms import is_known_transform\n\n\nclass _Strict(BaseModel):\n    # Unknown keys are errors, so a hallucinated field is rejected, not ignored.\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n\nclass FieldRule(_Strict):\n    \"\"\"Find a single value in the page text using a regex with one capture group.\"\"\"\n    regex: str\n    transform: str = \"text\"\n    group: int = 1\n    optional: bool = False\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        if not is_known_transform(v):\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown transform {v!r}\")\n        return v\n\n\nclass SummaryRule(_Strict):\n    \"\"\"Find a line starting with `label`; read one cell of it.\"\"\"\n    label: str\n    transform: str = \"number\"\n    cell: int = -1             # -1 = last cell on the line\n    optional: bool = False\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        if not is_known_transform(v):\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown transform {v!r}\")\n        return v\n\n\nclass ColumnRule(_Strict):\n    header: str                # header cell text, matched case-insensitively\n    field: str\n    transform: str = \"text\"\n    optional: bool = False     # True: a missing column is allowed\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        if not is_known_transform(v):\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown transform {v!r}\")\n        return v\n\n\nclass TableRule(_Strict):\n    header_starts_with: str    # text the header line starts with\n    stop_at: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)   # line prefixes ending the table\n    columns: list[ColumnRule]\n    # For transactions: the type column's text goes through txn_type via the column rule.\n    skip_if_blank: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)  # fields that must be non-empty\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def _has_columns(self):\n        if not self.columns:\n            raise ValueError(\"a table needs at least one column\")\n        return self\n\n\nclass FormatConfig(_Strict):\n    format_name: str\n    statement_type: Literal[\"pms\", \"aif\"]\n    provider: str\n    currency: str = \"INR\"\n    # Statement-level single values: client_id, strategy_name, period_start, period_end\n    fields: dict[str, FieldRule]\n    summary: dict[str, SummaryRule] = Field(default_factory=dict)\n    holdings: Optional[TableRule] = None\n    transactions: Optional[TableRule] = None\n\n    @field_validator(\"fields\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _required_fields(cls, v):\n        missing = {\"client_id\", \"period_start\", \"period_end\"} - set(v)\n        if missing:\n            raise ValueError(f\"missing required fields: {sorted(missing)}\")\n        return v\n```\n\nCreate `configs/abc_pms.json` as the first hand-written config. \"to\\\\s+(\\\\d{2}-[A-Za-z]{3}-\\\\d{4})\", \"transform\": \"date_dd_mon_yyyy\"}\n  },\n  \"summary\": {\n    \"opening_value\": {\"label\": \"Opening Value\"},\n    \"capital_inflows\": {\"label\": \"closing_value\": {\"label\": \"Closing Value\"},\n    \"cash_balance\": {\"label\": \"Cash Balance\"}\n  },\n  \"holdings\": {\n    \"header_starts_with\": \"Security\",\n    \"stop_at\": [\"Total\"],\n    \"columns\": [\n      {\"header\": \"Security\", \"field\": \"security_name\", \"transform\": \"text\"},\n      {\"header\": \"ISIN\", \"field\": \"isin\", \"transform\": Price\", \"field\": \"market_price\", \"transform\": \"number\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Mkt Value\", \"field\": \"market_value\", \"transform\": \"number\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Weight %\", \"security_name\", \"transform\": \"text\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Qty\", \"field\": \"quantity\", \"transform\": \"number\", \"optional\": true},\n      {\"header\": \"Amount\", \"field\": \"amount\", \"transform\": \"number\"}\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nNote one mismatch to fix: the models above name the table key `header_starts_with` in the JSON, matching the model field Add a line to your limitations note: \u201cCurrency text embedded in labels makes fingerprints currency-sensitive.\u201d\ncant we tackle it", "citations": []}], "sender": "human", "created_at": "2026-10-10T11:19:32.999961Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-10T11:19:32.999961Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a12588-b214-70b5-8c20-71dbd935344d"}, {"uuid": "01a1258a-20d2-726c-bad8-efe56ee98116", "text": "# Yes, we can fix it\n\nThe fix is to strip currency tokens from labels before they go into the fingerprint, so `cost (inr)` and `cost (usd)` both become `cost`.\n\n## Step 1: Edit `app/fingerprint.py`\n\nAdd this regex next to the other compiled patterns at the top:\n\n```python\n_CURRENCY = re.compile(r\"\\(?\\b(inr|usd|eur|gbp|rs)\\b\\.?\\)?|[\u20b9$\u20ac\u00a3]\", re.IGNORECASE)\n```\n\nThen replace `_normalise` with:\n\n```python\ndef _normalise(text: str) -> str:\n    text = text.strip().lower()\n    text = _CURRENCY.sub(\" \", text)          # currency is data, not layout\n    text = _SPACES.sub(\" \", text).strip()\n    return text.rstrip(\" :.-\")\n```\n\nThe existing code already skips labels shorter than 3 characters, so a label that was only a currency marker disappears.\n\n## Step 2: Add tests to `tests/test_fingerprint.py`\n\n```python\nfrom app.fingerprint import _normalise\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"a, b\", [\n    (\"Cost (INR)\", \"Cost (USD)\"),\n    (\"Amount (INR)\", \"Amount (EUR)\"),\n    (\"All amounts in INR\", \"All amounts in USD\"),\n    (\"Value (Rs.)\", \"Value (INR)\"),\n])\ndef test_currency_does_not_change_labels(a, b):\n    assert _normalise(a) == _normalise(b)\n\n\ndef test_currency_stripping_keeps_real_words():\n    assert _normalise(\"Cost (INR)\") == \"cost\"\n    assert _normalise(\"Currency\") == \"currency\"      # the word itself is a stable key\n    assert _normalise(\"Total Return\") == \"total return\"\n```\n\n## Step 3: Re-run and re-check the dumps\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -v\npython -c \"\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nfrom app.fingerprint import compute_fingerprint\nfrom samples.sample_data import PASSWORDS\nfor f in ['xyz_wealth','sterling_aif']:\n    fp = compute_fingerprint(read_document(f'samples/pdfs/{f}.pdf', PASSWORDS.get(f)))\n    print('==', f); print('\\n'.join(sorted(fp.labels))); print()\n\"\n```\n\nYou should now see:\n- XYZ: `all amounts in`, and the header `stock name | units held | cost | value | isin code | % of portfolio`\n- Sterling: `nav per unit` and `date | type | description | amount`, with no `(inr)`\n\n## What this does and doesn't solve\n\n- **Solved:** a currency change on its own no longer moves the fingerprint at all.\n- **Still true:** the fingerprint is a heuristic. Other things could leak monthly-varying text into labels, such as a heading that carries a quarter name (\"Q1 Review\", which the digit rule drops, but \"Quarterly Review\" wouldn't be dropped). The dump check is how you catch these, so keep doing it for every new format.\n- **A trade-off to mention in the interview:** the fix also means a USD statement from the same provider will fingerprint as a `MATCH`. That is what you want for layout recognition, but it is the parser's job to read the currency from the document. This is why `currency` is in the config's fields or defaults and not inferred from the fingerprint. In Part 5 I'll make sure a mismatched currency is surfaced in validation.\n\nUpdate your limitations note: *\"Fingerprint labels strip currency tokens, so a currency change alone isn't detected as drift; currency is read from the statement itself.\"*\n\n## Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 4: strip currency from fingerprint labels\"\ngit push\n```\n\nYou haven't yet pasted the Step 5a result. Please run `python -m pytest tests/test_config_spec.py -v` as well (you want 4 passed) and tell me both results. "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a12592-4ca2-75ee-b76a-85df8e871473"}, {"uuid": "01a12592-fab4-7f0d-86ac-96a7b713c453", "text": "# Step 5b: the engine for header fields and summary values\n\nYour 5a tests pass (4/4), so the config models are solid. This step adds:\n\n1. A small tightening of `config_spec.py`, so bad configs are rejected earlier\n2. The engine (`app/engine.py`), covering header fields and summary rows\n3. Hand-written configs for the other four samples\n4. Tests that compare engine output to each `expected.json`\n\nTables (holdings and transactions) come in 5c.\n\n## Step 1: Replace `app/config_spec.py`\n\nThree additions to what you have:\n\n- `fields` keys must come from a fixed list.\n- `summary` keys must be real `Summary` fields.\n- Each regex must compile and have enough capture groups.\n\nThese matter because in Part 7 an LLM will write these configs. Rejecting garbage at load time means the engine never sees it.\n\n```python\n\"\"\"The shape of a learned format config. The LLM (Part 7) must produce exactly this.\n\nEverything here is data. There is no code, so nothing in a config can execute.\n\"\"\"\nimport re\nfrom typing import Literal, Optional\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator\n\nfrom app.schema import Summary\nfrom app.transforms import is_known_transform\n\nALLOWED_FIELDS = {\"client_id\", \"strategy_name\", \"period_start\", \"period_end\", \"currency\"}\nSUMMARY_FIELDS = set(Summary.model_fields)\n\n\nclass _Strict(BaseModel):\n    # Unknown keys are errors, so a hallucinated field is rejected, not ignored.\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n\ndef _check_transform(v: str) -> str:\n    if not is_known_transform(v):\n        raise ValueError(f\"unknown transform {v!r}\")\n    return v\n\n\nclass FieldRule(_Strict):\n    \"\"\"Find a single value in the page text using a regex with a capture group.\"\"\"\n    regex: str\n    transform: str = \"text\"\n    group: int = 1\n    optional: bool = False\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        return _check_transform(v)\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def _regex_ok(self):\n        try:\n            compiled = re.compile(self.regex)\n        except re.error as e:\n            raise ValueError(f\"invalid regex: {e}\")\n        if compiled.groups < self.group:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"regex has {compiled.groups} capture group(s) but group={self.group}\")\n        return self\n\n\nclass SummaryRule(_Strict):\n    \"\"\"Find the line whose FIRST CELL equals `label` (case-insensitive); read one cell.\"\"\"\n    label: str\n    transform: str = \"number\"\n    cell: int = -1             # -1 = last cell on the line\n    optional: bool = False\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        return _check_transform(v)\n\n\nclass ColumnRule(_Strict):\n    header: str                # header cell text, matched case-insensitively\n    field: str\n    transform: str = \"text\"\n    optional: bool = False     # True: a missing column is allowed\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        return _check_transform(v)\n\n\nclass TableRule(_Strict):\n    header_starts_with: str    # text the header line starts with\n    stop_at: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)   # line prefixes ending the table\n    columns: list[ColumnRule]\n    skip_if_blank: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)  # fields that must be non-empty\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def _has_columns(self):\n        if not self.columns:\n            raise ValueError(\"a table needs at least one column\")\n        return self\n\n\nclass FormatConfig(_Strict):\n    format_name: str\n    statement_type: Literal[\"pms\", \"aif\"]\n    provider: str\n    currency: str = \"INR\"      # default, used if no 'currency' field rule is given\n    fields: dict[str, FieldRule]\n    summary: dict[str, SummaryRule] = Field(default_factory=dict)\n    holdings: Optional[TableRule] = None\n    transactions: Optional[TableRule] = None\n\n    @field_validator(\"fields\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _check_fields(cls, v):\n        missing = {\"client_id\", \"period_start\", \"period_end\"} - set(v)\n        if missing:\n            raise ValueError(f\"missing required fields: {sorted(missing)}\")\n        unknown = set(v) - ALLOWED_FIELDS\n        if unknown:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown field names: {sorted(unknown)}\")\n        return v\n\n    @field_validator(\"summary\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _check_summary_keys(cls, v):\n        unknown = set(v) - SUMMARY_FIELDS\n        if unknown:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown summary fields: {sorted(unknown)}\")\n        return v\n```\n\nAdd these tests to the end of `tests/test_config_spec.py`:\n\n```python\ndef test_unknown_field_name_rejected():\n    data = load(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"fields\"][\"favourite_colour\"] = {\"regex\": \"(x)\"}\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        FormatConfig.model_validate(data)\n\n\ndef test_unknown_summary_field_rejected():\n    data = load(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"summary\"][\"profit_margin\"] = {\"label\": \"Profit\"}\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        FormatConfig.model_validate(data)\n\n\ndef test_bad_regex_rejected():\n    data = load(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"fields\"][\"client_id\"][\"regex\"] = \"Client Code:(\\\\S+\"      # unbalanced bracket\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        FormatConfig.model_validate(data)\n\n\ndef test_regex_without_capture_group_rejected():\n    data = load(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"fields\"][\"client_id\"][\"regex\"] = \"Client Code:\"           # no group\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        FormatConfig.model_validate(data)\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `app/engine.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"The generic parsing engine. It knows nothing about any provider.\n\nAll provider knowledge lives in a FormatConfig. Given the same Document and the\nsame config, the output is always identical, and nothing here calls an LLM.\n\nDesign rule: never guess. If a required value can't be found or read, record an\nissue; at the end all issues are raised together as one ParseError.\n\"\"\"\nimport re\n\nfrom pydantic import ValidationError\n\nfrom app.config_spec import FormatConfig, SummaryRule\nfrom app.reader import Document, Line\nfrom app.schema import Statement, StatementType, Summary\nfrom app.transforms import TransformError, apply_transform\n\n_SPACES = re.compile(r\"\\s+\")\n\n\nclass ParseError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The config could not be applied to this document. Carries every problem found.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, issues: list[str]):\n        self.issues = issues\n        super().__init__(\"; \".join(issues))\n\n\ndef _norm(text: str) -> str:\n    return _SPACES.sub(\" \", text.strip().lower())\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ header fields\ndef extract_fields(doc: Document, cfg: FormatConfig, issues: list[str]) -> dict:\n    text = doc.text\n    out = {}\n    for name, rule in cfg.fields.items():\n        match = re.search(rule.regex, text)\n        if not match:\n            if not rule.optional:\n                issues.append(f\"field {name!r}: pattern not found in document\")\n            continue\n        try:\n            value = apply_transform(rule.transform, match.group(rule.group))\n        except TransformError as e:\n            issues.append(f\"field {name!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n        if value is None:\n            if not rule.optional:\n                issues.append(f\"field {name!r}: matched but the value was empty\")\n            continue\n        out[name] = value\n    return out\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ summary rows\ndef _lines_with_label(doc: Document, label: str) -> list[Line]:\n    target = _norm(label)\n    return [ln for ln in doc.lines\n            if len(ln.cells) >= 2 and _norm(ln.cells[0].text) == target]\n\n\ndef _read_summary_rule(doc: Document, name: str, rule: SummaryRule, issues: list[str]):\n    lines = _lines_with_label(doc, rule.label)\n    if not lines:\n        if not rule.optional:\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: no line labelled {rule.label!r}\")\n        return None\n\n    values = set()\n    for ln in lines:\n        try:\n            raw = ln.cells[rule.cell].text\n        except IndexError:\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: line {ln.text!r} has no cell {rule.cell}\")\n            return None\n        try:\n            values.add(apply_transform(rule.transform, raw))\n        except TransformError as e:\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: {e}\")\n            return None\n\n    if len(values) > 1:\n        # The same label printed twice with different numbers: don't pick one silently.\n        issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: label {rule.label!r} appears with \"\n                      f\"different values {sorted(map(str, values))}\")\n        return None\n    return values.pop()\n\n\ndef extract_summary(doc: Document, cfg: FormatConfig, issues: list[str]) -> dict:\n    out = {}\n    for name, rule in cfg.summary.items():\n        value = _read_summary_rule(doc, name, rule, issues)\n        if value is not None:\n            out[name] = value\n    return out\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ assembly\ndef parse_head(doc: Document, cfg: FormatConfig) -> Statement:\n    \"\"\"Statement-level fields and summary only. 5c adds holdings and transactions.\"\"\"\n    issues: list[str] = []\n    fields = extract_fields(doc, cfg, issues)\n    summary_values = extract_summary(doc, cfg, issues)\n    if issues:\n        raise ParseError(issues)\n\n    currency = fields.pop(\"currency\", None) or cfg.currency\n    try:\n        return Statement(\n            statement_type=StatementType(cfg.statement_type),\n            provider=cfg.provider,\n            currency=currency,\n            summary=Summary(**summary_values),\n            **fields,\n        )\n    except ValidationError as e:\n        raise ParseError([f\"{'.'.join(map(str, err['loc']))}: {err['msg']}\"\n                          for err in e.errors()]) from e\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    # python -m app.engine abc_pms samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf [password]\n    import json\n    import sys\n    from pathlib import Path\n\n    from app.reader import read_document\n\n    config = FormatConfig.model_validate_json(\n        (Path(\"configs\") / f\"{sys.argv[1]}.json\").read_text())\n    document = read_document(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None)\n    print(json.dumps(json.loads(parse_head(document, config).model_dump_json()), indent=2))\n```\n\n## Step 3: The other four configs\n\nCreate these four files in `configs/`. Every label and header is copied exactly as the reader dump printed it. Remember that JSON needs doubled backslashes (`\\\\d`).\n\n**`configs/xyz_wealth.json`**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"format_name\": \"xyz_wealth\",\n  \"statement_type\": \"pms\",\n  \"provider\": \"XYZ Wealth\",\n  \"currency\": \"INR\",\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"client_id\": {\"regex\": \"Investor ID\\\\s*\\\\.+\\\\s*(\\\\S+)\"},\n    \"strategy_name\": {\"regex\": \"Scheme\\\\s*:\\\\s*(.+)\"},\n    \"period_start\": {\"regex\": \"Statement Period\\\\s*:\\\\s*(\\\\d{2}/\\\\d{2}/\\\\d{4})\\\\s+to\", \"transform\": \"date_dd_mm_yyyy\"},\n    \"period_end\": {\"regex\": \"Statement Period\\\\s*:\\\\s*\\\\d{2}/\\\\d{2}/\\\\d{4}\\\\s+to\\\\s+(\\\\d{2}/\\\\d{2}/\\\\d{4})\", \"transform\": \"date_dd_mm_yyyy\"},\n    \"currency\": {\"regex\": \"All amounts in\\\\s+([A-Za-z]{3})\"}\n  },\n  \"summary\": {\n    \"opening_value\": {\"label\": \"Beginning Balance\"},\n    \"capital_inflows\": {\"label\": \"Deposits\"},\n    \"capital_outflows\": {\"label\": \"Withdrawals\", \"transform\": \"number_abs\"},\n    \"fees_charged\": {\"label\": \"Fees & Charges\", \"transform\": \"number_abs\"},\n    \"net_gain\": {\"label\": \"Gain for the Period\"},\n    \"closing_value\": {\"label\": \"Ending Balance\"},\n    \"cash_balance\": {\"label\": \"Cash / Liquid Balance\"}\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**`configs/meridian_capital.json`**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"format_name\": \"meridian_capital\",\n  \"statement_type\": \"pms\",\n  \"provider\": \"Meridian Capital\",\n  \"currency\": \"INR\",\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"client_id\": {\"regex\": \"Client Ref:\\\\s*(\\\\S+)\"},\n    \"strategy_name\": {\"regex\": \"Mandate:\\\\s*(.+)\"},\n    \"period_start\": {\"regex\": \"From\\\\s+(\\\\d{1,2}\\\\s+[A-Za-z]+\\\\s+\\\\d{4})\\\\s+to\", \"transform\": \"date_dd_month_yyyy\"},\n    \"period_end\": {\"regex\": \"From\\\\s+\\\\d{1,2}\\\\s+[A-Za-z]+\\\\s+\\\\d{4}\\\\s+to\\\\s+(\\\\d{1,2}\\\\s+[A-Za-z]+\\\\s+\\\\d{4})\", \"transform\": \"date_dd_month_yyyy\"},\n    \"currency\": {\"regex\": \"Reporting currency:\\\\s*([A-Za-z]{3})\"}\n  },\n  \"summary\": {\n    \"opening_value\": {\"label\": \"Portfolio value at start\"},\n    \"closing_value\": {\"label\": \"Portfolio value at end\"},\n    \"cash_balance\": {\"label\": \"Cash balance\"},\n    \"fees_charged\": {\"label\": \"Charges for the period\"}\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**`configs/sterling_aif.json`**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"format_name\": \"sterling_aif\",\n  \"statement_type\": \"aif\",\n  \"provider\": \"Sterling Growth Fund\",\n  \"currency\": \"INR\",\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"client_id\": {\"regex\": \"Investor Code:\\\\s*(\\\\S+)\"},\n    \"strategy_name\": {\"regex\": \"Fund:\\\\s*(.+)\"},\n    \"period_start\": {\"regex\": \"Period:\\\\s*(\\\\d{4}-\\\\d{2}-\\\\d{2})\\\\s+to\", \"transform\": \"date_iso\"},\n    \"period_end\": {\"regex\": \"Period:\\\\s*\\\\d{4}-\\\\d{2}-\\\\d{2}\\\\s+to\\\\s+(\\\\d{4}-\\\\d{2}-\\\\d{2})\", \"transform\": \"date_iso\"},\n    \"currency\": {\"regex\": \"Currency:\\\\s*([A-Za-z]{3})\"}\n  },\n  \"summary\": {\n    \"opening_value\": {\"label\": \"Opening Capital Account Balance\"},\n    \"capital_inflows\": {\"label\": \"Add: Capital Contributions\"},\n    \"capital_outflows\": {\"label\": This step adds:\n\n1. A small tightening of `config_spec.py`, so bad configs are rejected earlier\n2. The engine (`app/engine.py`), covering header fields and summary rows\n3. Hand-written configs for the other four samples\n4. Tests that compare engine output to each `expected.json`\n\nTables (holdings and transactions) come in 5c.\n\n## Step 1: Replace `app/config_spec.py`\n\nThree additions to what you have:\n\n- `fields` keys must come from a fixed list.\n- `summary` keys must be real `Summary` fields.\n- Each regex must compile and have enough capture groups.\n\nThese matter because in Part 7 an LLM will write these configs. Rejecting garbage at load time means the engine never sees it.\n\n```python\n\"\"\"The shape of a learned format config. The LLM (Part 7) must produce exactly this.\n\nEverything here is data. There is no code, so nothing in a config can execute.\n\"\"\"\nimport re\nfrom typing import Literal, Optional\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator\n\nfrom app.schema import Summary\nfrom app.transforms import is_known_transform\n\nALLOWED_FIELDS = {\"client_id\", \"strategy_name\", \"period_start\", \"period_end\", \"currency\"}\nSUMMARY_FIELDS = set(Summary.model_fields)\n\n\nclass _Strict(BaseModel):\n    # Unknown keys are errors, so a hallucinated field is rejected, not ignored.\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n\ndef _check_transform(v: str) -> str:\n    if not is_known_transform(v):\n        raise ValueError(f\"unknown transform {v!r}\")\n    return v\n\n\nclass FieldRule(_Strict):\n    \"\"\"Find a single value in the page text using a regex with a capture group.\"\"\"\n    regex: str\n    transform: str = \"text\"\n    group: int = 1\n    optional: bool = False\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        return _check_transform(v)\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def _regex_ok(self):\n        try:\n            compiled = re.compile(self.regex)\n        except re.error as e:\n            raise ValueError(f\"invalid regex: {e}\")\n        if compiled.groups < self.group:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"regex has {compiled.groups} capture group(s) but group={self.group}\")\n        return self\n\n\nclass SummaryRule(_Strict):\n    \"\"\"Find the line whose FIRST CELL equals `label` (case-insensitive); read one cell.\"\"\"\n    label: str\n    transform: str = \"number\"\n    cell: int = -1             # -1 = last cell on the line\n    optional: bool = False\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        return _check_transform(v)\n\n\nclass ColumnRule(_Strict):\n    header: str                # header cell text, matched case-insensitively\n    field: str\n    transform: str = \"text\"\n    optional: bool = False     # True: a missing column is allowed\n\n    @field_validator(\"transform\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _known(cls, v):\n        return _check_transform(v)\n\n\nclass TableRule(_Strict):\n    header_starts_with: str    # text the header line starts with\n    stop_at: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)   # line prefixes ending the table\n    columns: list[ColumnRule]\n    skip_if_blank: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)  # fields that must be non-empty\n\n    @model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def _has_columns(self):\n        if not self.columns:\n            raise ValueError(\"a table needs at least one column\")\n        return self\n\n\nclass FormatConfig(_Strict):\n    format_name: str\n    statement_type: Literal[\"pms\", \"aif\"]\n    provider: str\n    currency: str = \"INR\"      # default, used if no 'currency' field rule is given\n    fields: dict[str, FieldRule]\n    summary: dict[str, SummaryRule] = Field(default_factory=dict)\n    holdings: Optional[TableRule] = None\n    transactions: Optional[TableRule] = None\n\n    @field_validator(\"fields\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _check_fields(cls, v):\n        missing = {\"client_id\", \"period_start\", \"period_end\"} - set(v)\n        if missing:\n            raise ValueError(f\"missing required fields: {sorted(missing)}\")\n        unknown = set(v) - ALLOWED_FIELDS\n        if unknown:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown field names: {sorted(unknown)}\")\n        return v\n\n    @field_validator(\"summary\")\n    @classmethod\n    def _check_summary_keys(cls, v):\n        unknown = set(v) - SUMMARY_FIELDS\n        if unknown:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unknown summary fields: {sorted(unknown)}\")\n        return v\n```\n\nAdd these tests to the end of `tests/test_config_spec.py`:\n\n```python\ndef test_unknown_field_name_rejected():\n    data = load(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"fields\"][\"favourite_colour\"] = {\"regex\": \"(x)\"}\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        FormatConfig.model_validate(data)\n\n\ndef test_unknown_summary_field_rejected():\n    data = load(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"summary\"][\"profit_margin\"] = {\"label\": \"Profit\"}\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        FormatConfig.model_validate(data)\n\n\ndef test_bad_regex_rejected():\n    data = load(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"fields\"][\"client_id\"][\"regex\"] = \"Client Code:(\\\\S+\"      # unbalanced bracket\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        FormatConfig.model_validate(data)\n\n\ndef test_regex_without_capture_group_rejected():\n    data = load(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"fields\"][\"client_id\"][\"regex\"] = \"Client Code:\"           # no group\n    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):\n        FormatConfig.model_validate(data)\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `app/engine.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"The generic parsing engine. It knows nothing about any provider.\n\nAll provider knowledge lives in a FormatConfig. Given the same Document and the\nsame config, the output is always identical, and nothing here calls an LLM.\n\nDesign rule: never guess. If a required value can't be found or read, record an\nissue; at the end all issues are raised together as one ParseError.\n\"\"\"\nimport re\n\nfrom pydantic import ValidationError\n\nfrom app.config_spec import FormatConfig, SummaryRule\nfrom app.reader import Document, Line\nfrom app.schema import Statement, StatementType, Summary\nfrom app.transforms import TransformError, apply_transform\n\n_SPACES = re.compile(r\"\\s+\")\n\n\nclass ParseError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The config could not be applied to this document. Carries every problem found.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, issues: list[str]):\n        self.issues = issues\n        super().__init__(\"; \".join(issues))\n\n\ndef _norm(text: str) -> str:\n    return _SPACES.sub(\" \", text.strip().lower())\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ header fields\ndef extract_fields(doc: Document, cfg: FormatConfig, issues: list[str]) -> dict:\n    text = doc.text\n    out = {}\n    for name, rule in cfg.fields.items():\n        match = re.search(rule.regex, text)\n        if not match:\n            if not rule.optional:\n                issues.append(f\"field {name!r}: pattern not found in document\")\n            continue\n        try:\n            value = apply_transform(rule.transform, match.group(rule.group))\n        except TransformError as e:\n            issues.append(f\"field {name!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n        if value is None:\n            if not rule.optional:\n                issues.append(f\"field {name!r}: matched but the value was empty\")\n            continue\n        out[name] = value\n    return out\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ summary rows\ndef _lines_with_label(doc: Document, label: str) -> list[Line]:\n    target = _norm(label)\n    return [ln for ln in doc.lines\n            if len(ln.cells) >= 2 and _norm(ln.cells[0].text) == target]\n\n\ndef _read_summary_rule(doc: Document, name: str, rule: SummaryRule, issues: list[str]):\n    lines = _lines_with_label(doc, rule.label)\n    if not lines:\n        if not rule.optional:\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: no line labelled {rule.label!r}\")\n        return None\n\n    values = set()\n    for ln in lines:\n        try:\n            raw = ln.cells[rule.cell].text\n        except IndexError:\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: line {ln.text!r} has no cell {rule.cell}\")\n            return None\n        try:\n            values.add(apply_transform(rule.transform, raw))\n        except TransformError as e:\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: {e}\")\n            return None\n\n    if len(values) > 1:\n        # The same label printed twice with different numbers: don't pick one silently.\n        issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: label {rule.label!r} appears with \"\n                      f\"different values {sorted(map(str, values))}\")\n        return None\n    return values.pop()\n\n\ndef extract_summary(doc: Document, cfg: FormatConfig, issues: list[str]) -> dict:\n    out = {}\n    for name, rule in cfg.summary.items():\n        value = _read_summary_rule(doc, name, rule, issues)\n        if value is not None:\n            out[name] = value\n    return out\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ assembly\ndef parse_head(doc: Document, cfg: FormatConfig) -> Statement:\n    \"\"\"Statement-level fields and summary only. 5c adds holdings and transactions.\"\"\"\n    issues: list[str] = []\n    fields = extract_fields(doc, cfg, issues)\n    summary_values = extract_summary(doc, cfg, issues)\n    if issues:\n        raise ParseError(issues)\n\n    currency = fields.pop(\"currency\", None) or cfg.currency\n    try:\n        return Statement(\n            statement_type=StatementType(cfg.statement_type),\n            provider=cfg.provider,\n            currency=currency,\n            summary=Summary(**summary_values),\n            **fields,\n        )\n    except ValidationError as e:\n        raise ParseError([f\"{'.'.join(map(str, err['loc']))}: {err['msg']}\"\n                          for err in e.errors()]) from e\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    # python -m app.engine abc_pms samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf [password]\n    import json\n    import sys\n    from pathlib import Path\n\n    from app.reader import read_document\n\n    config = FormatConfig.model_validate_json(\n        (Path(\"configs\") / f\"{sys.argv[1]}.json\").read_text())\n    document = read_document(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None)\n    print(json.dumps(json.loads(parse_head(document, config).model_dump_json()), indent=2))\n```\n\n## Step 3: The other four configs\n\nCreate these four files in `configs/`. Every label and header is copied exactly as the reader dump printed it. All five formats match their `expected.json` on every header and summary field.\n\nCommit:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 5b: parsing engine for header fields and summary; configs for all 5 formats\"\ngit push\n```\n\n---\n\n# Step 5c: the table engine\n\nThis adds holdings and transactions, so the engine's output equals the **full** `expected.json`.\n\n## The problem to solve\n\nRows have varying numbers of cells (XYZ's \"Funds added\" row has 4 cells under a 5-cell header, and Meridian's `Total Equity` has 3). So we **assign each cell to a column by x-position**, not by counting.\n\n**The rule:** each header cell has an x-range. A data cell belongs to the header column whose range it overlaps most. Right-aligned numbers line up with the right edge of their header, and left-aligned text with the left edge, so overlap works for both.\n\n**Edge cases handled:**\n- Two cells landing in the same column are an error, never a silent merge.\n- A cell overlapping no column is an error.\n- Header cells that were split by the gap rule (e.g. a header with a wide internal space) must be matched against the config's `header` text, so we match by text and then take that cell's range.\n\n## Step 1: Add the table code to `app/engine.py`\n\nAdd these imports at the top, merging with the existing ones:\n\n```python\nfrom app.config_spec import ColumnRule, TableRule\nfrom app.reader import Cell\nfrom app.schema import Holding, Transaction\n```\n\nAdd this block **above** the `# assembly` section:\n\n```python\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tables\ndef _overlap(a: Cell, b: Cell) -> float:\n    return max(0.0, min(a.x1, b.x1) - max(a.x0, b.x0))\n\n\ndef _find_header(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str):\n    \"\"\"Index of the first line starting with header_starts_with that holds all columns.\"\"\"\n    start = _norm(rule.header_starts_with)\n    required = [_norm(c.header) for c in rule.columns if not c.optional]\n    for i, ln in enumerate(doc.lines):\n        if not _norm(ln.text).startswith(start):\n            continue\n        texts = {_norm(c.text) for c in ln.cells}\n        if all(r in texts for r in required):\n            return i\n    issues.append(f\"{label}: no header line starting with \"\n                  f\"{rule.header_starts_with!r} containing all required columns\")\n    return None\n\n\ndef _column_cells(header: Line, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Map each ColumnRule.field -> its header Cell (None if optional and absent).\"\"\"\n    by_text = {_norm(c.text): c for c in header.cells}\n    out = {}\n    for col in rule.columns:\n        cell = by_text.get(_norm(col.header))\n        if cell is None and not col.optional:\n            issues.append(f\"{label}: column {col.header!r} not in header\")\n        out[col.field] = cell\n    return out\n\n\ndef _assign(line: Line, columns: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Assign each cell on the line to the column it overlaps most. Raises on ambiguity.\"\"\"\n    assigned: dict = {}\n    for cell in line.cells:\n        best_field, best = None, 0.0\n        for field_name, hdr in columns.items():\n            if hdr is None:\n                continue\n            o = _overlap(cell, hdr)\n            if o > best:\n                best_field, best = field_name, o\n        if best_field is None:\n            raise TransformError(f\"cell {cell.text!r} sits under no known column\")\n        if best_field in assigned:\n            raise TransformError(\n                f\"two cells ({assigned[best_field]!r}, {cell.text!r}) fall in column \"\n                f\"{best_field!r}\")\n        assigned[best_field] = cell.text\n    return assigned\n\n\ndef extract_table(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> list[dict]:\n    idx = _find_header(doc, rule, issues, label)\n    if idx is None:\n        return []\n    header = doc.lines[idx]\n    columns = _column_cells(header, rule, issues, label)\n    if issues:\n        return []\n\n    stops = [_norm(s) for s in rule.stop_at]\n    rules = {c.field: c for c in rule.columns}\n    rows: list[dict] = []\n\n    for ln in doc.lines[idx + 1:]:\n        if ln.page != header.page:\n            break                                   # multi-page tables: see limitations\n        text = _norm(ln.text)\n        if any(text.startswith(s) for s in stops):\n            break\n        # A line with a single cell is a new section heading, so the table has ended.\n        if len(ln.cells) < 2:\n            break\n        try:\n            raw = _assign(ln, columns)\n            row = {f: apply_transform(rules[f].transform, raw.get(f)) for f in rules}\n        except TransformError as e:\n            issues.append(f\"{label} row {ln.text!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n        blank_required = [f for f in rule.skip_if_blank if row.get(f) is None]\n        if blank_required:\n            continue\n        rows.append(row)\n\n    if not rows and not issues:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: header found but no data rows\")\n    return rows\n```\n\n## Step 2: Replace `parse_head` with `parse`\n\nKeep `parse_head` if you like (the old tests use it), and add this below it:\n\n```python\ndef parse(doc: Document, cfg: FormatConfig) -> Statement:\n    \"\"\"Full deterministic parse: header, summary, holdings, transactions.\"\"\"\n    issues: list[str] = []\n    fields = extract_fields(doc, cfg, issues)\n    summary_values = extract_summary(doc, cfg, issues)\n    holdings = (extract_table(doc, cfg.holdings, issues, \"holdings\")\n                if cfg.holdings else [])\n    transactions = (extract_table(doc, cfg.transactions, issues, \"transactions\")\n                    if cfg.transactions else [])\n    if issues:\n        raise ParseError(issues)\n\n    currency = fields.pop(\"currency\", None) or cfg.currency\n    try:\n        return Statement(\n            statement_type=StatementType(cfg.statement_type),\n            provider=cfg.provider,\n            currency=currency,\n            summary=Summary(**summary_values),\n            holdings=[Holding(**h) for h in holdings],\n            transactions=[Transaction(**t) for t in transactions],\n            **fields,\n        )\n    except ValidationError as e:\n        raise ParseError([f\"{'.'.join(map(str, err['loc']))}: {err['msg']}\"\n                          for err in e.errors()]) from e\n```\n\nChange the `__main__` block's `parse_head(` call to `parse(`.\n\nOne subtle point: `extract_table` returns early with `[]` when `issues` is non-empty, and `issues` is shared across all rules. A header failure in holdings would therefore also skip transactions. That's acceptable for now (the statement fails anyway), but it means issues from later tables may be hidden. Note it for the limitations list.\n\n## Step 3: Table sections in the configs\n\n**Add to `configs/xyz_wealth.json`** (after `\"summary\": {...}`, with a comma):\n\n```json\n  \"holdings\": {\n \"date_dd_month_yyyy\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Nature\", \"field\": \"type\", \"transform\": \"txn_type\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Particulars\", \"field\": \"security_name\"},\n      {\"header\": \"transform\": \"date_iso\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Type\", \"field\": \"type\", \"transform\": \"txn_type\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Description\", \"field\": \"security_name\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Amount (INR)\", \"field\": \"amount\", \"transform\": \"number\"}\n    ]\n  }\n```\n\n**Add to `configs/helix_aif.json`:**\n\n```json\n  \"transactions\": {\n    \"header_starts_with\": \"Date\",\n \"txn_type\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Narration\", \"field\": \"security_name\"},\n      {\"header\": \"Amount\", \"field\": \"amount\", \"transform\": \"number\"}\n    ]\n  }\n```\n\n(ABC already has both tables. Its holdings `Total` stop works because the total row's first cell starts with `Total`.)\n\n## Step 4: Create `tests/test_engine_full.py`\n\n```python\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.config_spec import FormatConfig\nfrom app.engine import ParseError, parse\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nfrom app.schema import Statement\nfrom samples.generate import generate_all\nfrom samples.sample_data import PASSWORDS\n\nCONFIGS = Path(__file__).parent.parent / \"configs\"\nNAMES = [\"abc_pms\", \"xyz_wealth\", \"meridian_capital\", \"sterling_aif\", \"helix_aif\"]\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(scope=\"module\")\ndef samples(tmp_path_factory):\n    root = tmp_path_factory.mktemp(\"samples\")\n    generate_all(root)\n    return root\n\n\ndef cfg_dict(name):\n    return json.loads((CONFIGS / f\"{name}.json\").read_text())\n\n\ndef read(samples, name):\n    return read_document(samples / \"pdfs\" / f\"{name}.pdf\", PASSWORDS.get(name))\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name\", NAMES)\ndef test_full_parse_equals_expected(samples, name):\n    got = parse(read(samples, name), FormatConfig.model_validate(cfg_dict(name)))\n    expected = Statement.model_validate_json(\n        (samples / \"expected\" / f\"{name}.json\").read_text())\n    assert got.model_dump(exclude={\"source_file_hash\"}) == \\\n           expected.model_dump(exclude={\"source_file_hash\"})\n\n\ndef test_parsing_is_deterministic(samples):\n    cfg = FormatConfig.model_validate(cfg_dict(\"abc_pms\"))\n    doc = read(samples, \"abc_pms\")\n    assert parse(doc, cfg).model_dump_json() == parse(doc, cfg).model_dump_json()\n\n\ndef test_renamed_column_fails_loudly(samples):\n    data = cfg_dict(\"abc_pms\")\n    data[\"holdings\"][\"columns\"][2][\"header\"] = \"Units\"       # provider renamed Qty\n    with pytest.raises(ParseError, match=\"Units\"):\n        parse(read(samples, \"abc_pms\"), FormatConfig.model_validate(data))\n\n\ndef test_blank_cell_row_is_placed_by_position(samples):\n    stmt = parse(read(samples, \"xyz_wealth\"),\n                 FormatConfig.model_validate(cfg_dict(\"xyz_wealth\")))\n    funds = stmt.transactions[0]\n    assert funds.security_name == \"Funds added\"\n    assert funds.quantity is None and str(funds.amount) == \"100000.00\"\n\n\ndef test_total_row_is_not_a_holding(samples):\n    stmt = parse(read(samples, \"meridian_capital\"),\n                 FormatConfig.model_validate(cfg_dict(\"meridian_capital\")))\n    assert [h.security_name for h in stmt.holdings] == [\n        \"Sun Pharmaceutical Industries\", \"Titan Company\", \"Axis Bank\"]\n\n\ndef test_dr_cr_signs(samples):\n    stmt = parse(read(samples, \"meridian_capital\"),\n                 FormatConfig.model_validate(cfg_dict(\"meridian_capital\")))\n    amounts = [str(t.amount) for t in stmt.transactions]\n    assert amounts == [\"-57500.00\", \"4500.00\", \"67000.00\", \"-6000.00\"]\n```\n\n## Step 5: Run\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_engine_full.py -v\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\nI haven't run any of this. Likely trouble spots:\n\n- **Right-aligned numbers vs wide headers.** If a number's x-range doesn't overlap its header (for example a narrow number under a wide header and right-aligned), `_assign` raises \"sits under no known column\". Paste the error and the `python -m app.reader` dump for that file, and I'll adjust.\n- **Meridian's `Qty` column** is optional and its header text is `Qty`; the `Particulars` text may be wide enough to overlap `Qty`. If so, I'd switch to assigning by the cell's centre point.\n- **Multiple tables with the same header start**: `\"Date\"` in ABC matches only the transactions header, since the holdings header starts with `Security`.\n\n## Step 6: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 5c: table engine with position-based column assignment\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why assign by x-overlap and not cell count?** Blank cells vanish when text is flattened, so counting shifts every later value one column left. So we **assign each cell to a column by x-position**, not by counting.\n\n**The rule:** each header cell has an x-range. A data cell belongs to the header column whose range it overlaps most. Right-aligned numbers line up with the right edge of their header, and left-aligned text with the left edge, so overlap works for both.\n\n**Edge cases handled:**\n- Two cells landing in the same column are an error, never a silent merge.\n- A cell overlapping no column is an error.\n- Header cells that were split by the gap rule (e.g. a header with a wide internal space) must be matched against the config's `header` text, so we match by text and then take that cell's range.\n\n## Step 1: Add the table code to `app/engine.py`\n\nAdd these imports at the top, merging with the existing ones:\n\n```python\nfrom app.config_spec import ColumnRule, TableRule\nfrom app.reader import Cell\nfrom app.schema import Holding, Transaction\n```\n\nAdd this block **above** the `# assembly` section:\n\n```python\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tables\ndef _overlap(a: Cell, b: Cell) -> float:\n    return max(0.0, min(a.x1, b.x1) - max(a.x0, b.x0))\n\n\ndef _find_header(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str):\n    \"\"\"Index of the first line starting with header_starts_with that holds all columns.\"\"\"\n    start = _norm(rule.header_starts_with)\n    required = [_norm(c.header) for c in rule.columns if not c.optional]\n    for i, ln in enumerate(doc.lines):\n        if not _norm(ln.text).startswith(start):\n            continue\n        texts = {_norm(c.text) for c in ln.cells}\n        if all(r in texts for r in required):\n            return i\n    issues.append(f\"{label}: no header line starting with \"\n                  f\"{rule.header_starts_with!r} containing all required columns\")\n    return None\n\n\ndef _column_cells(header: Line, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Map each ColumnRule.field -> its header Cell (None if optional and absent).\"\"\"\n    by_text = {_norm(c.text): c for c in header.cells}\n    out = {}\n    for col in rule.columns:\n        cell = by_text.get(_norm(col.header))\n        if cell is None and not col.optional:\n            issues.append(f\"{label}: column {col.header!r} not in header\")\n        out[col.field] = cell\n    return out\n\n\ndef _assign(line: Line, columns: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Assign each cell on the line to the column it overlaps most. Raises on ambiguity.\"\"\"\n    assigned: dict = {}\n    for cell in line.cells:\n        best_field, best = None, 0.0\n        for field_name, hdr in columns.items():\n            if hdr is None:\n                continue\n            o = _overlap(cell, hdr)\n            if o > best:\n                best_field, best = field_name, o\n        if best_field is None:\n            raise TransformError(f\"cell {cell.text!r} sits under no known column\")\n        if best_field in assigned:\n            raise TransformError(\n                f\"two cells ({assigned[best_field]!r}, {cell.text!r}) fall in column \"\n                f\"{best_field!r}\")\n        assigned[best_field] = cell.text\n    return assigned\n\n\ndef extract_table(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> list[dict]:\n    idx = _find_header(doc, rule, issues, label)\n    if idx is None:\n        return []\n    header = doc.lines[idx]\n    columns = _column_cells(header, rule, issues, label)\n    if issues:\n        return []\n\n    stops = [_norm(s) for s in rule.stop_at]\n    rules = {c.field: c for c in rule.columns}\n    rows: list[dict] = []\n\n    for ln in doc.lines[idx + 1:]:\n        if ln.page != header.page:\n            break                                   # multi-page tables: see limitations\n        text = _norm(ln.text)\n        if any(text.startswith(s) for s in stops):\n            break\n        # A line with a single cell is a new section heading, so the table has ended.\n        if len(ln.cells) < 2:\n            break\n        try:\n            raw = _assign(ln, columns)\n            row = {f: apply_transform(rules[f].transform, raw.get(f)) for f in rules}\n        except TransformError as e:\n            issues.append(f\"{label} row {ln.text!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n        blank_required = [f for f in rule.skip_if_blank if row.get(f) is None]\n        if blank_required:\n            continue\n        rows.append(row)\n\n    if not rows and not issues:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: header found but no data rows\")\n    return rows\n```\n\n## Step 2: Replace `parse_head` with `parse`\n\nKeep `parse_head` if you like (the old tests use it), and add this below it:\n\n```python\ndef parse(doc: Document, cfg: FormatConfig) -> Statement:\n    \"\"\"Full deterministic parse: header, summary, holdings, transactions.\"\"\"\n    issues: list[str] = []\n    fields = extract_fields(doc, cfg, issues)\n    summary_values = extract_summary(doc, cfg, issues)\n    holdings = (extract_table(doc, cfg.holdings, issues, \"holdings\")\n                if cfg.holdings else [])\n    transactions = (extract_table(doc, cfg.transactions, issues, \"transactions\")\n                    if cfg.transactions else [])\n    if issues:\n        raise ParseError(issues)\n\n    currency = fields.pop(\"currency\", None) or cfg.currency\n    try:\n        return Statement(\n            statement_type=StatementType(cfg.statement_type),\n            provider=cfg.provider,\n            currency=currency,\n            summary=Summary(**summary_values),\n            holdings=[Holding(**h) for h in holdings],\n            transactions=[Transaction(**t) for t in transactions],\n            **fields,\n        )\n    except ValidationError as e:\n        raise Commit if you haven't already:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 5c: table engine, clearer header errors\"\ngit push\n```\n\n---\n\n# Part 6: Validation\n\n## What we're building and why\n\nThe brief asks: *\"Without an AI checking the output, how does the system know a deterministic parse is correct?\"* This part is the answer. A parse can run without errors and still be wrong, for example when a wrong column is read or a number is misplaced. Validation checks that the numbers are **internally consistent**.\n\n### Design decisions\n\n1. **Each check returns a result, not an exception.** Results have a severity: `error` (the numbers contradict each other), `warning` (suspicious but possible), or `skipped` (the data needed isn't in this statement). Skipped matters: Meridian doesn't print net gain, so the reconciliation check must skip, not fail.\n2. **Status is decided from the results:**\n   - any `error` \u2192 `needs_review`\n   - only warnings \u2192 `parsed_ok_with_warnings`\n   - no problems \u2192 `parsed_ok`\n3. **Tolerances, not exact equality.** Printed values are rounded, so we allow a small difference (default \u20b91 absolute, or 0.1% relative, whichever is larger).\n4. **Sign conventions differ per provider**, so flow checks compare magnitudes where a provider might print fees or outflows as negatives.\n5. **Checks never modify data.** Validation only reports.\n\n### The checks\n\n| # | Check | Applies to | Severity if it fails |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | ISIN format and checksum | holdings | error |\n| 2 | qty \u00d7 price \u2248 market value | holdings with qty and price | error |\n| 3 | Sum of holdings + cash \u2248 closing value | PMS with cash and closing | error |\n| 4 | Weights \u2248 value \u00f7 closing value | holdings with weights | warning |\n| 5 | Opening + inflows \u2212 outflows \u2212 fees + gain \u2248 closing | all with those fields | error |\n| 6 | Units \u00d7 NAV \u2248 closing value | AIF | error |\n| 7 | Commitment = called + uncalled | not checkable (called isn't stored), so skip | n/a |\n| 8 | Transaction dates inside the period | transactions | warning |\n| 9 | Transaction type `OTHER` | transactions | warning |\n| 10 | Fees in transactions \u2248 `fees_charged` | when both exist | warning |\n| 11 | Required data present (PMS has holdings, AIF has NAV and units) | all | error |\n\nCheck 5 needs care. For ABC: 1,200,000 + 50,000 \u2212 0 \u2212 8,000 + 88,000 = 1,330,000. \u2713. The sample's net gain is defined so that this holds, so we test with exactly that formula.\n\n## Step 1: Create `app/validation.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Internal-consistency checks on a parsed Statement. Never modifies the data.\n\nA check returns a list of Finding. Severity:\n  error   - the numbers contradict each other: a human must look\n  warning - suspicious but possible\n  skipped - not enough data to run the check (recorded, never silent)\n\"\"\"\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom decimal import Decimal\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom app.isin_util import is_valid_isin\nfrom app.schema import Statement, StatementType, TransactionType\n\nABS_TOLERANCE = Decimal(\"1.00\")       # rupees\nREL_TOLERANCE = Decimal(\"0.001\")      # 0.1 %\nWEIGHT_TOLERANCE = Decimal(\"0.05\")    # percentage points (printed to 2 dp)\n\n\nclass Severity(str, Enum):\n    ERROR = \"error\"\n    WARNING = \"warning\"\n    SKIPPED = \"skipped\"\n\n\nclass Status(str, Enum):\n    OK = \"parsed_ok\"\n    WARNINGS = \"parsed_ok_with_warnings\"\n    REVIEW = \"needs_review\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Finding:\n    check: str\n    severity: Severity\n    message: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ValidationReport:\n    findings: list\n\n    @property\n    def status(self) -> Status:\n        if any(f.severity == Severity.ERROR for f in self.findings):\n            return Status.REVIEW\n        if any(f.severity == Severity.WARNING for f in self.findings):\n            return Status.WARNINGS\n        return Status.OK\n\n    def of(self, severity: Severity) -> list:\n        return [f for f in self.findings if f.severity == severity]\n\n\ndef close(a: Decimal, b: Decimal, base: Optional[Decimal] = None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if a and b differ by less than the tolerance.\"\"\"\n    scale = abs(base if base is not None else b)\n    return abs(a - b) <= max(ABS_TOLERANCE, scale * REL_TOLERANCE)\n\n\ndef _skip(check, why):\n    return [Finding(check, Severity.SKIPPED, why)]\n\n\ndef _err(check, msg):\n    return [Finding(check, Severity.ERROR, msg)]\n\n\ndef _warn(check, msg):\n    return [Finding(check, Severity.WARNING, msg)]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- individual checks\ndef check_required_data(s: Statement) -> list:\n    out = []\n    sm = s.summary\n    if sm.closing_value is None:\n        out += _err(\"required_data\", \"closing_value is missing\")\n    if s.statement_type == StatementType.PMS and not s.holdings:\n        out += _err(\"required_data\", \"PMS statement has no holdings\")\n    if s.statement_type == StatementType.AIF:\n        if sm.nav_per_unit is None:\n            out += _err(\"required_data\", \"AIF statement has no NAV per unit\")\n        if sm.units_held is None:\n            out += _err(\"required_data\", \"AIF statement has no units held\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_isins(s: Statement) -> list:\n    if not s.holdings:\n        return _skip(\"isin\", \"no holdings\")\n    out = []\n    for h in s.holdings:\n        if h.isin is None:\n            out += _warn(\"isin\", f\"{h.security_name}: no ISIN\")\n        elif not is_valid_isin(h.isin):\n            out += _err(\"isin\", f\"{h.security_name}: invalid ISIN {h.isin}\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_qty_times_price(s: Statement) -> list:\n    rows = [h for h in s.holdings if h.quantity is not None and h.market_price is not None]\n    if not rows:\n        return _skip(\"qty_x_price\", \"no holdings with both quantity and price\")\n    out = []\n    for h in rows:\n        expected = h.quantity * h.market_price\n        if not close(expected, h.market_value):\n            out += _err(\"qty_x_price\",\n                        f\"{h.security_name}: {h.quantity} x {h.market_price} = {expected}, \"\n                        f\"but market value is {h.market_value}\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_holdings_plus_cash(s: Statement) -> list:\n    sm = s.summary\n    if not s.holdings or sm.cash_balance is None or sm.closing_value is None:\n        return _skip(\"holdings_plus_cash\", \"needs holdings, cash balance and closing value\")\n    total = sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings) + sm.cash_balance\n    if close(total, sm.closing_value):\n        return []\n    return _err(\"holdings_plus_cash\",\n                f\"holdings + cash = {total}, but closing value is {sm.closing_value}\")\n\n\ndef check_weights(s: Statement) -> list:\n    sm = s.summary\n    rows = [h for h in s.holdings if h.weight_pct is not None]\n    if not rows or not sm.closing_value:\n        return _skip(\"weights\", \"no weights or no closing value\")\n    out = []\n    for h in rows:\n        expected = h.market_value / sm.closing_value * 100\n        if abs(expected - h.weight_pct) > WEIGHT_TOLERANCE:\n            out += _warn(\"weights\",\n                         f\"{h.security_name}: weight {h.weight_pct}% but value/closing \"\n                         f\"is {expected.quantize(Decimal('0.01'))}%\")\n    total = sum(h.weight_pct for h in rows)\n    if total > Decimal(\"100.5\"):\n        out += _warn(\"weights\", f\"weights add up to {total}%, which is above 100%\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_reconciliation(s: Statement) -> list:\n    \"\"\"opening + inflows - outflows - fees + gain = closing (magnitudes, so a provider\n    printing fees as negatives still reconciles).\"\"\"\n    sm = s.summary\n    needed = [sm.opening_value, sm.closing_value, sm.capital_inflows,\n              sm.capital_outflows, sm.fees_charged, sm.net_gain]\n    if any(v is None for v in needed):\n        return _skip(\"reconciliation\", \"statement does not print every component\")\n    expected = (sm.opening_value + abs(sm.capital_inflows) - abs(sm.capital_outflows)\n                - abs(sm.fees_charged) + sm.net_gain)\n    if close(expected, sm.closing_value):\n        return []\n    return _err(\"reconciliation\",\n                f\"opening {sm.opening_value} + inflows {sm.capital_inflows} - outflows \"\n                f\"{sm.capital_outflows} - fees {sm.fees_charged} + gain {sm.net_gain} = \"\n                f\"{expected}, but closing value is {sm.closing_value}\")\n\n\ndef check_units_times_nav(s: Statement) -> list:\n    sm = s.summary\n    if s.statement_type != StatementType.AIF:\n        return _skip(\"units_x_nav\", \"not an AIF\")\n    if sm.units_held is None or sm.nav_per_unit is None or sm.closing_value is None:\n        return _skip(\"units_x_nav\", \"needs units, NAV and closing value\")\n    expected = sm.units_held * sm.nav_per_unit\n    if close(expected, sm.closing_value):\n        return []\n    return _err(\"units_x_nav\",\n                f\"{sm.units_held} units x NAV {sm.nav_per_unit} = {expected}, \"\n                f\"but closing value is {sm.closing_value}\")\n\n\ndef check_transaction_dates(s: Statement) -> list:\n    if not s.transactions:\n        return _skip(\"txn_dates\", \"no transactions\")\n    out = []\n    for t in s.transactions:\n        if not (s.period_start <= t.date <= s.period_end):\n            out += _warn(\"txn_dates\", f\"{t.date} ({t.security_name}) is outside the \"\n                                      f\"statement period\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_transaction_types(s: Statement) -> list:\n    others = [t for t in s.transactions if t.type == TransactionType.OTHER]\n    return [Finding(\"txn_types\", Severity.WARNING,\n                    f\"{t.date} {t.security_name}: unrecognised transaction type\")\n            for t in others]\n\n\ndef check_fees_vs_transactions(s: Statement) -> list:\n    sm = s.summary\n    fee_txns = [t for t in s.transactions if t.type == TransactionType.FEE]\n    if sm.fees_charged is None or not fee_txns:\n        return _skip(\"fees\", \"no fee total or no fee transactions\")\n    total = sum(abs(t.amount) for t in fee_txns)\n    if close(total, abs(sm.fees_charged)):\n        return []\n    return _warn(\"fees\", f\"fee transactions add up to {total}, but fees charged is \"\n                         f\"{sm.fees_charged}\")\n\n\nCHECKS = [\n    check_required_data, check_isins, check_qty_times_price, check_holdings_plus_cash,\n    check_weights, check_reconciliation, check_units_times_nav,\n    check_transaction_dates, check_transaction_types, check_fees_vs_transactions,\n]\n\n\ndef validate(statement: Statement) -> ValidationReport:\n    findings = []\n    for check in CHECKS:\n        findings.extend(check(statement))\n    return ValidationReport(findings)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    # python -m app.validation samples/expected/abc_pms.json\n    import sys\n    from pathlib import Path\n\n    stmt = Statement.model_validate_json(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())\n    report = validate(stmt)\n    print(\"status:\", report.status.value)\n    for f in report.findings:\n        print(f\"  [{f.severity.value:7}] {f.check}: {f.message}\")\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `tests/test_validation.py`\n\nThe key idea: **clean samples must pass, and deliberately corrupted copies must be caught.** If the corruption tests didn't exist, a validator that always returned \"ok\" would pass.\n\n```python\nfrom decimal import Decimal as D\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.schema import TransactionType\nfrom app.validation import Severity, Status, close, validate\nfrom samples.sample_data import ALL_SAMPLES\nfrom samples.generate import visible_copy\n\n\ndef stmt(name):\n    # What the engine would produce: only fields the PDF actually shows.\n    return visible_copy(name, ALL_SAMPLES[name]())\n\n\ndef errors(report):\n    return {f.check for f in report.of(Severity.ERROR)}\n\n\ndef warnings(report):\n    return {f.check for f in report.of(Severity.WARNING)}\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name\", list(ALL_SAMPLES))\ndef test_clean_samples_pass(name):\n    report = validate(stmt(name))\n    assert report.status in (Status.OK, Status.WARNINGS), report.findings\n    assert not errors(report)\n\n\ndef test_meridian_skips_reconciliation_not_fails():\n    report = validate(stmt(\"meridian_capital\"))\n    skipped = {f.check for f in report.of(Severity.SKIPPED)}\n    assert \"reconciliation\" in skipped\n    assert \"reconciliation\" not in errors(report)\n\n\ndef test_wrong_market_value_is_caught():\n    s = stmt(\"abc_pms\")\n    s.holdings[0].market_value += D(\"5000\")\n    report = validate(s)\n    assert report.status == "text", "text": "# Part 5 is done: 120 tests pass\n\nThe engine now parses all five formats end to end and matches every `expected.json`, with no LLM involved. Commit if you haven't already:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 5c: table engine, clearer header errors\"\ngit push\n```\n\n---\n\n# Part 6: Validation\n\n## What we're building and why\n\nThe brief asks: *\"Without an AI checking the output, how does the system know a deterministic parse is correct?\"* This part is the answer. A parse can run without errors and still be wrong, for example when a wrong column is read or a number is misplaced. Validation checks that the numbers are **internally consistent**.\n\n### Design decisions\n\n1. **Each check returns a result, not an exception.** Results have a severity: `error` (the numbers contradict each other), `warning` (suspicious but possible), or `skipped` (the data needed isn't in this statement). Skipped matters: Meridian doesn't print net gain, so the reconciliation check must skip, not fail.\n2. **Status is decided from the results:**\n   - any `error` \u2192 `needs_review`\n   - only warnings \u2192 `parsed_ok_with_warnings`\n   - no problems \u2192 `parsed_ok`\n3. **Tolerances, not exact equality.** Printed values are rounded, so we allow a small difference (default \u20b91 absolute, or 0.1% relative, whichever is larger).\n4. **Sign conventions differ per provider**, so flow checks compare magnitudes where a provider might print fees or outflows as negatives.\n5. **Checks never modify data.** Validation only reports.\n\n### The checks\n\n| # | Check | Applies to | Severity if it fails |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | ISIN format and checksum | holdings | error |\n| 2 | qty \u00d7 price \u2248 market value | holdings with qty and price | error |\n| 3 | Sum of holdings + cash \u2248 closing value | PMS with cash and closing | error |\n| 4 | Weights \u2248 value \u00f7 closing value | holdings with weights | warning |\n| 5 | Opening + inflows \u2212 outflows \u2212 fees + gain \u2248 closing | all with those fields | error |\n| 6 | Units \u00d7 NAV \u2248 closing value | AIF | error |\n| 7 | Commitment = called + uncalled | not checkable (called isn't stored), so skip | n/a |\n| 8 | Transaction dates inside the period | transactions | warning |\n| 9 | Transaction type `OTHER` | transactions | warning |\n| 10 | Fees in transactions \u2248 `fees_charged` | when both exist | warning |\n| 11 | Required data present (PMS has holdings, AIF has NAV and units) | all | error |\n\nCheck 5 needs care. For ABC: 1,200,000 + 50,000 \u2212 0 \u2212 8,000 + 88,000 = 1,330,000. \u2713. The sample's net gain is defined so that this holds, so we test with exactly that formula.\n\n## Step 1: Create `app/validation.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Internal-consistency checks on a parsed Statement. Never modifies the data.\n\nA check returns a list of Finding. Severity:\n  error   - the numbers contradict each other: a human must look\n  warning - suspicious but possible\n  skipped - not enough data to run the check (recorded, never silent)\n\"\"\"\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom decimal import Decimal\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom app.isin_util import is_valid_isin\nfrom app.schema import Statement, StatementType, TransactionType\n\nABS_TOLERANCE = Decimal(\"1.00\")       # rupees\nREL_TOLERANCE = Decimal(\"0.001\")      # 0.1 %\nWEIGHT_TOLERANCE = Decimal(\"0.05\")    # percentage points (printed to 2 dp)\n\n\nclass Severity(str, Enum):\n    ERROR = \"error\"\n    WARNING = \"warning\"\n    SKIPPED = \"skipped\"\n\n\nclass Status(str, Enum):\n    OK = \"parsed_ok\"\n    WARNINGS = \"parsed_ok_with_warnings\"\n    REVIEW = \"needs_review\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Finding:\n    check: str\n    severity: Severity\n    message: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ValidationReport:\n    findings: list\n\n    @property\n    def status(self) -> Status:\n        if any(f.severity == Severity.ERROR for f in self.findings):\n            return Status.REVIEW\n        if any(f.severity == Severity.WARNING for f in self.findings):\n            return Status.WARNINGS\n        return Status.OK\n\n    def of(self, severity: Severity) -> list:\n        return [f for f in self.findings if f.severity == severity]\n\n\ndef close(a: Decimal, b: Decimal, base: Optional[Decimal] = None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if a and b differ by less than the tolerance.\"\"\"\n    scale = abs(base if base is not None else b)\n    return abs(a - b) <= max(ABS_TOLERANCE, scale * REL_TOLERANCE)\n\n\ndef _skip(check, why):\n    return [Finding(check, Severity.SKIPPED, why)]\n\n\ndef _err(check, msg):\n    return [Finding(check, Severity.ERROR, msg)]\n\n\ndef _warn(check, msg):\n    return [Finding(check, Severity.WARNING, msg)]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- individual checks\ndef check_required_data(s: Statement) -> list:\n    out = []\n    sm = s.summary\n    if sm.closing_value is None:\n        out += _err(\"required_data\", \"closing_value is missing\")\n    if s.statement_type == StatementType.PMS and not s.holdings:\n        out += _err(\"required_data\", \"PMS statement has no holdings\")\n    if s.statement_type == StatementType.AIF:\n        if sm.nav_per_unit is None:\n            out += _err(\"required_data\", \"AIF statement has no NAV per unit\")\n        if sm.units_held is None:\n            out += _err(\"required_data\", \"AIF statement has no units held\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_isins(s: Statement) -> list:\n    if not s.holdings:\n        return _skip(\"isin\", \"no holdings\")\n    out = []\n    for h in s.holdings:\n        if h.isin is None:\n            out += _warn(\"isin\", f\"{h.security_name}: no ISIN\")\n        elif not is_valid_isin(h.isin):\n            out += _err(\"isin\", f\"{h.security_name}: invalid ISIN {h.isin}\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_qty_times_price(s: Statement) -> list:\n    rows = [h for h in s.holdings if h.quantity is not None and h.market_price is not None]\n    if not rows:\n        return _skip(\"qty_x_price\", \"no holdings with both quantity and price\")\n    out = []\n    for h in rows:\n        expected = h.quantity * h.market_price\n        if not close(expected, h.market_value):\n            out += _err(\"qty_x_price\",\n                        f\"{h.security_name}: {h.quantity} x {h.market_price} = {expected}, \"\n                        f\"but market value is {h.market_value}\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_holdings_plus_cash(s: Statement) -> list:\n    sm = s.summary\n    if not s.holdings or sm.cash_balance is None or sm.closing_value is None:\n        return _skip(\"holdings_plus_cash\", \"needs holdings, cash balance and closing value\")\n    total = sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings) + sm.cash_balance\n    if close(total, sm.closing_value):\n        return []\n    return _err(\"holdings_plus_cash\",\n                f\"holdings + cash = {total}, but closing value is {sm.closing_value}\")\n\n\ndef check_weights(s: Statement) -> list:\n    sm = s.summary\n    rows = [h for h in s.holdings if h.weight_pct is not None]\n    if not rows or not sm.closing_value:\n        return _skip(\"weights\", \"no weights or no closing value\")\n    out = []\n    for h in rows:\n        expected = h.market_value / sm.closing_value * 100\n        if abs(expected - h.weight_pct) > WEIGHT_TOLERANCE:\n            out += _warn(\"weights\",\n                         f\"{h.security_name}: weight {h.weight_pct}% but value/closing \"\n                         f\"is {expected.quantize(Decimal('0.01'))}%\")\n    total = sum(h.weight_pct for h in rows)\n    if total > Decimal(\"100.5\"):\n        out += _warn(\"weights\", f\"weights add up to {total}%, which is above 100%\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_reconciliation(s: Statement) -> list:\n    \"\"\"opening + inflows - outflows - fees + gain = closing (magnitudes, so a provider\n    printing fees as negatives still reconciles).\"\"\"\n    sm = s.summary\n    needed = [sm.opening_value, sm.closing_value, sm.capital_inflows,\n              sm.capital_outflows, sm.fees_charged, sm.net_gain]\n    if any(v is None for v in needed):\n        return _skip(\"reconciliation\", \"statement does not print every component\")\n    expected = (sm.opening_value + abs(sm.capital_inflows) - abs(sm.capital_outflows)\n                - abs(sm.fees_charged) + sm.net_gain)\n    if close(expected, sm.closing_value):\n        return []\n    return _err(\"reconciliation\",\n                f\"opening {sm.opening_value} + inflows {sm.capital_inflows} - outflows \"\n                f\"{sm.capital_outflows} - fees {sm.fees_charged} + gain {sm.net_gain} = \"\n                f\"{expected}, but closing value is {sm.closing_value}\")\n\n\ndef check_units_times_nav(s: Statement) -> list:\n    sm = s.summary\n    if s.statement_type != StatementType.AIF:\n        return _skip(\"units_x_nav\", \"not an AIF\")\n    if sm.units_held is None or sm.nav_per_unit is None or sm.closing_value is None:\n        return _skip(\"units_x_nav\", \"needs units, NAV and closing value\")\n    expected = sm.units_held * sm.nav_per_unit\n    if close(expected, sm.closing_value):\n        return []\n    return _err(\"units_x_nav\",\n                f\"{sm.units_held} units x NAV {sm.nav_per_unit} = {expected}, \"\n                f\"but closing value is {sm.closing_value}\")\n\n\ndef check_transaction_dates(s: Statement) -> list:\n    if not s.transactions:\n        return _skip(\"txn_dates\", \"no transactions\")\n    out = []\n    for t in s.transactions:\n        if not (s.period_start <= t.date <= s.period_end):\n            out += _warn(\"txn_dates\", f\"{t.date} ({t.security_name}) is outside the \"\n                                      f\"statement period\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check_transaction_types(s: Statement) -> list:\n    others = [t for t in s.transactions if t.type == TransactionType.OTHER]\n    return [Finding(\"txn_types\", Severity.WARNING,\n                    f\"{t.date} {t.security_name}: unrecognised transaction type\")\n            for t in others]\n\n\ndef check_fees_vs_transactions(s: Statement) -> list:\n    sm = s.summary\n    fee_txns = [t for t in s.transactions if t.type == TransactionType.FEE]\n    if sm.fees_charged is None or not fee_txns:\n        return _skip(\"fees\", \"no fee total or no fee transactions\")\n    total = sum(abs(t.amount) for t in fee_txns)\n    if close(total, abs(sm.fees_charged)):\n        return []\n    return _warn(\"fees\", f\"fee transactions add up to {total}, but fees charged is \"\n                         f\"{sm.fees_charged}\")\n\n\nCHECKS = [\n    check_required_data, check_isins, check_qty_times_price, check_holdings_plus_cash,\n    check_weights, check_reconciliation, check_units_times_nav,\n    check_transaction_dates, check_transaction_types, check_fees_vs_transactions,\n]\n\n\ndef validate(statement: Statement) -> ValidationReport:\n    findings = []\n    for check in CHECKS:\n        findings.extend(check(statement))\n    return ValidationReport(findings)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    # python -m app.validation samples/expected/abc_pms.json\n    import sys\n    from pathlib import Path\n\n    stmt = Statement.model_validate_json(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())\n    report = validate(stmt)\n    print(\"status:\", report.status.value)\n    for f in report.findings:\n        print(f\"  [{f.severity.value:7}] {f.check}: {f.message}\")\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `tests/test_validation.py`\n\nThe key idea: **clean samples must pass, and deliberately corrupted copies must be caught.** If
