The renamed-column, duplicate, drift and password cases pass too.\n\nI'd still like to see the live folder run (`python -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs`) at some point, but the email flow below will replace it as your demo.\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 8: pipeline orchestrator, document store, dedup, password list, drift policy\"\ngit push\n```\n\n# Part 9: Email ingestion\n\n## What this part does and the decisions behind it\n\nThe system connects to a Gmail inbox, picks out statement emails, saves their PDF attachments, and hands each one to the pipeline.\n\n| Decision | Choice | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| Protocol | IMAP with a Gmail **app password** | Much simpler than OAuth and the Gmail API. Trade-off: the credential is broad, so use a dedicated test account |\n| Mailbox access | **Read-only**: `select(readonly=True)` plus `BODY.PEEK` | The system can never mark, move or delete mail |\n| Classifying | Keyword scoring **before** anything reaches the pipeline | A random PDF (an invoice, a bank letter) must never be sent to an external LLM. That's a privacy and cost issue |\n| Several PDFs per email | Each is scored and processed separately | This covers the brief's \"single email with several statements\" stretch goal |\n| Idempotency | By `Message-ID` for emails, and by file hash (Part 8) for PDFs | Re-running ingestion, or a forwarded copy, creates no duplicates |\n| Attachment names | Sanitised | A name like `../../x.pdf` must not write outside our folder |\n| Real PDFs only | Must start with `%PDF-` | A `.pdf` name proves nothing |\n\n**The scoring rules** (an attachment is processed if its total is at least 2):\n\n| Signal | Score |\n|---|---|\n| Sender is on `STATEMENT_SENDERS` (optional allow-list) | +3 |\n| Subject mentions *statement, portfolio, PMS, AIF, capital account, valuation, holdings, NAV...* | +2 |\n| Attachment filename mentions the same words | +2 |\n| Body mentions them | +1 |\n| Subject mentions *invoice, receipt, newsletter...* | \u22121 |\n| Filename mentions *brochure, terms, invoice, factsheet...* | \u22123 |\n\nText is split into words first (`abc_pms.pdf` becomes `abc pms pdf`), because `_` isn't a word boundary in regexes. Every email gets a decision recorded (`processed`, `skipped` or `no_pdf`) with the score and reasons, so a wrongly skipped statement is visible on the review page and never lost silently.\n\n## Step 1: Small edits\n\n**`app/store.py`**: add this directly under the `SCHEMA = \"\"\"...\"\"\"` block:\n\n```python\nSCHEMA += \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS emails (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    message_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    subject TEXT, sender TEXT, received TEXT,\n    decision TEXT NOT NULL,\n    attachments_json TEXT,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n\"\"\"\n```\n\nThen add these methods at the end of the `Store` class:\n\n```python\n    def email_seen(self, message_id: str) -> bool:\n        with self._lock:\n            row = self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT 1 FROM emails WHERE message_id = ?\", (message_id,)).fetchone()\n        return row is not None\n\n    def record_email(self, message_id, subject, sender, received, decision, attachments_json):\n        with self._lock:\n            self.conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO emails (message_id, subject, sender, received, decision, \"\n                \"attachments_json) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) \"\n                \"ON CONFLICT(message_id) DO UPDATE SET decision=excluded.decision, \"\n                \"attachments_json=excluded.attachments_json\",\n                (message_id, subject, sender, received, decision, attachments_json))\n            self.conn.commit()\n\n    def list_emails(self) -> list:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM emails ORDER BY id DESC\").fetchall()\n```\n\nYour existing `statements.db` gets the new table automatically, since the schema uses `IF NOT EXISTS`.\n\n**`.gitignore`**: add a line. Downloaded attachments are real documents and must never be committed:\n\n```text\ndata/\n```\n\n**`.env.example`**: add these lines (the first two already exist):\n\n```text\nGMAIL_ADDRESS=your-test-account@gmail.com\nGMAIL_APP_PASSWORD=\nSTATEMENT_SENDERS=\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `app/email_ingest.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Email ingestion: find statement emails and feed their PDFs to the pipeline.\n\nDesign points:\n  - the mailbox is opened READ-ONLY and fetched with BODY.PEEK: we never change it\n  - emails are classified BEFORE anything reaches the pipeline, so unrelated PDFs\n    are never sent to the LLM\n  - idempotent: emails by Message-ID, PDFs by file hash (in the pipeline)\n  - attachment filenames are sanitised before touching the disk\n\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport imaplib\nimport json\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom datetime import date, timedelta\nfrom email import message_from_bytes, policy\nfrom email.utils import parseaddr, parsedate_to_datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Iterable, Optional, Protocol\n\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nfrom app.pipeline import Pipeline\nfrom app.store import Store\n\nload_dotenv()\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nTHRESHOLD = 2\nBODY_CHARS = 2000\nMAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 25 * 1024 * 1024\nMONTHS = [\"Jan\", \"Feb\", \"Mar\", \"Apr\", \"May\", \"Jun\",\n          \"Jul\", \"Aug\", \"Sep\", \"Oct\", \"Nov\", \"Dec\"]\n\nPOSITIVE = re.compile(\n    r\"\\b(statements?|portfolios?|pms|aif|capital account|valuation|holdings?|nav|\"\n    r\"investor report|account summary)\\b\")\nNEGATIVE = re.compile(\n    r\"\\b(invoice|receipt|ticket|boarding pass|newsletter|brochure|factsheet|fact sheet|\"\n    r\"terms|disclaimer|otp|resume|cv|quotation|payslip)\\b\")\n\n\nclass MailboxError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The mailbox could not be reached or read.\"\"\"\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ classification\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Classification:\n    score: int\n    reasons: tuple\n    threshold: int = THRESHOLD\n\n    @property\n    def accepted(self) -> bool:\n        return self.score >= self.threshold\n\n\ndef _words(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"'abc_pms.pdf' -> 'abc pms pdf', so word boundaries work on file names.\"\"\"\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \" \", (text or \"\").lower()).strip()\n\n\ndef sender_allowed(address: str, allowed: Iterable[str]) -> bool:\n    address = (address or \"\").lower()\n    domain = address.rpartition(\"@\")[2]\n    for entry in allowed:\n        entry = entry.strip().lower().lstrip(\"@\")\n        if entry and (address == entry or domain == entry):\n            return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef classify(subject: str, sender: str, body: str, filename: str,\n             allowed_senders: Iterable[str] = (), threshold: int = THRESHOLD) -> Classification:\n    score, reasons = 0, []\n\n    def add(points: int, why: str):\n        nonlocal score\n        score += points\n        reasons.append(f\"{why} ({points:+d})\")\n\n    if sender_allowed(sender, allowed_senders):\n        add(3, \"sender is on the allow-list\")\n    subj, fname, text = _words(subject), _words(filename), _words(body[:BODY_CHARS])\n    if m := POSITIVE.search(subj):\n        add(2, f\"subject mentions '{m.group(1)}'\")\n    if m := NEGATIVE.search(subj):\n        add(-1, f\"subject mentions '{m.group(1)}'\")\n    if m := POSITIVE.search(text):\n        add(1, f\"body mentions '{m.group(1)}'\")\n    if m := POSITIVE.search(fname):\n        add(2, f\"file name mentions '{m.group(1)}'\")\n    if m := NEGATIVE.search(fname):\n        add(-3, f\"file name mentions '{m.group(1)}'\")\n    return Classification(score, tuple(reasons), threshold)\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Attachment:\n    filename: str\n    data: bytes\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ParsedEmail:\n    message_id: str\n    subject: str\n    sender: str\n    received: Optional[str]\n    body: str\n    attachments: list[Attachment]\n\n\ndef safe_filename(name: str) -> str:\n    base = Path((name or \"\").replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")).name\n    base = re.sub(r\"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+\", \"_\", base).strip(\"._\") or \"attachment\"\n    if not base.lower().endswith(\".pdf\"):\n        base += \".pdf\"\n    return base[-80:]\n\n\ndef parse_email(raw: bytes) -> ParsedEmail:\n    msg = message_from_bytes(raw, policy=policy.default)\n    message_id = str(msg.get(\"message-id\") or \"\").strip() or \\\n        \"raw:\" + hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()\n    try:\n        received = parsedate_to_datetime(str(msg[\"date\"])).isoformat()\n    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n        received = None\n\n    body = \"\"\n    try:\n        part = msg.get_body(preferencelist=(\"plain\", \"html\"))\n        if part is not None:\n            body = part.get_content()\n            if part.get_content_type() == \"text/html\":\n                body = re.sub(r\"<[^>]+>\", \" \", body)\n    except (LookupError, ValueError, KeyError):\n        body = \"\"                      # undecodable body: classification just loses a signal\n\n    attachments = []\n    for part in msg.walk():\n        if part.is_multipart():\n            continue\n        name = part.get_filename() or \"\"\n        if not (part.get_content_type() == \"application/pdf\" or name.lower().endswith(\".pdf\")):\n            continue\n        data = part.get_payload(decode=True) or b\"\"\n        if b\"%PDF-\" not in data[:1024] or len(data) > MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES:\n            continue                   # not a real PDF, or too big\n        attachments.append(Attachment(name or \"attachment.pdf\", data))\n\n    return ParsedEmail(message_id, str(msg.get(\"subject\") or \"\"),\n                       parseaddr(str(msg.get(\"from\") or \"\"))[1].lower(),\n                       received, body, attachments)\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ mailbox access\nclass Mailbox(Protocol):\n    def recent_uids(self, since: date) -> list[str]: ...\n    def message_id(self, uid: str) -> Optional[str]: ...\n    def fetch(self, uid: str) -> bytes: ...\n\n\ndef imap_date(d: date) -> str:\n    return f\"{d.day:02d}-{MONTHS[d.month - 1]}-{d.year}\"      # locale-independent\n\n\nclass ImapMailbox:\n    def __init__(self, host: str, user: str, password: str, folder: str = \"INBOX\"):\n        self.host, self.user, self.password, self.folder = host, user, password, folder\n        self._m = None\n\n    def open(self):\n        try:\n            self._m = imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(self.host)\n            self._m.login(self.user, self.password)\n            status, _ = self._m.select(self.folder, readonly=True)     # never modifies mail\n        except imaplib.IMAP4.error as e:\n            raise MailboxError(\n                \"IMAP login failed. Gmail needs an APP PASSWORD (not your normal password), \"\n                f\"with 2-Step Verification on and IMAP enabled. Server said: {e}\") from e\n        except OSError as e:\n            raise MailboxError(f\"cannot reach {self.host}: {e}\") from e\n        if status != \"OK\":\n            raise MailboxError(f\"cannot open folder {self.folder!r}\")\n        return self\n\n    def __enter__(self):\n        return self.open()\n\n    def __exit__(self, *exc):\n        try:\n            self._m.close()\n            self._m.logout()\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n\n    def recent_uids(self, since: date) -> list[str]:\n        status, data = self._m.uid(\"search\", None, \"SINCE\", imap_date(since))\n        if status != \"OK\":\n            raise MailboxError(\"mailbox search failed\")\n        return [u.decode() for u in (data[0] or b\"\").split()]\n\n    def message_id(self, uid: str) -> Optional[str]:\n        status, data = self._m.uid(\"fetch\", uid, \"(BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS (MESSAGE-ID)])\")\n        if status != \"OK\" or not data or not isinstance(data[0], tuple):\n            return None\n        header = message_from_bytes(data[0][1])\n        return (header.get(\"Message-ID\") or \"\").strip() or None\n\n    def fetch(self, uid: str) -> bytes:\n        status, data = self._m.uid(\"fetch\", uid, \"(BODY.PEEK[])\")\n        if status != \"OK\" or not data or not isinstance(data[0], tuple):\n            raise MailboxError(f\"could not fetch message {uid}\")\n        return data[0][1]\n\n\ndef mailbox_from_env() -> ImapMailbox:\n    user = os.environ.get(\"GMAIL_ADDRESS\")\n    password = (os.environ.get(\"GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD\") or \"\").replace(\" \", \"\")  # Google shows spaces\n    if not user or not password:\n        raise MailboxError(\"GMAIL_ADDRESS and GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD must be set in .env\")\n    return ImapMailbox(os.environ.get(\"IMAP_HOST\", \"imap.gmail.com\"), user, password,\n                       os.environ.get(\"MAILBOX_FOLDER\", \"INBOX\"))\n\n\ndef senders_from_env() -> list[str]:\n    return [s.strip() for s in os.environ.get(\"STATEMENT_SENDERS\", \"\").split(\",\") if s.strip()]\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the ingestor\n@dataclass\nclass IngestSummary:\n    new_emails: int = 0\n    already_known: int = 0\n    processed: int = 0\n    skipped: int = 0\n    no_pdf: int = 0\n    attachments: list = field(default_factory=list)\n    errors: list = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nclass EmailIngestor:\n    def __init__(self, store: Store, pipeline: Pipeline,\n                 attachments_dir=\"data/attachments\", allowed_senders: Iterable[str] = (),\n                 threshold: int = THRESHOLD):\n        self.store = store\n        self.pipeline = pipeline\n        self.dir = Path(attachments_dir)\n        self.allowed = list(allowed_senders)\n        self.threshold = threshold\n\n    def run(self, mailbox: Mailbox, days: int = 30, today: Optional[date] = None,\n            dry_run: bool = False) -> IngestSummary:\n        since = (today or date.today()) - timedelta(days=days)\n        summary = IngestSummary()\n        for uid in mailbox.recent_uids(since):\n            try:\n                self._handle(mailbox, uid, summary, dry_run)\n            except MailboxError:\n                raise\n            except Exception as e:  # one bad message must not stop the run\n                log.exception(\"failed on message %s\", uid)\n                summary.errors.append(f\"message {uid}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}\")\n        return summary\n\n    def _save(self, att: Attachment) -> Path:\n        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        path = self.dir / f\"{hashlib.sha256(att.data).hexdigest()[:12]}_{safe_filename(att.filename)}\"\n        if not path.exists():\n            path.write_bytes(att.data)\n        return path\n\n    def _handle(self, mailbox: Mailbox, uid: str, summary: IngestSummary, dry_run: bool):\n        mid = mailbox.message_id(uid)\n        if mid and self.store.email_seen(mid):\n            summary.already_known += 1\n            return\n        mail = parse_email(mailbox.fetch(uid))\n        if self.store.email_seen(mail.message_id):       # covers emails with no Message-ID header\n            summary.already_known += 1\n            return\n\n        summary.new_emails += 1\n        details = []\n        for att in mail.attachments:\n            cls = classify(mail.subject, mail.sender, mail.body, att.filename,\n                           self.allowed, self.threshold)\n            entry = {\"filename\": att.filename, \"score\": cls.score,\n                     \"reasons\": list(cls.reasons), \"accepted\": cls.accepted}\n            if cls.accepted and not dry_run:\n                result = self.pipeline.process_file(self._save(att),\n                                                    source=f\"email:{mail.message_id}\")\n                entry.update(status=result.status.value, used_llm=result.used_llm,\n                             duplicate=result.duplicate)\n            details.append(entry)\n            summary.attachments.append({**entry, \"subject\": mail.subject})\n\n        if not mail.attachments:\n            decision = \"no_pdf\"\n            summary.no_pdf += 1\n        elif any(d[\"accepted\"] for d in details):\n            decision = \"processed\"\n            summary.processed += 1\n        else:\n            decision = \"skipped\"\n            summary.skipped += 1\n\n        if not dry_run:\n            self.store.record_email(mail.message_id, mail.subject, mail.sender, mail.received,\n                                    decision, json.dumps(details))\n\n\ndef main(argv=None):\n    # python -m app.email_ingest --days 2 [--dry-run]\n    import argparse\n\n    from app.registry import Registry\n\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Ingest statement emails\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--days\", type=int, default=30)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--db\", default=\"statements.db\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--dir\", default=\"data/attachments\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--dry-run\", action=\"store_true\",\n                    help=\"classify only: no files saved, nothing processed or recorded\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--review-new\", action=\"store_true\")\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n\n    store, registry = Store(args.db), Registry(args.db)\n    pipeline = Pipeline(store, registry, review_new_formats=args.review_new)\n    ingestor = EmailIngestor(store, pipeline, args.dir, senders_from_env())\n    try:\n        with mailbox_from_env() as mailbox:\n            summary = ingestor.run(mailbox, args.days, dry_run=args.dry_run)\n    except MailboxError as e:\n        print(f\"mailbox error: {e}\")\n        raise SystemExit(1)\n\n    for a in summary.attachments:\n        verdict = \"ACCEPT\" if a[\"accepted\"] else \"skip  \"\n        outcome = (f\"-> {a['status']}, llm={'yes' if a['used_llm'] else 'no'}\"\n                   f\"{', duplicate' if a.get('duplicate') else ''}\") if \"status\" in a else \"\"\n        print(f\"{verdict} score={a['score']:+d} {a['filename']:28} | {a['subject'][:40]} {outcome}\")\n        if not a[\"accepted\"] or args.dry_run:\n            for why in a[\"reasons\"]:\n                print(f\"         {why}\")\n    print(f\"\\nnew emails: {summary.new_emails} (already known: {summary.already_known}) | \"\n          f\"processed {summary.processed}, skipped {summary.skipped}, no PDF {summary.no_pdf}\")\n    for err in summary.errors:\n        print(\"error:\", err)\n    if not args.dry_run:\n        print(\"documents:\", store.counts())\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create `samples/send_test_email.py`\n\nThis puts realistic mail into your test inbox: a statement email with two PDFs samples.generate` and `python -m samples.next_month` first.\n\"\"\"\nimport io\nimport os\nimport smtplib\nimport sys\nfrom email.message import EmailMessage\nfrom email.utils import make_msgid\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\nfrom reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n\nPDFS = Path(__file__).parent / \"pdfs\"\n\n\ndef decoy_pdf() -> bytes:\n    buf = io.BytesIO()\n    c = msg[\"Message-ID\"] = make_msgid(domain=\"statement-parser.test\")\n    msg.set_content(body)\n    for name, data in attachments:\n        msg.add_attachment(data, maintype=\"application\",  with smtplib.SMTP_SSL(\"smtp.gmail.com\", 465) as smtp:\n        smtp.login(user, password)\n        for m in messages:\n            smtp.send_message(m)\n    print(f\"sent {len(messages)} email(s) to {user}\")\n```\n\n## Step 4: Create `tests/test_email_ingest.py`\n\nThese tests use a fake mailbox, so no Gmail is needed.\n\n```python\nimport imaplib\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom email import "# Part 8 is done: 181 tests pass\n\nThe key test is green: with a fake LLM holding exactly one reply, the second ABC statement parsed with **zero** LLM calls. Trade-off: the credential is broad, so use a dedicated test account |\n| Mailbox access | **Read-only**: `select(readonly=True)` plus `BODY.PEEK` | The system can never mark, move or delete mail |\n| Classifying | Keyword scoring **before** anything reaches the pipeline | A random PDF (an invoice, a bank letter) must never be sent to an external LLM. That's a privacy and cost issue |\n| Several PDFs per email | Each is scored and processed separately | This covers the brief's \"single email with several statements\" stretch goal |\n| Idempotency | By `Message-ID` for emails, and by file hash (Part 8) for PDFs | Re-running ingestion, or a forwarded copy, creates no duplicates |\n| Attachment names | Sanitised | A name like `../../x.pdf` must not write outside our folder |\n| Real PDFs only | Must start with `%PDF-` | A `.pdf` name proves nothing |\n\n**The scoring rules** (an attachment is processed if its total is at least 2):\n\n| Signal | Score |\n|---|---|\n| Sender is on `STATEMENT_SENDERS` (optional allow-list) | +3 |\n| Subject mentions *statement, portfolio, PMS, AIF, capital account, valuation, holdings, NAV...* | +2 |\n| Attachment filename mentions the same words | +2 |\n| Body mentions them | +1 |\n| Subject mentions *invoice, receipt, newsletter...* | \u22121 |\n| Filename mentions *brochure, terms, invoice, factsheet...* | \u22123 |\n\nText is split into words first (`abc_pms.pdf` becomes `abc pms pdf`), because `_` isn't a word boundary in regexes. Every email gets a decision recorded (`processed`, `skipped` or `no_pdf`) with the score and reasons, so a wrongly skipped statement is visible on the review page and never lost silently.\n\n## Step 1: Small edits\n\n**`app/store.py`**: add this directly under the `SCHEMA = \"\"\"...\"\"\"` block:\n\n```python\nSCHEMA += \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS emails (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    message_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    subject TEXT, sender TEXT, received TEXT,\n    decision TEXT NOT NULL,\n    attachments_json TEXT,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n\"\"\"\n```\n\nThen add these methods at the end of the `Store` class:\n\n```python\n    def email_seen(self, message_id: str) -> bool:\n        with self._lock:\n            row = self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT 1 FROM emails WHERE message_id = ?\", (message_id,)).fetchone()\n        return row is not None\n\n    def record_email(self, message_id, subject, sender, received, decision, attachments_json):\n        with self._lock:\n            self.conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO emails (message_id, subject, sender, received, decision, \"\n                \"attachments_json) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) \"\n                \"ON CONFLICT(message_id) DO UPDATE SET decision=excluded.decision, \"\n                \"attachments_json=excluded.attachments_json\",\n                (message_id, subject, sender, received, decision, attachments_json))\n            self.conn.commit()\n\n    def list_emails(self) -> list:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM emails ORDER BY id DESC\").fetchall()\n```\n\nYour existing `statements.db` gets the new table automatically, since the schema uses `IF NOT EXISTS`.\n\n**`.gitignore`**: add a line. statement emails and feed their PDFs to the pipeline.\n\nDesign points:\n  - the mailbox is opened READ-ONLY and fetched with BODY.PEEK: we never change it\n  - emails are classified BEFORE anything verdict = \"ACCEPT\" if a[\"accepted\"] else \"skip  \"\n        outcome = (f\"-> {a['status']}, llm={'yes' if a['used_llm'] else 'no'}\"\n                   f\"{', duplicate' if a.get('duplicate') else ''}\") if \"status\" in a else \"\"\n        print(f\"{verdict} score={a['score']:+d} {a['filename']:28} | {a['subject'][:40]} {outcome}\")\n        if not a[\"accepted\"] or args.dry_run:\n            for why in a[\"reasons\"]:\n                print(f\"         {why}\")\n    print(f\"\\nnew emails: {summary.new_emails} (already known: {summary.already_known}) | \"\n          f\"processed {summary.processed}, skipped {summary.skipped}, no PDF {summary.no_pdf}\")\n    for err in summary.errors:\n        print(\"error:\", err)\n    if not args.dry_run:\n        print(\"documents:\", store.counts())\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n## Step 3: Create `samples/send_test_email.py`\n\nThis puts realistic mail into your test inbox: a statement email with two PDFs samples.generate` and `python -m samples.next_month` first.\n\"\"\"\nimport io\nimport os\nimport smtplib\nimport sys\nfrom email.message import EmailMessage\nfrom email.utils import make_msgid\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\nfrom reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n\nPDFS = Path(__file__).parent / \"pdfs\"\n\n\ndef decoy_pdf() -> bytes:\n    buf = io.BytesIO()\n    c = canvas.Canvas(buf)\n    c.drawString(72, 750, \"Spring savings offers - product brochure\")\n    c.drawString(72, 730, \"Nothing financial to see here.\")\n    c.save()\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef message(address, subject, body, attachments=()):\n    msg = EmailMessage()\n    msg[\"From\"], msg[\"To\"], msg[\"Subject\"] = address, address, subject\n    msg[\"Message-ID\"] = make_msgid(domain=\"statement-parser.test\")\n    msg.set_content(body)\n    for name, data in attachments:\n        msg.add_attachment(data, maintype=\"application\", investor, your May statement is attached.\",\n                        [(\"abc_pms_may.pdf\", (PDFS / \"abc_pms_may.pdf\").read_bytes())])]\n    return [\n        message(address, \"Your April 2026 PMS message(address, \"Weekly newsletter\",\n                \"Market ideas for your portfolio this week.\",\n                [(\"brochure.pdf\", decoy_pdf())]),\n        message(address, \"Lunch on Friday?\", \"Are you free at 1pm?\"),\n    ]\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    load_dotenv()\n    user = os.environ.get(\"GMAIL_ADDRESS\")\n    password = (os.environ.get(\"GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD\")  with smtplib.SMTP_SSL(\"smtp.gmail.com\", 465) as smtp:\n        smtp.login(user, password)\n        for m in messages:\n            smtp.send_message(m)\n    print(f\"sent {len(messages)} email(s) On the account: turn on **2-Step Verification**, then create an **App password** (Google Account \u2192 Security \u2192 App passwords; the page is `myaccount.google.com/apppasswords`, and the menu path may differ). Google shows a 16-character code. Workspace and some protected accounts can't create these.\n3. Put it in your real `.env`:\n   ```text\n   GMAIL_ADDRESS=your-test-account@gmail.com\n   GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD=abcd efgh ijkl mnop\n   STATEMENT_SENDERS=\n   ```\n   Spaces are fine, since the code strips them. Never commit this file or paste it in a chat.\n4. IMAP is normally on by default for Gmail now. If login still fails, check the IMAP setting under Gmail \u2192 Settings \u2192 Forwarding and POP/IMAP.\n\n## Step 7: The live demo sequence\n\n```bash\nrm -f statements.db && rm -rf data\npython -m samples.generate\npython -m samples.next_month\npython -m samples.send_test_email\npython -m app.email_ingest --dry-run --days 2\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2\npython -m samples.send_test_email --may\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2\n```\n\nWhat you should see:\n\n| Step | Expected |\n|---|---|\n| Dry run | Two PDFs `ACCEPT`ed from the statement email, the brochure `skip`ped, with scores and reasons shown |\n| First real run | `abc_pms.pdf` and `xyz_wealth.pdf` learned (llm=yes) and `parsed_ok`. The brochure is never processed. Gemini may give a 503, so re-run if needed |\n| May email | `abc_pms_may.pdf` parsed with **llm=no**, which is the core constraint proven end to end through email |\n\nDelivery to your own inbox can take a few seconds, so re-run if the first dry run shows nothing.\n\nRetrying failures: the email run marks each email as seen, so a statement that ended in `learning_failed` or `password_required` isn't retried by the next email run. To retry, run the pipeline over the saved files, which retries only files that haven't finished:\n\n```bash\npython -m app.pipeline data/attachments\n```\n\n## Step 8: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 9: read-only IMAP ingestion, statement-email classifier, test sender\"\ngit push\n```\n\nCheck that `git status` shows neither `.env` nor `data/`.\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why classify before the pipeline?** A non-statement PDF must never be sent to an external LLM, for privacy and cost. The scoring explains itself, and every skipped email is recorded.\n2. **Why read-only IMAP?** The system can't alter the user's mailbox even with a bug.\n3. **Why two levels of dedup?** Message-ID stops re-fetching emails. File hash stops re-processing the same PDF from a forward or a different email.\n4. **Why IMAP and an app password instead of the Gmail API?** It's far simpler to set up and good enough for a test account. The cost is a broad credential and no per-message scopes. A production system would use OAuth with a read-only scope.\n5. **Why sanitise filenames?** Attachments are attacker-controlled input.\n\n## Limitations to add\n\n- Keyword scoring can misclassify. A personal **bank statement** contains \"statement\" and could pass classification, and the LLM might even learn it as an AIF. A stricter allow-list (`STATEMENT_SENDERS`) is the real defence.\n- Statement PDFs with no keyword in the subject, file name or body, from an unlisted sender, are skipped. They're recorded, but only a human notices.\n- Only PDF attachments are handled. Excel/CSV, password-in-body parsing, and links to download statements aren't.\n- A single PDF containing several clients' statements isn't split.\n- Only the first 2,000 characters of the body are scanned, and HTML is stripped crudely.\n- `SINCE` has date granularity, so each run re-checks headers for the whole window (cheap, since known Message-IDs are skipped).\n- Retrying a failed learning needs a manual `python -m app.pipeline data/attachments`.\n\nPaste the test results, and the live output if Gmail is working. Commit it:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 9: read-only IMAP ingestion, statement-email classifier, test sender\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## The failure is in the test-email sender, not the ingestion\n\nThe traceback is from `samples/send_test_email.py`, which logs in to Gmail's **SMTP** (sending) server. The server hung up during login, so no email was sent. The ingestion reads through **IMAP**, which is a separate path that this error doesn't touch. I can't tell from here which of these caused it:\n\n- **A wrong or malformed app password.** A bad password normally gives a clear \"535 authentication failed\" error, so a dropped connection is less typical, but it's the first thing to rule out.\n- **A Google Workspace or college account.** App passwords are often blocked on those, and SMTP may be restricted too.\n- **A network issue**, such as a VPN, proxy or campus Wi-Fi blocking port 465.\n\n## Step 1: Diagnose with IMAP (the path the ingestion actually uses)\n\n```bash\npython -c \"\nimport os, imaplib\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\nload_dotenv()\nu = os.environ.get('GMAIL_ADDRESS', '')\np = os.environ.get('GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD', '').replace(' ', '')\nprint('address:', repr(u), '| password length:', len(p))\nm = imaplib.IMAP4_SSL('imap.gmail.com')\nprint(m.login(u, p))\n\"\n```\n\nThis prints the password's length, not the password. Read the result:\n\n| Result | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| Length is **not 16** | The `.env` value is wrong (truncated, extra characters, or your normal password instead of an app password). Re-copy it from Google |\n| `('OK', ...)` | IMAP works. Your credentials are fine and only SMTP is the problem. Use Step 3 |\n| `AUTHENTICATIONFAILED` | The app password is invalid. Create a new one |\n| Cannot reach the host, or the connection drops | Network problem. Try a phone hotspot or turn off any VPN |\n\n## Step 2: Try the other SMTP port\n\nPort 587 with STARTTLS sometimes works when 465 doesn't. In `samples/send_test_email.py`, replace the final block, from `with smtplib.SMTP_SSL(...)` to the print, with:\n\n```python\n    try:\n        smtp = smtplib.SMTP_SSL(\"smtp.gmail.com\", 465, timeout=30)\n    except OSError:\n        smtp = smtplib.SMTP(\"smtp.gmail.com\", 587, timeout=30)\n        smtp.starttls()\n    with smtp:\n        smtp.login(user, password)\n        for m in messages:\n            smtp.send_message(m)\n    print(f\"sent {len(messages)} email(s) to {user}\")\n```\n\n## Step 3: Skip SMTP entirely\n\nYou don't need my sender script. The ingestor only reads the inbox, so any email that lands there works. This is just as good for a demo:\n\n1. From your **normal Gmail**, or any email app, compose a new email **to your test account**.\n2. Subject: `Your April 2026 PMS statements`. Attach `samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf` and `samples/pdfs/xyz_wealth.pdf`.\n3. Send a second email with subject `Weekly newsletter` and a random PDF you have, to show a skip.\n4. Later, send `samples/pdfs/abc_pms_may.pdf` with subject `Your May 2026 PMS statement` to show the zero-LLM case.\n\nThen run, with the test account's credentials in `.env`:\n\n```bash\npython -m app.email_ingest --dry-run --days 2\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2\n```\n\nThe dry run shows each attachment's score and reasons without processing anything. Delivery takes a few seconds, so re-run if the inbox looks empty.\n\n**If the IMAP check in Step 1 also fails**, the problem is the account or app password, and ingestion can't connect either. In that case:\n\n- Check that 2-Step Verification is on and that you're using the **app password** (16 characters), not the account password.\n- If it's a college or Workspace address, create a personal `@gmail.com` test account instead. That is the usual fix.\n\nPaste the Step 1 output and tell me which route you take. If you'd rather not fight Gmail now, we can move on to **Part 10: the review interface**, since the pipeline and ingestion code are already verified by tests. A silent hang-up points more to one of these:\n\n| Likely cause | How to check |\n|---|---|\n| Wrong, revoked or mistyped app password, or 2-Step Verification is off | Steps 1 and 3 below |\n| Your network blocks or drops port 465 (some Wi-Fi, college or VPN networks do this) | Step 2, then the port 587 fallback |\n| Gmail briefly rejecting the login, for example a new or flagged account | Wait a few minutes, then retry |\n\n## Step 1: Check what the script is actually reading\n\nThis prints only lengths, not the secret:\n\n```bash\npython -c \"\nimport os\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\nload_dotenv()\nu = os.environ.get('GMAIL_ADDRESS')\np = (os.environ.get('GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD') or '').replace(' ', '')\nprint('address:', u)\nprint('password length:', len(p), '| plain ASCII:', p.isascii())\n\"\n```\n\nYou should see `password length: 16` and `plain ASCII: True`. APP PASSWORD` | The password or account setup is wrong, so go to Step 3 |\n| `cannot reach imap.gmail.com` | Your network is blocking Gmail. Try a phone hotspot |\n\n## Step 3: If the login is rejected, regenerate the app password\n\n1. The account needs **2-Step Verification** turned on. App passwords aren't available without it.\n2. Use the dedicated test account. It tries port 465 first, falls back to 587, and gives a clear message on a bad password:\n\n```python\ndef connect(user, password):\n    try:\n        smtp = smtplib.SMTP_SSL(\"smtp.gmail.com\", 465, timeout=30)\n        smtp.login(user, password)\n        return smtp\n    except (smtplib.SMTPServerDisconnected, OSError):\n        print(\"port 465 failed, trying 587 (STARTTLS)...\")\n    smtp = smtplib.SMTP(\"smtp.gmail.com\", 587, timeout=30)\n    smtp.starttls()\n    smtp.login(user, password)\n    return smtp\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    load_dotenv()\n    user = os.environ.get(\"GMAIL_ADDRESS\")\n    password = (os.environ.get(\"GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD\") or \"\").replace(\" \", \"\")\n    if not user or not password:\n        sys.exit(\"Set GMAIL_ADDRESS and GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD in .env first\")\n    messages = build(user, may=\"--may\" in sys.argv)\n    try:\n        with connect(user, password) as smtp:\n            for m in messages:\n                smtp.send_message(m)\n    except smtplib.SMTPAuthenticationError:\n        sys.exit(\"Gmail rejected the login. Check that GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD is a fresh \"\n                 \"app password and 2-Step Verification is on.\")\n    except (smtplib.SMTPException, OSError) as e:\n        sys.exit(f\"could not send: {type(e).__name__}: {e}\")\n    print(f\"sent {len(messages)} email(s) to {user}\")\n```\n\nThen retry:\n\n```bash\npython -m samples.send_test_email\n```\n\n## Fallback: skip SMTP entirely\n\nYou don't need the script to demo email ingestion. Open Gmail in your browser (the test account, or any other account sending to it) and compose the same emails by hand:\n\n1. **Subject** `Your April 2026 PMS statements`, attach `samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf` and `samples/pdfs/xyz_wealth.pdf`.\n2. **Subject** `Weekly newsletter`, with the body \"Market ideas for your portfolio\", and attach any non-statement PDF (name it `brochure.pdf`).\n3. **Subject** `Lunch on Friday?`, with no attachment.\n\nThat produces the same three situations (statement, decoy, no attachment), and it's just as valid a demo. Make sure the app password really exists.** All of these must be true:\n\n- The account has **2-Step Verification on**. Without it, Google doesn't offer app passwords.\n- You created the app password **while signed in to that same account**. It's easy to create one in your main account and paste it into the config for the test account.\n- It hasn't been deleted, and you pasted the code shown at creation. Google shows it **only once**, so if you're unsure, delete it and generate a new one.\n- The account is a normal personal `@gmail.com`. College or Workspace accounts often have app passwords disabled by an admin.\n\n**4. A stale shell variable can override `.env`.** `load_dotenv` doesn't replace variables already set in your terminal. If you ever ran `export GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD=...`, that old value wins. ingestion works live\n\nYour output proves the whole chain through a real mailbox:\n\n| Output | What it proves |\n|---|---|\n| Dry run: `abc_pms.pdf` and `xyz_wealth.pdf` get `ACCEPT`, `brochure.pdf` gets `skip` (score -3) | The classifier explains every decision, and the decoy never reaches the pipeline or the LLM |\n| Real run: both statements `parsed_ok`, `llm=yes` | The locked XYZ PDF was opened via the password list, and two new formats were learned |\n| May email: `parsed_ok`, **`llm=no`** | The core constraint, end to end: mailbox, classifier, pipeline, stored config, no LLM |\n| Final run: `already known: 36` | Idempotency across runs |\n\nYour inbox had 33 other emails. They were recorded as `no_pdf`, which means `statements.db` now holds their subjects and senders. The file is gitignored (`*.db`), so it won't be committed, but keep that in mind for your limitations note (\"the system stores metadata of every email it sees\"). The review page will hide those by default.\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 9: read-only IMAP ingestion, statement-email classifier, test sender\"\ngit push\n```\n\nCheck `git status` first, so `.env` and `data/` don't appear.\n\n---\n\n# Part 10: The review interface\n\nThe brief asks for \"a simple way to see processed statements, their status, and which ones need human attention.\" We'll build a small web page backed by a read-only API.\n\n## Design decisions\n\n| Decision | Choice | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| Read-only | No approve/edit buttons | Fewer ways to corrupt data and less to explain. Add an \"approve\" action as the answer to a changed-requirement question in the interview |\n| Local only | Binds to `127.0.0.1`, no login | It shows financial data. Adding authentication is out of scope, so we don't expose it, and we say so |\n| Untrusted text | The page builds elements with `createElement` and text nodes only, never HTML strings. A Content-Security-Policy blocks everything but our own files | Email subjects, filenames and strategy names come from outside. A subject like `<script>...` must display as text and never run (stored XSS) |\n| No frameworks or CDNs | Plain HTML, CSS and JS served from our own folder | A strict CSP can't allow external scripts, and there's less to explain |\n| \"Needs attention\" | Every status except `parsed_ok` | `needs_review`, `failed`, `learning_failed` and `password_required` are exactly the cases where nothing is silently lost |\n| Money | The API returns exact decimal strings. The browser only formats them for display, with no arithmetic | The browser's number type is a float |\n\n## Step 1: Small edits\n\n**`requirements.txt`**: add this line (FastAPI's test client needs it), then install:\n\n```text\nhttpx>=0.27\n```\n\n```bash\npip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\n**`app/store.py`**: add this method at the end of the `Store` class:\n\n```python\n    def get_email(self, message_id: str) -> Optional[sqlite3.Row]:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT * FROM emails WHERE message_id = ?\", (message_id,)).fetchone()\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `app/api.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Read-only review API plus the review web page.\n\nThere are no write endpoints: this interface cannot change any data.\nThere is no authentication, so it binds to localhost by default. Do not expose it.\n\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport threading\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Query\nfrom fastapi.responses import FileResponse\nfrom fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles\n\nfrom app.pipeline import DocStatus\nfrom app.registry import Registry\nfrom app.store import Store\n\nWEB = Path(__file__).parent / \"web\"\nATTENTION = {s.value for s in DocStatus} - {DocStatus.PARSED_OK.value}\nCSP = (\"default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; \"\n       \"base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'\")\n\n\ndef _loads(text, default):\n    if not text:\n        return default\n    try:\n        return json.loads(text)\n    except json.JSONDecodeError:\n        return default\n\n\ndef _summary(row) -> dict:\n    issues = _loads(row[\"issues_json\"], [])\n    errors = [i for i in issues if i[\"severity\"] == \"error\"]\n    statement = _loads(row[\"statement_json\"], None) or {}\n    return {\n        \"id\": row[\"id\"],\n        \"filename\": row[\"filename\"],\n        \"status\": row[\"status\"],\n        \"needs_attention\": row[\"status\"] in ATTENTION,\n        \"provider\": row[\"provider\"],\n        \"strategy_name\": row[\"strategy_name\"],\n        \"client_id\": row[\"client_id\"],\n        \"statement_type\": row[\"statement_type\"],\n        \"period_start\": row[\"period_start\"],\n        \"period_end\": row[\"period_end\"],\n        \"closing_value\": (statement.get(\"summary\") or {}).get(\"closing_value\"),\n        \"currency\": statement.get(\"currency\"),\n        \"format_name\": row[\"format_name\"],\n        \"match_kind\": row[\"match_kind\"],\n        \"match_score\": row[\"match_score\"],\n        \"used_llm\": bool(row[\"used_llm\"]),\n        \"errors\": len(errors),\n        \"warnings\": len(issues) - len(errors),\n        \"headline\": row[\"error\"] or (errors[0][\"message\"] if errors else None),\n        \"updated_at\": row[\"updated_at\"],\n    }\n\n\ndef create_app(store: Store, registry: Registry) -> FastAPI:\n    # No interactive docs page: it needs external scripts, which our CSP forbids.\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"Statement review\", docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)\n    registry_lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def formats():\n        with registry_lock:\n            return registry.all_formats()\n\n    @app.middleware(\"http\")\n    async def security_headers(request, call_next):\n        response = await call_next(request)\n        response.headers[\"Content-Security-Policy\"] = CSP\n        response.headers[\"X-Content-Type-Options\"] = \"nosniff\"\n        response.headers[\"Cache-Control\"] = \"no-store\"\n        return response\n\n    @app.get(\"/\", include_in_schema=False)\n    def index():\n        return FileResponse(WEB / \"index.html\")\n\n    app.mount(\"/static\", StaticFiles(directory=WEB), name=\"static\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/summary\")\n    def summary():\n        counts = store.counts()\n        emails: dict = {}\n        for r in store.list_emails():\n            emails[r[\"decision\"]] = emails.get(r[\"decision\"], 0) + 1\n        return {\n            \"total\": sum(counts.values()),\n            \"documents\": counts,\n            \"needs_attention\": sum(n for s, n in counts.items() if s in ATTENTION),\n            \"llm_documents\": sum(1 for r in store.list() if r[\"used_llm\"]),\n            \"emails\": emails,\n            \"formats\": len(formats()),\n        }\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/documents\")\n    def documents(status: Optional[str] = Query(None), attention: bool = Query(False)):\n        if status is not None and status not in {s.value for s in DocStatus}:\n            raise HTTPException(422, f\"unknown status {status!r}\")\n        docs = [_summary(r) for r in store.list(status)]\n        return [d for d in docs if d[\"needs_attention\"]] if attention else docs\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/documents/{doc_id}\")\n    def document(doc_id: int):\n        row = store.get(doc_id)\n        if row is None:\n            raise HTTPException(404, \"no such document\")\n        detail = _summary(row)\n        issues = _loads(row[\"issues_json\"], [])\n        detail.update(\n            source=row[\"source\"],\n            error=row[\"error\"],\n            issues=sorted(issues, key=lambda i: i[\"severity\"] != \"error\"),   # errors first\n            validation=_loads(row[\"validation_json\"], None),\n            statement=_loads(row[\"statement_json\"], None),\n            email=None,\n        )\n        source = row[\"source\"] or \"\"\n        if source.startswith(\"email:\"):\n            mail = store.get_email(source[len(\"email:\"):])\n            if mail is not None:\n                detail[\"email\"] = {\"subject\": mail[\"subject\"], \"sender\": mail[\"sender\"],\n                                   \"received\": mail[\"received\"]}\n        return detail\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/emails\")\n    def emails(include_no_pdf: bool = Query(False)):\n        out = []\n        for r in store.list_emails():\n            if r[\"decision\"] == \"no_pdf\" and not include_no_pdf:\n                continue\n            out.append({\"id\": r[\"id\"], \"subject\": r[\"subject\"], \"sender\": r[\"sender\"],\n                        \"received\": r[\"received\"], \"decision\": r[\"decision\"],\n                        \"attachments\": _loads(r[\"attachments_json\"], [])})\n        return out\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/formats\")\n    def list_formats():\n        return [{\"id\": f[\"id\"], \"name\": f[\"name\"], \"version\": f[\"version\"],\n                 \"created_at\": f[\"created_at\"],\n                 \"label_count\": len(_loads(f[\"labels_json\"], [])),\n                 \"has_config\": f[\"config_json\"] is not None} for f in formats()]\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/formats/{format_id}\")\n    def format_detail(format_id: int):\n        for f in formats():\n            if f[\"id\"] == format_id:\n                return {\"id\": f[\"id\"], \"name\": f[\"name\"], \"version\": f[\"version\"],\n                        \"created_at\": f[\"created_at\"],\n                        \"config\": _loads(f[\"config_json\"], None),\n                        \"labels\": _loads(f[\"labels_json\"], [])}\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"no such format\")\n\n    return app\n\n\ndef main(argv=None):\n    # python -m app.api [--db statements.db] [--port 8000]\n    import argparse\n\n    import uvicorn\n\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Statement review page\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--db\", default=\"statements.db\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--host\", default=\"127.0.0.1\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.host not in (\"127.0.0.1\", \"localhost\", \"::1\"):\n        print(\"WARNING: this page has no login and shows financial data. \"\n              \"Do not expose it beyond your own machine.\")\n    print(f\"Review page: http://{args.host}:{args.port}\")\n    uvicorn.run(create_app(Store(args.db), Registry(args.db)), host=args.host, port=args.port)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n## Step 3: The web page (three files in a new `app/web/` folder)\n\n```bash\nmkdir app/web\n```\n\n**`app/web/index.html`**\n\n```html\n<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n  <meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n  <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n  <title>Statement review</title>\n  <link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"/static/style.css\">\n</head>\n<body>\n  <header>\n    <h1>Statement review</h1>\n    <button id=\"refresh\">Refresh</button>\n  </header>\n  <section id=\"cards\"></section>\n  <nav id=\"tabs\">\n    <button data-tab=\"documents\">Documents</button>\n    <button data-tab=\"emails\">Emails</button>\n    <button data-tab=\"formats\">Learned formats</button>\n  </nav>\n  <main>\n    <div id=\"filters\"></div>\n    <div id=\"list\"></div>\n    <div id=\"detail\"></div>\n  </main>\n  <script src=\"/static/app.js\"></script>\n</body>\n</html>\n```\n\n**`app/web/style.css`**\n\n```css\n:root { --ok: #1b7f3b; --warn: #b26a00; --bad: #b3261e; --info: #5b3fa8; --line: #d9dde3; }\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nbody { font: 14px/1.45 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #f6f7f9; color: #1d2430; }\nheader { display: flex; justify-content: \"yes\" : \"no\"],\n      [\"Source\", d.email ? 'email \"' + d.email.subject + '\" from ' + d.email.sender : d.source],\n      [\"Updated\", d.updated_at],\n    ]),\n    d.error ? el(\"p\", { class: \"error\" }, d.error) : null,\n  ];\n  if (d.issues.length) {\n    parts.push(el(\"h3\", {}, \"Issues\"), el(\"ul\", { class: \"issues\" }, d.issues.map((i) =>\n      el(\"li\", { class: i.severity === \"error\" ? el(\"ul\", { class: \"sub\" }, skipped.map(([c, why]) => el(\"li\", {}, c + \": \" + why))) : null);\n  }\n  if (st) {\n    const summary = Object.entries(st.summary).filter(([, v]) => v !== null);\n    parts.push(el(\"h3\", {}, \"Summary\"), kv(summary.map(([k, v]) => [k.replaceAll(\"_\", \" \"), num(v)])));\n    if (st.holdings.length) {\n      parts.push(el(\"h3\", {}, \"Holdings (\" + st.holdings.length + \")\"),\n        table([\"Security\", \"ISIN\", \"Quantity\", \"Cost\", \"Price\", \"Value\", \"Weight %\"],\n          st.holdings.map((h) => ({ cells: [h.security_name, txt(h.isin), num(h.quantity),\n            num(h.cost), num(h.market_price), num(h.market_value), txt(h.weight_pct)] }))));\n    }\n    if (st.transactions.length) {\n      parts.push(el(\"h3\", {}, \"Transactions (\" + st.transactions.length + \")\"),\n        table([\"Date\", \"Type\", \"Security\", \"Quantity\", \"Amount\"],\n          st.transactions.map((t) => ({ cells: [t.date, t.type, txt(t.security_name),\n            num(t.quantity), num(t.amount)] }))));\n    }\n  }\n  return el(\"div\", { class: \"panel\" }, parts);\n}\n\nasync function renderDocuments(filters, list, detail) {\n  const query = { attention: \"?attention=true\", ok: \"?status=parsed_ok\", all: \"\" }[state.filter];\n  const docs = await api(\"/api/documents\" + query);\n  filters.replaceChildren(filterBar([[\"attention\", \"Needs attention\"], [\"all\", \"All\"], [\"ok\", \"OK only\"]]));\n  list.replaceChildren(docs.length\n    ? table([\"Status\", \"File\", \"Provider\", \"Client\", \"Period\", \"Closing value\", \"Format\", \"Notes\"],\n      docs.map((d) => ({\n        selected: d.id === state.selected,\n        onclick: () => { state.selected = d.id; render(); },\n        cells: [\n          badge(d.status), d.filename,\n          el(\"div\", {}, txt(d.provider), el(\"div\", { class: \"sub\" }, txt(d.strategy_name))),\n          txt(d.client_id),\n          d.period_start ? \"yes\" : \"no\"))),\n          el(\"div\", {}, d.headline ? trunc(d.headline, 90) : null,\n            el(\"div\", { class: \"sub\" }, d.errors + \" error(s), \" + d.warnings + \" warning(s)\")),\n        ],\n      })))\n    : el(\"p\", { class: \"hint\" }, \"Nothing to show here.\"));\n  detail.replaceChildren(state.selected\n    ? The **Emails** tab shows only statement emails. Tick the checkbox to see your other 30+ inbox emails.\n5. The **Learned formats** tab shows the stored config JSON the LLM wrote, which is a strong thing to show in the interview.\n\nIf anything looks broken, open the browser developer console (right-click \u2192 Inspect \u2192 Console) and paste the error. Also tell me if you see an empty page.\n\n## Step 7: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 10: read-only review API and web page\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why is there no approve button?** It keeps the interface unable to change data. \"Add an approve action\" is a good answer to a changed-requirement question: a `reviewed` status, a `POST` endpoint, and (necessarily) authentication first.\n2. **What attack does `textContent` and the CSP stop?** An email subject like `<script>...` is stored in the database and later shown on the page. If the page inserted it as HTML, the script would run. `test_front_end_never_turns_untrusted_text_into_html` and the hostile-subject fixture cover this.\n3. **Why does the API hand over decimal strings?** JSON numbers become floats in JavaScript, which is the same reason we used `Decimal` everywhere else.\n4. **Why does \"needs attention\" include `failed` and `password_required`?** They're exactly the cases where a statement exists but its data isn't in the system. The page makes the gap visible.\n5. **Why localhost and no login?** It displays financial data. We state the limit instead of faking security.\n\n## Limitations to add\n\n- No authentication or authorisation. Anyone who can reach the port sees everything.\n- No actions: a flagged statement stays flagged forever, because there's no approve, reject or retry button.\n- No pagination or search. The list loads everything, which is fine for tens of documents and not for thousands.\n- No live updates (use Refresh).\n- No consolidated view across providers for one client (a stretch goal in the brief).\n- The browser formats numbers as floats for display. Values over about 15 significant digits would show rounded.\n\n## What's next: Part 11\n\nAbout six days remain before the 17 October deadline. Part 11 is what the interviewers read first:\n\n1. **Drift hardening and a mismatch check**: a statement-level check that the learned config isn't silently applying to a different provider.\n2. **README** with setup, configuration and how to run each part.\n3. **Design note** (assumptions, the four hard questions answered, LLM choice and failure behaviour).\n4. **Known limitations note**, as specific as we've been collecting them.\n5. **AI usage log** (we have a good list of where the AI misled me).\n6. **Sample outputs** for 3+ formats, and the **demo video** script.\n\nPaste the test results, tell me how the page looks, and we'll start with whichever of those you'd like to do first. The review page will hide those by default.\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 9: read-only IMAP ingestion, statement-email classifier, test sender\"\ngit push\n```\n\nCheck `git status` first, so `.env` and `data/` don't appear.\n\n---\n\n# Part 10: The review interface\n\nThe brief asks for \"a simple way to see processed statements, their status, and which ones need human attention.\" We'll build a small web page backed by a read-only API.\n\n## Design decisions\n\n| Decision | Choice | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| Read-only | No approve/edit buttons | Fewer ways to corrupt data and less to explain. Add an \"approve\" action as the answer to a changed-requirement question in the interview |\n| Local only | Binds to `127.0.0.1`, no login | It shows financial data. Adding authentication is out of scope, so we don't expose it, and we say so |\n| Untrusted text | The page builds elements with `createElement` and text nodes only, never HTML strings. A Content-Security-Policy blocks everything but our own files | Email subjects, filenames and strategy names come from outside. A subject like `<script>...` must display as text and never run (stored XSS) |\n| No frameworks or CDNs | Plain HTML, CSS and JS served from our own folder | A strict CSP can't allow external scripts, and there's less to explain |\n| \"Needs attention\" | Every status except `parsed_ok` | `needs_review`, `failed`, `learning_failed` and `password_required` are exactly the cases where nothing is silently lost |\n| Money | The API returns exact decimal strings. The browser only formats them for display, with no arithmetic | The browser's number type is a float |\n\n## Step 1: Small edits\n\n**`requirements.txt`**: add this line (FastAPI's test client needs it), then install:\n\n```text\nhttpx>=0.27\n```\n\n```bash\npip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\n**`app/store.py`**: add this method at the end of the `Store` class:\n\n```python\n    def get_email(self, message_id: str) -> Optional[sqlite3.Row]:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT * FROM emails WHERE message_id = ?\", (message_id,)).fetchone()\n```\n\n## Step 2: Create `app/api.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Read-only review API plus the review web page.\n\nThere are no write endpoints: this interface cannot change any data.\nThere is no authentication, so it binds to localhost by default. Do not expose it.\n\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport threading\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Query\nfrom fastapi.responses import FileResponse\nfrom fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles\n\nfrom app.pipeline import DocStatus\nfrom app.registry import Registry\nfrom app.store import Store\n\nWEB = Path(__file__).parent / \"web\"\nATTENTION = {s.value for s in DocStatus} - {DocStatus.PARSED_OK.value}\nCSP = (\"default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; \"\n       \"base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'\")\n\n\ndef _loads(text, default):\n    if not text:\n        return default\n    try:\n        return json.loads(text)\n    except json.JSONDecodeError:\n        return default\n\n\ndef _summary(row) -> dict:\n    issues = _loads(row[\"issues_json\"], [])\n    errors = [i for i in issues if i[\"severity\"] == \"error\"]\n    statement = _loads(row[\"statement_json\"], None) or {}\n    return {\n        \"id\": row[\"id\"],\n        \"filename\": row[\"filename\"],\n        \"status\": row[\"status\"],\n        \"needs_attention\": row[\"status\"] in ATTENTION,\n        \"provider\": row[\"provider\"],\n        \"strategy_name\": row[\"strategy_name\"],\n        \"client_id\": row[\"client_id\"],\n        \"statement_type\": row[\"statement_type\"],\n        \"period_start\": row[\"period_start\"],\n        \"period_end\": row[\"period_end\"],\n        \"closing_value\": (statement.get(\"summary\") or {}).get(\"closing_value\"),\n        \"currency\": statement.get(\"currency\"),\n        \"format_name\": row[\"format_name\"],\n        \"match_kind\": row[\"match_kind\"],\n        \"match_score\": row[\"match_score\"],\n        \"used_llm\": bool(row[\"used_llm\"]),\n        \"errors\": len(errors),\n        \"warnings\": len(issues) - len(errors),\n        \"headline\": row[\"error\"] or (errors[0][\"message\"] if errors else None),\n        \"updated_at\": row[\"updated_at\"],\n    }\n\n\ndef create_app(store: Store, registry: Registry) -> FastAPI:\n    # No interactive docs page: it needs external scripts, which our CSP forbids.\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"Statement review\", docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)\n    registry_lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def formats():\n        with registry_lock:\n            return registry.all_formats()\n\n    @app.middleware(\"http\")\n    async def security_headers(request, call_next):\n        response = await call_next(request)\n        response.headers[\"Content-Security-Policy\"] = CSP\n        response.headers[\"X-Content-Type-Options\"] = \"nosniff\"\n        response.headers[\"Cache-Control\"] = \"no-store\"\n        return response\n\n    @app.get(\"/\", include_in_schema=False)\n    def index():\n        return FileResponse(WEB / \"index.html\")\n\n    app.mount(\"/static\", StaticFiles(directory=WEB), name=\"static\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/summary\")\n    def summary():\n        counts = store.counts()\n        emails: dict = {}\n        for r in store.list_emails():\n            emails[r[\"decision\"]] = emails.get(r[\"decision\"], 0) + 1\n        return {\n            \"total\": sum(counts.values()),\n            \"documents\": counts,\n            \"needs_attention\": sum(n for s, n in counts.items() if s in ATTENTION),\n            \"llm_documents\": sum(1 for r in store.list() if r[\"used_llm\"]),\n            \"emails\": emails,\n            \"formats\": len(formats()),\n        }\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/documents\")\n    def documents(status: Optional[str] = Query(None), attention: bool = Query(False)):\n        if status is not None and status not in {s.value for s in DocStatus}:\n            raise HTTPException(422, f\"unknown status {status!r}\")\n        docs = [_summary(r) for r in store.list(status)]\n        return [d for d in docs if d[\"needs_attention\"]] if attention else docs\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/documents/{doc_id}\")\n    def document(doc_id: int):\n        row = store.get(doc_id)\n        if row is None:\n            raise HTTPException(404, \"no such document\")\n        detail = _summary(row)\n        issues = _loads(row[\"issues_json\"], [])\n        detail.update(\n            source=row[\"source\"],\n            error=row[\"error\"],\n            issues=sorted(issues, key=lambda i: i[\"severity\"] != \"error\"),   # errors first\n            validation=_loads(row[\"validation_json\"], None),\n            statement=_loads(row[\"statement_json\"], None),\n            email=None,\n        )\n        source = row[\"source\"] or \"\"\n        if source.startswith(\"email:\"):\n            mail = store.get_email(source[len(\"email:\"):])\n            if mail is not None:\n                detail[\"email\"] = {\"subject\": mail[\"subject\"], \"sender\": mail[\"sender\"],\n                                   \"received\": mail[\"received\"]}\n        return detail\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/emails\")\n    def emails(include_no_pdf: bool = Query(False)):\n        out = []\n        for r in \"sender\": r[\"sender\"],\n                        \"received\": r[\"received\"], \"decision\": r[\"decision\"],\n                        \"attachments\": _loads(r[\"attachments_json\"], [])})\n        return out\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/formats\")\n    def list_formats():\n        return [{\"id\": f[\"id\"], \"name\": f[\"name\"], \"version\": f[\"version\"],\n                 \"created_at\": f[\"created_at\"],\n                 \"label_count\": len(_loads(f[\"labels_json\"], [])),\n                 \"has_config\": f[\"config_json\"] is not None} for f in formats()]\n\n    @app.get(\"/api/formats/{format_id}\")\n    def format_detail(format_id: int):\n        for f in formats():\n            if f[\"id\"] == format_id:\n                return {\"id\": f[\"id\"], \"name\": f[\"name\"], \"version\": f[\"version\"],\n                        \"created_at\": f[\"created_at\"],\n                        \"config\": _loads(f[\"config_json\"], None),\n [--port 8000]\n    import argparse\n\n    import uvicorn\n\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Statement review page\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--db\", default=\"statements.db\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--host\", default=\"127.0.0.1\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.host not in (\"127.0.0.1\", \"localhost\", \"::1\"):\n        print(\"WARNING: this page has no login and shows financial data. \"\n              \"Do not expose it beyond your own machine.\")\n    print(f\"Review page: \"warn\" : \"ok\"),\n    card(\"parsed OK\", s.documents.parsed_ok || 0, () => go(\"documents\", \"ok\")),\n    card(\"used the LLM\", s.llm_documents, null),\n    card(\"statement emails\", s.emails.processed || 0, () => go(\"emails\")),\n    card(\"known formats\", s.formats, () => go(\"formats\")),\n  );\n}\n\nasync function docDetail(id) {\n  const d = await api(\"/api/documents/\" + id);\n  const st = d.statement;\n  const parts = [\n    el(\"h2\", {}, d.filename, \" \", badge(d.status)),\n    kv([\n      [\"Provider\", d.provider], [\"Strategy\", d.strategy_name], [\"Client\", d.client_id],\n      [\"Type\", d.statement_type && d.statement_type.toUpperCase()],\n      [\"Period\", d.period_start && (d.period_start + \" \u2192 \" + d.period_end)],\n      [\"Currency\", d.currency],\n      [\"Format\", d.format_name && (d.format_name + \" (\" + d.match_kind + \", score \" + d.match_score + \")\")],\n      [\"LLM used\", d.used_llm ? \"yes\" : \"no\"],\n      [\"Source\", d.email ? Also tell me if you see an empty page.\n\n## Step 7: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 10: read-only review API and web page\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why is there no approve button?** It keeps the interface unable to change data. \"Add an approve action\" is a good answer to a changed-requirement question: a `reviewed` status, a `POST` endpoint, and (necessarily) authentication first.\n2. **What attack does `textContent` and the CSP stop?** An email subject like `<script>...` is stored in the database and later shown on the page. If the page inserted it as HTML, the script would run. `test_front_end_never_turns_untrusted_text_into_html` and the hostile-subject fixture cover this.\n3. **Why does the API hand over decimal strings?** JSON numbers become floats in JavaScript, which is the same reason we used `Decimal` everywhere else.\n4. **Why does \"needs attention\" include `failed` and `password_required`?** They're exactly the cases where a statement exists but its data isn't in the system. The page makes the gap visible.\n5. **Why localhost and no login?** It displays financial data. We state the limit instead of faking security.\n\n## Limitations to add\n\n- No authentication or authorisation. Anyone who can reach the port sees everything.\n- No actions: a flagged statement stays flagged forever, because there's no approve, reject or retry button.\n- No pagination or search. The list loads everything, which is fine for tens of documents and not for thousands.\n- No live updates (use Refresh).\n- No consolidated view across providers for one client (a stretch goal in the brief).\n- The browser formats numbers as floats for display. Values over about 15 significant digits would show rounded.\n\n## What's next: Part 11\n\nAbout six days remain before the 17 October deadline.
