The outer fence below uses four backticks because the README contains code blocks:\n\n````markdown\n# Self-learning PMS/AIF statement parser\n\nReads PMS and AIF statements from email, extracts holdings, transactions and summary\nfigures into one standard structure, and **uses an LLM only the first time it sees a\nstatement layout**. Every later statement in a known layout is parsed by plain code,\nwith no LLM call.\n\nBuilt for the Activv Money internship assignment by <your name>.\n\n## How it works\n\n```\nGmail (IMAP, read-only) \u2500\u2500\u25ba classify: is this a statement email?\n                                   \u2502 only accepted PDFs continue\n                                   \u25bc\nPDF \u2500\u25ba hash (already done? skip) \u2500\u25ba read (try passwords) \u2500\u25ba fingerprint \u2500\u25ba registry\n                                                                              \u2502\n                      MATCH / DRIFT: parse with the STORED config (no LLM) \u25c4\u2500\u2524\n                      UNKNOWN: ask the LLM once for a config \u2500\u25ba 4 gates \u2500\u25ba store\n                                   \u2502\n                                   \u25bc\n                     validate the numbers \u2500\u25ba parsed_ok / needs_review \u2500\u25ba SQLite \u2500\u25ba review page\n```\n\n**What is \"learned\"?** A JSON config (validated by Pydantic) describing one layout:\nregexes for header fields, row labels for summary values, and column headers for tables,\neach paired with a named transform from a fixed whitelist (`number`, `number_abs`,\n`number_drcr`, `percent`, date formats, ...). A config is data, never code, so nothing the\nLLM returns can execute.\n\n**Four gates before a learned config is stored:**\n1. the reply is a single valid JSON object\n2. it satisfies the config schema (known keys, transforms, fields; valid regexes)\n3. the engine can parse the very document it was learned from, without errors\n4. validation finds no errors in the parsed numbers (holdings + cash = closing value,\n   quantity x price = value, ISIN checksums, weights, reconciliation, ...)\n\nIf a gate fails, the problems are sent back to the LLM (3 attempts in total). Nothing\nis stored unless all four gates pass.\n\n**When the LLM is called:** (a) the format has never been seen, or (b) a known format's\nstored config provably no longer fits the document (the layout changed). A normal parse\nof a known format never calls it. `tests/test_pipeline.py` proves this with a fake LLM\nthat holds exactly one reply.\n\n## Setup\n\nPython 3.10+ (developed on 3.13).\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1\npip install -r requirements.txt\ncp .env.example .env               # then edit .env\n```\n\n### Configuration (`.env`, never committed)\n\n| Variable | Needed for | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | learning new formats | Free key from Google AI Studio |\n| `LLM_MODEL` | learning | Default `gemini-3.8-flash`. Models get retired, so this is configurable |\n| `PDF_PASSWORDS` | locked PDFs | Comma-separated list tried in order (e.g. PAN, date of birth) |\n| `GMAIL_ADDRESS`, `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` | email ingestion | Use a dedicated test account and an app password (2-Step Verification on) |\n| `STATEMENT_SENDERS` | email (optional) | Comma-separated senders or domains that count as trusted statement sources |\n| `IMAP_HOST`, `MAILBOX_FOLDER` | email (optional) | Defaults `imap.gmail.com`, `INBOX` |\n\nThe demo password for the sample locked PDF is `demo1234` (fake).\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\npython -m samples.generate         # 5 synthetic statements + answer keys (samples/pdfs, samples/expected)\npython -m samples.next_month       # a \"next month\" ABC statement and two broken variants\n\npython -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs                # process a folder (or one file)\npython -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs --review-new   # send every newly learned format to review\n\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2 --dry-run      # classify only, change nothing\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2                # fetch, classify, process\npython -m samples.send_test_email [--may]          # put test emails in your test inbox\n\npython -m app.api                                  # review page at http://127.0.0.1:8000\npython -m app.learner samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf     # learn one format and print the report\npython -m samples.export_outputs --db demo.db      # write per-document JSON outputs\n```\n\nFailed documents (`password_required`, `failed`, `learning_failed`) are retried by\nre-running `python -m app.pipeline data/attachments` (saved email attachments).\n\n## Statuses\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `parsed_ok` | Parsed and every runnable check passed |\n| `needs_review` | Parsed, but a check failed, the layout drifted, or a config was re-learned |\n| `password_required` | Encrypted and none of the configured passwords opens it |\n| `failed` | Unreadable, or has no text layer (scanned) |\n| `learning_failed` | New format, but the LLM was unavailable or produced no valid config |\n\nValidation checks that cannot run (for example, the PDF does not print inflows) are\nreported as *skipped*, never hidden.\n\n## LLM provider and failure behaviour\n\nProvider: **Google Gemini** (`google-genai`), model set by `LLM_MODEL`.\n\n| Failure | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No API key | `learning_failed` immediately, with a clear message. No network call |\n| Network error, 429, 5xx | Retried 4 times with exponential backoff, then `learning_failed` |\n| Other API errors (401, 403, 404) | `learning_failed` immediately (retrying cannot help) |\n| Reply is not valid, fails a gate | Problems fed back to the LLM, up to 3 attempts, then `learning_failed` |\n\nNothing is stored for a failed learning attempt. The statement text of the *first*\ndocument in each new layout is sent to the LLM provider (see `docs/limitations.md`).\n\n## Project layout\n\n```\napp/\n  reader.py        PDF -> lines -> cells with x-positions; password / scanned handling\n  fingerprint.py   stable \"label\" set describing a layout; Jaccard similarity\n  registry.py      SQLite store of learned formats (config + fingerprint, versioned)\n  config_spec.py   what a legal config may contain (strict; rejects anything else)\n  transforms.py    whitelist of value parsers the config may name\n  engine.py        generic, provider-agnostic parser: Document + config -> Statement\n  validation.py    arithmetic consistency checks (errors, warnings, skipped)\n  llm.py           Gemini client behind a tiny interface (retries, clear failures)\n  learner.py       prompt + the four gates + retry loop\n  pipeline.py      orchestration, statuses, dedup by file hash\n  store.py         SQLite store of documents and emails\n  email_ingest.py  read-only IMAP, statement-email classifier, attachment handling\n  api.py, web/     read-only review API and page\nsamples/           synthetic statement generator, next-month variants, outputs/\nconfigs/           hand-written reference configs (used by tests); learned/ = written by the LLM\ntests/             pytest suite (no network or API key needed)\ndocs/              design note, limitations, AI usage log\n```\n\nAt runtime the system reads configs from the registry in SQLite, not from `configs/`.\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\nNo network or API key needed: the LLM and the mailbox are replaced by fakes.\n\n## Data and safety\n\nAll sample data is synthetic: fictional providers, invented client IDs, valid-checksum\nISINs, a fake password. No real client data is in this repository. `.env`, databases and\ndownloaded attachments (`data/`) are gitignored.\n````\n\n## Step 3: docs/limitations.md\n\nCreate `docs/limitations.md`. This is the note the brief calls \"a strength, not a weakness\" when specific. I built it from everything we found along the way. **Before submitting, verify each item you can** (the \"Evidence\" lines say how), and delete any you can't explain. The brief says to list what you can't explain, and nothing is worth claiming that you don't understand.\n\n````markdown\n# Known limitations\n\nEach item says what happens, so none of these are silent unless stated.\n\n## Reading PDFs\n- **Scanned (image-only) PDFs** are rejected as `failed` (\"no extractable text\"). No OCR.\n- **Only text-based PDFs generated by software** were tested (ReportLab). Real statements add\n  repeating page headers and footers, rotated text, watermarks and odd fonts, none tested.\n- **Cells are split at a fixed horizontal gap (5pt).** Tightly packed columns can merge into one\n  cell; large-font headings split into several cells.\n- **A table is read from one page only.** Rows continuing on page 2 are dropped without an\n  engine error. This is usually caught by the holdings-total check, but not when the statement\n  prints no cash balance or closing value.\n- **Wrapped rows** (a security name on two lines) are not supported. They produce an error or a\n  wrong row.\n- **Subtotal rows inside a table** (for example per asset class) are read as data unless named\n  in `stop_at`, which ends the whole table.\n- **Two columns whose x-ranges overlap** can misplace a cell. The engine errors when two cells\n  land in one column, but not when a single cell lands in the wrong one.\n- **Excel and CSV statements are not supported.** One PDF holding several clients' statements is\n  not split (an email with several PDFs is handled).\n\n## Fingerprint and format recognition\n- **A single renamed column barely changes the similarity score**, so the fingerprint cannot\n  detect it. Detection relies on the engine's missing-column check, which is why a renamed\n  column triggers a re-learn rather than a DRIFT status.\n- **Thresholds (0.85 match, 0.50 drift) are judgement, not tuned** on a real corpus.\n- **Header cells containing digits are dropped** from the fingerprint (e.g. \"Q1 Value\"), and\n  short headings are joined with spaces, so the representation is a heuristic, not a principle.\n- **Currency words are stripped from labels**, so a currency change alone is not detected;\n  currency is read from the statement itself.\n- **Two products of one provider with the same layout share one format**, and a white-label\n  template used by several providers would too.\n- **A DRIFT layout that still parses is flagged but not registered**, so the same drifted layout\n  is flagged again every month until a human acts. There is no approve action.\n\n## Config language and engine\n- **Header fields come from regexes over the whole document text, first match wins.** A earlier\n  occurrence of the same label elsewhere on the page would be captured instead.\n- **No protection against slow regexes** (catastrophic backtracking) in an LLM-written config.\n  There is no timeout.\n- **Summary values must be a line whose first cell is the label and whose last cell is the\n  value.** Layouts that put values above labels, or two label/value pairs side by side, are\n  not expressible.\n- **Signs are recorded as printed.** Only the config's transform (`number_abs`, `number_drcr`)\n  decides the sign, so a wrong choice by the LLM flips an amount without any parse error.\n- **One NAV per statement.** Statements with several unit classes, several currencies, or\n  capital called/uncalled per tranche are not supported. \"Capital called to date\" is printed\n  by one sample and deliberately not stored.\n- **Schema gaps:** realised vs unrealised gains, XIRR, sector, accrued interest and benchmark\n  returns are not captured.\n- **Transaction types are matched by keyword.** An unrecognised label becomes `other`, which\n  validation reports as an error (so the statement needs review).\n- **Day/month order is chosen by the config.** If the LLM picks the wrong date transform, only\n  the \"transactions within the period\" check can reveal it.\n\n## Learning with the LLM\n- **A learned config is proven on one document only.** It may overfit (for example a stop line\n  that works this month). Later statements are still validated numerically, so most breakage\n  shows up as `needs_review`, but a config that is wrong in a way that preserves the arithmetic\n  would not be detected.\n- **Prompt injection is mitigated, not eliminated.** The LLM can only return data, the text is\n  delimited and flagged as untrusted, and gates 3 and 4 reject configs that do not really parse.\n  A manipulated config that parses this document correctly but misreads others would pass.\n- **Statement text is sent to a third party** (Gemini) the first time a layout is seen. That\n  text contains the client's ID, holdings and balances. The free tier may use prompts to improve\n  Google's products. This project only ever used synthetic data; real use would need a data\n  agreement and redaction of identifiers before the call.\n- **Prompts are capped at 400 lines or 40,000 characters.** Longer documents are truncated, so\n  a table past the cut cannot be learned.\n- **One fictional example in the prompt.** Unusual layouts may fail all 3 attempts and end as\n  `learning_failed`.\n- **A newly learned format is accepted automatically** (a warning only) unless `--review-new` is\n  used. A re-learned config for a changed layout is registered before a human confirms it, so a\n  wrong one would match future documents.\n- **Availability:** during development the first model name was retired (404) and a later call hit\n  a 503 spike. Both are reported clearly; learning is paused, not skipped silently.\n\n## Validation\n- **Errors that cancel out are invisible** (two wrong holdings that offset).\n- **A statement that prints little can pass trivially.** The report lists skipped checks (for\n  example Meridian has no reconciliation), but nothing fails because many were skipped.\n- **Tolerance is 0.1% or 1 unit.** Reconciliation accepts two formulas (gain before or after\n  fees), which loosens it slightly.\n- **Weights are compared against only two denominators** (closing value or holdings total).\n- **Cost basis is never validated.** There is no independent figure to compare.\n- **No continuity check across months** (this month's opening value against last month's closing).\n- **The fee-total check is a warning, not an error.**\n\n## Pipeline and storage\n- **Deduplication is by file bytes.** The same statement re-issued as a different PDF is processed\n  again, and the same figures can be stored twice.\n- **Failed documents are not retried automatically.** After an email run, a statement that ended\n  `learning_failed` or `password_required` needs `python -m app.pipeline data/attachments`.\n- **Passwords come from a flat list.** A statement whose password is not in the list stays\n  `password_required`, and a password containing a comma cannot be entered.\n- **Statements are stored as JSON blobs**, not normalised tables, so there is no cross-provider\n  query and no consolidated view for one client (a stretch goal not built).\n- **SQLite with a single process.** There is one lock around writes but no migrations, no\n  concurrent workers and no backups.\n- **Unexpected exceptions become `failed`** with the exception text; a bug in our own code and a\n  bad document look the same on the review page.\n\n## Email\n- **Classification is keyword scoring.** A personal bank statement mentions \"statement\" and\n  passes; a real statement with no keyword in the subject, filename or body, from a sender not in\n  `STATEMENT_SENDERS`, is skipped. Skips are recorded and visible, not lost.\n- **PDF attachments only.** Download links, password-in-body emails and other file types are ignored.\n- **Only the first 2,000 characters of the body are read**, and HTML is stripped crudely.\n- **IMAP with an app password** gives broad mailbox access. A production system would use OAuth\n  with a read-only scope. The system opens the mailbox read-only and never changes mail.\n- **Metadata of every email seen is stored** (subject, sender), including unrelated ones.\n- **Downloaded attachments are saved unencrypted** under `data/`.\n- **Attachments over 25 MB are ignored**, and the search window is date-granular.\n\n## Review interface\n- **No authentication, no actions, no pagination, no live updates.** It binds to localhost.\n  Flagged statements cannot be approved, rejected or retried from the page.\n- **Numbers are displayed through the browser's float formatting**, so values beyond about 15\n  significant digits would show rounded (stored values are exact decimals).\n- **The JavaScript has no automated tests.**\n\n## Testing\n- **All tests use five synthetic statements I generated**, plus two variants. The configs, PDFs\n  and answer keys came from the same author, so the suite shows the design is consistent, not\n  that it handles real-world statements.\n````\n\n## Step 4: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 11a: output export, README, limitations note\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Before the next part\n\n1. **Put your name and the repo link** in the README placeholders.\n2. **Verify three limitations yourself.** For each one you can't verify, I'd rather you cut it than claim it. Every later statement in a known layout is parsed by plain code,\nwith no LLM call.\n\nBuilt for the Activv Money internship assignment by <your name>.\n\n## How it works\n\n```\nGmail (IMAP, read-only) \u2500\u2500\u25ba classify: is this a statement email?\n                                   \u2502 only accepted PDFs continue\n                                   \u25bc\nPDF \u2500\u25ba hash (already done? skip) \u2500\u25ba read (try passwords) \u2500\u25ba fingerprint \u2500\u25ba registry\n                                                                              \u2502\n                      MATCH / DRIFT: parse with the STORED config (no LLM) \u25c4\u2500\u2524\n                      UNKNOWN: ask the LLM once for a config \u2500\u25ba 4 gates \u2500\u25ba store\n                                   \u2502\n                                   \u25bc\n                     validate the numbers \u2500\u25ba parsed_ok / needs_review \u2500\u25ba SQLite \u2500\u25ba review page\n```\n\n**What is \"learned\"?** A JSON config (validated by Pydantic) describing one layout:\nregexes for header fields, row labels for summary values, and column headers for tables,\neach paired with a named transform from a fixed whitelist (`number`, `number_abs`,\n`number_drcr`, `percent`, date formats, ...). A config is data, never code, so nothing the\nLLM returns can execute.\n\n**Four gates before a learned config is stored:**\n1. the reply is a single valid JSON object\n2. it satisfies the config schema (known keys, transforms, fields; valid regexes)\n3. the engine can parse the very document it was learned from, without errors\n4. validation finds no errors in the parsed numbers (holdings + cash = closing value,\n   quantity x price = value, ISIN checksums, weights, reconciliation, ...)\n\nIf a gate fails, the problems are sent back to the LLM (3 attempts in total). Nothing\nis stored unless all four gates pass.\n\n**When the LLM is called:** (a) the format has never been seen, or (b) a known format's\nstored config provably no longer fits the document (the layout changed). A normal parse\nof a known format never calls it. `tests/test_pipeline.py` proves this with a fake LLM\nthat holds exactly one reply.\n\n## Setup\n\nPython 3.10+ (developed on 3.13).\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1\npip install -r requirements.txt\ncp .env.example .env               # then edit .env\n```\n\n### Configuration (`.env`, never committed)\n\n| Variable | Needed for | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | learning new formats | Free key from Google AI Studio |\n| `LLM_MODEL` | learning | Default `gemini-3.8-flash`. Models get retired, so this is configurable |\n| `PDF_PASSWORDS` | locked PDFs | Comma-separated list tried in order (e.g. PAN, date of birth) |\n| `GMAIL_ADDRESS`, `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` | email ingestion | Use a dedicated test account and an app password (2-Step Verification on) |\n| `STATEMENT_SENDERS` | email (optional) | Comma-separated senders or domains that count as trusted statement sources |\n| `IMAP_HOST`, `MAILBOX_FOLDER` | email (optional) | Defaults `imap.gmail.com`, `INBOX` |\n\nThe demo password for the sample locked PDF is `demo1234` (fake).\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\npython -m samples.generate         # 5 synthetic statements + answer keys (samples/pdfs, samples/expected)\npython -m samples.next_month       # a \"next month\" ABC statement and two broken variants\n\npython -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs                # process a folder (or one file)\npython -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs --review-new   # send every newly learned format to review\n\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2 --dry-run      # classify only, change nothing\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2                # fetch, classify, process\npython -m samples.send_test_email [--may]          # put test emails in your test inbox\n\npython -m app.api                                  # review page at http://127.0.0.1:8000\npython -m app.learner samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf     # learn one format and print the report\npython -m samples.export_outputs --db demo.db      # write per-document JSON outputs\n```\n\nFailed documents (`password_required`, `failed`, `learning_failed`) are retried by\nre-running `python -m app.pipeline data/attachments` (saved email attachments).\n\n## Statuses\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `parsed_ok` | Parsed and every runnable check passed |\n| `needs_review` | Parsed, but a check failed, the layout drifted, or a config was re-learned |\n| `password_required` | Encrypted and none of the configured passwords opens it |\n| `failed` | Unreadable, or has no text layer (scanned) |\n| `learning_failed` | New format, but the LLM was unavailable or produced no valid config |\n\nValidation checks that cannot run (for example, the PDF does not print inflows) are\nreported as *skipped*, never hidden.\n\n## LLM provider and failure behaviour\n\nProvider: **Google Gemini** (`google-genai`), model set by `LLM_MODEL`.\n\n| Failure | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No API key | `learning_failed` immediately, with a clear message. No network call |\n| Network error, 429, 5xx | Retried 4 times with exponential backoff, then `learning_failed` |\n| Other API errors (401, 403, 404) | `learning_failed` immediately (retrying cannot help) |\n| Reply is not valid, fails a gate | Problems fed back to the LLM, up to 3 attempts, then `learning_failed` |\n\nNothing is stored for a failed learning attempt. The statement text of the *first*\ndocument in each new layout is sent to the LLM provider (see `docs/limitations.md`).\n\n## Project layout\n\n```\napp/\n  reader.py        PDF -> lines -> cells with x-positions; password / scanned handling\n  fingerprint.py   stable \"label\" set describing a layout; Jaccard similarity\n  registry.py      SQLite store of learned formats (config + fingerprint, versioned)\n  config_spec.py   what a legal config may contain (strict; rejects anything else)\n  transforms.py    whitelist of value parsers the config may name\n  engine.py        generic, provider-agnostic parser: Document + config -> Statement\n  validation.py    arithmetic consistency checks (errors, warnings, skipped)\n  llm.py           Gemini client behind a tiny interface (retries, clear failures)\n  learner.py       prompt + the four gates + retry loop\n  pipeline.py      orchestration, statuses, dedup by file hash\n  store.py         SQLite store of documents and emails\n  email_ingest.py  read-only IMAP, statement-email classifier, attachment handling\n  api.py, web/     read-only review API and page\nsamples/           synthetic statement generator, next-month variants, outputs/\nconfigs/           hand-written reference configs (used by tests); learned/ = written by the LLM\ntests/             pytest suite (no network or API key needed)\ndocs/              design note, limitations, AI usage log\n```\n\nAt runtime the system reads configs from the registry in SQLite, not from `configs/`.\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\nNo network or API key needed: the LLM and the mailbox are replaced by fakes.\n\n## Data and safety\n\nAll sample data is synthetic: fictional providers, invented client IDs, valid-checksum\nISINs, a fake password. No real client data is in this repository. `.env`, databases and\ndownloaded attachments (`data/`) are gitignored.\n````\n\n## Step 3: docs/limitations.md\n\nCreate `docs/limitations.md`. This is the note the brief calls \"a strength, not a weakness\" when specific. I built it from everything we found along the way. **Before submitting, verify each item you can** (the \"Evidence\" lines say how), and delete any you can't explain. The brief says to list what you can't explain, and nothing is worth claiming that you don't understand.\n\n````markdown\n# Known limitations\n\nEach item says what happens, so none of these are silent unless stated.\n\n## Reading PDFs\n- **Scanned (image-only) PDFs** are rejected as `failed` (\"no extractable text\"). No OCR.\n- **Only text-based PDFs generated by software** were tested (ReportLab). Real statements add\n  repeating page headers and footers, rotated text, watermarks and odd fonts, none tested.\n- **Cells are split at a fixed horizontal gap (5pt).** Tightly packed columns can merge into one\n  cell; large-font headings split into several cells.\n- **A table is read from one page only.** Rows continuing on page 2 are dropped without an\n  engine error. This is usually caught by the holdings-total check, but not when the statement\n  prints no cash balance or closing value.\n- **Wrapped rows** (a security name on two lines) are not supported. They produce an error or a\n  wrong row.\n- **Subtotal rows inside a table** (for example per asset class) are read as data unless named\n  in `stop_at`, which ends the whole table.\n- **Two columns whose x-ranges overlap** can misplace a cell. The engine errors when two cells\n  land in one column, but not when a single cell lands in the wrong one.\n- **Excel and CSV statements are not supported.** One PDF holding several clients' statements is\n  not split (an email with several PDFs is handled).\n\n## Fingerprint and format recognition\n- **A single renamed column barely changes the similarity score**, so the fingerprint cannot\n  detect it. Detection relies on the engine's missing-column check, which is why a renamed\n  column triggers a re-learn rather than a DRIFT status.\n- **Thresholds (0.85 match, 0.50 drift) are judgement, not tuned** on a real corpus.\n- **Header cells containing digits are dropped** from the fingerprint (e.g. \"Q1 Value\"), and\n  short headings are joined with spaces, so the representation is a heuristic, not a principle.\n- **Currency words are stripped from labels**, so a currency change alone is not detected;\n  currency is read from the statement itself.\n- **Two products of one provider with the same layout share one format**, and a white-label\n  template used by several providers would too.\n- **A DRIFT layout that still parses is flagged but not registered**, so the same drifted layout\n  is flagged again every month until a human acts. There is no approve action.\n\n## Config language and engine\n- **Header fields come from regexes over the whole document text, first match wins.** A earlier\n  occurrence of the same label elsewhere on the page would be captured instead.\n- **No protection against slow regexes** (catastrophic backtracking) in an LLM-written config.\n  There is no timeout.\n- **Summary values must be a line whose first cell is the label and whose last cell is the\n  value.** Layouts that put values above labels, or two label/value pairs side by side, are\n  not expressible.\n- **Signs are recorded as printed.** Only the config's transform (`number_abs`, `number_drcr`)\n  decides the sign, so a wrong choice by the LLM flips an amount without any parse error.\n- **One NAV per statement.** Statements with several unit classes, several currencies, or\n  capital called/uncalled per tranche are not supported. \"Capital called to date\" is printed\n  by one sample and deliberately not stored.\n- **Schema gaps:** realised vs unrealised gains, XIRR, sector, accrued interest and benchmark\n  returns are not captured.\n- **Transaction types are matched by keyword.** An unrecognised label becomes `other`, which\n  validation reports as an error (so the statement needs review).\n- **Day/month order is chosen by the config.** If the LLM picks the wrong date transform, only\n  the \"transactions within the period\" check can reveal it.\n\n## Learning with the LLM\n- **A learned config is proven on one document only.** It may overfit (for example a stop line\n  that works this month). Later statements are still validated numerically, so most breakage\n  shows up as `needs_review`, but a config that is wrong in a way that preserves the arithmetic\n  would not be detected.\n- **Prompt injection is mitigated, not eliminated.** The LLM can only return data, the text is\n  delimited and flagged as untrusted, and gates 3 and 4 reject configs that do not really parse.\n  A manipulated config that parses this document correctly but misreads others would pass.\n- **Statement text is sent to a third party** (Gemini) the first time a layout is seen. That\n  text contains the client's ID, holdings and balances. The free tier may use prompts to improve\n  Google's products. This project only ever used synthetic data; real use would need a data\n  agreement and redaction of identifiers before the call.\n- **Prompts are capped at 400 lines or 40,000 characters.** Longer documents are truncated, so\n  a table past the cut cannot be learned.\n- **One fictional example in the prompt.** Unusual layouts may fail all 3 attempts and end as\n  `learning_failed`.\n- **A newly learned format is accepted automatically** (a warning only) unless `--review-new` is\n  used. A re-learned config for a changed layout is registered before a human confirms it, so a\n  wrong one would match future documents.\n- **Availability:** during development the first model name was retired (404) and a later call hit\n  a 503 spike. Both are reported clearly; learning is paused, not skipped silently.\n\n## Validation\n- **Errors that cancel out are invisible** (two wrong holdings that offset).\n- **A statement that prints little can pass trivially.** The report lists skipped checks (for\n  example Meridian has no reconciliation), but nothing fails because many were skipped.\n- **Tolerance is 0.1% or 1 unit.** Reconciliation accepts two formulas (gain before or after\n  fees), which loosens it slightly.\n- **Weights are compared against only two denominators** (closing value or holdings total).\n- **Cost basis is never validated.** There is no independent figure to compare.\n- **No continuity check across months** (this month's opening value against last month's closing).\n- **The fee-total check is a warning, not an error.**\n\n## Pipeline and storage\n- **Deduplication is by file bytes.** The same statement re-issued as a different PDF is processed\n  again, and the same figures can be stored twice.\n- **Failed documents are not retried automatically.** After an email run, a statement that ended\n  `learning_failed` or `password_required` needs `python -m app.pipeline data/attachments`.\n- **Passwords come from a flat list.** A statement whose password is not in the list stays\n  `password_required`, and a password containing a comma cannot be entered.\n- **Statements are stored as JSON blobs**, not normalised tables, so there is no cross-provider\n  query and no consolidated view for one client (a stretch goal not built).\n- **SQLite with a single process.** There is one lock around writes but no migrations, no\n  concurrent workers and no backups.\n- **Unexpected exceptions become `failed`** with the exception text; a bug in our own code and a\n  bad document look the same on the review page.\n\n## Email\n- **Classification is keyword scoring.** A personal bank statement mentions \"statement\" and\n  passes; a real statement with no keyword in the subject, filename or body, from a sender not in\n  `STATEMENT_SENDERS`, is skipped. Skips are recorded and visible, not lost.\n- **PDF attachments only.** Download links, password-in-body emails and other file types are ignored.\n- **Only the first 2,000 characters of the body are read**, and HTML is stripped crudely.\n- **IMAP with an app password** gives broad mailbox access. A production system would use OAuth\n  with a read-only scope. The system opens the mailbox read-only and never changes mail.\n- **Metadata of every email seen is stored** (subject, sender), including unrelated ones.\n- **Downloaded attachments are saved unencrypted** under `data/`.\n- **Attachments over 25 MB are ignored**, and the search window is date-granular.\n\n## Review interface\n- **No authentication, no actions, no pagination, no live updates.** It binds to localhost.\n  Flagged statements cannot be approved, rejected or retried from the page.\n- **Numbers are displayed through the browser's float formatting**, so values beyond about 15\n  significant digits would show rounded (stored values are exact decimals).\n- **The JavaScript has no automated tests.**\n\n## Testing\n- **All tests use five synthetic statements I generated**, plus two variants. The configs, PDFs\n  and answer keys came from the same author, so the suite shows the design is consistent, not\n  that it handles real-world statements.\n````\n\n## Step 4: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 11a: output export, README, limitations note\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Before the next part\n\n1. **Put your name and the repo link** in the README placeholders.\n2. **Verify three limitations yourself.** For each one you can't verify, I'd rather you cut it than claim it. Quick experiments:\n   - *Page break:* generate a very long ABC statement (add 60 holdings to `abc_may()`) and see what happens.\n   - *Wrapped row:* edit a name in a sample to be long enough to wrap.\n   - *Regex first match:* what happens if the client code appears twice?\n3. **Run the full flow once on a clean database** and keep the output, since it's your demo script.\n\n## Next: Part 11b\n\nThe remaining deliverables, written from our conversation history:\n\n- **Design note**: assumptions recorded where the brief was silent, plus your answers to its four hard questions.\n- **AI usage log** with the specific places the AI misled me: the wrong comments in `sample_data.py`, the `PdfminerException` wrapping, the stale model name, the unchecked column fields, and the fingerprint leak caught only by reading the dump.\n- **Demo video script** and **submission email**.\n- **An interview rehearsal**: the questions they're likely to ask and how your code answers each.\n\nPaste the test result for `test_export.py`, say how the web page looked, and tell me whether you want to do Part 11b next or first stress-test the system on messier statements. print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))\"`):\n\n```text\nREVIEW_TOKEN=\n```\n\n**`app/store.py`**, edit 1: add below the `emails` block:\n\n```python\nSCHEMA += \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reviews (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    document_id INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    decision TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (decision IN ('approved', 'rejected', 'reopened')),\n    note TEXT,\n    reviewed_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_reviews_doc ON reviews(document_id);\n\"\"\"\n\n# A document joined with its LATEST review decision (if any).\n_FROM = (\"FROM documents d LEFT JOIN reviews r \"\n         \"ON r.id = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM reviews WHERE document_id = d.id)\")\n_SELECT = (\"SELECT d.*, r.decision AS review_decision, r.note AS review_note, \"\n           \"r.reviewed_at AS reviewed_at\")\n```\n\nYour existing `statements.db` gets the new table automatically.\n\n**`app/store.py`**, edit 2: add these methods at the end of the `Store` class:\n\n```python\n    def query(self, *, status=None, attention=False, q=None, limit=25, offset=0):\n        \"\"\"One page of documents plus the total match count.\n        attention = flagged AND not yet resolved by a person.\"\"\"\n        where, params = [], []\n        if status:\n            where.append(\"d.status = ?\")\n            params.append(status)\n        if attention:\n            where.append(\"d.status != 'parsed_ok' \"\n                         \"AND (r.decision IS NULL OR r.decision = 'reopened')\")\n        if q and q.strip():\n            like = \"%\" + q.strip().replace(\"\\\\\", \"\\\\\\\\\").replace(\"%\", \"\\\\%\").replace(\"_\", \"\\\\_\") + \"%\"\n            cols = [\"d.filename\", \"d.provider\", \"d.client_id\", \"d.strategy_name\", \"d.format_name\"]\n            where.append(\"(\" + \" OR \".join(f\"{c} LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\\\'\" for c in cols) + \")\")\n            params += [like] * len(cols)\n        clause = (\"WHERE \" + \" AND \".join(where)) if where else \"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            total = self.conn.execute(f\"SELECT COUNT(*) {_FROM} {clause}\", params).fetchone()[0]\n            rows = self.conn.execute(\n                f\"{_SELECT} {_FROM} {clause} ORDER BY d.id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?\",\n                [*params, limit, offset]).fetchall()\n        return rows, total\n\n    def get_with_review(self, doc_id: int) -> Optional[sqlite3.Row]:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\n                f\"{_SELECT} {_FROM} WHERE d.id = ?\", (doc_id,)).fetchone()\n\n    def add_review(self, doc_id: int, decision: str, note: str = \"\"):\n        with self._lock:\n            self.conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO reviews (document_id, decision, note) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (doc_id, decision, note or None))\n            self.conn.commit()\n\n    def review_history(self, doc_id: int) -> list:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT * FROM reviews WHERE document_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC\",\n                (doc_id,)).fetchall()\n\n    def review_counts(self) -> dict:\n        with self._lock:\n            rows = self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT decision, COUNT(*) AS n FROM reviews \"\n                \"WHERE id IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM reviews GROUP BY document_id) \"\n                \"GROUP BY decision\").fetchall()\n        got = {r[\"decision\"]: r[\"n\"] for r in rows}\n        return {\"approved\": got.get(\"approved\", 0), \"rejected\": got.get(\"rejected\", 0)}\n```\n\nThe search text is escaped before it goes into `LIKE`, so typing `%` searches for a literal percent sign. (errors[0][\"message\"] if errors else None),\n        \"updated_at\": row[\"updated_at\"],\n    }\n\n\nclass ReviewIn(BaseModel):\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n    decision: or len(token) < 16:\n        raise ValueError(\"the access token must be at least 16 characters\")\n    token_bytes = token.encode()\n\n    def require_token(x_review_token: str = FastAPI(title=\"Statement review\", docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)\n    api = APIRouter(prefix=\"/api\", dependencies=[Depends(require_token)])\n    registry_lock = response.headers[\"Cache-Control\"] = \"no-store\"\n        return response\n\n    @app.get(\"/\", include_in_schema=False)\n    def index():\n        return FileResponse(WEB / \"index.html\")\n\n    app.mount(\"/static\", StaticFiles(directory=WEB), name=\"static\")\n\n    @api.get(\"/summary\")\n    def summary():\n        counts = store.counts()\n        emails: dict = {}\n        for r in store.list_emails():\n            emails[r[\"decision\"]] = emails.get(r[\"decision\"], 0) + 1\n        _, attention = store.query(attention=True, limit=1)\n        return {\n            \"total\": sum(counts.values()),\n            \"documents\": counts,\n            \"needs_attention\": attention,\n            \"reviewed\": store.review_counts(),\n            \"llm_documents\": sum(1 for r in store.list() if r[\"used_llm\"]),\n            \"emails\": emails,\n            \"formats\": len(formats()),\n        }\n\n    @api.get(\"/documents\")\n    def documents(status: Optional[str] = Query(None), attention: bool = Query(False),\n                  q: Optional[str] = Query(None, max_length=100),\n                  limit: int = Query(25, ge=1, le=200), offset: int = Query(0, ge=0)):\n        if status is not None and status not in {s.value for s in DocStatus}:\n            raise HTTPException(422, f\"unknown status {status!r}\")\n        rows, total = store.query(status=status, attention=attention, q=q,\n                                  limit=limit, offset=offset)\n        return {\"items\": [_summary(r) for r in rows], \"total\": total,\n                \"limit\": limit, \"offset\": offset}\n\n    @api.get(\"/documents/{doc_id}\")\n    def document(doc_id: int):\n        row = store.get_with_review(doc_id)\n        if row is None:\n            raise HTTPException(404, \"no such document\")\n        detail = _summary(row)\n        issues = _loads(row[\"issues_json\"], [])\n        detail.update(\n            source=row[\"source\"],\n            error=row[\"error\"],\n            issues=sorted(issues, key=lambda i: i[\"severity\"] != \"error\"),   # errors first\n            validation=_loads(row[\"validation_json\"], None),\n            statement=_loads(row[\"statement_json\"], None),\n            review_history=[{\"decision\": h[\"decision\"], \"note\": h[\"note\"],\n                             \"reviewed_at\": h[\"reviewed_at\"]}\n                            for h in store.review_history(doc_id)],\n            email=None,\n        )\n        source = row[\"source\"] or \"\"\n        if source.startswith(\"email:\"):\n            mail = store.get_email(source[len(\"email:\"):])\n            if mail is not None:\n                detail[\"email\"] = {\"subject\": mail[\"subject\"], \"sender\": mail[\"sender\"],\n                                   \"received\": mail[\"received\"]}\n        return detail\n\n    @api.post(\"/documents/{doc_id}/review\")\n    def review(doc_id: int, body: ReviewIn):\n        row = store.get_with_review(doc_id)\n        if row is None:\n            raise HTTPException(404, \"no such document\")\n        status, current = row[\"status\"], row[\"review_decision\"]\n        resolved = current in RESOLVED\n        if status not in ATTENTION:\n            raise HTTPException(409, \"only flagged documents can be reviewed\")\n        if body.decision == \"approved\" and status != \"needs_review\":\n            raise HTTPException(409, \"there is no parsed data to approve; dismiss it instead\")\n        if body.decision == \"reopened\" and not resolved:\n            raise HTTPException(409, \"nothing to reopen\")\n        if body.decision in RESOLVED and resolved:\n            raise HTTPException(409, \"already reviewed; reopen it first\")\n        store.add_review(doc_id, body.decision, body.note.strip())\n        return document(doc_id)\n\n    @api.get(\"/emails\")\n    def emails(include_no_pdf: bool = Query(False), limit: int = Query(100, ge=1, le=500)):\n        out = []\n        for r in store.list_emails():\n            if r[\"decision\"] == \"no_pdf\" and not include_no_pdf:\n                continue\n            out.append({\"id\": r[\"id\"], \"subject\": r[\"subject\"], \"sender\": r[\"sender\"],\n                        \"received\": r[\"received\"], \"decision\": r[\"decision\"],\n \"has_config\": f[\"config_json\"] is not None} for f in formats()]\n\n    @api.get(\"/formats/{format_id}\")\n    def format_detail(format_id: int):\n        for f in formats():\n            if ap.add_argument(\"--host\", default=\"127.0.0.1\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n\n    token = os.environ.get(\"REVIEW_TOKEN\", beyond your own machine.\")\n    print(f\"Review page: http://{args.host}:{args.port}\")\n    print(f\"Access token: {token}\" if generated else \"Access token: REVIEW_TOKEN from .env\")\n }\n.login-box p { margin: 0; }\n```\n\n**`app.js`**\n\n```js\n\"use strict\";\n\n// Everything shown here comes from PDFs and emails, so it is untrusted text.\n// el() only creates elements and text head + \",\" : \"\") + tail + (frac ? \".\" + frac : \"\");\n}\nconst txt = (v) => (v === null || v === undefined || v === \"\") ? \"\u2013\" : String(v);\nconst trunc = (s, n) => (s.length > n ? s.slice(0, n - 1) + \"\u2026\" : s);\n\n// ------------------------------------------------------------------ access token\nfunction showLogin(message) {\n  $(\"login-error\").textContent = message || \"\";\n  $(\"login\").hidden = false;\n  $(\"token\").value = \"\";\n  $(\"token\").focus();\n}\n\nasync function api(path, options) {\n  const opts = options || {};\n  const headers = { \"X-Review-Token\": token };\n  if (opts.body) headers[\"Content-Type\"] = \"application/json\";\n  const response = await fetch(path, { method: opts.method || \"GET\", headers, body: opts.body });\n  if (response.status === 401) {\n    showLogin(token ? It does not approve the learned config. print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))\"`):\n\n```text\nREVIEW_TOKEN=\n```\n\n**`app/store.py`**, edit 1: add below the `emails` block:\n\n```python\nSCHEMA += \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reviews (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    document_id INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    decision TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (decision IN ('approved', 'rejected', 'reopened')),\n    note TEXT,\n    reviewed_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_reviews_doc ON reviews(document_id);\n\"\"\"\n\n# A document joined with its LATEST review decision (if any).\n_FROM = (\"FROM documents d LEFT JOIN reviews r \"\n         \"ON r.id = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM reviews WHERE document_id = d.id)\")\n_SELECT = (\"SELECT d.*, r.decision AS review_decision, r.note AS review_note, \"\n           \"r.reviewed_at AS reviewed_at\")\n```\n\nYour existing `statements.db` gets the new table automatically.\n\n**`app/store.py`**, edit 2: add these methods at the end of the `Store` class:\n\n```python\n    def query(self, *, status=None, attention=False, q=None, limit=25, offset=0):\n        \"\"\"One page of documents plus the total match count.\n        attention = flagged AND not yet resolved by a person.\"\"\"\n        where, params = [], []\n        if status:\n            where.append(\"d.status = ?\")\n            params.append(status)\n        if attention:\n            where.append(\"d.status != 'parsed_ok' \"\n                         \"AND (r.decision IS NULL OR r.decision = 'reopened')\")\n        if q and q.strip():\n            like = \"%\" + q.strip().replace(\"\\\\\", \"\\\\\\\\\").replace(\"%\", \"\\\\%\").replace(\"_\", \"\\\\_\") + \"%\"\n            cols = [\"d.filename\", \"d.provider\", \"d.client_id\", \"d.strategy_name\", \"d.format_name\"]\n            where.append(\"(\" + \" OR \".join(f\"{c} LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\\\'\" for c in cols) + \")\")\n            params += [like] * len(cols)\n        clause = (\"WHERE \" + \" AND \".join(where)) if where else \"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            total = self.conn.execute(f\"SELECT COUNT(*) {_FROM} {clause}\", params).fetchone()[0]\n            rows = self.conn.execute(\n                f\"{_SELECT} {_FROM} {clause} ORDER BY d.id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?\",\n                [*params, limit, offset]).fetchall()\n        return rows, total\n\n    def get_with_review(self, doc_id: int) -> Optional[sqlite3.Row]:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\n                f\"{_SELECT} {_FROM} WHERE d.id = ?\", (doc_id,)).fetchone()\n\n    def add_review(self, doc_id: int, decision: str, note: str = \"\"):\n        with self._lock:\n            self.conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO reviews (document_id, decision, note) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (doc_id, decision, note or None))\n            self.conn.commit()\n\n    def review_history(self, doc_id: int) -> list:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT * FROM reviews WHERE document_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC\",\n                (doc_id,)).fetchall()\n\n    def review_counts(self) -> dict:\n        with self._lock:\n            rows = self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT decision, COUNT(*) AS n FROM reviews \"\n                \"WHERE id IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM reviews GROUP BY document_id) \"\n                \"GROUP BY decision\").fetchall()\n        got = {r[\"decision\"]: r[\"n\"] for r in rows}\n        return {\"approved\": got.get(\"approved\", 0), \"rejected\": got.get(\"rejected\", 0)}\n```\n\nThe search text is escaped before it goes into `LIKE`, so typing `%` searches for a literal percent sign. Check these in the browser:\n\n1. **Sign-in**: a wrong token gives \"That token was not accepted\"; the right one opens the page.\n2. **Look and layout**: clicking a row opens the detail drawer on the right.\n3. **Approve**: open `abc_pms_bad_numbers.pdf`, add a note and click **Approve data**. The \"Need attention\" card drops by one, the row shows an \"Approved by reviewer\" pill, and the history is listed. Click **Reopen** to undo.\n4. **Dismiss**: do the same on a locked or failed document (the button says **Dismiss**).\n5. **Search**: type `xyz` or a client ID.\n6. **Pagination**: temporarily change `const PAGE = 25;` to `3` in `app.js`, hard-refresh, and watch the pager. Change it back afterwards.\n7. **Live updates**: in a second terminal, run `python -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs --db statements.db`, and watch the cards update within 20 seconds without pressing Refresh.\n8. **Numbers**: `13,30,000.00` should appear in lakh grouping, and units like `1,000` should have no decimals.\n\nPaste anything odd, plus any red errors from the browser console.\n\n## Step 7: Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 10b: access token, review actions, search, pagination, polling, redesign\"\ngit push\n```\n\nCheck that `git status` doesn't show `.env`.\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why is review a separate append-only table instead of changing the status?** The original machine verdict (`needs_review`) stays visible, every decision keeps its history, and a mistaken approval can be reopened. Editing the status would erase what the system originally thought.\n2. **Why a custom header rather than a cookie?** A cookie is sent automatically by the browser, so another website could trick it into posting a review (CSRF). A custom header can only be set by our own page, and we enable no CORS, so other sites can't.\n3. **What does approval mean?** The reviewer confirms the *extracted data*. It does not approve the learned config. A `config_relearned` document still has a re-learned config registered before anyone confirms it, which I keep as a limitation.\n4. **Why compare tokens with `hmac.compare_digest`?** A plain `==` can leak how many leading characters matched through timing.\n5. **Why polling?** It's the simplest mechanism that works. Websockets add a persistent connection for a page that updates every few minutes at most.\n6. **Why format numbers as text?** Browsers convert JSON numbers to 64-bit floats. We regroup digits in a string, so the exact decimal is never rounded.\n\n## Update the Review interface section of your limitations note\n\nWhen you write `docs/limitations.md` (Part 11a), use this in place of the old section:\n\n````markdown\n## Review interface\n- **Access control is a single shared token**, sent over plain HTTP, with no rate limiting.\n  There are no user accounts, so the review history records the decision and time but not *who*\n  made it. It is meant for localhost only.\n- **Reviewing confirms extracted data, not the learned config.** A re-learned config is\n  registered before a person confirms it; the page cannot approve, revert or edit a config.\n- **Review actions cannot edit data.** A wrong number can be rejected, not corrected.\n- **No consolidated view across providers for one client.** Client identifiers are\n  provider-specific and nothing links them.\n- **Search is a substring match** on file name, provider, client, strategy and format.\n- **Updates are polled every 20 seconds**, not pushed. While a detail panel is open it is not\n  refreshed, so it can lag behind changes made elsewhere.\n- **Display only:** numbers are regrouped as text (exact), but dates and times are shown as\n  stored (UTC for review timestamps).\n- **The JavaScript has no automated tests** beyond two source checks (no HTML injection, no\n  float conversion). Layout is checked by hand.\n````\n\n## What's next\n\nI'd still do **Part 11a** (README, limitations, sample outputs) and then **11b** (design note, AI usage log, demo script). Only the **new** `api.py` returns that field. The old one doesn't, and it also accepts any token without checking it.\n\nThe old server from your earlier browser check is probably still running on port 8000. That explains why you saw the sign-in screen (the new HTML and JavaScript are read from disk on every request) but got old API answers. The tests pass because they build the new app in memory and never touch that process.\n\n## Fix\n\n1. Find the terminal where you ran `python -m app.api` earlier and press **Ctrl+C**. If you can't find it:\n   ```bash\n   lsof -i :8000\n   kill <PID>\n   ```\n   Use the PID number from the output.\n2. Start the new server:\n   ```bash\n   python -m app.api\n   ```\n   Check that it prints an `Access token:` line. If it says the address is already in use, the old server is still running.\n3. In the browser, click **Sign out**, hard-refresh (Cmd+Shift+R), and sign in with the token from the terminal.\n\n## Confirm which server you're talking to\n\nWith the server running, in another terminal:\n\n```bash\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/summary\n```\n\n| Output | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `401` | New server (no token sent, so it refuses) |\n| `200` | Old server is still running |\n\n## If it still fails on the new server\n\nPaste the output of this, replacing `<token>` with your token:\n\n```bash\ncurl -s -H \"X-Review-Token: <token>\" http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/summary\n```\n\nThe response should contain a `\"reviewed\": {\"approved\": 0, \"rejected\": 0}` entry. If it doesn't, we have a real bug and I'll look at `api.py`.\n\nI'm deliberately not making the JavaScript tolerate a missing `reviewed` field. To see live updating, you need to feed the system a statement it hasn't seen.\n\n## A proper live-update test\n\n**1. Prepare the page.** Open it, click the **All** filter (not \"Needs attention\", because a new document that parses cleanly wouldn't appear in that list), and note two things:\n\n- the **Documents** card number (for example 9)\n- the **\"Updated 6:54:12 PM\"** text next to the Refresh button\n\nThen leave the tab in the foreground. Polling pauses when the tab is hidden, and don't press Refresh.\n\n**2. In a second terminal, create and process a brand new statement.** It's an ABC statement for June with a different client, so its bytes are new:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p data\npython -c \"\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom samples.generate import render_pdf\nfrom samples.next_month import abc_may\ns = abc_may()\ns.client_id = 'AB9999'\ns.period_start, s.period_end = date(2026, 6, 1), date(2026, 6, 30)\ns.transactions[0].date = date(2026, 6, 29)\nrender_pdf('abc_pms', s, Path('data/live_demo.pdf'))\nprint('created data/live_demo.pdf')\n\"\npython -m app.pipeline data/live_demo.pdf --db statements.db\n```\n\nThe pipeline should print `parsed_ok ... match=match llm=no`, since ABC is a known format. This also demonstrates the core constraint once more.\n\n**3. Switch back to the browser and just wait**, up to 20 seconds, without touching anything.\n\n## What should change by itself\n\n| Where | Before | After (within ~20 s) |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Documents** card | e.g. 9 | **+1** |\n| **Parsed OK** card | e.g. 5 | **+1** |\n| The list (on the All filter) | | A new row `live_demo.pdf` appears at the top, client `AB9999`, period `2026-06-01 \u2192 2026-06-30` |\n| \"Updated \u2026\" text next to Refresh | old time | A newer time. This one changes on **every** poll, even when the data didn't, so it proves polling is running |\n\nIf you also want to see the \"Need attention\" card move, run the same command with the tampered variant. Replace `abc_may()` with `abc_may(tamper=True)` and the output filename with `data/live_demo_bad.pdf` in both places. That one lands in `needs_review`, so the red/amber card goes up by one.\n\n## If nothing changes after 30 seconds\n\n- The \"Updated\" time doesn't move: the tab was in the background or the sign-in expired. Hard-refresh and sign in again.\n- The time moves but the counts don't: the pipeline wrote to a different database. The page reads `statements.db` in the folder where you ran `python -m app.api`, so check both terminals are in the project root.\n- Paste the pipeline's output and I'll look.\n\n## Why it's built this way\n\nThe page asks the server for fresh numbers every 20 seconds (polling). It deliberately leaves the open detail panel alone while polling, so a note you're typing doesn't get wiped. That's why the list and cards update but an open drawer doesn't. You can say that in the interview, and it's already in the limitations note.\n\n## Commit and continue\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Part 10b: access token, review actions, search, pagination, polling, redesign\"\ngit push\n```\n\n`data/` is gitignored, so the demo PDF won't be committed. Now we can move on to **Part 11a** (the README, the limitations note and the sample output export) and then **11b** (the design note, the AI usage log, the demo script and the submission email). I'll use the updated Review interface section from earlier and add `REVIEW_TOKEN` to the README's configuration table. Email ingestion | Done: read-only IMAP, a scored classifier, and the decision for each email is recorded |\n| 2. Document handling | PDF and passwords done. **Excel/CSV is not built** (the brief calls it \"a plus\") |\n| 3. Format recognition | Done: fingerprint, registry, and the MATCH/DRIFT/UNKNOWN verdicts |\n| 4. Learning a new format | Done: Gemini writes a config once, four gates check it, and it's stored |\n| 5. Deterministic parsing | Done: the stored config only, and a test proves a second statement makes zero LLM calls |\n| 6. Standard output | Done: one schema covers PMS and AIF |\n| 7. Validation | Done: errors, warnings, and skipped checks are all reported |\n| 8. Review and visibility | Done: web page with search, review actions, and a token |\n\nThe stretch goals:\n- **Layout drift** is done.\n- **Several statements in one email** is done (each PDF is handled separately). One PDF holding several clients is not.\n- **A consolidated view across providers** is not built, for the reason I gave earlier.\n\nSo the core objectives are met. What's still missing from the submission is the writing: the README, the limitations note, the design note, the AI usage log and the demo video.\n\n## What I'd worry about\n\nEverything we've tested came from five PDFs that I generated and a configuration that I wrote. That shows the design is consistent, but not that it copes with real statements. The brief says the interviewers will run it on \"statements you have not seen before,\" some \"deliberately messy.\" The failures I'd expect are all already on our limitations list:\n\n1. A **holdings table that continues onto page 2** (the engine stops at the page break).\n2. **Wrapped rows**, where a long security name takes two lines.\n3. **Repeated headers or footers** on every page.\n4. **Subtotal rows** inside a table.\n\nOf these, a multi-page table and repeated headers are the most likely in real statements, so I'd fix those first. Excel/CSV support is optional, and I'd do it only if everything else is finished.\n\n## Suggested plan (today is the 11th, the deadline is the 17th)\n\n| Day | Work |\n|---|---|\n| 12th | Harden the engine: multi-page tables, repeated page headers, wrapped rows, with tests |\n| 13th | Stress test: make 3 or 4 deliberately messy PDFs (a different layout from our five) and run the whole flow, including the live LLM. Fix what breaks, and log the rest as limitations |\n| 14th | Documents: README, limitations, design note, AI usage log |\n| 15th | Record the demo video |\n| 16th | Clean-up, secrets check, a rehearsal, **and submit** |\n\nSubmit on the 16th. A buffer day matters more than one more feature. For the secrets check:\n\n```bash\ngit ls-files | grep -iE \"\\.env|\\.db|credentials|token\"\n```\n\nIt should print nothing except `.env.example`.\n\n## The demo\n\nThere are two separate demos, and you need both.\n\n**1. The video** (linked in your submission email, 5 to 7 minutes). Keep it to this order:\n\n1. The problem and the one rule, in 30 seconds: the LLM is called only for unseen formats.\n2. Reset and start: `rm -f statements.db && python -m samples.generate && python -m samples.next_month`.\n3. Run `python -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs` and read the output aloud. Point out `llm=yes` for new formats and `llm=no` for the May statement.\n4. Open the review page. Show a flagged statement (bad numbers) with its errors and passed checks, then a parsed one. Approve one and show the history.\n5. Open the Learned formats tab and show the stored config: \"this is what the LLM wrote, accepted only after four checks\".\n6. Email: send a test email, run `python -m app.email_ingest`, and show the decoy PDF being skipped, with its reasons.\n7. Close with the limitations: two or three honest ones.\n\n**2. The live interview** (\"bring your laptop with the solution running\"). Before you go in:\n\n- Run the whole flow once on a clean database, so you know it works that day.\n- Have `.env` filled in and the review page open.\n- Check your internet and the Gemini key right before the call.\n- Have the demo video as a backup, in case Gemini returns a 503 (we saw one).\n\nWhen they hand you an unseen statement, drop it in a folder and run `python -m app.pipeline <folder>`. If it fails, don't hide it. Show the status, read the error, and explain what would fix it. The brief says \"handles unfamiliar input without silent errors\", and a clear failure scores better than a pretended success.\n\n## What you must be able to do\n\n- **Explain every file.** \"The AI wrote that part\" is not an answer, and the brief says so. We should rehearse this: I can quiz you file by file.\n- **Answer the four hard questions** (recognise, store, verify, drift) in your own words.\n- **Absorb a changed requirement.** Likely ones: a new field (schema, config spec, prompt), Excel files (a new reader producing the same `Document`), OAuth for Gmail (swap `email_ingest`), another LLM (the `llm.py` interface), or a consolidated view (an investor table linking identifiers).\n\nOne more thing: **the brief requires your AI conversation history.** This chat is that history. Export or save it now, before you lose track of it. The note on \"where it helped and where it misled you\" is the part we've been collecting material for.\n\n## Next step\n\nDo you want to start the hardening work now, beginning with multi-page tables and repeated headers? Or move straight to the documents and leave the engine as it is? I'd harden first, because it's the one place where interview day could go badly.
