"01a12c26-7079-7977-bec1-8d41b4de872d"}, {"uuid": "01a12c2c-b4f5-767b-80c1-846319a26f45", "text": "# Hardening: multi-page tables, page headers and footers, wrapped rows\n\nI haven't run any of this, so treat the tests as the judge.\n\n## What we're fixing\n\n| Messy case | Today | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| Table continues on page 2 | Rows after the page break are dropped | Table continues across pages |\n| Table header repeated on each page | Ends the table | Skipped as a repeat |\n| Running header or `Page 2 of 3` footer | Ends the table or leaks into the data | Removed by the reader, or skipped by the engine |\n| Long name wraps onto a second line | An error or a wrong row | Lines are rejoined into one name |\n| Same header appears twice with a table end between | Silently ignored | **Loud error**: it could be a continuation or a second table, and we can't tell which |\n| A header failure in one table | Hid issues in other tables | Each table reports its own issues |\n\n## The ideas\n\n1. **Page furniture** is margin text that repeats on several pages. The reader detects it by exact text match plus a margin position (top or bottom 60pt). Page numbers are normalised first (`Page 2 of 3` becomes `page #`). Exact matching matters: if I normalised all digits, two different holdings (`Fund 12` and `Fund 14`) could look like repeats and be deleted silently. I nearly designed it that way, and my own test data would have exposed it.\n2. **Wrapped rows** are detected by geometry plus content. A line is a wrap only if it sits very close under the previous one **and** contains only text columns (no numbers, dates or ISINs). Rows with numbers are never merged, so tightly spaced tables don't collapse into one row.\n3. **Fail loudly** when it's ambiguous, as in the rest of the project.\n\nThe geometry threshold is derived from the sample layout: a wrapped line sits 4pt below the previous (half the 8pt line height), while a new row sits 8pt below (a full line height). The cut-off is 0.75 of the line height, between 0.5 and 1.0.\n\n## Step 1: Replace `app/reader.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Reads a PDF into a normalised form: pages -> lines -> cells (with x-positions).\n\nNothing outside this module touches pdfplumber.\n\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport re\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport pdfplumber\nfrom pdfminer.pdfdocument import PDFPasswordIncorrect\nfrom pdfplumber.utils.exceptions import PdfminerException\n\n# Words closer than this (in PDF points) belong to the same cell. A normal space at\n# 8-9pt is about 2-3pt; the gap between adjacent table cells is at least ~12pt.\nCELL_GAP = 5.0\n# Words whose vertical positions differ by less than this are on the same line.\nLINE_TOLERANCE = 3.0\n# Lines this close to the top or bottom edge of a page can be repeating page furniture.\nMARGIN = 60.0\n\n\nclass ReaderError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for all reader failures.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass PasswordRequiredError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The PDF is encrypted and no password was supplied.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass WrongPasswordError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"A password was supplied but it does not open the PDF.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass NoTextLayerError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The PDF has no extractable text (probably a scan). OCR is out of scope.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnreadableDocumentError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The file is corrupt or not a PDF.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Cell:\n    text: str\n    x0: float\n    x1: float\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Line:\n    page: int          # 1-based\n    top: float\n    cells: tuple[Cell, ...]\n    bottom: float = 0.0    # 0.0 = unknown; the engine then never guesses about wrapping\n\n    @property\n    def text(self) -> str:\n        return \" \".join(c.text for c in self.cells)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Document:\n    lines: list[Line] = field(default_factory=list)\n    page_count: int = 0\n    page_heights: dict = field(default_factory=dict)    # page number -> height in points\n\n    @property\n    def text(self) -> str:\n        return \"\\n\".join(line.text for line in self.lines)\n\n\ndef file_sha256(path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Hash of the raw bytes. Used to avoid processing the same file twice.\"\"\"\n    h = hashlib.sha256()\n    with open(path, \"rb\") as f:\n        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b\"\"):\n            h.update(chunk)\n    return h.hexdigest()\n\n\ndef _group_into_lines(words: list[dict], page_no: int, gap: float) -> list[Line]:\n    lines: list[Line] = []\n    current: list[dict] = []\n    current_top: Optional[float] = None\n\n    def flush():\n        if not current:\n            return\n        current.sort(key=lambda w: w[\"x0\"])\n        cells: list[list[dict]] = [[current[0]]]\n        for w in current[1:]:\n            if w[\"x0\"] - cells[-1][-1][\"x1\"] > gap:\n                cells.append([w])\n            else:\n                cells[-1].append(w)\n        lines.append(Line(\n            page=page_no,\n            top=round(min(w[\"top\"] for w in current), 2),\n            cells=tuple(\n                Cell(text=\" \".join(w[\"text\"] for w in group),\n                     x0=round(group[0][\"x0\"], 2), x1=round(group[-1][\"x1\"], 2))\n                for group in cells\n            ),\n            bottom=round(max(w[\"bottom\"] for w in current), 2),\n        ))\n\n    for w in sorted(words, key=lambda w: (w[\"top\"], w[\"x0\"])):\n        if current_top is None or abs(w[\"top\"] - current_top) > LINE_TOLERANCE:\n            flush()\n            current, current_top = [w], w[\"top\"]\n        else:\n            current.append(w)\n    flush()\n    return lines\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ page furniture\n_PAGE_MARKS = [\n    (re.compile(r\"\\bpage\\s*\\d+(\\s*(of|/)\\s*\\d+)?\\b\"), \"page #\"),    # Page 2 / Page 2 of 3\n    (re.compile(r\"^\\W*\\d+\\s*(of|/)\\s*\\d+\\W*$\"), \"# of #\"),          # 2 of 3 / 2/3\n    (re.compile(r\"^\\W*\\d{1,4}\\W*$\"), \"#\"),                          # a lone page number\n]\n\n\ndef _furniture_key(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Exact lower-cased text, except that page numbers are made equal on every page.\n    Other digits are NOT normalised, so two different holdings never look alike.\"\"\"\n    t = \" \".join(text.lower().split())\n    for pattern, replacement in _PAGE_MARKS:\n        t = pattern.sub(replacement, t)\n    return t\n\n\ndef strip_page_furniture(doc: Document, margin: float = MARGIN) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Remove running headers and footers: margin lines whose text repeats on 2+ pages.\n\n    Top margin:    the first page's copy is kept (it is usually the real title).\n    Bottom margin: every copy is removed (footers and page numbers carry no data).\n    A line that appears in the margin of only ONE page is never removed.\n    \"\"\"\n    if doc.page_count < 2:\n        return\n\n    def zone(ln: Line) -> Optional[str]:\n        if ln.top < margin:\n            return \"top\"\n        height = doc.page_heights.get(ln.page)\n        if height and ln.bottom > height - margin:\n            return \"bottom\"\n        return None\n\n    seen: dict = defaultdict(set)\n    for ln in doc.lines:\n        z = zone(ln)\n        if z:\n            seen[(z, _furniture_key(ln.text))].add(ln.page)\n    repeating = {key for key, pages in seen.items() if len(pages) >= 2}\n\n    def is_furniture(ln: Line) -> bool:\n        z = zone(ln)\n        if not z or (z, _furniture_key(ln.text)) not in repeating:\n            return False\n        return z == \"bottom\" or ln.page > 1\n\n    doc.lines = [ln for ln in doc.lines if not is_furniture(ln)]\n\n\ndef read_document(path, password: Optional[str] = None, gap: float = CELL_GAP,\n                  strip_furniture: bool = True) -> Document:\n    path = Path(path)\n    try:\n        pdf = pdfplumber.open(path, password=password or \"\")\n    except PdfminerException as e:\n        # pdfplumber wraps the real pdfminer error; the original is in e.args[0].\n        cause = e.args[0] if e.args else None\n        if isinstance(cause, PDFPasswordIncorrect):\n            if password:\n                raise WrongPasswordError(f\"The password does not open {path.name}\") from e\n            raise PasswordRequiredError(f\"{path.name} is password protected\") from e\n        raise UnreadableDocumentError(f\"{path.name} could not be read: {cause or e}\") from e\n    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:\n        raise UnreadableDocumentError(f\"{path.name} could not be read: {e}\") from e\n\n    doc = Document()\n    with pdf:\n        doc.page_count = len(pdf.pages)\n        for page_no, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):\n            doc.page_heights[page_no] = float(page.height)\n            words = page.extract_words(use_text_flow=False, keep_blank_chars=False)\n            doc.lines.extend(_group_into_lines(words, page_no, gap))\n\n    if not doc.lines:\n        raise NoTextLayerError(f\"{path.name} has no extractable text (scanned PDF?)\")\n    if strip_furniture:\n        strip_page_furniture(doc)\n    return doc\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    # Quick look at what the reader sees:\n    #   python -m app.reader samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf\n    #   python -m app.reader samples/pdfs/xyz_wealth.pdf demo1234\n    import sys\n\n    document = read_document(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)\n    for ln in document.lines:\n        print(f\"p{ln.page} y={ln.top:6.1f} | \" + \" | \".join(c.text for c in ln.cells))\n```\n\n## Step 2: Replace the tables section of `app/engine.py`\n\nAdd `from typing import Optional` to the imports. Then replace everything from the `# tables` comment down to (but not including) the `# assembly` comment with this:\n\n```python\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tables\n# A line is a WRAP of the previous one only if the gap between them is under this fraction\n# of the line height. In our layouts a wrapped line sits half a line-height below (0.5) and\n# a new row a full line-height below (1.0); 0.75 sits between them.\nWRAP_GAP = 0.75\n# These transforms accept almost any text, so they cannot prove that a line is a data row.\nWEAK_TRANSFORMS = {\"text\", \"isin\", \"txn_type\"}\n\n\ndef _overlap(a: Cell, b: Cell) -> float:\n    return max(0.0, min(a.x1, b.x1) - max(a.x0, b.x0))\n\n\ndef _find_header(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str):\n    \"\"\"Index of the first line starting with header_starts_with that holds all columns.\n\n    If a line starts correctly but lacks some required columns, the error names\n    exactly which ones (the likeliest sign that the provider renamed a column).\n    \"\"\"\n    start = _norm(rule.header_starts_with)\n    required = [c.header for c in rule.columns if not c.optional]\n    best_missing = None\n    for i, ln in enumerate(doc.lines):\n        if not _norm(ln.text).startswith(start):\n            continue\n        texts = {_norm(c.text) for c in ln.cells}\n        missing = [h for h in required if _norm(h) not in texts]\n        if not missing:\n            return i\n        if best_missing is None or len(missing) < len(best_missing):\n            best_missing = missing\n\n    if best_missing:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: header line found but column(s) {best_missing} \"\n                      f\"are missing (layout may have changed)\")\n    else:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: no header line starting with \"\n                      f\"{rule.header_starts_with!r}\")\n    return None\n\n\ndef _column_cells(header: Line, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Map each ColumnRule.field -> its header Cell (None if optional and absent).\"\"\"\n    by_text = {_norm(c.text): c for c in header.cells}\n    out = {}\n    for col in rule.columns:\n        cell = by_text.get(_norm(col.header))\n        if cell is None and not col.optional:\n            issues.append(f\"{label}: column {col.header!r} not in header\")\n        out[col.field] = cell\n    return out\n\n\ndef _assign(line: Line, columns: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Assign each cell on the line to the column it overlaps most. Raises on ambiguity.\"\"\"\n    assigned: dict = {}\n    for cell in line.cells:\n        best_field, best = None, 0.0\n        for field_name, hdr in columns.items():\n            if hdr is None:\n                continue\n            o = _overlap(cell, hdr)\n            if o > best:\n                best_field, best = field_name, o\n        if best_field is None:\n            raise TransformError(f\"cell {cell.text!r} sits under no known column\")\n        if best_field in assigned:\n            raise TransformError(\n                f\"two cells ({assigned[best_field]!r}, {cell.text!r}) fall in column \"\n                f\"{best_field!r}\")\n        assigned[best_field] = cell.text\n    return assigned\n\n\ndef _tight(a: Optional[Line], b: Optional[Line]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if b sits directly under a, closer than a new row would.\"\"\"\n    if a is None or b is None or a.page != b.page:\n        return False\n    ha, hb = a.bottom - a.top, b.bottom - b.top\n    if ha <= 0 or hb <= 0:\n        return False                      # no vertical extent recorded: never guess\n    return (b.top - a.bottom) < WRAP_GAP * min(ha, hb)\n\n\ndef _looks_like_data(ln: Line, columns: dict, rules: dict) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Does this line parse as a data row (at least one number or date that reads cleanly)?\"\"\"\n    try:\n        placed = _assign(ln, columns)\n    except TransformError:\n        return False\n    strong = [f for f in placed if rules[f].transform not in WEAK_TRANSFORMS]\n    if not strong:\n        return False\n    try:\n        values = [apply_transform(rules[f].transform, placed[f]) for f in strong]\n    except TransformError:\n        return False\n    return any(v is not None for v in values)\n\n\ndef _append(row: dict, placed: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Add a wrapped line's text after what the row already holds in each column.\"\"\"\n    for f, t in placed.items():\n        row[f] = f\"{row[f]} {t}\" if row.get(f) else t\n\n\ndef extract_table(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> list[dict]:\n    problems: list[str] = []          # this table's own problems; never hidden by other tables\n    idx = _find_header(doc, rule, problems, label)\n    if idx is None:\n        issues.extend(problems)\n        return []\n    header = doc.lines[idx]\n    columns = _column_cells(header, rule, problems, label)\n    if problems:\n        issues.extend(problems)\n        return []\n\n    lines = doc.lines\n    rules = {c.field: c for c in rule.columns}\n    text_fields = {f for f, c in rules.items() if c.transform == \"text\"}\n    stops = [_norm(s) for s in rule.stop_at]\n    header_key = _norm(header.text)\n\n    rows: list[tuple[dict, Line]] = []     # (raw text per field, line the row started on)\n    last_row_line: Optional[Line] = None   # last line that belonged to a row\n    pending: dict = {}                     # text-only lines waiting for the row below them\n    pending_line: Optional[Line] = None\n    ended = False\n\n    for j in range(idx + 1, len(lines)):\n        ln = lines[j]\n        nxt = lines[j + 1] if j + 1 < len(lines) else None\n        text = _norm(ln.text)\n        single = len(ln.cells) == 1\n\n        if ended:\n            # After the table ended, the same header again is ambiguous: a continuation,\n            # or a second table? We cannot tell, so we refuse to guess.\n            if text == header_key:\n                problems.append(\n                    f\"{label}: the header line appears again on page {ln.page} after the \"\n                    f\"table ended; cannot tell a continuation from a second table\")\n                break\n            continue\n\n        if text == header_key:                          # header repeated on a later page\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n            continue\n        if any(text.startswith(s) for s in stops):      # totals row: the table is over\n            ended = True\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n            continue\n        if single and \"continued\" in text:              # \"(continued)\" marker\n            continue\n        if (single and lines[j - 1].page != ln.page and nxt is not None\n                and (_norm(nxt.text) == header_key or _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules))):\n            continue                                    # running header at the top of a page\n\n        try:\n            placed = _assign(ln, columns)\n        except TransformError as e:\n            if single:\n                ended = True                            # a heading far from every column\n            else:\n                problems.append(f\"{label} row {ln.text!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n\n        if all(f in text_fields for f in placed):       # text only: a heading or a wrapped name\n            if pending and _tight(pending_line, ln):    # a third line of a wrapped-above name\n                _append(pending, placed)\n                pending_line = ln\n                continue\n            if rows and not pending and _tight(last_row_line, ln):\n                _append(rows[-1][0], placed)            # wrapped BELOW its row\n                last_row_line = ln\n                continue\n            if nxt is not None and _tight(ln, nxt) and _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules):\n                pending, pending_line = dict(placed), ln    # wrapped ABOVE its row\n                continue\n            if single:                                  # a section heading: the table ended\n                ended = True\n                pending, pending_line = {}, None\n                continue\n\n        row = dict(placed)\n        if pending:\n            if _tight(pending_line, ln):\n                for f, t in pending.items():\n                    row[f] = f\"{t} {row[f]}\" if row.get(f) else t\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n        rows.append((row, ln))\n        last_row_line = ln\n\n    out: list[dict] = []\n    for raw, first_line in rows:\n        try:\n            row = {f: apply_transform(rules[f].transform, raw.get(f)) for f in rules}\n        except TransformError as e:\n            problems.append(f\"{label} row {first_line.text!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n        if any(row.get(f) is None for f in rule.skip_if_blank):\n            continue\n        out.append(row)\n\n    if not out and not problems:\n        problems.append(f\"{label}: header found but no data rows\")\n    issues.extend(problems)\n    return out\n```\n\n## Step 3: Edit `samples/generate.py`\n\nSo we can generate messy PDFs. Add `from typing import Optional` to the imports.\n\n**Replace `make_table`:**\n\n```python\ndef make_table(rows, widths, right_cols=(), header=True, total_row=False, box=False, font=8,\n               repeat_rows=0, valign=None):\n    t = Table(rows, colWidths=widths, hAlign=\"LEFT\", repeatRows=repeat_rows)\n    style = [\n        (\"FONTNAME\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), \"Helvetica\"),\n        (\"FONTSIZE\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), font),\n        (\"TOPPADDING\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 2),\n        (\"BOTTOMPADDING\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 2),\n    ]\n    for c in right_cols:\n        style.append((\"ALIGN\", (c, 0), (c, -1), \"RIGHT\"))\n    if header:\n        style += [(\"FONTNAME\", (0, 0), (-1, 0), \"Helvetica-Bold\"),\n                  (\"LINEBELOW\", (0, 0), (-1, 0), 0.6, colors.black)]\n    if total_row:\n        style += [(\"FONTNAME\", (0, -1), (-1, -1), \"Helvetica-Bold\"),\n                  (\"LINEABOVE\", (0, -1), (-1, -1), 0.6, colors.black)]\n    if box:\n        style += [(\"BOX\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 1, colors.black),\n                  (\"BACKGROUND\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), colors.whitesmoke)]\n    if valign:\n        style.append((\"VALIGN\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), valign))\n    t.setStyle(TableStyle(style))\n    return t\n```\n\n**Replace `abc_story`:**\n\n```python\ndef _wrap_name(name: str, limit: int = 28) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Break a long name over two lines (the PDF shows two lines; the data stays one name).\"\"\"\n    if len(name) <= limit:\n        return name\n    cut = name.rfind(\" \", 0, limit)\n    return name if cut <= 0 else name[:cut] + \"\\n\" + name[cut + 1:]\n\n\ndef abc_story(s: Statement, qty_header: str = \"Qty\", wrap: bool = False,\n              repeat_header: bool = False, valign: Optional[str] = None):\n    sm = s.summary\n    rows = [[\"Security\", \"ISIN\", qty_header, \"Cost\", \"Mkt Price\", \"Mkt Value\", \"Weight %\"]]\n    for h in s.holdings:\n        name = _wrap_name(h.security_name) if wrap else h.security_name\n        rows.append([name, h.isin, qty(h.quantity), indian(h.cost),\n                     indian(h.market_price), indian(h.market_value), str(h.weight_pct)])\n    rows.append([\"Total\", \"\", \"\", indian(sum(h.cost for h in s.holdings)), \"\",\n                 indian(sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings)),\n                 str(sum(h.weight_pct for h in s.holdings))])\n    labels = {T.BUY: \"Buy\", T.SELL: \"Sell\", T.DIVIDEND: \"Dividend\",\n              T.FEE: \"Fee\", T.INFLOW: \"Inflow\", T.OUTFLOW: \"Outflow\"}\n    return [\n        P(\"ABC Portfolio Managers\", TITLE),\n        P(\"Portfolio Statement\", H2),\n        info_row(f\"Client Code: {s.client_id}\",\n                 f\"Period: {d_mon(s.period_start)} to {d_mon(s.period_end)}\"),\n        info_row(f\"Strategy: {s.strategy_name}\", f\"Currency: {s.currency}\"),\n        P(\"Account Summary\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Opening Value\", indian(sm.opening_value)),\n            (\"Add: Inflows\", indian(sm.capital_inflows)),\n            (\"Less: Outflows\", indian(sm.capital_outflows)),\n            (\"Less: Fees Charged\", indian(sm.fees_charged)),\n            (\"Net Gain\", indian(sm.net_gain)),\n            (\"Closing Value\", indian(sm.closing_value)),\n            (\"Cash Balance\", indian(sm.cash_balance)),\n        ]),\n        P(\"Equity Holdings\", H2),\n        make_table(rows, [135, 80, 38, 68, 58, 72, 50], right_cols=(2, 3, 4, 5, 6),\n                   total_row=True, repeat_rows=1 if repeat_header else 0, valign=valign),\n        P(\"Transactions\", H2),\n        txn_table(s, labels, d_mon, indian,\n                  [\"Date\", \"Type\", \"Security\", \"Qty\", \"Amount\"], [70, 60, 190, 50, 90]),\n    ]\n```\n\n**Replace `render_pdf`** and add `_furniture` just above it:\n\n```python\ndef _furniture(canvas, doc):\n    \"\"\"A running header on pages 2+ and a 'Page n' footer on every page.\"\"\"\n    canvas.saveState()\n    canvas.setFont(\"Helvetica\", 7)\n    if doc.page > 1:\n        canvas.drawString(36, A4[1] - 22, \"ABC Portfolio Managers - Confidential\")\n    canvas.drawString(36, 20, f\"Page {doc.page}\")\n    canvas.restoreState()\n\n\ndef render_pdf(name: str, s: Statement, path: Path, furniture: bool = False, **story_kwargs):\n    doc = SimpleDocTemplate(str(path), pagesize=A4, Only page numbers are normalised.\n2. **Why does a wrapped line need both closeness and text-only content?** Closeness alone would merge every row of a tightly spaced table. Content alone would merge section headings. Together they identify wraps.\n3. **Why does a repeated header after the table ended raise an error?** Opening and closing holdings tables often share a header, and merging them would silently double-count. Wrapped numeric cells are not supported.\n- **Page margins are assumed to be 60pt.** Furniture outside that band is not detected.\n- **A table whose header appears again after a totals row or heading is rejected** as\n  ambiguous, so statements with opening and closing holdings under an identical header fail\n  loudly and need review.\n- **A security whose name starts with a `stop_at` word** (for example \"Total Systems Ltd\" with\n  stop word \"Total\") ends the table early. Validation will usually flag the missing rows.\n```\n\n## What's next\n\n1. Send me the test result. "type": "text", "text": "# Hardening: multi-page tables, page headers and footers, wrapped rows\n\nI haven't run any of this, so treat the tests as the judge.\n\n## What we're fixing\n\n| Messy case | Today | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| Table continues on page 2 | Rows after the page break are dropped | Table continues across pages |\n| Table header repeated on each page | Ends the table | Skipped as a repeat |\n| Running header or `Page 2 of 3` footer | Ends the table or leaks into the data | Removed by the reader, or skipped by the engine |\n| Long name wraps onto a second line | An error or a wrong row | Lines are rejoined into one name |\n| Same header appears twice with a table end between | Silently ignored | **Loud error**: it could be a continuation or a second table, and we can't tell which |\n| A header failure in one table | Hid issues in other tables | Each table reports its own issues |\n\n## The ideas\n\n1. **Page furniture** is margin text that repeats on several pages. The reader detects it by exact text match plus a margin position (top or bottom 60pt). Page numbers are normalised first (`Page 2 of 3` becomes `page #`). Exact matching matters: if I normalised all digits, two different holdings (`Fund 12` and `Fund 14`) could look like repeats and be deleted silently. I nearly designed it that way, and my own test data would have exposed it.\n2. **Wrapped rows** are detected by geometry plus content. A line is a wrap only if it sits very close under the previous one **and** contains only text columns (no numbers, dates or ISINs). Rows with numbers are never merged, so tightly spaced tables don't collapse into one row.\n3. **Fail loudly** when it's ambiguous, as in the rest of the project.\n\nThe geometry threshold is derived from the sample layout: a wrapped line sits 4pt below the previous (half the 8pt line height), while a new row sits 8pt below (a full line height). The cut-off is 0.75 of the line height, between 0.5 and 1.0.\n\n## Step 1: Replace `app/reader.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Reads a PDF into a normalised form: pages -> lines -> cells (with x-positions).\n\nNothing outside this module touches pdfplumber.\n\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport re\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport pdfplumber\nfrom pdfminer.pdfdocument import PDFPasswordIncorrect\nfrom pdfplumber.utils.exceptions import PdfminerException\n\n# Words closer than this (in PDF points) belong to the same cell. A normal space at\n# 8-9pt is about 2-3pt; the gap between adjacent table cells is at least ~12pt.\nCELL_GAP = 5.0\n# Words whose vertical positions differ by less than this are on the same line.\nLINE_TOLERANCE = 3.0\n# Lines this close to the top or bottom edge of a page can be repeating page furniture.\nMARGIN = 60.0\n\n\nclass ReaderError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for all reader failures.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass PasswordRequiredError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The PDF is encrypted and no password was supplied.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass WrongPasswordError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"A password was supplied but it does not open the PDF.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass NoTextLayerError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The PDF has no extractable text (probably a scan). OCR is out of scope.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnreadableDocumentError(ReaderError):\n    \"\"\"The file is corrupt or not a PDF.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Cell:\n    text: str\n    x0: float\n    x1: float\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Line:\n    page: int          # 1-based\n    top: float\n    cells: tuple[Cell, ...]\n    bottom: float = 0.0    # 0.0 = unknown; the engine then never guesses about wrapping\n\n    @property\n    def text(self) -> str:\n        return \" \".join(c.text for c in self.cells)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Document:\n    lines: list[Line] = field(default_factory=list)\n    page_count: int = 0\n    page_heights: dict = field(default_factory=dict)    # page number -> height in points\n\n    @property\n    def text(self) -> str:\n        return \"\\n\".join(line.text for line in self.lines)\n\n\ndef file_sha256(path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Hash of the raw bytes. Used to avoid processing the same file twice.\"\"\"\n    h = hashlib.sha256()\n    with open(path, \"rb\") as f:\n        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b\"\"):\n            h.update(chunk)\n    return h.hexdigest()\n\n\ndef _group_into_lines(words: list[dict], page_no: int, gap: float) -> list[Line]:\n    lines: list[Line] = []\n    current: list[dict] = []\n    current_top: Optional[float] = None\n\n    def flush():\n        if not current:\n            return\n        current.sort(key=lambda w: w[\"x0\"])\n        cells: list[list[dict]] = [[current[0]]]\n        for w in current[1:]:\n            if w[\"x0\"] - cells[-1][-1][\"x1\"] > gap:\n                cells.append([w])\n            else:\n                cells[-1].append(w)\n        lines.append(Line(\n            page=page_no,\n            top=round(min(w[\"top\"] for w in current), 2),\n            cells=tuple(\n                Cell(text=\" \".join(w[\"text\"] for w in group),\n                     x0=round(group[0][\"x0\"], 2), x1=round(group[-1][\"x1\"], 2))\n                for group in cells\n            ),\n            bottom=round(max(w[\"bottom\"] for w in current), 2),\n        ))\n\n    for w in sorted(words, key=lambda w: (w[\"top\"], w[\"x0\"])):\n        if current_top is None or abs(w[\"top\"] - current_top) > LINE_TOLERANCE:\n            flush()\n            current, current_top = [w], w[\"top\"]\n        else:\n            current.append(w)\n    flush()\n    return lines\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ page furniture\n_PAGE_MARKS = [\n    (re.compile(r\"\\bpage\\s*\\d+(\\s*(of|/)\\s*\\d+)?\\b\"), \"page #\"),    # Page 2 / Page 2 of 3\n    (re.compile(r\"^\\W*\\d+\\s*(of|/)\\s*\\d+\\W*$\"), \"# of #\"),          # 2 of 3 / 2/3\n    (re.compile(r\"^\\W*\\d{1,4}\\W*$\"), \"#\"),                          # a lone page number\n]\n\n\ndef _furniture_key(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Exact lower-cased text, except that page numbers are made equal on every page.\n    Other digits are NOT normalised, so two different holdings never look alike.\"\"\"\n    t = \" \".join(text.lower().split())\n    for pattern, replacement in _PAGE_MARKS:\n        t = pattern.sub(replacement, t)\n    return t\n\n\ndef strip_page_furniture(doc: Document, margin: float = MARGIN) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Remove running headers and footers: margin lines whose text repeats on 2+ pages.\n\n    Top margin:    the first page's copy is kept (it is usually the real title).\n    Bottom margin: every copy is removed (footers and page numbers carry no data).\n    A line that appears in the margin of only ONE page is never removed.\n    \"\"\"\n    if doc.page_count < 2:\n        return\n\n    def zone(ln: Line) -> Optional[str]:\n        if ln.top < margin:\n            return \"top\"\n        height = doc.page_heights.get(ln.page)\n        if height and ln.bottom > height - margin:\n            return \"bottom\"\n        return None\n\n    seen: dict = defaultdict(set)\n    for ln in doc.lines:\n        z = zone(ln)\n        if z:\n            seen[(z, _furniture_key(ln.text))].add(ln.page)\n    repeating = {key for key, pages in seen.items() if len(pages) >= 2}\n\n    def is_furniture(ln: Line) -> bool:\n        z = zone(ln)\n        if not z or (z, _furniture_key(ln.text)) not in repeating:\n            return False\n        return z == \"bottom\" or ln.page > 1\n\n    doc.lines = [ln for ln in doc.lines if not is_furniture(ln)]\n\n\ndef read_document(path, password: Optional[str] = None, gap: float = CELL_GAP,\n                  strip_furniture: bool = True) -> Document:\n    path = Path(path)\n    try:\n        pdf = pdfplumber.open(path, password=password or \"\")\n    except PdfminerException as e:\n        # pdfplumber wraps the real pdfminer error; the original is in e.args[0].\n        cause = e.args[0] if e.args else None\n        if isinstance(cause, PDFPasswordIncorrect):\n            if password:\n                raise WrongPasswordError(f\"The password does not open {path.name}\") from e\n            raise PasswordRequiredError(f\"{path.name} is password protected\") from e\n        raise UnreadableDocumentError(f\"{path.name} could not be read: {cause or e}\") from e\n    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:\n        raise UnreadableDocumentError(f\"{path.name} could not be read: {e}\") from e\n\n    doc = Document()\n    with pdf:\n        doc.page_count = len(pdf.pages)\n        for page_no, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):\n            doc.page_heights[page_no] = float(page.height)\n            words = page.extract_words(use_text_flow=False, keep_blank_chars=False)\n            doc.lines.extend(_group_into_lines(words, page_no, gap))\n\n    if not doc.lines:\n        raise NoTextLayerError(f\"{path.name} has no extractable text (scanned PDF?)\")\n    if strip_furniture:\n        strip_page_furniture(doc)\n    return doc\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    # Quick look at what the reader sees:\n    #   python -m app.reader samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf\n    #   python -m app.reader samples/pdfs/xyz_wealth.pdf demo1234\n    import sys\n\n    document = read_document(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)\n    for ln in document.lines:\n        print(f\"p{ln.page} y={ln.top:6.1f} | \" + \" | \".join(c.text for c in ln.cells))\n```\n\n## Step 2: Replace the tables section of `app/engine.py`\n\nAdd `from typing import Optional` to the imports. Then replace everything from the `# tables` comment down to (but not including) the `# assembly` comment with this:\n\n```python\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tables\n# A line is a WRAP of the previous one only if the gap between them is under this fraction\n# of the line height. In our layouts a wrapped line sits half a line-height below (0.5) and\n# a new row a full line-height below (1.0); 0.75 sits between them.\nWRAP_GAP = 0.75\n# These transforms accept almost any text, so they cannot prove that a line is a data row.\nWEAK_TRANSFORMS = {\"text\", \"isin\", \"txn_type\"}\n\n\ndef _overlap(a: Cell, b: Cell) -> float:\n    return max(0.0, min(a.x1, b.x1) - max(a.x0, b.x0))\n\n\ndef _find_header(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str):\n    \"\"\"Index of the first line starting with header_starts_with that holds all columns.\n\n    If a line starts correctly but lacks some required columns, the error names\n    exactly which ones (the likeliest sign that the provider renamed a column).\n    \"\"\"\n    start = _norm(rule.header_starts_with)\n    required = [c.header for c in rule.columns if not c.optional]\n    best_missing = None\n    for i, ln in enumerate(doc.lines):\n        if not _norm(ln.text).startswith(start):\n            continue\n        texts = {_norm(c.text) for c in ln.cells}\n        missing = [h for h in required if _norm(h) not in texts]\n        if not missing:\n            return i\n        if best_missing is None or len(missing) < len(best_missing):\n            best_missing = missing\n\n    if best_missing:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: header line found but column(s) {best_missing} \"\n                      f\"are missing (layout may have changed)\")\n    else:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: no header line starting with \"\n                      f\"{rule.header_starts_with!r}\")\n    return None\n\n\ndef _column_cells(header: Line, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Map each ColumnRule.field -> its header Cell (None if optional and absent).\"\"\"\n    by_text = {_norm(c.text): c for c in header.cells}\n    out = {}\n    for col in rule.columns:\n        cell = by_text.get(_norm(col.header))\n        if cell is None and not col.optional:\n            issues.append(f\"{label}: column {col.header!r} not in header\")\n        out[col.field] = cell\n    return out\n\n\ndef _assign(line: Line, columns: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Assign each cell on the line to the column it overlaps most. Raises on ambiguity.\"\"\"\n    assigned: dict = {}\n    for cell in line.cells:\n        best_field, best = None, 0.0\n        for field_name, hdr in columns.items():\n            if hdr is None:\n                continue\n            o = _overlap(cell, hdr)\n            if o > best:\n                best_field, best = field_name, o\n        if best_field is None:\n            raise TransformError(f\"cell {cell.text!r} sits under no known column\")\n        if best_field in assigned:\n            raise TransformError(\n                f\"two cells ({assigned[best_field]!r}, {cell.text!r}) fall in column \"\n                f\"{best_field!r}\")\n        assigned[best_field] = cell.text\n    return assigned\n\n\ndef _tight(a: Optional[Line], b: Optional[Line]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if b sits directly under a, closer than a new row would.\"\"\"\n    if a is None or b is None or a.page != b.page:\n        return False\n    ha, hb = a.bottom - a.top, b.bottom - b.top\n    if ha <= 0 or hb <= 0:\n        return False                      # no vertical extent recorded: never guess\n    return (b.top - a.bottom) < WRAP_GAP * min(ha, hb)\n\n\ndef _looks_like_data(ln: Line, columns: dict, rules: dict) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Does this line parse as a data row (at least one number or date that reads cleanly)?\"\"\"\n    try:\n        placed = _assign(ln, columns)\n    except TransformError:\n        return False\n    strong = [f for f in placed if rules[f].transform not in WEAK_TRANSFORMS]\n    if not strong:\n        return False\n    try:\n        values = [apply_transform(rules[f].transform, placed[f]) for f in strong]\n    except TransformError:\n        return False\n    return any(v is not None for v in values)\n\n\ndef _append(row: dict, placed: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Add a wrapped line's text after what the row already holds in each column.\"\"\"\n    for f, t in placed.items():\n        row[f] = f\"{row[f]} {t}\" if row.get(f) else t\n\n\ndef extract_table(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> list[dict]:\n    problems: list[str] = []          # this table's own problems; never hidden by other tables\n    idx = _find_header(doc, rule, problems, label)\n    if idx is None:\n        issues.extend(problems)\n        return []\n    header = doc.lines[idx]\n    columns = _column_cells(header, rule, problems, label)\n    if problems:\n        issues.extend(problems)\n        return []\n\n    lines = doc.lines\n    rules = {c.field: c for c in rule.columns}\n    text_fields = {f for f, c in rules.items() if c.transform == \"text\"}\n    stops = [_norm(s) for s in rule.stop_at]\n    header_key = _norm(header.text)\n\n    rows: list[tuple[dict, Line]] = []     # (raw text per field, line the row started on)\n    last_row_line: Optional[Line] = None   # last line that belonged to a row\n    pending: dict = {}                     # text-only lines waiting for the row below them\n    pending_line: Optional[Line] = None\n    ended = False\n\n    for j in range(idx + 1, len(lines)):\n        ln = lines[j]\n        nxt = lines[j + 1] if j + 1 < len(lines) else None\n        text = _norm(ln.text)\n        single = len(ln.cells) == 1\n\n        if ended:\n            # After the table ended, the same header again is ambiguous: a continuation,\n            # or a second table? We cannot tell, so we refuse to guess.\n            if text == header_key:\n                problems.append(\n                    f\"{label}: the header line appears again on page {ln.page} after the \"\n                    f\"table ended; cannot tell a continuation from a second table\")\n                break\n            continue\n\n        if text == header_key:                          # header repeated on a later page\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n            continue\n        if any(text.startswith(s) for s in stops):      # totals row: the table is over\n            ended = True\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n            continue\n        if single and \"continued\" in text:              # \"(continued)\" marker\n            continue\n        if (single and lines[j - 1].page != ln.page and nxt is not None\n                and (_norm(nxt.text) == header_key or _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules))):\n            continue                                    # running header at the top of a page\n\n        try:\n            placed = _assign(ln, columns)\n        except TransformError as e:\n            if single:\n                ended = True                            # a heading far from every column\n            else:\n                problems.append(f\"{label} row {ln.text!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n\n        if all(f in text_fields for f in placed):       # text only: a heading or a wrapped name\n            if pending and _tight(pending_line, ln):    # a third line of a wrapped-above name\n                _append(pending, placed)\n                pending_line = ln\n                continue\n            if rows and not pending and _tight(last_row_line, ln):\n                _append(rows[-1][0], placed)            # wrapped BELOW its row\n                last_row_line = ln\n                continue\n            if nxt is not None and _tight(ln, nxt) and _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules):\n                pending, pending_line = dict(placed), ln    # wrapped ABOVE its row\n                continue\n            if single:                                  # a section heading: the table ended\n                ended = True\n                pending, pending_line = {}, None\n                continue\n\n        row = dict(placed)\n        if pending:\n            if _tight(pending_line, ln):\n                for f, t in pending.items():\n                    row[f] = f\"{t} {row[f]}\" if row.get(f) else t\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n        rows.append((row, ln))\n        last_row_line = ln\n\n    out: list[dict] = []\n    for raw, first_line in rows:\n        try:\n            row = {f: apply_transform(rules[f].transform, raw.get(f)) for f in rules}\n        except TransformError as e:\n            problems.append(f\"{label} row {first_line.text!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n        if any(row.get(f) is None for f in rule.skip_if_blank):\n            continue\n        out.append(row)\n\n    if not out and not problems:\n        problems.append(f\"{label}: header found but no data rows\")\n    issues.extend(problems)\n    return out\n```\n\n## Step 3: Edit `samples/generate.py`\n\nSo we can generate messy PDFs. Add `from typing import Optional` to the imports.\n\n**Replace `make_table`:**\n\n```python\ndef make_table(rows, widths, right_cols=(), header=True, total_row=False, box=False, font=8,\n style.append((\"ALIGN\", (c, 0), (c, -1), \"RIGHT\"))\n    if header:\n        style += [(\"FONTNAME\", (0, 0), (-1, 0), \"Helvetica-Bold\"),\n                  (\"LINEBELOW\", (0, 0), (-1, 0), 0.6,    style += [(\"BOX\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 1, colors.black),\n                  (\"BACKGROUND\", (0, 0), (-1, -1), colors.whitesmoke)]\n    if valign:\n        style.append((\"VALIGN\", (0, 0), (-1,   ]),\n        P(\"Equity Holdings\", H2),\n        make_table(rows, [135, 80, 38, 68, 58, 72, 50], right_cols=(2, 3, 4, 5, 6),\n                   total_row=True, repeat_rows=1 if repeat_header else The three PDF tests rely on how ReportLab lays things out, and that's where my estimates could be wrong:\n\n- ReportLab might not render `\\n` inside a cell as two lines.\n- Line spacing might differ from my 12pt estimate, so a threshold could be off.\n- The page counts I assert (`>= 3` and `== 2`) come from estimates.\n\nIf a PDF test fails, paste the pytest error plus this dump, which shows what the reader sees:\n\n```bash\npython -c \"\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nd = read_document('samples/stress_pdfs/stress_two_pages.pdf', strip_furniture=False)\nfor l in d.lines:\n    print(l.page, round(l.top,1), round(l.bottom-l.top,1), ' | '.join(c.text for c in l.cells))\n\" | head -70\n```\n\n## Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Harden engine: multi-page tables, page furniture, wrapped rows, per-table issues\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why does the reader compare exact text for furniture?** Normalising all digits would make `Fund 12` and `Fund 14` look identical, so a real row at the bottom of two pages could be deleted silently. Only page numbers are normalised.\n2. **Why does a wrapped line need both closeness and text-only content?** Closeness alone would merge every row of a tightly spaced table. Content alone would merge section headings. Together they identify wraps.\n3. **Why does a repeated header after the table ended raise an error?** Opening and closing holdings tables often share a header, and merging them would silently double-count. An error costs a human a minute, while silent double counting costs trust.\n4. **Why a threshold of 0.75?** A wrap is half a line-height below, a new row a full line-height. 0.75 sits in the middle.\n5. **What does `test_without_furniture_removal...` prove?** The engine on its own never drops rows quietly. Remove the reader's cleanup and it refuses.\n\n## Update the limitations note\n\nRemove these two items from the PDF section: *\"A table is read from one page only\"* and *\"Wrapped rows are not supported\"*. Add:\n\n```markdown\n- **Multi-page tables work only when the table's own lines are intact.** A running header or\n  footer that appears in the margin of only one page of a two-page document cannot be told apart\n  from content. The engine skips a lone line at the top of a new page only if a data row or\n  the repeated header follows it.\n- **Wrapped names are detected by geometry (a line under 0.75 line-heights below the previous\n  one) and content (text columns only).** In a tightly spaced table, a name wrapped *above*\n  its row is read as belonging to the previous row. Wrapped numeric cells are not supported.\n- **Page margins are assumed to be 60pt.** Furniture outside that band is not detected.\n- **A table whose header appears again after a totals row or heading is rejected** as\n  ambiguous, so statements with opening and closing holdings under an identical header fail\n  loudly and need review.\n- **A security whose name starts with a `stop_at` word** (for example \"Total Systems Ltd\" with\n  stop word \"Total\") ends the table early. Validation will usually flag the missing rows.\n```\n\n## What's next\n\n1. Send me the test result. If the PDF tests need tuning, we'll fix them against the dump.\n2. **Stress test with the live LLM.** We'll build 3 or 4 statements with layouts quite different from our five and see what Gemini and the engine do. Whatever breaks becomes a fix or a limitations entry.\n3. **The code walkthrough you asked for.** When the code is frozen, I'll explain every file in detail: what goes in, what comes out, why it's built that way, and the question an interviewer would ask about it. "01a12c53-7288-7bbb-8a73-3ac120d9c65f", "text": "# One failure, and it's a real bug in my logic\n\n20 of 21 pass, including all three real messy PDFs (3 pages with repeated headers and wrapped names, 2 pages, and names wrapped above their row), and the test that proves the engine fails loudly instead of dropping rows. The failing case is a name wrapped over **three** lines.\n\n## What went wrong\n\nHere is the sequence for `One` / `Two` / `Three + numbers`:\n\n1. The engine reaches `One`, a text-only line. It asks: \"is the line right below me a data row?\"\n2. The line below is `Two`, which is also text-only, so the answer is no.\n3. The engine concludes that `One` is a section heading and **ends the table**. Zero rows come out.\n\nThe two-line wrap worked because there the next line is the data row. My \"wrapped above\" check looked only one line ahead, and a three-line name needs it to look through a chain. The test I wrote exposed it. Without that test, the first statement with a long name would have produced an empty table.\n\n## Fix: edit `app/engine.py`\n\n**1. Add this helper just above `extract_table`:**\n\n```python\ndef _leads_to_data(lines: list, j: int, columns: dict, rules: dict, text_fields: set,\n                   max_lines: int = 4) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if line j is followed, through lines that each sit tightly under the one above,\n    by a data row. That is what a name wrapped over several lines above its row looks like.\n    A heading followed by a far-away table, or by a text line that never reaches data,\n    returns False.\"\"\"\n    k = j\n    for _ in range(max_lines):\n        if k + 1 >= len(lines) or not _tight(lines[k], lines[k + 1]):\n            return False\n        nxt = lines[k + 1]\n        if _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules):\n            return True\n        try:\n            placed = _assign(nxt, columns)\n        except TransformError:\n            return False\n        if not all(f in text_fields for f in placed):\n            return False\n        k += 1\n    return False\n```\n\n**2. In `extract_table`, replace this condition:**\n\n```python\n            if nxt is not None and _tight(ln, nxt) and _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules):\n                pending, pending_line = dict(placed), ln    # wrapped ABOVE its row\n                continue\n```\n\n**with:**\n\n```python\n            if _leads_to_data(lines, j, columns, rules, text_fields):\n                pending, pending_line = dict(placed), ln    # wrapped ABOVE its row\n                continue\n```\n\nThe rest of the function stays as it is. `nxt` is still used by the running-header check earlier in the loop.\n\n## Add one more test\n\nAppend to `tests/test_hardening.py`. It checks the opposite direction: text lines that never reach a data row must still end the table, so the fix doesn't swallow footnotes:\n\n```python\ndef test_text_lines_that_never_reach_a_data_row_still_end_the_table():\n    names, _ = run([\n        ln(1, 100, **HEADER), data(1, 116, \"Alpha\", 1),\n        ln(1, 150, name=\"Notes\"), ln(1, 162, name=\"Some footnote\"),\n    ])\n    assert names == [\"Alpha\"]\n```\n\n## Run\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_hardening.py -v\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\nYou should see 22 passing in that file and about 271 in the full suite. Then the end-to-end check on the real messy PDFs:\n\n```bash\npython -m samples.stress\nrm -f stress.db\npython -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf --db stress.db\npython -m app.pipeline samples/stress_pdfs --db stress.db\n```\n\nThe first command learns ABC and calls Gemini once. The second should print three `parsed_ok match=match llm=no` lines.\n\n## Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Harden engine: multi-page tables, page furniture, wrapped rows, per-table issues\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## For your AI usage log\n\nThis is a clean example for the \"where it misled me\" section. I wrote the wrap detection with a one-line lookahead and tested only the two-line case. A three-line test, written as an edge case, found the gap before any real statement did. The lesson is that the tests need to probe where the logic changes shape (1 line, 2, 3), not just the example you had in mind.\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **How does the engine tell a heading from the start of a wrapped name?** A heading is not followed by a data row through tightly spaced lines. A wrapped name is.\n2. **Why `max_lines=4`?** It bounds the lookahead. A longer text run is far more likely to be prose than a name, and a bounded loop can't scan the whole page.\n\n## What's next\n\nSend me the results of those two commands. If they're green, the engine is frozen, apart from fixes found by the stress test. The failing case is a name wrapped over **three** lines.\n\n## What went wrong\n\nHere is the sequence for `One` / `Two` / `Three + numbers`:\n\n1. The engine reaches `One`, a text-only line. It asks: \"is the line right below me a data row?\"\n2. The line below is `Two`, which is also text-only, so the answer is no.\n3. The engine concludes that `One` is a section heading and **ends the table**. Zero rows come out.\n\nThe two-line wrap worked because there the next line is the data row. My \"wrapped above\" check looked only one line ahead, and a three-line name needs it to look through a chain. The test I wrote exposed it. Without that test, the first statement with a long name would have produced an empty table.\n\n## Fix: edit `app/engine.py`\n\n**1. Add this helper just above `extract_table`:**\n\n```python\ndef _leads_to_data(lines: list, j: int, columns: dict, rules: dict, text_fields: set,\n                   max_lines: int = 4) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if line j is followed, through lines that each sit tightly under the one above,\n    by a data row. That is what a name wrapped over several lines above its row looks like.\n    A heading followed by a far-away table, or by a text line that never reaches data,\n    returns False.\"\"\"\n    k = j\n    for _ in range(max_lines):\n        if k + 1 >= len(lines) or not _tight(lines[k], lines[k + 1]):\n            return False\n        nxt = lines[k + 1]\n        if _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules):\n            return True\n        try:\n            placed = _assign(nxt, columns)\n        except TransformError:\n            return False\n        if not all(f in text_fields for f in placed):\n            return False\n        k += 1\n    return False\n```\n\n**2. In `extract_table`, replace this condition:**\n\n```python\n            if nxt is not None and _tight(ln, nxt) and _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules):\n                pending, pending_line = dict(placed), ln    # wrapped ABOVE its row\n                continue\n```\n\n**with:**\n\n```python\n            if _leads_to_data(lines, j, columns, rules, text_fields):\n                pending, pending_line = dict(placed), ln    # wrapped ABOVE its row\n                continue\n```\n\nThe rest of the function stays as it is. `nxt` is still used by the running-header check earlier in the loop.\n\n## Add one more test\n\nAppend to `tests/test_hardening.py`. It checks the opposite direction: text lines that never reach a data row must still end the table, so the fix doesn't swallow footnotes:\n\n```python\ndef test_text_lines_that_never_reach_a_data_row_still_end_the_table():\n    names, _ = run([\n        ln(1, 100, **HEADER), data(1, 116, \"Alpha\", 1),\n        ln(1, 150, name=\"Notes\"), ln(1, 162, name=\"Some footnote\"),\n    ])\n    assert names == [\"Alpha\"]\n```\n\n## Run\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_hardening.py -v\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\nYou should see 22 passing in that file and about 271 in the full suite. Then the end-to-end check on the real messy PDFs:\n\n```bash\npython -m samples.stress\nrm -f stress.db\npython -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf --db stress.db\npython -m app.pipeline samples/stress_pdfs --db stress.db\n```\n\nThe first command learns ABC and calls Gemini once. The second should print three `parsed_ok match=match llm=no` lines.\n\n## Commit\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Harden engine: multi-page tables, page furniture, wrapped rows, per-table issues\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## For your AI usage log\n\nThis is a clean example for the \"where it misled me\" section. I wrote the wrap detection with a one-line lookahead and tested only the two-line case. A three-line test, written as an edge case, found the gap before any real statement did. The lesson is that the tests need to probe where the logic changes shape (1 line, 2, 3), not just the example you had in mind.\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **How does the engine tell a heading from the start of a wrapped name?** A heading is not followed by a data row through tightly spaced lines. A wrapped name is.\n2. **Why `max_lines=4`?** It bounds the lookahead. A longer text run is far more likely to be prose than a name, and a bounded loop can't scan the whole page.\n\n## What's next\n\nSend me the results of those two commands. If they're green, the engine is frozen, apart from fixes found by the stress test. Then:\n\n1. **Stress test with live Gemini**: I'll give you 3 or 4 deliberately different layouts (for example, a statement with a side-by-side summary box, one with negative numbers in both styles, and one with a two-line header). We run them and log what breaks.\n2. **The code walkthrough you asked for**: each file, what goes in, what comes out, why it exists, and the likely interview question, followed by a quiz.\n\nWhich would you like first? I'd do the walkthrough first, since the stress test may need a fix and the walkthrough is easier to learn while the code is stable.", "citations": []}], "sender": "assistant", "created_at": "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a12c53-7288-7bbb-8a73-3ac120d9c65f"}, {"uuid": "01a12ebe-c389-7e9a-820d-9e10aac892ab", "text": "# The stress test passes end to end\n\nYour output shows the core constraint again, this time on messy input. ABC was learned once (`llm=yes`), and then a 3-page statement with repeated headers and page footers, a 2-page one, and one with wrapped names all parsed with `llm=no`. Nothing was dropped, and the three-line-wrap fix didn't break the others.\n\nYou didn't paste the final `pytest` run, so confirm it and commit:\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -q\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Harden engine: multi-page tables, page furniture, wrapped rows, per-table issues\"\ngit push\n```\n\nI'm treating the code as frozen, except for fixes the interview turns up. The live-Gemini stress test with unfamiliar layouts is still worth doing afterwards, but understanding your own code comes first.\n\n---\n\n# Code walkthrough, part 1 of 3: from PDF to fingerprint\n\nParts 2 and 3 follow, and each ends with a short quiz. I'll go through each file in the order data flows through it, with its role, inputs and outputs, how it works, why it's built that way, and the question an interviewer would ask.\n\n## The whole system as one story\n\nA PDF arrives. The **reader** turns it into lines of cells with positions. The **fingerprint** reduces it to the text that never changes month to month, and the **registry** asks whether we've seen that layout. If yes, the **engine** follows the stored config. If no, the **learner** asks Gemini for a config and checks it before storing. **Validation** then checks the numbers, and the **pipeline** assigns a status and saves it. The **email module** feeds PDFs in, and the **API and web page** show the results.\n\n## `schema.py`: the shape of the answer\n\n**Role:** defines the one structure every provider's statement becomes.\n**Out:** `Statement` (with `Summary`, a list of `Holding`, a list of `Transaction`), plus the enums `StatementType` and `TransactionType`.\n\n- **Decimal everywhere.** Floats can't represent 0.1 exactly, and money can't tolerate that.\n- **Almost everything in `Summary` and `Holding` is optional.** A PMS has no NAV per unit, and an AIF has no holdings, so one schema fits both.\n- **Lenient on suspicious data, strict on impossible data.** A bad ISIN is kept, because validation flags it later, while `period_end` before `period_start` is rejected outright.\n- **Small normalisers.** ISINs are uppercased and stripped of spaces, and currency is uppercased.\n\n*Interview question: \"Why can an AIF statement and a PMS statement share one schema?\"* Because the fields that don't apply to one type are optional. Validation, not the schema, decides which fields a given type must have (a PMS must have holdings).\n\n## `transforms.py`: the whitelist of trusted functions\n\n**Role:** converts raw text such as `\"(12,000.00)\"` into a clean value. This file is the **safety boundary** for the LLM.\n**In:** a transform name and a raw string. **Out:** a `Decimal`, a date, a string or an enum, or `None` for an empty cell.\n\n- **`TRANSFORMS` is a dictionary of name to function.** `apply_transform(name, raw)` refuses any name that isn't in it, so an LLM can pick behaviour but never invent it.\n- **`number`** strips currency symbols, treats brackets or a leading or trailing minus as negative, and removes commas. Removing commas handles lakh grouping (`3,45,000`) and international grouping (`345,000`) with one rule.\n- **`number` deliberately rejects `\"1,234 Dr\"`.** `number_drcr` is a separate opt-in transform. Guessing a sign is a silent error, whereas a refusal is a loud one.\n- **`number_abs`** gives the magnitude. XYZ prints fees as `(12,000.00)` while we store fees as positive, so its config uses this.\n- **Dates:** each format is its own transform (`date_dd_mm_yyyy` and so on). Whether `04/05/2026` means 4 May or 5 April is decided by the config, never guessed.\n- **`txn_type`** matches keywords in order (the first match wins) and falls back to `OTHER`, which validation reports as an error.\n\n*Interview question: \"What stops the LLM from running arbitrary code?\"* The config can only name transforms from this registry, and `config_spec` rejects unknown names before anything is stored.\n\n## `isin_util.py`: a free correctness check\n\n**Role:** computes and validates the ISIN check digit, which is a Luhn-style checksum.\n**How:** letters become numbers (A=10 to Z=35), and the Luhn algorithm runs over the resulting digits, doubling every second digit from the right (starting with the rightmost digit of the first 11 characters, because the check digit sits to its right).\n**Used by:** the sample generator (to make valid ISINs) and validation (to catch a misread ISIN with no AI involved).\n\n*Interview question: \"How does a misread digit get caught?\"* About 90% of single-digit errors change the checksum.\n\n## `reader.py`: PDF to lines of cells\n\n**Role:** the only file that touches pdfplumber. Swapping the PDF library would change only this file.\n**In:** a path and an optional password. **Out:** a `Document` with `lines` (each a list of `Cell(text, x0, x1)`), `page_count` and `page_heights`.\n\n1. **Opening.** pdfplumber wraps every pdfminer error in `PdfminerException`, so the reader unwraps it. This produced four distinct errors: password required, wrong password, no text layer (a scan), and unreadable. The pipeline reacts differently to each. (My first version missed that wrapping. Your failing tests caught it.)\n2. **Words to lines.** Words are sorted by position, and those within 3pt vertically form a line.\n3. **Lines to cells.** Within a line, a horizontal gap over 5pt starts a new cell. A word space is about 2 to 3pt and a column gap is at least 12pt.\n4. **Positions are kept.** A blank cell vanishes when text is flattened (XYZ's \"Funds added\" row has no Units value), so counting cells would shift every later value one column left. Positions let the engine place values correctly.\n5. **Page furniture removal.** Lines in the top or bottom 60pt whose text repeats on 2 or more pages are removed. Page numbers are normalised (`Page 2 of 3` becomes `page #`), but other digits are not. That's deliberate: normalising all digits would make `Sample Company 17` and `Sample Company 46` look identical, and a real holding could be deleted. The page-1 copy of a top line (the title) is kept.\n6. **`file_sha256`** hashes the raw bytes, for deduplication later.\n\n*Interview question: \"Why x-positions instead of just text?\"* A blank cell disappears when flattened, so counting cells silently puts values in the wrong column.\n\n## `fingerprint.py`: what stays the same every month\n\n**Role:** reduces a document to the set of text that doesn't change monthly, which is the layout's identity.\n**In:** a `Document`. **Out:** `Fingerprint(labels, digest)`, where `labels` is a set of strings and `digest` is a hash of the sorted set.\n\nThe rule is that **digits mean \"this changes monthly\"**.\n- A line with no digits (a heading or a table header) is kept. If it has a colon, only the keys are kept (`strategy | currency`, not the strategy name). A short heading of 3 or fewer cells is joined into one string (`abc portfolio managers`).\n- A two-cell `label | value` line keeps only the label (`opening value`).\n- A data row (holdings, transactions) with 3 or more cells and numbers is dropped.\n- Labels are lower-cased, currency words are stripped (`cost (inr)` becomes `cost`), and labels with a month name are dropped.\n- `similarity()` is Jaccard: shared labels divided by all labels.\n\n*Interview question: \"What happens when a provider renames one column?\"* The Jaccard score barely moves (one label out of about 17), so the fingerprint can't detect it. The **engine's missing-column check** does, and that's why the pipeline re-learns instead of reporting drift. This is the same split you saw live with `abc_pms_units.pdf`.\n\n## `registry.py`: the memory of learned formats\n\n**Role:** a SQLite table of known formats.\n**Columns:** name, version, fingerprint hash, labels (JSON), config (JSON), created time.\n\n- **`add_format`** stores a fingerprint and a config, and increments the version for a repeated name. A re-learned layout becomes version 2 and keeps version 1.\n- **`match(fp)`** returns `MATCH`, `DRIFT` or `UNKNOWN`. An exact digest match is `MATCH` with a score of 1.0. Otherwise it takes the best Jaccard score: 0.85 or more is `MATCH`, 0.50 to 0.85 is `DRIFT`, and below 0.50 is `UNKNOWN`. It also returns the stored config.\n- Both thresholds are judgement calls, not tuned on a real corpus. Your limitations note says so.\n\n*Interview question: \"Why three outcomes and not two?\"* `DRIFT` means \"a known provider whose layout changed\", which is a distinct signal that should lead to review.\n\n## Quiz for part 1\n\nAnswer these in your own words (no peeking), and send me your answers. I'll correct them and point out gaps.\n\n1. A PDF row has a blank Units cell. What goes wrong if the engine counts cells, and how does the reader prevent it?\n2. Why does `number` raise an error on `\"500.00 Dr\"` instead of returning 500 or -500?\n3. Why does the fingerprint drop `Infosys | INE009A01021 | 150 | ...` but keep `Opening Value | 12,00,000.00` as `opening value`?\n4. A provider renames `Qty` to `Units`. Does the fingerprint notice? What does, and what does the pipeline do next?\n5. Why isn't every digit normalised when removing page footers?\n\nWhen you've answered, I'll continue with **part 2: config spec, engine, validation, LLM client and learner**, which is the core the interviewers will probe hardest.", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-12T06:13:38.661618Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-12T06:13:56.337437Z", "flags": null, "type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "summaries": [{"summary": "Verifying whether the stress test output confirms the fix."}, {"summary": "Planning a multi-part walkthrough of the finished codebase."}, {"summary": "Detailing the core data model and PDF parsing modules."}], "cut_off": false, "truncated": true, "hidden": false, "thinking_hidden": true, "alternative_display_type": null, "signature": null}, {"start_timestamp": "2026-10-12T06:13:56.337481Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-12T06:14:20.911447Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "# The stress test passes end to end\n\nYour output shows the core constraint again, this time on messy input. A short heading of 3 or fewer cells is joined into one string (`abc portfolio managers`).\n- A two-cell `label | value` line keeps only the label (`opening value`).\n- A data row (holdings, transactions) with 3 or more cells and numbers is dropped.\n- Labels are lower-cased, currency words are stripped (`cost (inr)` becomes `cost`), and labels with a month name are dropped.\n- `similarity()` is Jaccard: shared labels divided by all labels.\n\n*Interview question: \"What happens when a provider renames one column?\"* The Jaccard score barely moves (one label out of about 17), so the fingerprint can't detect it. The **engine's missing-column check** does, and that's why the pipeline re-learns instead of reporting drift. This is the same split you saw live with `abc_pms_units.pdf`.\n\n## `registry.py`: the memory of learned formats\n\n**Role:** a SQLite table of known formats.\n**Columns:** name, version, fingerprint hash, labels (JSON), config (JSON), created time.\n\n- **`add_format`** stores a fingerprint and a config, and increments the version for a repeated name. A re-learned layout becomes version 2 and keeps version 1.\n- **`match(fp)`** returns `MATCH`, `DRIFT` or `UNKNOWN`. An exact digest match is `MATCH` with a score of 1.0. Otherwise it takes the best Jaccard score: 0.85 or more is `MATCH`, 0.50 to 0.85 is `DRIFT`, and below 0.50 is `UNKNOWN`. It also returns the stored config.\n- Both thresholds are judgement calls, not tuned on a real corpus. Your limitations note says so.\n\n*Interview question: \"Why three outcomes and not two?\"* `DRIFT` means \"a known provider whose layout changed\", which is a distinct signal that should lead to review.\n\n## Quiz for part 1\n\nAnswer these in your own words (no peeking), and send me your answers. I'll correct them and point out gaps.\n\n1. A PDF row has a blank Units cell. What goes wrong if the engine counts cells, and how does the reader prevent it?\n2. Why does `number` raise an error on `\"500.00 Dr\"` instead of returning 500 or -500?\n3. Why does the fingerprint drop `Infosys | INE009A01021 | 150 | ...` but keep `Opening Value | 12,00,000.00` as `opening value`?\n4. A provider renames `Qty` to `Units`. Does the fingerprint notice? What does, and what does the pipeline do next?\n5.
