They answer the brief's four hard questions.\n\nYou skipped the part 1 quiz, so the answer key is at the end of this message. Try the questions yourself first, then check.\n\n## `config_spec.py`: the rules a config must follow\n\n**Role:** defines what a legal learned config is. It is the **gatekeeper** between the LLM's output and everything else.\n**In:** a dictionary (parsed JSON). **Out:** a validated `FormatConfig`, or a `ValidationError`.\n\nThe config has four kinds of instruction:\n\n| Part | Meaning | Example |\n|---|---|---|\n| `fields` | Single values found by regex over the page text | `client_id`: `Client Code:\\s*(\\S+)` |\n| `summary` | A line whose **first cell** equals a label; read one cell | `opening_value`: label `Opening Value` |\n| `holdings` / `transactions` | A table: header text, stop lines, and column to field to transform | `Mkt Value` to `market_value` with `number` |\n| Top level | `statement_type`, `provider`, `currency`, `format_name` | `pms`, `ABC Portfolio Managers` |\n\nWhat it rejects:\n- **Unknown keys** (`extra=\"forbid\"`), so a hallucinated key fails loudly and isn't ignored.\n- **Unknown transforms**, checked against the registry.\n- **Invalid regexes**, or a regex with fewer capture groups than requested.\n- **Unknown field names**: `fields` must come from a fixed list, `summary` keys must be real `Summary` fields, and table column fields must be real `Holding` or `Transaction` fields with no duplicates. (We added the last check when we realised an invented `\"field\": \"profit\"` would be silently ignored.)\n- A missing `client_id`, `period_start` or `period_end`.\n\n**Why it exists:** the same checks guard hand-written and LLM-written configs. Everything stored in the registry has passed this file.\n\n*Interview question: \"What exactly do you store when you learn a format, and why that representation?\"* A JSON config, validated by Pydantic. I rejected generated Python code because executing LLM output is a security risk (prompt injection), it's hard to audit, and it can't be guaranteed deterministic. A config is data: it can't run anything, a human can read and diff it, and the same engine reads every one. The cost is that a layout my engine can't express can't be learned, and that failure is loud.\n\n## `engine.py`: the generic parser\n\n**Role:** `parse(Document, FormatConfig)` returns a `Statement`. It **knows nothing about any provider**: all provider knowledge is in the config. Same input, same output, no LLM, no randomness.\n**Rule:** never guess. Problems are collected in a list, and a `ParseError` carries all of them at the end.\n\n### Header fields (`extract_fields`)\nRuns each regex over the whole document text (cells of a line joined by one space, lines by newlines) with `re.search`, so the first match wins. It applies the named transform. A missing or unreadable required field is an issue, not a default.\n\n### Summary values (`extract_summary`)\nFinds lines with 2 or more cells whose **first cell equals** the label (case-insensitive) and reads one cell, the last by default. Two details:\n- **Equality, not \"starts with\".** `Total` can't accidentally match `Total Equity`, because a wrong match becomes impossible, not just unlikely.\n- If the same label appears twice with **different values**, that's an error. The engine can't know which is right, so it won't pick one.\n\n### Tables (`extract_table`), the hardest part\n1. **Find the header:** the first line starting with `header_starts_with` that contains every required column as an exact cell. If a line starts correctly but lacks a column, the message names the missing column (probably a rename). If no line starts correctly, the table is gone or the config belongs to another format. These are different human responses.\n2. **Place each cell by x-overlap:** each data cell goes to the header column it overlaps most. Right-aligned numbers and left-aligned text both work. If two cells land in one column, or a cell sits under no column, it's an error. This is what makes XYZ's blank-Units row parse correctly.\n3. **Decide when the table ends:** a `stop_at` prefix (like `Total`), a single-cell heading, or the end of the document. A table now continues across pages.\n4. **Skip page furniture and repeated headers:** a repeated header on a new page, a `(continued)` marker, and a lone running header at the top of a page (only if a header or data row follows it).\n5. **Join wrapped names:** a text-only line is part of a name if it sits tightly under or above a data row. \"Tightly\" means the gap is under 0.75 of a line height, since a wrapped line sits about 0.5 below and a new row about 1.0. Lines with numbers are never merged.\n6. **Refuse ambiguity:** if the same header appears again *after* the table ended, the engine can't tell a continuation from a second table, so it raises an error instead of guessing.\n7. **Each table's issues are its own:** a failure in holdings no longer hides transactions.\n\n### Assembly (`parse`)\nCombines fields, summary, holdings and transactions into a `Statement`. Currency comes from a `currency` field rule, or the config's default. Any Pydantic error becomes a `ParseError` too.\n\n*Interview question: \"Without an AI checking the output, how does the system know a deterministic parse is correct?\"* The engine itself only proves it found values. The next file proves they're consistent.\n\n## `validation.py`: how a deterministic parse is checked\n\n**Role:** looks only at the numbers, with no AI, and asks whether they agree with each other.\n**In:** a `Statement`. **Out:** a `ValidationReport` with `issues`, `passed` checks and `skipped` checks.\n\n| Check | Question it asks | Severity |\n|---|---|---|\n| Closing value present, not negative | Did we get the key figure? | error |\n| PMS has holdings | Did the table parse at all? | error |\n| ISIN checksums | Is each ISIN plausible? | error (bad), warning (missing) |\n| Quantity \u00d7 price \u2248 market value | Did we read the right columns? | error |\n| Holdings + cash \u2248 closing value | Does the table add up? | error |\n| Weights match value \u00f7 (closing or holdings total) | Are percentages consistent? | error |\n| Units \u00d7 NAV \u2248 closing value | AIF consistency | error |\n| 0 \u2264 uncalled \u2264 committed | AIF commitment | error |\n| Opening + inflows \u2212 outflows \u2212 fees + gain \u2248 closing | Does the whole period reconcile? | error |\n| Transaction dates inside the period | Right date format? | error |\n| Unrecognised transaction type (`other`) | Did a label slip through? | error |\n| Fee transactions \u2248 fees charged | Summary vs detail | warning |\n| Currency not INR | Unusual | warning |\n\nDesign choices:\n- **Three outcomes per check: passed, failed, skipped.** Meridian prints no flows, so its reconciliation is *skipped*, never silently passed. The report says so, and the review page shows it.\n- **Errors mean `needs_review`; warnings don't.** Something that's odd but not provably wrong shouldn't block a statement.\n- **A tolerance of 0.1% or 1 rupee, whichever is larger,** because providers round. Too tight causes false alarms, too loose hides errors.\n- **Sign-agnostic where providers differ.** Fee comparisons use absolute values. Reconciliation accepts two formulas (gain before or after fees).\n- **Weights are compared to two denominators** (closing value or holdings total), because providers differ on whether cash is in the base.\n\n*Interview question: \"What can validation not catch?\"* Two errors that cancel out, a statement that prints so little that few checks run (the report lists what was skipped), and cost basis, for which there's no independent figure. All three are on your limitations list.\n\n## `llm.py`: the LLM behind a tiny interface\n\n**Role:** the only file that talks to Gemini. The rest of the system depends on one method, `complete(system, prompt) -> str`, so swapping providers changes one class.\n\n**Failure behaviour** (this is what the brief asked you to document):\n\n| Situation | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No API key | `LLMNotConfiguredError` immediately, before any network call |\n| Network error, 408, 429, 5xx | Retried 4 times with waits of 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds, then `LLMCallError` |\n| 401, 403, 404, 400 | `LLMCallError` immediately, because retrying can't help |\n| Empty or blocked reply | `LLMCallError` |\n\nSettings: `temperature=0`, a JSON response type, and the system instruction passed separately. The model name comes from `LLM_MODEL`. You saw all of this live: the retired model name gave a clear 404, and a 503 spike was retried and then reported.\n\n*Interview question: \"What happens if the LLM call fails?\"* Nothing is stored, the document gets status `learning_failed` with the reason, and it's retried by re-running the pipeline. The system never skips learning silently or invents a config.\n\n## `learner.py`: learning a format once, safely\n\n**Role:** given a document with an unknown layout, obtain a config from the LLM and only accept it if it **proves itself**.\n**In:** a `Document` and an LLM client. **Out:** a `LearnResult` (success, config, parsed statement, report, attempts, failure kind, history of problems).\n\n**The prompt** has four parts: instructions (generated from the live schema and transform list, so it can't drift from the code; a test enforces that every transform has help text), one fictional example (a test confirms the example is a valid config), the statement text, and, on a retry, the previous reply plus the problems found.\n\n**The four gates:**\n1. **Valid JSON** (code fences are tolerated, chatty text isn't).\n2. **`FormatConfig` validation:** the form is right.\n3. **The engine parses the very document it was learned from** without errors: the content matches reality. This catches a label that doesn't exist.\n4. **Validation finds no errors:** the numbers are consistent. This catches a config that reads the wrong column. Our test swaps `Cost` and `Mkt Value`: gates 1 to 3 pass because every value is a valid number, and only the arithmetic exposes it.\n\nOn failure, the problems go back to the LLM, up to 3 attempts. Nothing is stored unless all four gates pass.\n\n**Security:**\n- **The system chooses the stored `format_name`** (a slug of the provider), never the LLM, because it ends up in a database.\n- **Delimiters:** the statement text sits between two markers, and any `<<<` or `>>>` inside the text is neutralised, so a PDF can't forge the end marker and \"escape\" into the instructions.\n- **Gate 3 catches any exception** from an untrusted config, so a bad config can't crash the learner.\n- **The LLM only returns data.** The worst a successful injection can do is produce a config that fails the gates, or one that parses this document correctly but misreads others (the honest limitation).\n\n*Interview question: \"How does the system learn once and then never use the LLM again?\"* The learner stores `fingerprint + config` in the registry, and the next statement of that layout matches the fingerprint and runs the stored config in `engine.py`. The only code path that calls the LLM is `learn_and_register`, and `test_second_statement_of_known_format_makes_zero_llm_calls` proves the second call never happens, with a fake LLM that holds exactly one reply.\n\n## Quiz for part 2\n\n1. A config says the summary label is `Closing Balance`, but the PDF says `Closing Value`. Which gate stops it, and why can't an earlier one?\n2. A config swaps the `Cost` and `Mkt Value` columns. Which gate catches it, and which check actually fires?\n3. Why does a summary label match the *whole* first cell and not a prefix?\n4. A statement's holdings table ends with `Total 11,35,000.00 12,45,000.00`. How does the engine avoid reading that as a holding?\n5. What does it mean when the report says `reconciliation` was *skipped*, and why is that better than passing?\n6. Why does the system, and not the LLM, choose `format_name`?\n\n## Answer key for the part 1 quiz\n\n1. Counting cells would shift every later value one column left, so the amount lands under Units. The reader keeps each cell's x-position, so the engine places values by overlap.\n2. Silent sign guesses are worse than loud failures. `number_drcr` is an explicit opt-in, so a config that uses `number` on a Dr/Cr column fails visibly.\n3. Holdings rows change monthly (security names, quantities), so they'd change the fingerprint for no reason. `Opening Value | 12,00,000.00` is label plus value, and the label never changes, so it's kept as `opening value`.\n4. The fingerprint barely changes, because one label out of about 17 differs. The engine's missing-column check notices it, and the pipeline then re-learns a new config version and flags the document for review.\n5. Normalising every digit would make `Sample Company 17` and `Sample Company 46` look like repeats, and the engine could delete a real row. What does it mean when the report says `reconciliation` was *skipped*, and why is that better than passing?\n6. Why does the system, and not the LLM, choose `format_name`?\n\n## Answer key for the part 1 quiz\n\n1. Counting cells would shift every later value one column left, so the amount lands under Units. The reader keeps each cell's x-position, so the engine places values by overlap.\n2. Silent sign guesses are worse than loud failures. `number_drcr` is an explicit opt-in, so a config that uses `number` on a Dr/Cr column fails visibly.\n3. Holdings rows change monthly (security names, quantities), so they'd change the fingerprint for no reason. `Opening Value | 12,00,000.00` is label plus value, and the label never changes, so it's kept as `opening value`.\n4. The fingerprint barely changes, because one label out of about 17 differs. The engine's missing-column check notices it, and the pipeline then re-learns a new config version and flags the document for review.\n5. Normalising every digit would make `Sample Company 17` and `Sample Company 46` look like repeats, and the engine could delete a real row. Only page numbers are normalised.\n\nWhen you've answered the part 2 quiz, I'll continue with **part 3: pipeline, store, email, API, web page and tests**, followed by a mock interview with the hardest questions in order.", "citations": []}], "sender": "assistant", "created_at": "2026-10-12T20:34:42.601622Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-12T20:34:42.601622Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a131d2-4a2d-75cf-b2dd-f743274d95b9"}, {"uuid": "01a136eb-f59c-7681-b142-a9cacd0ca878", "text": "lets move to part 3", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-13T20:20:04.473842Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-13T20:20:04.473842Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "lets move to part 3", "citations": []}], "sender": "human", "created_at": "2026-10-13T20:20:04.474147Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-13T20:20:04.474147Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a131d2-4a2d-7e5c-b1c5-bb2210ef9165"}, {"uuid": "01a136eb-f59c-7bad-98db-20feaa8155ee", "text": "# Code walkthrough, part 3 of 3: the system around the core\n\nThis part covers everything that turns the parser into an application. Parts 1 and 2 answered \"how is one PDF read and checked?\". This part answers \"what happens to it, who sees it, and what can go wrong around it?\"\n\n## `pipeline.py`: the conductor\n\n**Role:** takes one file and produces one stored result with a status. It contains almost no parsing logic. It calls the other modules in the right order and decides what each outcome means.\n**In:** a path. **Out:** a `ProcessResult` (also saved to the database).\n\n**The flow for one file:**\n1. **Hash the bytes.** If the hash is already stored with status `parsed_ok` or `needs_review`, return it as a duplicate. Nothing else runs.\n2. **Read it,** trying no password first, then each one in `PDF_PASSWORDS`.\n3. **Fingerprint it and ask the registry** for MATCH, DRIFT or UNKNOWN.\n4. **Known format:** run the stored config and validate it, with **no LLM**.\n   - If the match was DRIFT and the config still parses, keep the result but add a `layout_drift` error note.\n   - If the stored config can't parse the document (a renamed column, say), record `stored_config_failed` and go to step 5.\n5. **Unknown format, or the stored config failed:** call `learn_and_register`. This is the **only** place the LLM is reached.\n6. **Decide the status** and save it.\n\n| Status | When |\n|---|---|\n| `parsed_ok` | Parsed, no validation errors, no error-level notes |\n| `needs_review` | A check failed, the layout drifted, or a config was re-learned (`config_relearned` is an error-level note) |\n| `password_required` | Locked and no configured password works |\n| `failed` | Unreadable, scanned, or an unexpected exception |\n| `learning_failed` | New or changed format, but the LLM was unavailable or produced nothing valid |\n\n**Decisions worth knowing:**\n- **Only `parsed_ok` and `needs_review` count as done.** The other three can be retried: add the password, wait for the LLM to recover, re-run, and the same row is updated.\n- **A catch-all turns any unexpected exception into `failed`.** One bad file must never stop a batch. The cost is that our own bugs and bad documents look alike on the review page (a limitation you've already written down).\n- **New formats are accepted automatically** (a warning note) unless `--review-new` is passed, in which case every newly learned format goes to human review.\n\n*Interview question: \"When exactly is the LLM called?\"* Two cases: the format is unknown, or a known format's stored config provably no longer fits (that's effectively a new format). A normal parse of a known format never reaches it. `test_second_statement_of_known_format_makes_zero_llm_calls` proves it with a fake LLM that holds exactly one reply, so a second call would crash the test.\n\n## `store.py`: what we remember\n\n**Role:** a SQLite database of processed documents, emails and human reviews.\n\n| Table | Key | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| `documents` | `file_hash` (unique) | One row per distinct PDF: status, parsed statement as JSON, issues, validation report, format, whether the LLM was used |\n| `emails` | `message_id` (unique) | Every email seen, the decision (`processed`, `skipped`, `no_pdf`), and each attachment's score and reasons |\n| `reviews` | autoincrement id | **Append-only** human decisions (`approved`, `rejected`, `reopened`) with a note and a timestamp |\n\nChoices:\n- **`upsert` requires every column.** A reprocessed file can't keep stale values (say, an old error) from an earlier attempt.\n- **Reviews are a separate append-only table.** The machine's status and data are never edited, so you can always see what the system originally thought, every decision keeps its history, and a mistaken approval can be reopened. The current review of a document is its latest row, found with a join on `MAX(id)`.\n- **\"Needs attention\" is a query:** status is not `parsed_ok` **and** the latest review is missing or `reopened`.\n- **Search escapes `%` and `_`,** so they match literally, and column names come from our own list, never from user input.\n- **One lock around the connection** (`check_same_thread=False`), because the web server uses several threads.\n- Statements are stored as JSON blobs, so there is no cross-provider SQL and no consolidated view (a limitation).\n\n*Interview question: \"Why not just change the status when someone approves?\"* It would erase what the system thought, lose the history, and make mistakes irreversible.\n\n## `email_ingest.py`: getting PDFs in safely\n\n**Role:** connect to the mailbox, decide which attachments are statements, hand only those to the pipeline.\n\n**Reading the mailbox (`ImapMailbox`):**\n- IMAP over SSL with an app password. The folder is opened **read-only** and messages are fetched with `BODY.PEEK`, so the system can never mark, move or delete mail, even through a bug.\n- It searches `SINCE` a date. Dates are formatted by hand, so the system's locale can't break the search.\n- Login failures get a message explaining app passwords. You saw this live: the placeholder address produced `AUTHENTICATIONFAILED`.\n\n**Parsing an email (`parse_email`):**\n- A missing `Message-ID` falls back to a hash of the raw bytes.\n- An attachment must be a PDF by type or name, **and** start with `%PDF-` (the file's magic bytes), and be under 25 MB. A `.pdf` name proves nothing.\n- Filenames are sanitised, so `../../evil.pdf` becomes `evil.pdf` and can't escape the data folder. Attachments are attacker-controlled input.\n\n**Classification (`classify`):** a score per attachment, accepted at 2 or more.\n\n| Signal | Points |\n|---|---|\n| Sender on the allow-list | +3 |\n| Subject mentions statement, portfolio, PMS, AIF, NAV, etc. | +2 |\n| Filename mentions them | +2 |\n| Body mentions them | +1 |\n| Subject mentions invoice, newsletter, etc. | \u22121 |\n| Filename mentions brochure, invoice, factsheet, etc. | \u22123 |\n\nText is split into words first (`abc_pms.pdf` becomes `abc pms pdf`), so word boundaries work and `Navigation` doesn't match `nav`. Every decision records its reasons, so you saw `brochure.pdf` skipped with `score=-3` and why.\n\n**Why classify before the pipeline?** A random PDF must never be sent to an external LLM. That's a privacy and cost point.\n\n**Idempotency at two levels:**\n- **By `Message-ID`:** a cheap header fetch checks whether the email was already handled, so known emails aren't downloaded again.\n- **By file hash** (in the pipeline): a forwarded copy of the same PDF is recognised as a duplicate.\n\n**Important gap:** an email is marked as seen even if its PDF later ended as `learning_failed` or `password_required`. Retry by running `python -m app.pipeline data/attachments`.\n\n*Interview question: \"How do you tell a statement email from any other?\"* Weighted keyword signals with recorded reasons, plus an optional sender allow-list, with every skip logged. The weakness is that a personal bank statement mentions \"statement\" and would pass, so the allow-list is the real defence.\n\n## `api.py` and `web/`: seeing what happened\n\n**Role:** a small API plus a web page for reviewing results.\n\n**API (FastAPI):**\n- Every `/api` call requires an **access token** in an `X-Review-Token` header, compared with `hmac.compare_digest` (a constant-time check, so timing can't leak the token). The token must be at least 16 characters. There are no user accounts, no HTTPS and no rate limiting, so it stays on localhost, and you should say exactly that.\n- **Why a header and not a cookie?** A cookie is sent automatically by the browser, so another website could trick it into posting a review (CSRF). Our own page sets the header explicitly, and with no CORS enabled other sites can't.\n- Endpoints: `summary`, `documents` (paged, filtered, searchable), a document's detail, `emails`, `formats`, and one write: **`POST /documents/{id}/review`**.\n- **Review rules** (violations return HTTP 409): only flagged documents can be reviewed; only `needs_review` documents can be approved (an unreadable file has no data to approve, only to dismiss); `reopen` only after a decision; no second decision without reopening. Input is validated strictly (extra fields rejected, notes limited to 1000 characters).\n- **Headers:** a Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'none'`, scripts only from our own origin), `nosniff` and `no-store`. The interactive docs page is disabled, since it would need external scripts.\n\n**The page (`app.js`):**\n- **Untrusted text is never turned into HTML.** An email subject like `<script>\u2026` is stored and later shown. The `el()` helper only creates elements and text nodes, and a test fails if `innerHTML` and similar calls appear in the file. The CSP is a second layer.\n- **Money is never a float.** The API sends exact decimal strings, and the page regroups the digits into lakh style (`13,30,000.00`) as text. A test fails if `Number(`, `parseFloat` or `toFixed` appear.\n- **Polling every 20 seconds** (not websockets, which would be more machinery than this page needs). Polling skips the open detail panel so a note being typed isn't wiped, and a sequence counter drops stale responses.\n- The token lives in `sessionStorage`, so it disappears when the tab closes.\n\n*Interview question: \"A flagged statement is wrong. Can the reviewer fix it?\"* No. They can approve, reject or reopen, but not edit data. A correction workflow would be a natural extension: an edited-values table plus audit trail, and real authentication so we know *who* edited.\n\n## `samples/`: where the test material comes from\n\n| File | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `sample_data.py` | The **single source of truth**: numbers for five fictional statements, built so everything reconciles |\n| `generate.py` | Draws five differently laid-out PDFs from that data, encrypts XYZ, and writes `expected.json` **from the same objects**, so the answer key can't disagree with the PDF |\n| `next_month.py` | A May ABC statement (known layout) plus two broken variants, for the zero-LLM and drift demos |\n| `stress.py` | Messy ABC variants: many pages, repeated headers and footers, wrapped names |\n| `send_test_email.py` | Puts realistic test emails in your inbox |\n| `export_outputs.py` | Writes the system's per-document output for the submission |\n\nOne honest point: `expected.json` shows **only what the PDF prints** (`NOT_SHOWN`), because XYZ prints no per-share price and Meridian prints no inflow or gain. Otherwise the engine would be graded on data that isn't in the document.\n\n## The tests: what each family proves\n\n| Family | Examples | What it proves |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Golden files** | `test_engine_full`, `test_hardening` | Output equals the answer key, field by field |\n| **Failure paths** | wrong password, scanned PDF, renamed column, LLM down, missing key | Every failure is loud and has the right status |\n| **The core constraint** | one-reply fake LLM in `test_pipeline` | A known format never calls the LLM |\n| **Corruption** | inflated value, wrong ISIN, wrong weight | Validation catches bad numbers |\n| **Security** | hostile filename, forged delimiters, `<script>` subject, token required, no `innerHTML`, no floats | Untrusted input stays inert |\n| **Fakes instead of the network** | `FakeLLM`, `FakeMailbox` | Tests need no key, no Gmail and no internet |\n\nThe honest limit: every test uses synthetic statements **written by the same author** as the configs and the answer keys. The suite shows the design is consistent, not that it handles real statements. Say that before an interviewer does.\n\n## One document, end to end\n\nTake `abc_pms_units.pdf` (the same ABC layout with `Qty` renamed to `Units`), arriving by email:\n\n1. `email_ingest` fetches the message, finds a real PDF, and scores it at 5 or more. It's saved under `data/attachments/<hash>_...pdf`.\n2. The pipeline hashes it: new.\n3. The reader produces lines and cells.\n4. The fingerprint is almost identical to ABC's (one label of about 17 differs), so the registry says **MATCH**.\n5. The engine runs ABC's stored config and raises a `ParseError`: *column 'Qty' not in header*.\n6. The pipeline records `stored_config_failed` and calls the learner, which sends the layout to Gemini.\n7. The four gates pass, and **version 2** of the ABC config is stored.\n8. Status is `needs_review`, with a `config_relearned` note: \"layout changed, please confirm.\"\n9. A reviewer opens it on the page, sees the note, and approves or rejects. The original status stays in the history.\n\nEvery step is either a pure function or a recorded decision.\n\n## Quiz for part 3\n\n1. A forwarded copy of a statement arrives in a second email. List every mechanism that stops it from being processed twice, and say which one fires first.\n2. What can a person do to a `needs_review` document, what can't they do, and what stays unchanged after they approve?\n3. Why is the API token in a header and not a cookie?\n4. Why does `abc_pms_units.pdf` end as `needs_review` and not `parsed_ok`, even though it parsed and validated?\n5. An email's PDF ended as `learning_failed` because Gemini returned a 503. What happens on the next `email_ingest` run, and how do you get it processed?\n6. Why does the page format `1330000.00` as text and not with `Number()`?\n\n## Answer key for the part 2 quiz\n\n1. **Gate 3** (parse the document). Gates 1 and 2 never look at the PDF: the JSON is valid and a label is just a string. Only running the engine on the real document finds that `Closing Balance` doesn't exist.\n2. **Gate 4** catches it, because every value is a valid number and Gate 3 passes. The checks that fire are `holding_arithmetic` (quantity \u00d7 price no longer equals market value) and `holdings_total_mismatch`.\n3. A prefix match would let `Total` match `Total Equity` or `Net Gain` match `Net Gain on Sale`. Equality makes a wrong match impossible, not just unlikely.\n4. `stop_at` contains `Total`. The row's text starts with it, so the table ends before the row and it never becomes a holding. (Meridian uses `Total Equity`.)\n5. The statement doesn't print inflows, outflows or gain, so the check can't run. Reporting \"passed\" would suggest it was verified. Reporting \"skipped\" with a reason tells the reviewer how much was actually checked.\n6. The LLM's output is untrusted and the name is stored and used as an identifier. We derive a slug from the provider ourselves, so a name like `../../evil; DROP TABLE` can't get in. A test covers exactly that string.\n\n## What's next\n\nSend me your answers to the **part 1, 2 and 3 quizzes**, even partial or rough. Explaining it in your own words is what the interview tests, and I'll correct gaps.\n\nAfter that, there are two options. I'd do both:\n1. **A mock interview.** I ask the hard questions in order, including \"run this on a statement you've never seen\", \"add Excel support\", \"add another LLM\" and \"why did you choose X over Y\", and you answer.\n2. **Part 11**: the README, limitations note, design note, AI usage log, demo script and submission email. We've kept the material for these all along, so most of it is assembly.\n\nWhich would you like first? Status is `needs_review`, with a `config_relearned` note: \"layout changed, please confirm.\"\n9. A reviewer opens it on the page, sees the note, and approves or rejects. The outer fence below has four backticks because the README contains code blocks.\n\n````markdown\n# Self-learning PMS/AIF statement parser\n\nReads PMS and AIF statements from email, extracts holdings, transactions and summary\nfigures into one standard structure, and **uses an LLM only the first time it sees a\nstatement layout**. Every later statement in a known layout is parsed by plain code,\nwith no LLM call.\n\nBuilt by <your name> for the Activv Money internship assignment.\nNotes: [design note](docs/design_note.md) \u00b7 [known limitations](docs/limitations.md) \u00b7\n[AI usage log](docs/ai_usage_log.md)\n\n## How it works\n\n```\nGmail (IMAP, read-only) \u2500\u2500\u25ba classify: is this a statement email?\n                                   \u2502 only accepted PDFs continue\n                                   \u25bc\nPDF \u2500\u25ba hash (already done? skip) \u2500\u25ba read (try passwords) \u2500\u25ba fingerprint \u2500\u25ba registry\n                                                                              \u2502\n                      MATCH / DRIFT: parse with the STORED config (no LLM) \u25c4\u2500\u2524\n                      UNKNOWN: ask the LLM once for a config \u2500\u25ba 4 gates \u2500\u25ba store\n                                   \u2502\n                                   \u25bc\n                     validate the numbers \u2500\u25ba parsed_ok / needs_review \u2500\u25ba SQLite \u2500\u25ba review page\n```\n\n**What is \"learned\"?** A JSON config (validated by Pydantic) describing one layout: regexes\nfor header fields, row labels for summary values, and column headers for tables, each paired\nwith a named transform from a fixed whitelist (`number`, `number_abs`, `number_drcr`,\n`percent`, date formats, ...). A config is data, never code, so nothing the LLM returns can\nexecute.\n\n**Four gates before a learned config is stored:**\n1. the reply is a single valid JSON object\n2. it satisfies the config schema (known keys, transforms and fields; valid regexes)\n3. the engine can parse the very document it was learned from, without errors\n4. validation finds no errors in the parsed numbers (holdings + cash = closing value,\n   quantity x price = value, ISIN checksums, weights, reconciliation, ...)\n\nIf a gate fails, the problems are sent back to the LLM (3 attempts in total). Nothing is\nstored unless all four gates pass.\n\n**When the LLM is called:** (a) the format has never been seen, or (b) a known format's\nstored config provably no longer fits the document (the layout changed). A normal parse of\na known format never calls it. `tests/test_pipeline.py` proves this with a fake LLM that\nholds exactly one reply.\n\n## Requirements coverage\n\n| Brief | Status |\n|---|---|\n| Email ingestion | Done: read-only IMAP, scored classifier, every decision recorded |\n| PDF, password-protected PDFs | Done (multi-page tables, repeated headers/footers, wrapped names) |\n| Excel / CSV (\"a plus\") | **Not built** |\n| Format recognition, learning, deterministic parsing | Done |\n| Standard output, validation | Done |\n| Review interface | Done: web page + API with token, search, paging, approve/reject/reopen |\n| Stretch: layout-change detection | Done (DRIFT status; changed layouts are re-learned and flagged) |\n| Stretch: several statements in one email | Done (each PDF handled separately) |\n| Stretch: consolidated view per client | **Not built** (see design note) |\n\n## Setup\n\nPython 3.10+ (developed on 3.13).\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1\npip install -r requirements.txt\ncp .env.example .env               # then edit .env\npython -m app.preflight            # checks the setup (add --llm --mail for live checks)\n```\n\n### Configuration (`.env`, never committed)\n\n| Variable | Needed for | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | learning new formats | Free key from Google AI Studio |\n| `LLM_MODEL` | learning | Default `gemini-3.8-flash`. Models get retired, so this is configurable |\n| `PDF_PASSWORDS` | locked PDFs | Comma-separated, tried in order (e.g. PAN, date of birth) |\n| `REVIEW_TOKEN` | review page | 16+ characters. If unset, a random token is printed at start |\n| `GMAIL_ADDRESS`, `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` | email ingestion | Dedicated test account, app password (2-Step Verification on) |\n| `STATEMENT_SENDERS` | email (optional) | Comma-separated senders or domains treated as trusted sources |\n| `IMAP_HOST`, `MAILBOX_FOLDER` | email (optional) | Defaults `imap.gmail.com`, `INBOX` |\n\nThe demo password of the sample locked PDF is `demo1234` (fake).\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\npython -m samples.generate          # 5 synthetic statements + answer keys\npython -m samples.next_month        # a \"next month\" ABC statement + two broken variants\npython -m samples.stress            # messy ABC variants: 3 pages, wrapped names, footers\n\npython -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs --db statements.db       # a folder, or a single file\npython -m app.pipeline <path> --db statements.db --review-new  # review every new format\n\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2 --dry-run      # classify only, change nothing\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2                # fetch, classify, process\npython -m samples.send_test_email [--may]          # put test emails in your test inbox\n\npython -m app.api --db statements.db               # review page, http://127.0.0.1:8000\npython -m app.learner samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf     # learn one format and print the report\npython -m samples.export_outputs --db statements.db   # write per-document JSON outputs\n```\n\nFailed documents (`password_required`, `failed`, `learning_failed`) are retried by running\nthe pipeline over them again. Saved email attachments are in `data/attachments`.\n\n## Statuses\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `parsed_ok` | Parsed and every runnable check passed |\n| `needs_review` | Parsed, but a check failed, the layout drifted, or a config was re-learned |\n| `password_required` | Encrypted and none of the configured passwords opens it |\n| `failed` | Unreadable, scanned (no text layer), or an unexpected error |\n| `learning_failed` | New format, but the LLM was unavailable or produced no valid config |\n\nValidation checks that cannot run (for example the PDF does not print inflows) are reported\nas *skipped*, never hidden. A reviewer can approve, reject or reopen a flagged document on\nthe page. That never changes the stored status or data.\n\n## LLM provider and failure behaviour\n\nProvider: **Google Gemini** (`google-genai`), model set by `LLM_MODEL`.\n\n| Failure | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No API key | `learning_failed` immediately, clear message, no network call |\n| Network error, 429, 5xx | Retried 4 times with exponential backoff, then `learning_failed` |\n| Other API errors (401, 403, 404) | `learning_failed` immediately (retrying cannot help) |\n| Reply invalid or fails a gate | Problems fed back to the LLM, up to 3 attempts, then `learning_failed` |\n\nNothing is stored for a failed learning attempt. The text of the first document in each new\nlayout is sent to the provider (see the limitations note).\n\n## Project layout\n\n```\napp/\n  reader.py        PDF -> lines -> cells with x-positions; passwords; page furniture\n  fingerprint.py   stable \"label\" set describing a layout; Jaccard similarity\n  registry.py      SQLite store of learned formats (config + fingerprint, versioned)\n  config_spec.py   what a legal config may contain (strict; rejects anything else)\n  transforms.py    whitelist of value parsers the config may name\n  engine.py        generic, provider-agnostic parser: Document + config -> Statement\n  validation.py    arithmetic consistency checks (errors, warnings, skipped)\n  llm.py           Gemini client behind a tiny interface (retries, clear failures)\n  learner.py       prompt + the four gates + retry loop\n  pipeline.py      orchestration, statuses, dedup by file hash\n  store.py         SQLite store: documents, emails, human reviews\n  email_ingest.py  read-only IMAP, statement-email classifier, attachment handling\n  api.py, web/     review API and page\n  preflight.py     pre-demo setup check\nsamples/           synthetic generator, variants, stress files, outputs/\nconfigs/           hand-written reference configs (tests); learned/ = written by the LLM\ntests/             pytest suite (no network or API key needed)\ndocs/              design note, limitations, AI usage log\n```\n\nAt runtime configs are read from the registry in SQLite, not from `configs/`.\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\nNo network or key needed: the LLM and the mailbox are replaced by fakes. All test data is\nsynthetic and written by the same author as the configs (see limitations).\n\n## Data and safety\n\nAll sample data is synthetic: fictional providers, invented client IDs, valid-checksum ISINs,\na fake password. No real client data is in this repository. `.env`, databases and downloaded\nattachments (`data/`) are gitignored.\n````\n\n## Step 3: `docs/limitations.md` (replace the earlier draft)\n\n````markdown\n# Known limitations\n\nEach item says what happens. Where a failure is silent, it says so.\n\n## Reading PDFs\n- **Scanned (image-only) PDFs** are rejected as `failed` (\"no extractable text\"). No OCR.\n- **Only text PDFs generated by one library (ReportLab) were tested.** Real statements add\n  logos, watermarks, rotated text, landscape pages, multi-column page layouts and odd fonts.\n  None of these was tested.\n- **Cells are split at a fixed 5pt gap.** Tightly packed columns can merge into one cell, and\n  large-font headings split into several cells.\n- **Page furniture** (repeating headers/footers) is detected only in the top and bottom 60pt and\n  only when the exact text repeats on 2+ pages (page numbers are normalised). A running header\n  on one page of a two-page document cannot be told apart from content; the engine skips a\n  lone line at the top of a new page only if a data row or the repeated header follows it.\n- **Wrapped names** are joined by geometry (a line less than 0.75 line-heights below the previous\n  one) plus content (text columns only). In a tightly spaced table, a name wrapped *above* its\n  row is attached to the *previous* row. Wrapped numeric cells are not supported.\n- **Subtotal rows inside a table** are read as data unless named in `stop_at`, which ends the\n  whole table. Validation usually flags the resulting total mismatch.\n- **A security whose name starts with a `stop_at` word** (e.g. \"Total Systems\" with stop word\n  \"Total\") ends the table early.\n- **A header that reappears after the table ended is rejected** as ambiguous, so a statement\n  with opening and closing holdings under an identical header fails loudly.\n- **Two columns whose x-ranges overlap** can misplace a cell. The engine errors when two cells\n  land in one column, but not when a single cell lands in the wrong one.\n- **Excel and CSV statements are not supported.** One PDF holding several clients' statements is\n  not split (an email with several PDFs is handled).\n\n## Fingerprint and format recognition\n- **A single renamed column barely changes the similarity score**, so the fingerprint cannot\n  detect it. Detection relies on the engine's missing-column check, which is why a renamed\n  column triggers a re-learn and not a DRIFT status.\n- **Thresholds (0.85 match, 0.50 drift) are judgement, not tuned** on a real corpus.\n- **Header cells containing digits are dropped** from the fingerprint (e.g. \"Q1 Value\"), and\n  short headings are joined with spaces, so the representation is a heuristic.\n- **Currency words are stripped from labels**, so a currency change alone is not detected;\n  currency is read from the statement itself.\n- **Two products of one provider with the same layout share one format**, and so would a\n  white-label template used by several providers.\n- **A DRIFT layout that still parses is flagged but not registered**, so it is flagged again\n  every month until a human acts.\n\n## Config language and engine\n- **Header fields come from regexes over the whole document text, first match wins.** An earlier\n  occurrence of the same label elsewhere on the page would be captured instead.\n- **No protection against slow regexes** (catastrophic backtracking) in an LLM-written config.\n  There is no timeout.\n- **Summary values must be a line whose first cell is the label and whose last cell is the\n  value.** Values above labels, or two label/value pairs side by side, cannot be expressed.\n- **Signs are recorded as printed.** Only the config's transform (`number_abs`, `number_drcr`)\n  decides the sign, so a wrong choice by the LLM flips an amount without any parse error.\n- **One NAV per statement.** Several unit classes, several currencies, or per-tranche capital\n  are not supported. \"Capital called to date\" is printed by one sample and deliberately not stored.\n- **Schema gaps:** realised vs unrealised gains, XIRR, sector, accrued interest and benchmark\n  returns are not captured.\n- **Transaction types are matched by keyword.** An unrecognised label becomes `other`, which\n  validation reports as an error.\n- **Day/month order is chosen by the config.** If the LLM picks the wrong date transform, only\n  the \"transactions within the period\" check can reveal it.\n\n## Learning with the LLM\n- **A learned config is proven on one document only.** It may overfit (e.g. a stop line that\n  works this month). Later statements are still validated numerically, so most breakage shows up\n  as `needs_review`, but a config that is wrong in a way that preserves the arithmetic would\n  not be detected.\n- **Prompt injection is mitigated, not eliminated.** The LLM can only return data, the text is\n  delimited and marked as untrusted, and gates 3 and 4 reject configs that do not really parse.\n  A manipulated config that parses this document correctly but misreads others would pass.\n- **Statement text is sent to a third party** (Gemini) the first time a layout is seen. It\n  contains the client ID, holdings and balances. The free tier may use prompts to improve\n  Google's products. Only synthetic data was used here; real use needs a data agreement and\n  redaction of identifiers before the call.\n- **Prompts are capped at 400 lines or 40,000 characters.** A table past the cut cannot be learned.\n- **One fictional example in the prompt.** Unusual layouts may fail all 3 attempts and end as\n  `learning_failed`.\n- **A newly learned format is accepted automatically** (a warning only) unless `--review-new` is\n  used. A re-learned config for a changed layout is registered before a human confirms it, so a\n  wrong one would match future documents.\n- **Availability:** during development the first model name was retired (404) and one call hit a\n  503 spike. Both are reported clearly; learning is paused, never skipped silently.\n\n## Validation\n- **Errors that cancel out are invisible** (two wrong holdings that offset each other).\n- **A statement that prints little can pass trivially.** The report lists skipped checks (e.g.\n  Meridian has no reconciliation), but nothing fails because many were skipped.\n- **Tolerance is 0.1% or 1 unit.** Reconciliation accepts two formulas (gain before or after fees),\n  which loosens it slightly.\n- **Weights are compared against only two denominators** (closing value or holdings total).\n- **Cost basis is never validated** (no independent figure to compare).\n- **No continuity check across months** (opening value vs last month's closing).\n- **The fee-total check is a warning, not an error.**\n\n## Pipeline and storage\n- **Deduplication is by file bytes.** The same statement re-issued as a different PDF is\n  processed again and can be stored twice.\n- **Failed documents are not retried automatically.** After an email run, a `learning_failed` or\n  `password_required` statement needs the pipeline run over `data/attachments`.\n- **Passwords come from a flat list.** An unlisted password leaves the statement\n  `password_required`, and a password containing a comma cannot be entered.\n- **Statements are stored as JSON blobs**, so there is no cross-provider query and no\n  consolidated view for one client. Client identifiers are provider-specific and nothing links them.\n- **SQLite, one process.** One lock around the connection; no migrations, workers or backups.\n- **Unexpected exceptions become `failed`** with the exception text, so a bug in our code and a\n  bad document look the same on the review page.\n\n## Email\n- **Classification is keyword scoring.** A personal bank statement mentions \"statement\" and\n  passes; a real statement with no keyword in the subject, filename or body, from a sender not in\n  `STATEMENT_SENDERS`, is skipped. Skips are recorded and visible.\n- **PDF attachments only.** Download links, password-in-body emails and other file types are ignored.\n- **Only the first 2,000 characters of the body are read**, and HTML is stripped crudely.\n- **IMAP with an app password** gives broad mailbox access. A production system would use OAuth\n  with a read-only scope. The system opens the mailbox read-only and never changes mail.\n- **Metadata of every email seen is stored** (subject, sender), including unrelated ones.\n- **Downloaded attachments are saved unencrypted** under `data/`.\n- **Attachments over 25 MB are ignored**, and the search window is date-granular.\n\n## Review interface\n- **Access control is a single shared token** over plain HTTP, with no rate limiting. There are\n  no user accounts, so the review history records the decision and time but not *who*. Intended\n  for localhost only.\n- **Reviewing confirms extracted data, not the learned config.** A re-learned config is\n  registered before a person confirms it; the page cannot approve, revert or edit a config.\n- **Reviewers cannot edit data.** A wrong number can be rejected, not corrected.\n- **Search is a substring match**; no pagination of emails or formats.\n- **Updates are polled every 20 seconds.** An open detail panel is not refreshed.\n- **The JavaScript has no automated tests** beyond two source checks (no HTML injection, no float\n  conversion). Layout was checked by hand.\n\n## Testing\n- **Every test uses five synthetic statements and a few variants I generated.** The configs, PDFs\n  and answer keys come from one author, so the suite shows the design is consistent, not that it\n  handles real-world statements.\n````\n\n## Step 4: `docs/design_note.md`\n\nPut your name at the top. Under \"Clarification questions\", say whether you actually asked any.\n\n````markdown\n# Design note\n\n## The problem in one paragraph\nInvestors receive PMS and AIF statements from many providers, each with its own layout. The\nsystem must read them from email into one structure, calling an LLM only when it meets a layout\nit has never seen. Later statements in a known layout must be parsed by deterministic code.\n\n## The four questions from the brief\n\n**1. How does the system recognise a known format?**\nA *fingerprint*: the set of label-like lines (provider name, headings, row labels, table header\nrows) with everything that changes monthly removed. Lines containing digits are dropped (dates,\namounts, holdings, client IDs), so next month's statement has the same fingerprint. Similarity is\nJaccard over the label sets: 0.85+ is a match, 0.50-0.85 is drift, below 0.50 is unknown.\n\n**2. What is stored when it learns, and why that representation?**\nA validated JSON config: regexes for header fields, row labels for summary values, column headers\nfor tables, and a named transform per value. Alternatives I rejected:\n- *LLM-generated Python code.* Maximum flexibility, but executing model output is a security risk\n  (a PDF can inject instructions), it is hard to audit, and nothing guarantees determinism.\n- *An LLM call per statement.* Slow, costly, and different answers for the same input. This is\n  what the brief rules out.\n- *Hashing the whole text as the fingerprint.* It changes every month.\n\nThe cost of the choice: a layout my engine cannot express (values above labels, two tables side\nby side) cannot be learned. That fails loudly and goes to review.\n\n**3. Without an AI, how does the system know a parse is correct?**\nTwo layers. The engine refuses to guess: a missing column, a missing label, two cells in one\ncolumn, or an unreadable number raises an error naming the problem. Then validation checks the\nnumbers against each other: holdings + cash = closing value, quantity x price = market value,\nweights, units x NAV, opening + flows - fees + gain = closing, ISIN checksums, dates within the\nperiod. Errors send the statement to `needs_review`. Checks that cannot run are reported as\n*skipped*, never as passed.\n\n**4. What happens when a known provider quietly changes its layout?**\nThree defences. A renamed column makes the stored config fail in the engine; the pipeline\nre-learns a new config version (the old one is kept) and flags the document for review. A\nmoderate layout change gives a DRIFT fingerprint: if the stored config still parses, the result\nis flagged `layout_drift`. A change that parses but misreads is caught by validation. The\nfingerprint alone cannot see a single renamed column (the score barely moves), which is why the\nengine and validation are the real safety nets.\n\n## Architecture\nreader -> fingerprint -> registry -> (stored config | learner) -> engine -> validation ->\npipeline/store -> API and page. The email module feeds the pipeline. See the README diagram.\nEach module has one job and a narrow interface; the reader is the only file that touches the PDF\nlibrary, and `llm.py` is the only file that touches the provider.\n\n## Where the LLM is, and how it is kept in check\nIt writes a config for an unseen layout, and nothing else. Four gates before storage: valid JSON,\nschema-valid, parses the very document it was learned from, and the parsed numbers validate.\nProblems go back to the LLM (3 attempts). The system, not the LLM, chooses the stored name. The\nstatement text is delimited and marked untrusted. Failure handling is in the README.\n\n## Assumptions (the brief was silent)\n- A *format* is one provider's layout, identified by its fingerprint.\n- Statements are text PDFs; scanned PDFs are out of scope.\n- Passwords come from a configured list, tried in order (real ones are often a PAN or date of birth).\n- Fees and capital outflows are stored as positive amounts; other signs are stored as printed.\n- Currency defaults to INR unless the statement states one.\n- A statement email is recognised by weighted keyword signals plus an optional sender allow-list.\n  Every skip is recorded with its reasons.\n- Newly learned formats are accepted automatically (flagged with a warning) unless `--review-new`.\n- A re-learned config for a known provider always goes to human review.\n- Gmail via IMAP and an app password, opened read-only, on a dedicated test account.\n- All data is synthetic: five fictional providers (3 PMS, 2 AIF), one password-protected.\n- Clarification questions: <say whether you asked any, and what you decided where the brief was silent>\n\n## Trade-offs worth knowing\n| Decision | Gain | Cost |\n|---|---|---|\n| Config instead of code | Safe, auditable, deterministic | Limited to layouts the engine can express |\n| Strict config schema | An LLM's invented keys fail loudly | A few false rejections |\n| Fail loudly on ambiguity | No silent wrong numbers | More statements go to review |\n| Review decisions in their own table | The machine's verdict and its history are never lost | An extra join |\n| Read-only mailbox and API | Bugs cannot damage mail or data | No write-back features |\n| Token auth, localhost | Simple and honest | Not production security |\n| Polling, not websockets | Much less machinery | Up to 20 seconds of lag |\n\n## Testing approach\nGolden files (output equals a generated answer key), failure paths (wrong password, scanned PDF,\nrenamed column, LLM down), corruption tests (validation must catch them), security tests (hostile\nfilenames and subjects, forged prompt delimiters, token required), and a test that counts LLM\ncalls to prove a known format makes none. The LLM and mailbox are replaced by fakes. The weakness:\nall data is synthetic and written by me, so the suite shows consistency, not real-world coverage.\n\n## How the design would absorb changes\n- *Excel input:* a second reader that produces the same `Document` (rows as lines, columns as\n  cells with synthetic positions); fingerprint, engine and validation are reused.\n- *Another LLM:* implement `complete(system, prompt)` for it; nothing else changes.\n- *Gmail OAuth:* replace `ImapMailbox` with a class that has the same three methods.\n- *A new field:* add it to the schema. Allowed summary fields, column fields and the prompt are\n  derived from the schema, so the config rules and the prompt update themselves.\n- *Consolidated view:* add an investor table linking provider client IDs (e.g. by PAN) and\n  aggregate over it. I did not build it because I would have had to invent the identity data.\n- *Corrections:* an edited-values table with an audit trail, after real authentication.\n- *Privacy:* redact identifiers before text goes to the LLM.\n````\n\n## Step 5: `docs/ai_usage_log.md`\n\nThe brief wants your chat history plus a short note on where the AI helped most and where it misled you.
