ap.add_argument(\"--llm\", action=\"store_true\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--mail\", action=\"store_true\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n    raise SystemExit(1 if run_checks(args.llm, args.mail) else 0)\n```\n\n`tests/test_preflight.py`:\n\n```python\nfrom app.preflight import run_checks\n\n\ndef test_missing_key_is_reported(monkeypatch, capsys):\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"GEMINI_API_KEY\", raising=False)\n    failures = run_checks()\n    assert failures >= 1\n    assert \"[FAIL] GEMINI_API_KEY is set\" in capsys.readouterr().out\n```\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/test_preflight.py -q\npython -m app.preflight --llm --mail\n```\n\n## Step 2: `README.md` (replace the earlier draft)\n\nFill in the two `<...>` placeholders. The outer fence below has four backticks because the README contains code blocks.\n\n````markdown\n# Self-learning PMS/AIF statement parser\n\nReads PMS and AIF statements from email, extracts holdings, transactions and summary\nfigures into one standard structure, and **uses an LLM only the first time it sees a\nstatement layout**. Every later statement in a known layout is parsed by plain code,\nwith no LLM call.\n\nBuilt by <your name> for the Activv Money internship assignment.\nNotes: [design note](docs/design_note.md) \u00b7 [known limitations](docs/limitations.md) \u00b7\n[AI usage log](docs/ai_usage_log.md)\n\n## How it works\n\n```\nGmail (IMAP, read-only) \u2500\u2500\u25ba classify: is this a statement email?\n                                   \u2502 only accepted PDFs continue\n                                   \u25bc\nPDF \u2500\u25ba hash (already done? skip) \u2500\u25ba read (try passwords) \u2500\u25ba fingerprint \u2500\u25ba registry\n                                                                              \u2502\n                      MATCH / DRIFT: parse with the STORED config (no LLM) \u25c4\u2500\u2524\n                      UNKNOWN: ask the LLM once for a config \u2500\u25ba 4 gates \u2500\u25ba store\n                                   \u2502\n                                   \u25bc\n                     validate the numbers \u2500\u25ba parsed_ok / needs_review \u2500\u25ba SQLite \u2500\u25ba review page\n```\n\n**What is \"learned\"?** A JSON config (validated by Pydantic) describing one layout: regexes\nfor header fields, row labels for summary values, and column headers for tables, each paired\nwith a named transform from a fixed whitelist (`number`, `number_abs`, `number_drcr`,\n`percent`, date formats, ...). A config is data, never code, so nothing the LLM returns can\nexecute.\n\n**Four gates before a learned config is stored:**\n1. the reply is a single valid JSON object\n2. it satisfies the config schema (known keys, transforms and fields; valid regexes)\n3. the engine can parse the very document it was learned from, without errors\n4. validation finds no errors in the parsed numbers (holdings + cash = closing value,\n   quantity x price = value, ISIN checksums, weights, reconciliation, ...)\n\nIf a gate fails, the problems are sent back to the LLM (3 attempts in total). Nothing is\nstored unless all four gates pass.\n\n**When the LLM is called:** (a) the format has never been seen, or (b) a known format's\nstored config provably no longer fits the document (the layout changed). A normal parse of\na known format never calls it. `tests/test_pipeline.py` proves this with a fake LLM that\nholds exactly one reply.\n\n## Requirements coverage\n\n| Brief | Status |\n|---|---|\n| Email ingestion | Done: read-only IMAP, scored classifier, every decision recorded |\n| PDF, password-protected PDFs | Done (multi-page tables, repeated headers/footers, wrapped names) |\n| Excel / CSV (\"a plus\") | **Not built** |\n| Format recognition, learning, deterministic parsing | Done |\n| Standard output, validation | Done |\n| Review interface | Done: web page + API with token, search, paging, approve/reject/reopen |\n| Stretch: layout-change detection | Done (DRIFT status; changed layouts are re-learned and flagged) |\n| Stretch: several statements in one email | Done (each PDF handled separately) |\n| Stretch: consolidated view per client | **Not built** (see design note) |\n\n## Setup\n\nPython 3.10+ (developed on 3.13).\n\n```bash\npython -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1\npip install -r requirements.txt\ncp .env.example .env               # then edit .env\npython -m app.preflight            # checks the setup (add --llm --mail for live checks)\n```\n\n### Configuration (`.env`, never committed)\n\n| Variable | Needed for | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | learning new formats | Free key from Google AI Studio |\n| `LLM_MODEL` | learning | Default `gemini-3.8-flash`. Models get retired, so this is configurable |\n| `PDF_PASSWORDS` | locked PDFs | Comma-separated, tried in order (e.g. PAN, date of birth) |\n| `REVIEW_TOKEN` | review page | 16+ characters. If unset, a random token is printed at start |\n| `GMAIL_ADDRESS`, `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` | email ingestion | Dedicated test account, app password (2-Step Verification on) |\n| `STATEMENT_SENDERS` | email (optional) | Comma-separated senders or domains treated as trusted sources |\n| `IMAP_HOST`, `MAILBOX_FOLDER` | email (optional) | Defaults `imap.gmail.com`, `INBOX` |\n\nThe demo password of the sample locked PDF is `demo1234` (fake).\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\npython -m samples.generate          # 5 synthetic statements + answer keys\npython -m samples.next_month        # a \"next month\" ABC statement + two broken variants\npython -m samples.stress            # messy ABC variants: 3 pages, wrapped names, footers\n\npython -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs --db statements.db       # a folder, or a single file\npython -m app.pipeline <path> --db statements.db --review-new  # review every new format\n\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2 --dry-run      # classify only, change nothing\npython -m app.email_ingest --days 2                # fetch, classify, process\npython -m samples.send_test_email [--may]          # put test emails in your test inbox\n\npython -m app.api --db statements.db               # review page, http://127.0.0.1:8000\npython -m app.learner samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf     # learn one format and print the report\npython -m samples.export_outputs --db statements.db   # write per-document JSON outputs\n```\n\nFailed documents (`password_required`, `failed`, `learning_failed`) are retried by running\nthe pipeline over them again. Saved email attachments are in `data/attachments`.\n\n## Statuses\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `parsed_ok` | Parsed and every runnable check passed |\n| `needs_review` | Parsed, but a check failed, the layout drifted, or a config was re-learned |\n| `password_required` | Encrypted and none of the configured passwords opens it |\n| `failed` | Unreadable, scanned (no text layer), or an unexpected error |\n| `learning_failed` | New format, but the LLM was unavailable or produced no valid config |\n\nValidation checks that cannot run (for example the PDF does not print inflows) are reported\nas *skipped*, never hidden. A reviewer can approve, reject or reopen a flagged document on\nthe page. That never changes the stored status or data.\n\n## LLM provider and failure behaviour\n\nProvider: **Google Gemini** (`google-genai`), model set by `LLM_MODEL`.\n\n| Failure | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No API key | `learning_failed` immediately, clear message, no network call |\n| Network error, 429, 5xx | Retried 4 times with exponential backoff, then `learning_failed` |\n| Other API errors (401, 403, 404) | `learning_failed` immediately (retrying cannot help) |\n| Reply invalid or fails a gate | Problems fed back to the LLM, up to 3 attempts, then `learning_failed` |\n\nNothing is stored for a failed learning attempt. The text of the first document in each new\nlayout is sent to the provider (see the limitations note).\n\n## Project layout\n\n```\napp/\n  reader.py        PDF -> lines -> cells with x-positions; passwords; page furniture\n  fingerprint.py   stable \"label\" set describing a layout; Jaccard similarity\n  registry.py      SQLite store of learned formats (config + fingerprint, versioned)\n  config_spec.py   what a legal config may contain (strict; rejects anything else)\n  transforms.py    whitelist of value parsers the config may name\n  engine.py        generic, provider-agnostic parser: Document + config -> Statement\n  validation.py    arithmetic consistency checks (errors, warnings, skipped)\n  llm.py           Gemini client behind a tiny interface (retries, clear failures)\n  learner.py       prompt + the four gates + retry loop\n  pipeline.py      orchestration, statuses, dedup by file hash\n  store.py         SQLite store: documents, emails, human reviews\n  email_ingest.py  read-only IMAP, statement-email classifier, attachment handling\n  api.py, web/     review API and page\n  preflight.py     pre-demo setup check\nsamples/           synthetic generator, variants, stress files, outputs/\nconfigs/           hand-written reference configs (tests); learned/ = written by the LLM\ntests/             pytest suite (no network or API key needed)\ndocs/              design note, limitations, AI usage log\n```\n\nAt runtime configs are read from the registry in SQLite, not from `configs/`.\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest -q\n```\n\nNo network or key needed: the LLM and the mailbox are replaced by fakes. All test data is\nsynthetic and written by the same author as the configs (see limitations).\n\n## Data and safety\n\nAll sample data is synthetic: fictional providers, invented client IDs, valid-checksum ISINs,\na fake password. No real client data is in this repository. `.env`, databases and downloaded\nattachments (`data/`) are gitignored.\n````\n\n## Step 3: `docs/limitations.md` (replace the earlier draft)\n\n````markdown\n# Known limitations\n\nEach item says what happens. Where a failure is silent, it says so.\n\n## Reading PDFs\n- **Scanned (image-only) PDFs** are rejected as `failed` (\"no extractable text\"). No OCR.\n- **Only text PDFs generated by one library (ReportLab) were tested.** Real statements add\n  logos, watermarks, rotated text, landscape pages, multi-column page layouts and odd fonts.\n  None of these was tested.\n- **Cells are split at a fixed 5pt gap.** Tightly packed columns can merge into one cell, and\n  large-font headings split into several cells.\n- **Page furniture** (repeating headers/footers) is detected only in the top and bottom 60pt and\n  only when the exact text repeats on 2+ pages (page numbers are normalised). A running header\n  on one page of a two-page document cannot be told apart from content; the engine skips a\n  lone line at the top of a new page only if a data row or the repeated header follows it.\n- **Wrapped names** are joined by geometry (a line less than 0.75 line-heights below the previous\n  one) plus content (text columns only). In a tightly spaced table, a name wrapped *above* its\n  row is attached to the *previous* row. Wrapped numeric cells are not supported.\n- **Subtotal rows inside a table** are read as data unless named in `stop_at`, which ends the\n  whole table. Validation usually flags the resulting total mismatch.\n- **A security whose name starts with a `stop_at` word** (e.g. \"Total Systems\" with stop word\n  \"Total\") ends the table early.\n- **A header that reappears after the table ended is rejected** as ambiguous, so a statement\n  with opening and closing holdings under an identical header fails loudly.\n- **Two columns whose x-ranges overlap** can misplace a cell. The engine errors when two cells\n  land in one column, but not when a single cell lands in the wrong one.\n- **Excel and CSV statements are not supported.** One PDF holding several clients' statements is\n  not split (an email with several PDFs is handled).\n\n## Fingerprint and format recognition\n- **A single renamed column barely changes the similarity score**, so the fingerprint cannot\n  detect it. Detection relies on the engine's missing-column check, which is why a renamed\n  column triggers a re-learn and not a DRIFT status.\n- **Thresholds (0.85 match, 0.50 drift) are judgement, not tuned** on a real corpus.\n- **Header cells containing digits are dropped** from the fingerprint (e.g. \"Q1 Value\"), and\n  short headings are joined with spaces, so the representation is a heuristic.\n- **Currency words are stripped from labels**, so a currency change alone is not detected;\n  currency is read from the statement itself.\n- **Two products of one provider with the same layout share one format**, and so would a\n  white-label template used by several providers.\n- **A DRIFT layout that still parses is flagged but not registered**, so it is flagged again\n  every month until a human acts.\n\n## Config language and engine\n- **Header fields come from regexes over the whole document text, first match wins.** An earlier\n  occurrence of the same label elsewhere on the page would be captured instead.\n- **No protection against slow regexes** (catastrophic backtracking) in an LLM-written config.\n  There is no timeout.\n- **Summary values must be a line whose first cell is the label and whose last cell is the\n  value.** Values above labels, or two label/value pairs side by side, cannot be expressed.\n- **Signs are recorded as printed.** Only the config's transform (`number_abs`, `number_drcr`)\n  decides the sign, so a wrong choice by the LLM flips an amount without any parse error.\n- **One NAV per statement.** Several unit classes, several currencies, or per-tranche capital\n  are not supported. \"Capital called to date\" is printed by one sample and deliberately not stored.\n- **Schema gaps:** realised vs unrealised gains, XIRR, sector, accrued interest and benchmark\n  returns are not captured.\n- **Transaction types are matched by keyword.** An unrecognised label becomes `other`, which\n  validation reports as an error.\n- **Day/month order is chosen by the config.** If the LLM picks the wrong date transform, only\n  the \"transactions within the period\" check can reveal it.\n\n## Learning with the LLM\n- **A learned config is proven on one document only.** It may overfit (e.g. a stop line that\n  works this month). Later statements are still validated numerically, so most breakage shows up\n  as `needs_review`, but a config that is wrong in a way that preserves the arithmetic would\n  not be detected.\n- **Prompt injection is mitigated, not eliminated.** The LLM can only return data, the text is\n  delimited and marked as untrusted, and gates 3 and 4 reject configs that do not really parse.\n  A manipulated config that parses this document correctly but misreads others would pass.\n- **Statement text is sent to a third party** (Gemini) the first time a layout is seen. It\n  contains the client ID, holdings and balances. The free tier may use prompts to improve\n  Google's products. Only synthetic data was used here; real use needs a data agreement and\n  redaction of identifiers before the call.\n- **Prompts are capped at 400 lines or 40,000 characters.** A table past the cut cannot be learned.\n- **One fictional example in the prompt.** Unusual layouts may fail all 3 attempts and end as\n  `learning_failed`.\n- **A newly learned format is accepted automatically** (a warning only) unless `--review-new` is\n  used. A re-learned config for a changed layout is registered before a human confirms it, so a\n  wrong one would match future documents.\n- **Availability:** during development the first model name was retired (404) and one call hit a\n  503 spike. Both are reported clearly; learning is paused, never skipped silently.\n\n## Validation\n- **Errors that cancel out are invisible** (two wrong holdings that offset each other).\n- **A statement that prints little can pass trivially.** The report lists skipped checks (e.g.\n  Meridian has no reconciliation), but nothing fails because many were skipped.\n- **Tolerance is 0.1% or 1 unit.** Reconciliation accepts two formulas (gain before or after fees),\n  which loosens it slightly.\n- **Weights are compared against only two denominators** (closing value or holdings total).\n- **Cost basis is never validated** (no independent figure to compare).\n- **No continuity check across months** (opening value vs last month's closing).\n- **The fee-total check is a warning, not an error.**\n\n## Pipeline and storage\n- **Deduplication is by file bytes.** The same statement re-issued as a different PDF is\n  processed again and can be stored twice.\n- **Failed documents are not retried automatically.** After an email run, a `learning_failed` or\n  `password_required` statement needs the pipeline run over `data/attachments`.\n- **Passwords come from a flat list.** An unlisted password leaves the statement\n  `password_required`, and a password containing a comma cannot be entered.\n- **Statements are stored as JSON blobs**, so there is no cross-provider query and no\n  consolidated view for one client. Client identifiers are provider-specific and nothing links them.\n- **SQLite, one process.** One lock around the connection; no migrations, workers or backups.\n- **Unexpected exceptions become `failed`** with the exception text, so a bug in our code and a\n  bad document look the same on the review page.\n\n## Email\n- **Classification is keyword scoring.** A personal bank statement mentions \"statement\" and\n  passes; a real statement with no keyword in the subject, filename or body, from a sender not in\n  `STATEMENT_SENDERS`, is skipped. Skips are recorded and visible.\n- **PDF attachments only.** Download links, password-in-body emails and other file types are ignored.\n- **Only the first 2,000 characters of the body are read**, and HTML is stripped crudely.\n- **IMAP with an app password** gives broad mailbox access. A production system would use OAuth\n  with a read-only scope. The system opens the mailbox read-only and never changes mail.\n- **Metadata of every email seen is stored** (subject, sender), including unrelated ones.\n- **Downloaded attachments are saved unencrypted** under `data/`.\n- **Attachments over 25 MB are ignored**, and the search window is date-granular.\n\n## Review interface\n- **Access control is a single shared token** over plain HTTP, with no rate limiting. There are\n  no user accounts, so the review history records the decision and time but not *who*. Intended\n  for localhost only.\n- **Reviewing confirms extracted data, not the learned config.** A re-learned config is\n  registered before a person confirms it; the page cannot approve, revert or edit a config.\n- **Reviewers cannot edit data.** A wrong number can be rejected, not corrected.\n- **Search is a substring match**; no pagination of emails or formats.\n- **Updates are polled every 20 seconds.** An open detail panel is not refreshed.\n- **The JavaScript has no automated tests** beyond two source checks (no HTML injection, no float\n  conversion). Layout was checked by hand.\n\n## Testing\n- **Every test uses five synthetic statements and a few variants I generated.** The configs, PDFs\n  and answer keys come from one author, so the suite shows the design is consistent, not that it\n  handles real-world statements.\n````\n\n## Step 4: `docs/design_note.md`\n\nPut your name at the top. Under \"Clarification questions\", say whether you actually asked any.\n\n````markdown\n# Design note\n\n## The problem in one paragraph\nInvestors receive PMS and AIF statements from many providers, each with its own layout. The\nsystem must read them from email into one structure, calling an LLM only when it meets a layout\nit has never seen. Later statements in a known layout must be parsed by deterministic code.\n\n## The four questions from the brief\n\n**1. How does the system recognise a known format?**\nA *fingerprint*: the set of label-like lines (provider name, headings, row labels, table header\nrows) with everything that changes monthly removed. Lines containing digits are dropped (dates,\namounts, holdings, client IDs), so next month's statement has the same fingerprint. Similarity is\nJaccard over the label sets: 0.85+ is a match, 0.50-0.85 is drift, below 0.50 is unknown.\n\n**2. What is stored when it learns, and why that representation?**\nA validated JSON config: regexes for header fields, row labels for summary values, column headers\nfor tables, and a named transform per value. Alternatives I rejected:\n- *LLM-generated Python code.* Maximum flexibility, but executing model output is a security risk\n  (a PDF can inject instructions), it is hard to audit, and nothing guarantees determinism.\n- *An LLM call per statement.* Slow, costly, and different answers for the same input. This is\n  what the brief rules out.\n- *Hashing the whole text as the fingerprint.* It changes every month.\n\nThe cost of the choice: a layout my engine cannot express (values above labels, two tables side\nby side) cannot be learned. That fails loudly and goes to review.\n\n**3. Without an AI, how does the system know a parse is correct?**\nTwo layers. The engine refuses to guess: a missing column, a missing label, two cells in one\ncolumn, or an unreadable number raises an error naming the problem. Then validation checks the\nnumbers against each other: holdings + cash = closing value, quantity x price = market value,\nweights, units x NAV, opening + flows - fees + gain = closing, ISIN checksums, dates within the\nperiod. Errors send the statement to `needs_review`. Checks that cannot run are reported as\n*skipped*, never as passed.\n\n**4. What happens when a known provider quietly changes its layout?**\nThree defences. A renamed column makes the stored config fail in the engine; the pipeline\nre-learns a new config version (the old one is kept) and flags the document for review. A\nmoderate layout change gives a DRIFT fingerprint: if the stored config still parses, the result\nis flagged `layout_drift`. A change that parses but misreads is caught by validation. The\nfingerprint alone cannot see a single renamed column (the score barely moves), which is why the\nengine and validation are the real safety nets.\n\n## Architecture\nreader -> fingerprint -> registry -> (stored config | learner) -> engine -> validation ->\npipeline/store -> API and page. The email module feeds the pipeline. See the README diagram.\nEach module has one job and a narrow interface; the reader is the only file that touches the PDF\nlibrary, and `llm.py` is the only file that touches the provider.\n\n## Where the LLM is, and how it is kept in check\nIt writes a config for an unseen layout, and nothing else. Four gates before storage: valid JSON,\nschema-valid, parses the very document it was learned from, and the parsed numbers validate.\nProblems go back to the LLM (3 attempts). The system, not the LLM, chooses the stored name. The\nstatement text is delimited and marked untrusted. Failure handling is in the README.\n\n## Assumptions (the brief was silent)\n- A *format* is one provider's layout, identified by its fingerprint.\n- Statements are text PDFs; scanned PDFs are out of scope.\n- Passwords come from a configured list, tried in order (real ones are often a PAN or date of birth).\n- Fees and capital outflows are stored as positive amounts; other signs are stored as printed.\n- Currency defaults to INR unless the statement states one.\n- A statement email is recognised by weighted keyword signals plus an optional sender allow-list.\n  Every skip is recorded with its reasons.\n- Newly learned formats are accepted automatically (flagged with a warning) unless `--review-new`.\n- A re-learned config for a known provider always goes to human review.\n- Gmail via IMAP and an app password, opened read-only, on a dedicated test account.\n- All data is synthetic: five fictional providers (3 PMS, 2 AIF), one password-protected.\n- Clarification questions: <say whether you asked any, and what you decided where the brief was silent>\n\n## Trade-offs worth knowing\n| Decision | Gain | Cost |\n|---|---|---|\n| Config instead of code | Safe, auditable, deterministic | Limited to layouts the engine can express |\n| Strict config schema | An LLM's invented keys fail loudly | A few false rejections |\n| Fail loudly on ambiguity | No silent wrong numbers | More statements go to review |\n| Review decisions in their own table | The machine's verdict and its history are never lost | An extra join |\n| Read-only mailbox and API | Bugs cannot damage mail or data | No write-back features |\n| Token auth, localhost | Simple and honest | Not production security |\n| Polling, not websockets | Much less machinery | Up to 20 seconds of lag |\n\n## Testing approach\nGolden files (output equals a generated answer key), failure paths (wrong password, scanned PDF,\nrenamed column, LLM down), corruption tests (validation must catch them), security tests (hostile\nfilenames and subjects, forged prompt delimiters, token required), and a test that counts LLM\ncalls to prove a known format makes none. The LLM and mailbox are replaced by fakes. The weakness:\nall data is synthetic and written by me, so the suite shows consistency, not real-world coverage.\n\n## How the design would absorb changes\n- *Excel input:* a second reader that produces the same `Document` (rows as lines, columns as\n  cells with synthetic positions); fingerprint, engine and validation are reused.\n- *Another LLM:* implement `complete(system, prompt)` for it; nothing else changes.\n- *Gmail OAuth:* replace `ImapMailbox` with a class that has the same three methods.\n- *A new field:* add it to the schema. Allowed summary fields, column fields and the prompt are\n  derived from the schema, so the config rules and the prompt update themselves.\n- *Consolidated view:* add an investor table linking provider client IDs (e.g. by PAN) and\n  aggregate over it. I did not build it because I would have had to invent the identity data.\n- *Corrections:* an edited-values table with an audit trail, after real authentication.\n- *Privacy:* redact identifiers before text goes to the LLM.\n````\n\n## Step 5: `docs/ai_usage_log.md`\n\nThe brief wants your chat history plus a short note on where the AI helped most and where it misled you. This conversation **is** the history. Export or copy it into `docs/ai_chat_history.md` or a PDF, **but first redact personal details**: your test Gmail address (it appears in the `send_test_email` output) and your Mac username in file paths. I don't know claude.ai's exact export menu, so check there, or copy and paste.\n\n````markdown\n# AI usage log\n\nTool: Claude (claude.ai chat), used for design discussion, code and tests. The full\nconversation is in `docs/ai_chat_history.*`. I ran every command and test myself and pasted the\nresults back; the AI never ran any of this code.\n\n## Where it helped most\n- Explaining PMS/AIF statements and the validation arithmetic I did not know.\n- Laying out the build order so I could test the engine with hand-written configs before adding\n  the LLM. That made it possible to tell an engine bug from a bad LLM reply.\n- Writing boilerplate (Pydantic models, FastAPI, test fixtures) and generating messy test PDFs.\n- Thinking of failure modes and security issues I had not considered (stored XSS from email\n  subjects, forged prompt delimiters, CSRF, path traversal in attachment names).\n- Drafting the documents from the history of what actually went wrong.\n\n## How I steered it\n- I chose the hybrid config approach after comparing the three options, and rejected generated code.\n- I asked why there was one AIF and three PMS formats, which led to five formats (3 PMS, 2 AIF).\n- I used Gemini because it is free.\n- I asked to fix the limitations I did not like (currency in the fingerprint, the plain review\n  page, auth, paging, search, review actions) and agreed to skip the consolidated view.\n\n## Where it misled me (all found by running tests or reading output)\n| # | What the AI got wrong | How it was found | Fix |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Code comments in the sample data stated wrong totals (it added numbers in its head) | Recomputed from the generated PDFs | Corrected the comments |\n| 2 | The XYZ answer key stored fees and outflows positive, while the PDF printed them in brackets | Compared the PDF text with `expected.json` | New `number_abs` transform |\n| 3 | The reader caught pdfminer's exceptions, but pdfplumber wraps them in `PdfminerException` | 3 failing reader tests | Unwrap `e.args[0]` |\n| 4 | The first fingerprint passed its tests while storing the strategy name and splitting titles into cells | Reading the printed label list | Keys-only labels, join short headings |\n| 5 | Currency text (`Cost (INR)`) in fingerprint labels | I noticed it in the dumps | Strip currency tokens |\n| 6 | A test asserted a message (\"Units\") that the code never produced | A failing test | `_find_header` now names missing columns |\n| 7 | The config schema did not check table column field names, so an invented field would be silently ignored | Found while designing the learner | Validate against the schema |\n| 8 | The default model name (`gemini-2.5-flash`) had been retired | Live 404 | Model in `.env`, new default |\n| 9 | My test claimed searching for `_` returns nothing; the sample names contain underscores | A failing test | Rewrote the test (the code was right) |\n| 10 | Wrapped-name detection looked one line ahead, so a three-line name ended the table | A failing edge-case test | `_leads_to_data` follows the chain |\n| 11 | The review page failed with \"Cannot read properties of undefined\" | I was still running the old server | Restarted the server (a version mismatch, not a code bug) |\n\nLessons: tests only prove what they assert, so I read output and dumps as well; failure-path\ntests found more bugs than happy-path ones; the AI states assumptions about libraries and model\nnames confidently, so each needs checking against reality.\n\n## What I Then the **secrets check**:\n\n```bash\ngit status                                     # .env, *.db, data/ must NOT be listed\ngit ls-files | grep -iE \"(^|/)\\.env$|\\.db$|credentials|token\\.json\"   # should print nothing\ngit grep -n \"AIza\"                             # Gemini keys start with this; should print nothing\ngit log --all --oneline -- .env                # should print nothing: .env was never committed\n```\n\nThen a **fresh clone test**, which catches a missing file or requirement that works only on your machine:\n\n```bash\ngit add . && git commit -m \"Part 11: documents, preflight, sample outputs\" && git push\ncd /tmp && rm -rf fresh && git clone <your-repo-url> fresh && cd fresh\npython -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate\npip install -r requirements.txt && python -m pytest -q\n```\n\nThe suite must pass without your `.env`. The LLM is used once per new layout, then never again.\" |\n| 0:30 | `rm -f statements.db; python -m samples.generate; python -m samples.next_month` | \"Five fictional providers, one password-protected.\" |\n| 1:00 | `python -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs` | Point to `llm=yes` for each new format, **`llm=no`** for `abc_pms_may.pdf`, the bad-numbers file flagged, and the units file re-learned |\n| 2:30 | Review page, Needs attention | Open the bad-numbers file: errors in red, the checks that passed |\n| 3:15 | Approve it, add a note, show the history | \"The machine's verdict is never edited\" |\n| 3:45 | Learned formats tab | \"This is what the LLM wrote, accepted only after four gates\" |\n| 4:30 | Email: `python -m app.email_ingest --days 2 --dry-run`, then the real run | The classifier accepts statements, skips the brochure with reasons |\n| 5:30 | `docs/limitations.md` | Two or three honest limits |\n| 6:15 | Close | \"Not built: Excel and the consolidated view; I'd add them like this...\" |\n\nUpload as unlisted on YouTube, or share a Drive link with \"anyone with the link\". One-time preparation (do this tonight, and again before the interview)\n\n```bash\nsource .venv/bin/activate\npython -m app.preflight --llm --mail            # every line must say OK\npython -m pytest -q\n\nrm -f warm.db\nfor f in abc_pms xyz_wealth meridian_capital sterling_aif helix_aif; do\n  python -m app.pipeline samples/pdfs/$f.pdf --db warm.db\ndone\ncp warm.db warm_backup.db                       # a clean copy to start from\n```\n\nThis calls Gemini five times. How to read what comes out\n\n| Line says | Meaning | What to say |\n|---|---|---|\n| `match=unknown llm=yes parsed_ok` | Learned a new layout, and its numbers validate | \"First time I've seen this, so the LLM wrote a config. Step 2: `samples/messy_check.py`\n\nIt compares each stored result to its answer key and sorts it into one of four outcomes.\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Compares what the system produced for the messy statements with the answer keys.\n\n    python -m samples.messy_check --db messy.db\n\nThe dangerous outcome is a statement that is parsed_ok but holds wrong data (a silent error).\nExit code is 1 if there is any.\n\"\"\"\nimport argparse\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app.schema import Statement\nfrom app.store import Store\n\nEXPECTED = Path(__file__).parent / \"messy_expected\"\n\n\ndef diff(a, b, path=\"\"):\n    out = []\n    if isinstance(a, dict) and isinstance(b, dict):\n        for key in sorted(set(a) | set(b)):\n            out += diff(a.get(key), b.get(key), f\"{path}.{key}\" if path else key)\n    elif isinstance(a, list) and isinstance(b, list):\n        if len(a) != len(b):\n            out.append(f\"{path}: {len(a)} items, expected {len(b)}\")\n        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(a, b)):\n            out += diff(x, y, f\"{path}[{i}]\")\n    elif a != b:\n        out.append(f\"{path}: got {a!r}, expected {b!r}\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef check(db: str) -> int:\n    store = Store(db)\n    silent = 0\n    counts = {\"correct\": 0, \"flagged\": 0, \"not_parsed\": 0, \"silent\": 0}\n    for row in reversed(store.list()):                     # oldest first\n        stem = Path(row[\"filename\"]).stem\n        issues = json.loads(row[\"issues_json\"] or \"[]\")\n        head = f\"{row['filename']:30} {row['status']:17} {'LLM' if row['used_llm'] else 'no LLM':7}\"\n\n        if not row[\"statement_json\"]:\n            counts[\"not_parsed\"] += 1\n            print(f\"{head} NOT PARSED (loud): {(row['error'] or '')[:140]}\")\n            for issue in issues[:3]:\n                print(f\"      - {issue['message'][:170]}\")\n            continue\n\n        key = EXPECTED / f\"{stem}.json\"\n        if not key.exists():\n            print(f\"{head} parsed (no answer key)\")\n            continue\n        got = Statement.model_validate_json(row[\"statement_json\"]).model_dump(\n            exclude={\"source_file_hash\"})\n        want = Statement.model_validate_json(key.read_text()).model_dump(\n            exclude={\"source_file_hash\"})\n        problems = diff(got, want)\n\n        if not problems:\n            counts[\"correct\" if row[\"status\"] == \"parsed_ok\" else \"flagged\"] += 1\n            suffix = \"\" if row[\"status\"] == \"parsed_ok\" else \"  (correct, but flagged for review)\"\n            print(f\"{head} CORRECT{suffix}\")\n            continue\n        if row[\"status\"] == \"parsed_ok\":\n            silent += 1\n            counts[\"silent\"] += 1\n            print(f\"{head} *** SILENT ERROR: parsed_ok but {len(problems)} value(s) differ\")\n        else:\n            counts[\"flagged\"] += 1\n            print(f\"{head} WRONG DATA, but net_gain=closing - opening - inflows + outflows + fees,         # 43,000\n        ),\n    )\n\n\ndef pinnacle_story(s: Statement):\n    sm = s.summary\n    rows = [[\"Security\\nName\", \"ISIN\\nCode\", \"Quantity\", \"Total\\nCost\", \"Market\\nPrice\",\n             \"Market\\nValue\", \"Weight\\n(%)\"]]\n    for h in s.holdings:\n        rows.append([h.security_name, h.isin, qty(h.quantity), indian(h.cost),\n                     indian(h.market_price), indian(h.market_value), str(h.weight_pct)])\n    rows.append([\"Total\", \"\", \"\", indian(sum(h.cost for h in s.holdings)), \"\",\n                 indian(sum(h.market_value for h in s.holdings)),\n                 str(sum(h.weight_pct for h in s.holdings))])\n    labels = {T.BUY: \"Buy\", T.SELL: \"Sell\", T.DIVIDEND: \"Dividend\", T.FEE: \"Fee\"}\n    return [\n        P(\"Pinnacle Capital\", TITLE),\n        P(\"Portfolio Statement\", H2),\n        P(f\"Client Code: {s.client_id}\"),\n        P(f\"Strategy: {s.strategy_name}\"),\n        P(f\"Period: {d_slash(s.period_start)} to {d_slash(s.period_end)}\"),\n        P(f\"Currency: {s.currency}\"),\n        P(\"Account Summary\", H2),\n        kv_table([\n            (\"Opening Value\", indian(sm.opening_value)),\n            (\"Inflows\", indian(sm.capital_inflows)),\n            (\"Outflows\", indian(sm.capital_outflows)),\n            (\"Fees Charged\", indian(sm.fees_charged)),\n            (\"Net Gain\", indian(sm.net_gain)),\n            (\"Closing Value\", indian(sm.closing_value)),\n            (\"Cash Balance\", indian(sm.cash_balance)),\n        ]),\n        P(\"Holdings\", H2),\n        make_table(rows, [125, 85, 50, 70, 60, 80, 50], right_cols=(2, 3, 4, 5, 6), total_row=True),\n        P(\"Transactions\", H2),\n        txn_table(s, labels, d_slash, indian, [\"Date\", \"Type\", \"Security\", \"Qty\", \"Amount\"],\n                  [70, 60, 190, 50, 90]),\n    ]\n\n\n# layer).\"\"\"\n    import pypdfium2 as pdfium\n\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n        src = Path(tmp) / \"abc.pdf\"\n        render_pdf(\"abc_pms\", ALL_SAMPLES[\"abc_pms\"](), src)\n        pdf = pdfium.PdfDocument(str(src))\n        try:\n            image = pdf[0].render(scale=2).to_pil().convert(\"RGB\")\n        finally:\n            pdf.close()\n    c = canvas.Canvas(str(dst), pagesize=A4)\n    c.drawImage(ImageReader(image), 0, 0, width=A4[0], height=A4[1])\n    c.save()\n\n\ndef write_messy(out_dir=HERE) -> dict:\n    out = Path(out_dir)\n    pdfs, exist_ok=True)\n    written = {}\n\n    def emit(stem, statement, story, folder=pdfs, **kwargs):\n        path = folder / f\"{stem}.pdf\"\n        build(path, story, **kwargs)\n        (expected / Nothing was marked `parsed_ok` with wrong data.\n\n| File | Result | What it shows |\n|---|---|---|\n| `messy_orion` | `parsed_ok`, **CORRECT** | Odd column names, two negative styles, a different date format and an extra table were all learned correctly |\n| `messy_scanned` | `failed`, no LLM call | Rejected at the door with a clear reason |\n| `messy_nova` | `learning_failed` | Two label/value pairs per line can't be expressed |\n| `messy_quantum` | `learning_failed` | Two causes, below |\n| `messy_pinnacle` | `learning_failed` | Two-line headers can't be expressed |\n| `messy_orion_injected` | **Not tested yet** | The 429 was because you ran it without `LLM_MODEL=`, so it used the default model that's out of quota |\n\nTwo things to note:\n\n- **Gate 4 saved a silent error.** On Nova's attempt 3, the model read the wrong cells: units 1500.25 \u00d7 NAV 1500.25 and \"opening 800\". Gates 1 to 3 passed, and `units_nav_mismatch` plus `reconciliation_mismatch` rejected it. That's a good example for your demo and AI log.\n- **All of this ran on a lite model** (`gemini-3.5-flash-lite`), so a stronger model may do better. Say so in your notes.\n\n## What was failing\n\n1. **Nova:** a summary rule matches only a line's *first* cell, so the second pair (`Units Held | 800.0000`) can't be reached.\n2. **Quantum, cause A:** the model wrote `header_starts_with` as `\"Instrument | Sector | Qty\"`, copying my display format, but the engine compares text joined by spaces. My prompt was unclear, and the engine should tolerate it.\n3. **Quantum, cause B:** the PDF has printed columns (`Sector`, `Unrealised P&L`) the config has no field for, and the engine errors on any cell under an unmapped column.\n4. **Pinnacle:** each header spans two lines, and the engine only reads one.\n\nAll four are **common in real statements**, and all four failed loudly. I'd fix them in one round, because the changes are small and additive. It's Thursday, so this is the last engine work. Tomorrow is documents, video and submitting.\n\n## Change 1: `app/config_spec.py`\n\nIn `SummaryRule`, add `label_cell`:\n\n```python\nclass SummaryRule(_Strict):\n    \"\"\"Find the line whose cell number `label_cell` equals `label` (case-insensitive);\n    read one cell of it.\"\"\"\n    label: str\n    transform: str = \"number\"\n    cell: int = -1             # -1 = last cell on the line\n    label_cell: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)   # which cell holds the label (side-by-side pairs)\n    optional: bool = False\n```\n\nIn `TableRule`, add `header_lines`:\n\n```python\nclass TableRule(_Strict):\n    header_starts_with: str    # text the header line starts with\n    header_lines: int = Field(default=1, ge=1, le=3)   # header printed over 1 to 3 lines\n    stop_at: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)   # line prefixes ending the table\n    columns: list[ColumnRule]\n    skip_if_blank: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)  # fields that must be non-empty\n```\n\nBoth have defaults, so every config already stored in your registry stays valid.\n\n## Change 2: `app/engine.py`\n\n**A. Summary section.** Replace `_lines_with_label` and `_read_summary_rule` with:\n\n```python\ndef _lines_with_label(doc: Document, label: str, label_cell: int = 0) -> list[Line]:\n    target = _norm(label)\n    return [ln for ln in doc.lines\n            if len(ln.cells) >= 2 and len(ln.cells) > label_cell\n            and _norm(ln.cells[label_cell].text) == target]\n\n\ndef _read_summary_rule(doc: Document, name: str, rule: SummaryRule, issues: list[str]):\n    lines = _lines_with_label(doc, rule.label, rule.label_cell)\n    if not lines:\n        if not rule.optional:\n            where = \"\" if rule.label_cell == 0 else f\" in cell {rule.label_cell}\"\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: no line labelled {rule.label!r}{where}\")\n        return None\n\n    values = set()\n    for ln in lines:\n        index = rule.cell if rule.cell >= 0 else len(ln.cells) + rule.cell\n        if not 0 <= index < len(ln.cells):\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: line {ln.text!r} has no cell {rule.cell}\")\n            return None\n        if index == rule.label_cell:\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: the value cell is the label cell on line {ln.text!r}\")\n            return None\n        try:\n            values.add(apply_transform(rule.transform, ln.cells[index].text))\n        except TransformError as e:\n            issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: {e}\")\n            return None\n\n    if len(values) > 1:\n        # The same label printed twice with different numbers: don't pick one silently.\n        issues.append(f\"summary {name!r}: label {rule.label!r} appears with \"\n                      f\"different values {sorted(map(str, values))}\")\n        return None\n    return values.pop()\n```\n\n**B. Tables section.** Add this next to `WRAP_GAP` and `WEAK_TRANSFORMS`:\n\n```python\n# Key prefix for printed columns that the config has no field for (they are read, then ignored).\nSKIP = \"\\x00skip:\"\n\n\ndef _prefix(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalised text with ' | ' cell separators read as spaces (LLMs often copy them).\"\"\"\n    return _norm(text.replace(\"|\", \" \"))\n\n\ndef _merge_header(lines: list, idx: int, n: int) -> Line:\n    \"\"\"Merge n stacked header lines into one. Cells that overlap horizontally are joined\n    top to bottom: 'Market' above 'Value' becomes 'Market Value'.\"\"\"\n    merged: list = []                      # each [text, x0, x1]\n    for hl in lines[idx: idx + n]:\n        for cell in hl.cells:\n            for m in merged:\n                if min(m[2], cell.x1) - max(m[1], cell.x0) > 0:\n                    m[0] = f\"{m[0]} {cell.text}\"\n                    m[1], m[2] = min(m[1], cell.x0), max(m[2], cell.x1)\n                    break\n            else:\n                merged.append([cell.text, cell.x0, cell.x1])\n    merged.sort(key=lambda m: m[1])\n    first = lines[idx]\n    return Line(first.page, first.top, tuple(Cell(m[0], m[1], m[2]) for m in merged),\n                lines[idx + n - 1].bottom)\n```\n\n**C. Replace `_find_header`, `_assign` and `extract_table`** with these versions:\n\n```python\ndef _find_header(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str):\n    \"\"\"(index, header line) of the first line that starts the header and holds every required\n    column. With header_lines > 1 the stacked lines are merged first.\n\n    If a line starts correctly but lacks some required columns, the error names exactly which\n    ones (the likeliest sign that the provider renamed a column).\"\"\"\n    start = _prefix(rule.header_starts_with)\n    required = [c.header for c in rule.columns if not c.optional]\n    n = rule.header_lines\n    lines = doc.lines\n    best_missing = None\n    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):\n        header = ln\n        if n > 1:\n            if i + n > len(lines) or any(x.page != ln.page for x in lines[i:i + n]):\n                continue\n            header = _merge_header(lines, i, n)\n            starts = _norm(ln.text).startswith(start) or _norm(header.text).startswith(start)\n        else:\n            starts = _norm(ln.text).startswith(start)\n        if not starts:\n            continue\n        texts = {_norm(c.text) for c in header.cells}\n        missing = [h for h in required if _norm(h) not in texts]\n        if not missing:\n            return i, header\n        if best_missing is None or len(missing) < len(best_missing):\n            best_missing = missing\n\n    if best_missing:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: header line found but column(s) {best_missing} \"\n                      f\"are missing (layout may have changed)\")\n    else:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: no header line starting with \"\n                      f\"{rule.header_starts_with!r}\")\n    return None\n\n\ndef _assign(line: Line, columns: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Assign each cell on the line to the column it overlaps most. Raises on ambiguity.\n    Cells under a printed column the config does not use are dropped, not errors.\"\"\"\n    assigned: dict = {}\n    for cell in line.cells:\n        best_field, best = None, 0.0\n        for field_name, hdr in columns.items():\n            if hdr is None:\n                continue\n            o = _overlap(cell, hdr)\n            if o > best:\n                best_field, best = field_name, o\n        if best_field is None:\n            raise TransformError(f\"cell {cell.text!r} sits under no known column\")\n        if best_field.startswith(SKIP):\n            continue\n        if best_field in assigned:\n            raise TransformError(\n                f\"two cells ({assigned[best_field]!r}, {cell.text!r}) fall in column \"\n                f\"{best_field!r}\")\n        assigned[best_field] = cell.text\n    return assigned\n\n\ndef extract_table(doc: Document, rule: TableRule, issues: list[str], label: str) -> list[dict]:\n    problems: list[str] = []          # this table's own problems; never hidden by other tables\n    found = _find_header(doc, rule, problems, label)\n    if found is None:\n        issues.extend(problems)\n        return []\n    idx, header = found\n    columns = _column_cells(header, rule, problems, label)\n    if problems:\n        issues.extend(problems)\n        return []\n    used = [c for c in columns.values() if c is not None]\n    for k, cell in enumerate(header.cells):\n        if cell not in used:\n            columns[f\"{SKIP}{k}\"] = cell          # printed, but the config has no field for it\n\n    lines = doc.lines\n    n = rule.header_lines\n    rules = {c.field: c for c in rule.columns}\n    text_fields = {f for f, c in rules.items() if c.transform == \"text\"}\n    stops = [_prefix(s) for s in rule.stop_at]\n    printed = {_norm(hl.text) for hl in lines[idx: idx + n]}   # header as printed, per line\n    first_key = _norm(lines[idx].text)\n\n    rows: list[tuple[dict, Line]] = []     # (raw text per field, line the row started on)\n    last_row_line: Optional[Line] = None   # last line that belonged to a row\n    pending: dict = {}                     # text-only lines waiting for the row below them\n    pending_line: Optional[Line] = None\n    ended = False\n\n    for j in range(idx + n, len(lines)):\n        ln = lines[j]\n        nxt = lines[j + 1] if j + 1 < len(lines) else None\n        text = _norm(ln.text)\n        single = len(ln.cells) == 1\n\n        if ended:\n            # After the table ended, the same header again is ambiguous: a continuation,\n            # or a second table? We cannot tell, so we refuse to guess.\n            if text == first_key:\n                problems.append(\n                    f\"{label}: the header line appears again on page {ln.page} after the \"\n                    f\"table ended; cannot tell a continuation from a second table\")\n                break\n            continue\n\n        if text in printed:                             # header repeated on a later page\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n            continue\n        if any(text.startswith(s) for s in stops):      # totals row: the table is over\n            ended = True\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n            continue\n        if single and \"continued\" in text:              # \"(continued)\" marker\n            continue\n        if (single and lines[j - 1].page != ln.page and nxt is not None\n                and (_norm(nxt.text) in printed or _looks_like_data(nxt, columns, rules))):\n            continue                                    # running header at the top of a page\n\n        try:\n            placed = _assign(ln, columns)\n        except TransformError as e:\n            if single:\n                ended = True                            # a heading far from every column\n            else:\n                problems.append(f\"{label} row {ln.text!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n        if not placed:                                  # only cells under unused columns\n            continue\n\n        if all(f in text_fields for f in placed):       # text only: a heading or a wrapped name\n            if pending and _tight(pending_line, ln):    # a further line of a wrapped-above name\n                _append(pending, placed)\n                pending_line = ln\n                continue\n            if rows and not pending and _tight(last_row_line, ln):\n                _append(rows[-1][0], placed)            # wrapped BELOW its row\n                last_row_line = ln\n                continue\n            if _leads_to_data(lines, j, columns, rules, text_fields):\n                pending, pending_line = dict(placed), ln    # wrapped ABOVE its row\n                continue\n            if single:                                  # a section heading: the table ended\n                ended = True\n                pending, pending_line = {}, None\n                continue\n\n        row = dict(placed)\n        if pending:\n            if _tight(pending_line, ln):\n                for f, t in pending.items():\n                    row[f] = f\"{t} {row[f]}\" if row.get(f) else t\n            pending, pending_line = {}, None\n        rows.append((row, ln))\n        last_row_line = ln\n\n    out: list[dict] = []\n    for raw, first_line in rows:\n        try:\n            row = {f: apply_transform(rules[f].transform, raw.get(f)) for f in rules}\n        except TransformError as e:\n            problems.append(f\"{label} row {first_line.text!r}: {e}\")\n            continue\n        if any(row.get(f) is None for f in rule.skip_if_blank):\n            continue\n        out.append(row)\n\n    if not out and not problems:\n        problems.append(f\"{label}: header found but no data rows\")\n    issues.extend(problems)\n    return out\n```\n\n## Change 3: `app/learner.py`\n\nThe model needs to know about the new options. With header_lines > 1 the stacked lines are merged first.\n\n    If a line starts correctly but lacks some required columns, the error names exactly which\n    ones (the likeliest sign that the provider renamed a column).\"\"\"\n    start = _prefix(rule.header_starts_with)\n    required = [c.header for c in rule.columns if not c.optional]\n    n = rule.header_lines\n    lines = doc.lines\n    best_missing = None\n    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):\n        header = ln\n        if n > 1:\n            if i + n > len(lines) or any(x.page != ln.page for x in lines[i:i + n]):\n                continue\n            header = _merge_header(lines, i, n)\n            starts = _norm(ln.text).startswith(start) or _norm(header.text).startswith(start)\n        else:\n            starts = _norm(ln.text).startswith(start)\n        if not starts:\n            continue\n        texts = {_norm(c.text) for c in header.cells}\n        missing = [h for h in required if _norm(h) not in texts]\n        if not missing:\n            return i, header\n        if best_missing is None or len(missing) < len(best_missing):\n            best_missing = missing\n\n    if best_missing:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: header line found but column(s) {best_missing} \"\n                      f\"are missing (layout may have changed)\")\n    else:\n        issues.append(f\"{label}: no header line starting with \"\n                      f\"{rule.header_starts_with!r}\")\n    return None\n\n\ndef _assign(line: Line, columns: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Assign each cell on the line to the column it overlaps most. This is a new layer on top, and it goes through the same `Pipeline` as the command line.\n\n## Security decisions\n\nAn upload button turns a read-only page into one that accepts files from outside, so here is how it's contained:\n\n| Risk | Handling |\n|---|---|\n| Anyone reaching the port uploads files | Same token check as every other call |\n| Huge or fake files | 25 MB limit, checked on the declared size and while streaming. Must contain `%PDF-` |\n| Hostile file names | Sanitised (`../../evil.pdf` becomes `evil.pdf`) and prefixed with a hash |\n| PDF passwords end up in logs | Sent in an **HTTP header** (URL-encoded), never in the URL, because the server logs URLs. Not stored, not echoed back |\n| Two jobs corrupting the database | One job at a time. A second gets HTTP 409 \"another job is running\" |\n| Reset wiping real data | Demo endpoints return 404 unless started with `--demo`. `--demo` refuses any database file whose name doesn't contain \"demo\". Replace `app/registry.py` completely:\n\n```python\n\"\"\"SQLite store of learned formats. Safe to share between threads.\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport sqlite3\nimport threading\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom app.fingerprint import (\n    DRIFT_THRESHOLD, MATCH_THRESHOLD, Fingerprint, similarity,\n)\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS formats (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    name TEXT NOT NULL,\n    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    fingerprint_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    labels_json TEXT NOT NULL,\n    config_json TEXT,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\nclass MatchKind(str, Enum):\n    MATCH = \"match\"      # same format\n    DRIFT = \"drift\"      # looks like a known format but the layout changed\n    UNKNOWN = \"unknown\"  # never seen\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass MatchResult:\n    kind: MatchKind\n    format_id: Optional[int] = None\n    format_name: Optional[str] = None\n    score: float = 0.0\n    config: Optional[dict] = None\n\n\nclass Registry:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: str = \":memory:\"):\n        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, check_same_thread=False)\n        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n        self._lock = threading.RLock()       # re-entrant: match() calls all_formats()\n        with self._lock:\n            self.conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n\n    def add_format(self, name: str, fp: Fingerprint, config: Optional[dict] = None) -> int:\n        with self._lock:\n            cur = self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) FROM formats WHERE name = ?\", (name,))\n            version = cur.fetchone()[0] + 1\n            cur = self.conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO formats (name, version, fingerprint_hash, labels_json, config_json)\"\n                \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                (name, version, fp.digest, json.dumps(sorted(fp.labels)),\n                 json.dumps(config) if config is not None else None))\n            self.conn.commit()\n            return cur.lastrowid\n\n    def all_formats(self) -> list:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM formats ORDER BY id\").fetchall()\n\n    def clear(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Forget every learned format (used only by the demo reset).\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM formats\")\n            self.conn.commit()\n\n    def match(self, fp: Fingerprint) -> MatchResult:\n        with self._lock:\n            best = None\n            best_score = 0.0\n            for row in self.all_formats():\n                if row[\"fingerprint_hash\"] == fp.digest:\n                    return self._result(MatchKind.MATCH, row, 1.0)\n                score = similarity(fp.labels, frozenset(json.loads(row[\"labels_json\"])))\n                if score > best_score:\n                    best, best_score = row, score\n\n            if best is None or best_score < DRIFT_THRESHOLD:\n                return MatchResult(MatchKind.UNKNOWN, score=best_score)\n            kind = MatchKind.MATCH if best_score >= MATCH_THRESHOLD else MatchKind.DRIFT\n            return self._result(kind, best, best_score)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _result(kind, row, score) -> MatchResult:\n        cfg = json.loads(row[\"config_json\"]) if row[\"config_json\"] else None\n        return MatchResult(kind, row[\"id\"], row[\"name\"], score, cfg)\n```\n\n## Step 2: Small edits\n\n**`app/store.py`**: add this method at the end of the `Store` Likely trouble spots:\n\n- **`test_every_step_plays_in_order...`** is the strictest, because it needs the fake LLM replies in exactly the order the steps call it. If it fails, the assertion message shows which step and why.\n- **`content=` in `client.post`** depends on your httpx and Starlette versions. If it raises a `TypeError`, paste it.\n- **`test_workbench_endpoints_need_the_token`** builds an unauthenticated client. If it fails for one path, the dependency order on that route needs a look.\n- **Old tests** in `test_api.py` use `create_app(store, registry, TOKEN)`, which still works because `bench` and `demo` are optional. If any fail, paste them.\n\nOnce it's green, commit:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Workbench: upload, retry, mailbox fetch, demo simulator\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Step 8: Try it in the browser\n\n```bash\nrm -f demo.db\npython -m app.api --db demo.db --demo\n```\n\nSign in with the printed token (or your `REVIEW_TOKEN`). The page opens on **Workbench**. Check these in order:\n\n1. **Prepare demo files**: a banner says the files are ready in `data/demo`.\n2. **Run all steps**: each card shows a spinner, then a green **\u2713 as expected**. Gemini is called about six times, so a 503 on one step is possible. Press **Run** on that step to retry, and if you need to replay from scratch, use Reset.\n3. **Step 5 then 6** (locked, then unlock): the same file goes from *Password needed* to *OK*. Then open the Documents tab. A locked document in the *Needs attention* list now has a **Try again** box in the drawer.\n4. **Drag a PDF** from `samples/pdfs` onto the drop zone. A new file prompts a wait and a result line. A file you already processed shows *duplicate*.\n5. **Drop a locked PDF without a password** and see *Password needed*. Then type `demo1234` in the password box and drop it again.\n6. **Inbox simulator**: *Deliver April mail* shows a table with two accepted PDFs and the brochure skipped with its reasons. Press it again and everything says *already known*. Then *Deliver May mail* parses with **LLM no**.\n7. **Reset demo data**: the confirm dialog appears, and then every card goes back to zero.\n8. **Drop a non-PDF** (a `.txt`) and see the rejection message.\n9. **Real Gmail**: *Check (dry run)* lists what's in your inbox, and *Send April mail to my Gmail* followed by *Fetch & process* runs the real path.\n\nThe JavaScript has no automated tests beyond the pattern scans, so a blank panel or red console error in step 1 is the likeliest failure. If something looks wrong, open the browser console (right-click \u2192 Inspect \u2192 Console) and paste the message.\n\n## How to use it\n\n**Demo video:**\n1. `rm -f demo.db && python -m app.api --db demo.db --demo`\n2. Do one practice run, reset, and then record: *Prepare demo files*, then step through the eight cards one at a time, reading each card's talking point aloud. Each card already holds the line you'd say.\n3. Switch to Documents, show *Needs attention*, open the bad-numbers file, then approve it. Show the *Learned formats* tab. Finish with the inbox simulator.\n4. Keep the access token off screen.\n\n**Interview with messy statements:**\n1. Before the session, start `python -m app.api --db demo.db --demo`, press **Run all steps** once so the five layouts are already learned (the \"warm\" state), and don't reset.\n2. When they email you a statement, save the PDF and **drop it on the Workbench**. If it's locked, type the password first. Or use **Mailbox \u2192 Fetch & process** if they send it to your Gmail account.\n3. Read the result line aloud, open the document, and explain each issue.\n4. If a document ends `learning_failed` (for example, a Gemini 503), open it in the drawer and press **Retry processing**.\n5. As a fallback with no internet, the inbox simulator and the known-format steps still work, and the learned configs are in the database.\n\n## Security and limitation notes\n\nAdd these to `docs/limitations.md` under *Review interface*:\n\n```markdown\n- **The page can now run the pipeline.** Anyone with the access token can upload a PDF (25 MB\n  limit, must start with `%PDF-`) or fetch the mailbox, which can send that document's text to\n  the LLM provider. There are no per-user accounts, quotas or virus scanning.\n- **Passwords typed into the page travel in an HTTP header over plain HTTP** (localhost only).\n  They are used for that one run, never stored or logged, and are not part of the URL.\n- **Uploaded files and email attachments are saved unencrypted** under `data/`. Retry works only\n  for files saved there; a document processed from the command line must be uploaded again.\n- **One job at a time.** A second request gets \"another job is running\". There is no progress\n  stream, so a slow LLM call shows only a spinner and the page must stay open.\n- **Demo mode can wipe the database.** It only starts on a database whose file name contains\n  \"demo\", the reset needs a confirm dialog and the word RESET, and the demo files are generated\n  into `data/demo` (not into `samples/`).\n```\n\nUpdate the README's *Run it* block with one line, and describe the Workbench in a sentence:\n\n```bash\npython -m app.api --db demo.db --demo    # review page + Workbench (upload, mailbox, demo simulator)\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why not just parse in the browser?** The page never parses anything. It calls the same `Pipeline` as the command line, so there is exactly one code path and one set of tests.\n2. **Why is the password in a header, not the URL?** Servers log URLs, and a password in a log is a leak.\n3. **Why one job at a time?** The pipeline and the registry share a database. Serialising jobs removes a whole class of races, and the page never starts two jobs on purpose.\n4. **Why is demo mode a separate flag, and why a database named \"demo\"?** The reset button destroys data. Making it impossible to run against a real database by accident is cheaper than adding a warning.\n5. **What does Retry do that re-uploading wouldn't?** It finds the saved file by hash, so you don't have to re-upload it, and it updates the same document row rather than creating a second one.\n\nSend me the test results and what the browser looks like. Then we'll add the final line to the README and move on to the documents, fresh-clone test and demo recording. no longer need the terminal except to start the server. The new **Workbench** tab has three parts:\n\n| Part | What it does | Available |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Process a statement** | Drag one or more PDFs onto the page (optional password) and the pipeline runs on them. This is for the messy statement the interviewer emails you | Always |\n| **Mailbox** | \"Check (dry run)\" and \"Fetch & process\" for your real Gmail inbox | Always |\n| **Demo simulator** | Eight scripted steps with talking points and \u2713/\u2717 expected-outcome checks, a simulated inbox that works without Gmail, and a reset button | Only with `--demo` |\n\nThe drawer for any unfinished document (`password_required`, `failed`, `learning_failed`) also gets a **Retry** box with a password field. That fixes the \"failed documents need a manual terminal command\" limitation.\n\nThe pipeline, engine and validation are untouched. This is a new layer on top, and it goes through the same `Pipeline` as the command line.\n\n## Security decisions\n\nAn upload button turns a read-only page into one that accepts files from outside, so here is how it's contained:\n\n| Risk | Handling |\n|---|---|\n| Anyone reaching the port uploads files | Same token check as every other call |\n| Huge or fake files | 25 MB limit, checked on the declared size and while streaming. Must contain `%PDF-` |\n| Hostile file names | Sanitised (`../../evil.pdf` becomes `evil.pdf`) and prefixed with a hash |\n| PDF passwords end up in logs | Sent in an **HTTP header** (URL-encoded), never in the URL, because the server logs URLs. Not stored, not echoed back |\n| Two jobs corrupting the database | One job at a time. A second gets HTTP 409 \"another job is running\" |\n| Reset wiping real data | Demo endpoints return 404 unless started with `--demo`. `--demo` refuses any database file whose name doesn't contain \"demo\". Reset also needs a confirm dialog and the word `RESET` in the request |\n| Page-injected HTML | Same rule as before: the page only builds text nodes (the test still scans `app.js`) |\n\nI haven't run any of this. The tests are the judge, and the JavaScript has no tests beyond the banned-pattern scans, so the browser check at the end is essential.\n\n## Step 1: Make the registry thread-safe\n\nThe web server now writes (during processing) while the page reads. Replace `app/registry.py` completely:\n\n```python\n\"\"\"SQLite store of learned formats. Safe to share between threads.\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport sqlite3\nimport threading\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom app.fingerprint import (\n    DRIFT_THRESHOLD, MATCH_THRESHOLD, Fingerprint, similarity,\n)\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS formats (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    name TEXT NOT NULL,\n    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    fingerprint_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    labels_json TEXT NOT NULL,\n    config_json TEXT,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\nclass MatchKind(str, Enum):\n    MATCH = \"match\"      # same format\n    DRIFT = \"drift\"      # looks like a known format but the layout changed\n    UNKNOWN = \"unknown\"  # never seen\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass MatchResult:\n    kind: MatchKind\n    format_id: Optional[int] = None\n    format_name: Optional[str] = None\n    score: float = 0.0\n    config: Optional[dict] = None\n\n\nclass Registry:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: str = \":memory:\"):\n        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, check_same_thread=False)\n        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n        self._lock = threading.RLock()       # re-entrant: match() calls all_formats()\n        with self._lock:\n            self.conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n\n    def add_format(self, name: str, fp: Fingerprint, config: Optional[dict] = None) -> int:\n        with self._lock:\n            cur = self.conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) FROM formats WHERE name = ?\", (name,))\n            version = cur.fetchone()[0] + 1\n            cur = self.conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO formats (name, version, fingerprint_hash, labels_json, config_json)\"\n                \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                (name, version, fp.digest, json.dumps(sorted(fp.labels)),\n                 json.dumps(config) if config is not None else None))\n            self.conn.commit()\n            return cur.lastrowid\n\n    def all_formats(self) -> list:\n        with self._lock:\n            return self.conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM formats ORDER BY id\").fetchall()\n\n    def clear(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Forget every learned format (used only by the demo reset).\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self.conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM formats\")\n            self.conn.commit()\n\n    def match(self, fp: Fingerprint) -> MatchResult:\n        with self._lock:\n            best = None\n            best_score = 0.0\n            for row in self.all_formats():\n                if row[\"fingerprint_hash\"] == fp.digest:\n                    return self._result(MatchKind.MATCH, row, 1.0)\n                score = similarity(fp.labels, frozenset(json.loads(row[\"labels_json\"])))\n                if score > best_score:\n                    best, best_score = row, score\n\n            if best is None or best_score < DRIFT_THRESHOLD:\n                return MatchResult(MatchKind.UNKNOWN, score=best_score)\n            kind = MatchKind.MATCH if best_score >= MATCH_THRESHOLD else MatchKind.DRIFT\n            return self._result(kind, best, best_score)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _result(kind, row, score) -> MatchResult:\n        cfg = json.loads(row[\"config_json\"]) if row[\"config_json\"] else None\n        return MatchResult(kind, row[\"id\"], row[\"name\"], score, cfg)\n```\n\n## Step 2: Small edits\n\n**`app/store.py`**: add this method at the end of the `Store` If it fails, the assertion message shows which step and why.\n- **`content=` in `client.post`** depends on your httpx and Starlette versions. If it raises a `TypeError`, paste it.\n- **`test_workbench_endpoints_need_the_token`** builds an unauthenticated client. If it fails for one path, the dependency order on that route needs a look.\n- **Old tests** in `test_api.py` use `create_app(store, registry, TOKEN)`, which still works because `bench` and `demo` are optional. If any fail, paste them.\n\nOnce it's green, commit:\n\n```bash\ngit add .\ngit commit -m \"Workbench: upload, retry, mailbox fetch, demo simulator\"\ngit push\n```\n\n## Step 8: Try it in the browser\n\n```bash\nrm -f demo.db\npython -m app.api --db demo.db --demo\n```\n\nSign in with the printed token (or your `REVIEW_TOKEN`). The page opens on **Workbench**. Check these in order:\n\n1. **Prepare demo files**: a banner says the files are ready in `data/demo`.\n2. **Run all steps**: each card shows a spinner, then a green **\u2713 as expected**. Gemini is called about six times, so a 503 on one step is possible. Press **Run** on that step to retry, and if you need to replay from scratch, use Reset.\n3. **Step 5 then 6** (locked, then unlock): the same file goes from *Password needed* to *OK*. Then open the Documents tab. A locked document in the *Needs attention* list now has a **Try again** box in the drawer.\n4. **Drag a PDF** from `samples/pdfs` onto the drop zone. A new file prompts a wait and a result line. A file you already processed shows *duplicate*.\n5. **Drop a locked PDF without a password** and see *Password needed*. Then type `demo1234` in the password box and drop it again.\n6. **Inbox simulator**: *Deliver April mail* shows a table with two accepted PDFs and the brochure skipped with its reasons. Press it again and everything says *already known*. Then *Deliver May mail* parses with **LLM no**.\n7. **Reset demo data**: the confirm dialog appears, and then every card goes back to zero.\n8. **Drop a non-PDF** (a `.txt`) and see the rejection message.\n9. **Real Gmail**: *Check (dry run)* lists what's in your inbox, and *Send April mail to my Gmail* followed by *Fetch & process* runs the real path.\n\nThe JavaScript has no automated tests beyond the pattern scans, so a blank panel or red console error in step 1 is the likeliest failure. If something looks wrong, open the browser console (right-click \u2192 Inspect \u2192 Console) and paste the message.\n\n## How to use it\n\n**Demo video:**\n1. `rm -f demo.db && python -m app.api --db demo.db --demo`\n2. Do one practice run, reset, and then record: *Prepare demo files*, then step through the eight cards one at a time, reading each card's talking point aloud. Each card already holds the line you'd say.\n3. Switch to Documents, show *Needs attention*, open the bad-numbers file, then approve it. Show the *Learned formats* tab. Finish with the inbox simulator.\n4. Keep the access token off screen.\n\n**Interview with messy statements:**\n1. Before the session, start `python -m app.api --db demo.db --demo`, press **Run all steps** once so the five layouts are already learned (the \"warm\" state), and don't reset.\n2. When they email you a statement, save the PDF and **drop it on the Workbench**. If it's locked, type the password first. Or use **Mailbox \u2192 Fetch & process** if they send it to your Gmail account.\n3. Read the result line aloud, open the document, and explain each issue.\n4. If a document ends `learning_failed` (for example, a Gemini 503), open it in the drawer and press **Retry processing**.\n5. As a fallback with no internet, the inbox simulator and the known-format steps still work, and the learned configs are in the database.\n\n## Security and limitation notes\n\nAdd these to `docs/limitations.md` under *Review interface*:\n\n```markdown\n- **The page can now run the pipeline.** Anyone with the access token can upload a PDF (25 MB\n  limit, must start with `%PDF-`) or fetch the mailbox, which can send that document's text to\n  the LLM provider. There are no per-user accounts, quotas or virus scanning.\n- **Passwords typed into the page travel in an HTTP header over plain HTTP** (localhost only).\n  They are used for that one run, never stored or logged, and are not part of the URL.\n- **Uploaded files and email attachments are saved unencrypted** under `data/`. Retry works only\n  for files saved there; a document processed from the command line must be uploaded again.\n- **One job at a time.** A second request gets \"another job is running\". There is no progress\n  stream, so a slow LLM call shows only a spinner and the page must stay open.\n- **Demo mode can wipe the database.** It only starts on a database whose file name contains\n  \"demo\", the reset needs a confirm dialog and the word RESET, and the demo files are generated\n  into `data/demo` (not into `samples/`).\n```\n\nUpdate the README's *Run it* block with one line, and describe the Workbench in a sentence:\n\n```bash\npython -m app.api --db demo.db --demo    # review page + Workbench (upload, mailbox, demo simulator)\n```\n\n## Be ready to explain\n\n1. **Why not just parse in the browser?** The page never parses anything. It calls the same `Pipeline` as the command line, so there is exactly one code path and one set of tests.\n2. **Why is the password in a header, not the URL?** Servers log URLs, and a password in a log is a leak.\n3. **Why one job at a time?** The pipeline and the registry share a database. Serialising jobs removes a whole class of races, and the page never starts two jobs on purpose.\n4. **Why is demo mode a separate flag, and why a database named \"demo\"?** The reset button destroys data. Making it impossible to run against a real database by accident is cheaper than adding a warning.\n5. **What does Retry do that re-uploading wouldn't?** It finds the saved file by hash, so you don't have to re-upload it, and it updates the same document row rather than creating a second one.\n\nSend me the test results and what the browser looks like. Then we'll add the final line to the README and move on to the documents, fresh-clone test and demo recording.
