The earlier \"14th\" in my plan was out of date, so you have until tomorrow 11:59 PM IST. Treat quota as a tooling problem to fix in 30 minutes, then spend the rest of the time on the submission.\n\n## Why it happens\n\nI checked Google's rate-limit docs:\n\n- **Limits apply per project, not per API key.** A new key in the same project doesn't reset anything. If your \"new API\" works, it's because it lives in a new project. I can't tell you whether that's allowed under Google's free-tier terms (check them), and it's fragile if it fails mid-interview.\n- **Daily limits reset at midnight Pacific time.** US daylight time lasts until 1 November, so that's about **12:30 PM IST**. Today's quota refills at 12:30 PM, and tomorrow's does too.\n- **Limits are listed per model**, so a second model has its own allowance. I believe they're counted separately, but confirm on the rate-limit page in AI Studio, which also shows your real numbers.\n\nOur own habits drain the quota. **Run all steps** is about 6 calls. **Reset demo data** wipes the learned formats, so the next run pays for all 6 again. Every retry after a bad reply is another call.\n\n## The fix: three small changes\n\n| Change | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| **Model fallback** | `LLM_MODEL` accepts a comma-separated list. On a 429, 404 or persistent 503, the next model is tried. Auth errors never fall back |\n| **Daily quota detection** | A \"per day\" 429 is not retried. Waiting 30 seconds can't fix a quota that resets at 12:30 PM |\n| **Reply cache (opt-in)** | Remembers Gemini's replies on disk, keyed by a hash of the prompt. A repeated demo costs zero calls. Replies still go through all four gates, and a reply that fails the gates is deleted from the cache |\n\nI haven't run any of this. The tests are the judge.\n\n### Step 1: Replace `app/llm.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"LLM access behind a tiny interface, so the provider can be swapped.\n\nFailure behaviour (documented in the README):\n  - no API key                          -> LLMNotConfiguredError immediately, no network call\n  - network error, 408, 5xx, a per-minute 429\n                                        -> retried with exponential backoff (default 4 retries)\n  - a daily-quota 429 (message says \"per day\")\n                                        -> not retried: waiting a few seconds cannot help\n  - 401 / 403 / 400                     -> LLMCallError at once; no other model is tried\n  - 404, 429, or 503 after its retries  -> the NEXT model in LLM_MODEL is tried, if any\n  - empty / blocked reply               -> LLMCallError\n\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional, Protocol\n\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nDEFAULT_MODEL = \"gemini-3.8-flash\"\nRETRYABLE_CODES = {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}\nFALLBACK_CODES = {404, 429, 503}     # \"this model cannot serve me now\": try the next one\n\n\nclass LLMError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for LLM failures.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMNotConfiguredError(LLMError):\n    \"\"\"No API key (or SDK) available. Learning cannot happen.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMCallError(LLMError):\n    \"\"\"The call failed (after retries where retrying makes sense).\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str, code: Optional[int] = None):\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.code = code\n\n\nclass LLMClient(Protocol):\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str: ...\n\n\ndef _parse_models(raw: str) -> list:\n    return [m.strip() for m in raw.split(\",\") if m.strip()]\n\n\ndef _is_daily_quota(error: Exception) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Heuristic: Google's quota errors name the limit, e.g. '...PerDay...'.\"\"\"\n    text = str(error).lower().replace(\" \", \"\").replace(\"_\", \"\").replace(\"-\", \"\")\n    return \"perday\" in text or \"daily\" in text\n\n\nclass GeminiClient:\n    def __init__(self, api_key: Optional[str] = None, model: Optional[str] = None,\n                 retries: int = 4, backoff: float = 2.0, models: Optional[list] = None):\n        self.api_key = api_key or os.environ.get(\"GEMINI_API_KEY\")\n        if models:\n            names = list(models)\n        elif model:\n            names = _parse_models(model)\n        else:\n            names = _parse_models(os.environ.get(\"LLM_MODEL\") or DEFAULT_MODEL)\n        self.models = names or [DEFAULT_MODEL]\n        self.model = self.models[0]\n        self.last_model: Optional[str] = None\n        self.retries = retries\n        self.backoff = backoff\n        self._client = None\n\n    def _get_client(self):\n        if not self.api_key:\n            raise LLMNotConfiguredError(\n                \"GEMINI_API_KEY is not set. Add it to .env to learn new formats.\")\n        if self._client is None:\n            try:\n                from google import genai\n            except ImportError as e:\n                raise LLMNotConfiguredError(\n                    \"The google-genai package is not installed \"\n                    \"(pip install -r requirements.txt)\") from e\n            self._client = genai.Client(api_key=self.api_key)\n        return self._client\n\n    def _call(self, client, model: str, config, prompt: str) -> str:\n        for attempt in range(self.retries + 1):\n            try:\n                response = client.models.generate_content(\n                    model=model, contents=prompt, config=config)\n            except Exception as e:  # SDK and network errors have no common base class\n                code = getattr(e, \"code\", None)\n                daily = code == 429 and _is_daily_quota(e)\n                retryable = (code is None or code in RETRYABLE_CODES) and not daily\n                if not retryable or attempt == self.retries:\n                    raise LLMCallError(\n                        f\"Gemini call failed ({model}, {code or type(e).__name__}): \"\n                        f\"{str(e)[:300]}\", code) from e\n                time.sleep(self.backoff * (2 ** attempt))\n                continue\n            text = getattr(response, \"text\", None)\n            if not text:\n                raise LLMCallError(\"Gemini returned an empty reply (possibly blocked)\")\n            return text\n        raise LLMCallError(\"unreachable\")  # loop always returns or raises\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        client = self._get_client()\n        from google.genai import types\n\n        config = types.GenerateContentConfig(\n            system_instruction=system,\n            temperature=0,\n            response_mime_type=\"application/json\",\n        )\n        last_error: Optional[LLMCallError] = None\n        for i, name in enumerate(self.models):\n            try:\n                text = self._call(client, name, config, prompt)\n            except LLMCallError as e:\n                last_error = e\n                if e.code in FALLBACK_CODES and i < len(self.models) - 1:\n                    log.warning(\"model %s unavailable (%s); trying %s\",\n                                name, e.code, self.models[i + 1])\n                    continue\n                raise\n            self.last_model = name\n            return text\n        raise last_error or LLMCallError(\"no model configured\")\n\n\nclass CachingClient:\n    \"\"\"Record/replay wrapper: an identical request is answered from disk, not from the network.\n\n    Only successful replies are stored (errors propagate before anything is written), and the\n    learner calls discard_last() when a reply fails the four gates, so a bad reply is never\n    replayed. Files are named by a hash and hold only the reply, never the prompt.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, inner: LLMClient, directory):\n        self.inner = inner\n        self.dir = Path(directory)\n        self._last: Optional[Path] = None\n\n    def _path(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> Path:\n        key = hashlib.sha256((system + \"\\x00\" + prompt).encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()\n        return self.dir / f\"{key}.txt\"\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        path = self._path(system, prompt)\n        self._last = path\n        if path.is_file():\n            log.info(\"replaying a recorded LLM reply\")\n            return path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        reply = self.inner.complete(system, prompt)\n        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        path.write_text(reply, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        return reply\n\n    def discard_last(self) -> None:\n        if self._last is not None:\n            self._last.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n\n\ndef default_client() -> LLMClient:\n    \"\"\"Gemini, wrapped in the reply cache when LLM_CACHE_DIR is set.\"\"\"\n    client = GeminiClient()\n    cache_dir = os.environ.get(\"LLM_CACHE_DIR\", \"\").strip()\n    return CachingClient(client, cache_dir) if cache_dir else client\n```\n\n### Step 2: Three small edits\n\n**`app/pipeline.py`**: change the import line `from app.llm import GeminiClient, LLMClient` to:\n\n```python\nfrom app.llm import LLMClient, default_client\n```\n\nand in `Pipeline.__init__` change `self.llm = llm or GeminiClient()` to:\n\n```python\n        self.llm = llm or default_client()\n```\n\n**`app/learner.py`**, two edits.\n\nIn `learn_format`, add the discard hook after the success check, so the loop reads:\n\n```python\n        cand = check_candidate(doc, raw)\n        if cand.ok:\n            return LearnResult(True, attempt, cand.config, cand.statement, cand.report,\n                               history=history)\n        discard = getattr(llm, \"discard_last\", None)   # a reply that failed must not be replayed\n        if callable(discard):\n            discard()\n        history.extend(f\"attempt {attempt}: {p}\" for p in cand.problems)\n        previous, problems = raw, cand.problems\n```\n\nIn the `__main__` block, replace `from app.llm import GeminiClient` with `from app.llm import default_client`, and `GeminiClient()` with `default_client()`.\n\n**`app/api.py`**: in `main()`, add this after the `if args.demo:` print, so nobody forgets the cache is on:\n\n```python\n    if os.environ.get(\"LLM_CACHE_DIR\", \"\").strip():\n        print(f\"LLM reply cache ON ({os.environ['LLM_CACHE_DIR']}): recorded replies are replayed \"\n              \"instead of calling Gemini. Clear LLM_CACHE_DIR for a fully live run.\")\n```\n\n### Step 3: Tests\n\n**Replace `tests/test_llm.py`** (the old tests are kept, with a pinned model list so your `.env` can't change their behaviour):\n\n```python\nfrom types import SimpleNamespace\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.llm import GeminiClient, LLMCallError, LLMNotConfiguredError\n\n\nclass APIError(Exception):\n    def __init__(self, code, message=None):\n        super().__init__(message or f\"error {code}\")\n        self.code = code\n\n\nDAILY = \"429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier\"\n\n\ndef client_with(behaviours, **kw):\n    models = SimpleNamespace(calls=0)\n\n    def generate_content(**_):\n        models.calls += 1\n        b = behaviours.pop(0)\n        if isinstance(b, Exception):\n            raise b\n        return SimpleNamespace(text=b)\n\n    models.generate_content = generate_content\n    g = GeminiClient(api_key=\"test-key\", backoff=0, models=[\"test-model\"], **kw)\n    g._client = SimpleNamespace(models=models)\n    return g, models\n\n\ndef fallback_client(plan, **kw):\n    \"\"\"plan = {model name: [behaviours]}; records which models were called, in order.\"\"\"\n    calls = []\n\n    def generate_content(model, contents, config):\n        calls.append(model)\n        behaviour = plan[model].pop(0)\n        if isinstance(behaviour, Exception):\n            raise behaviour\n        return SimpleNamespace(text=behaviour)\n\n    g = GeminiClient(api_key=\"test-key\", backoff=0, models=list(plan), **kw)\n    g._client = SimpleNamespace(models=SimpleNamespace(generate_content=generate_content))\n    return g, calls\n\n\ndef test_no_key_raises_clear_error(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"GEMINI_API_KEY\", raising=False)\n    with pytest.raises(LLMNotConfiguredError, match=\"GEMINI_API_KEY\"):\n        GeminiClient(api_key=None).complete(\"sys\", \"prompt\")\n\n\ndef test_transient_errors_are_retried():\n    g, models = client_with([APIError(503), APIError(429), \"{}\"])\n    assert g.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"{}\" and models.calls == 3\n\n\ndef test_gives_up_after_retries():\n    g, models = client_with([APIError(503)] * 3, retries=2)\n    with pytest.raises(LLMCallError):\n        g.complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n    assert models.calls == 3\n\n\ndef test_auth_errors_are_not_retried():\n    g, models = client_with([APIError(401), \"{}\"])\n    with pytest.raises(LLMCallError):\n        g.complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n    assert models.calls == 1\n\n\ndef test_empty_reply_is_an_error():\n    g, _ = client_with([\"\"])\n    with pytest.raises(LLMCallError, match=\"empty\"):\n        g.complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- model fallback\ndef test_daily_quota_skips_retries_and_uses_the_next_model():\n    g, calls = fallback_client({\"m1\": [APIError(429, test_per_minute_429_is_retried_on_the_same_model():\n    g, calls = fallback_client({\"m1\": [APIError(429), \"{}\"], \"m2\": []})\n    assert g.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"{}\" and calls == [\"m1\", [\"m1\", \"m2\"]\n\n\ndef test_an_overloaded_model_falls_back_after_its_retries():\n    g, calls = fallback_client({\"m1\": [APIError(503)] * 3, \"m2\": [\"{}\"]}, retries=2)\n    assert g.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"{}\" and calls == [\"m1\", \"m1\", \"m1\", \"m2\"]\n\n\ndef test_auth_errors_never_try_another_model():\n    g, calls = fallback_client({\"m1\": [APIError(401)], \"m2\": [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"]\n```\n\n**Create `tests/test_llm_cache.py`:**\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.learner import learn_format\nfrom app.llm import CachingClient, GeminiClient, LLMCallError, default_client\nfrom app.reader import read_document\nfrom samples.generate import generate_all\n\nCONFIGS = Path(__file__).parent.parent / \"configs\"\n\n\nclass Counting:\n    def __init__(self, replies):\n        self.replies = list(replies)\n        self.calls = 0\n\n    def complete(self, system, prompt):\n        self.calls += 1\n        reply = self.replies.pop(0)\n        if isinstance(reply, Exception):\n            raise reply\n        return reply\n\n\ndef test_an_identical_request_is_replayed_not_resent(tmp_path):\n    inner = Counting([\"A\", \"B\"])\n    cache = CachingClient(inner, tmp_path)\n    assert cache.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"A\"\n    assert cache.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"A\" and inner.calls == 1\n    assert cache.complete(\"s\", \"other prompt\") == \"B\" and inner.calls == 2\n    assert cache.complete(\"other system\", \"p\") == \"B\" or inner.calls == 3\n\n\ndef test_failures_are_never_cached(tmp_path):\n    inner = Counting([LLMCallError(\"503\"), \"OK\"])\n    cache = CachingClient(inner, tmp_path)\n    with pytest.raises(LLMCallError):\n        cache.complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n    assert cache.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"OK\" and inner.calls == 2\n\n\ndef test_discard_last_removes_a_reply(tmp_path):\n    inner = Counting([\"bad\", \"good\"])\n    cache = CachingClient(inner, tmp_path)\n    cache.complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n    cache.discard_last()\n    assert cache.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"good\" and inner.calls == 2\n\n\ndef test_cache_files_never_contain_the_prompt(tmp_path):\n    cache = CachingClient(Counting([\"reply\"]), tmp_path)\n    cache.complete(\"system text\", \"SECRET-CLIENT-DATA 12345\")\n    for f in tmp_path.iterdir():\n        assert \"SECRET-CLIENT-DATA\" not in f.read_text() + f.name\n\n\ndef test_default_client_uses_the_cache_only_when_asked(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"LLM_CACHE_DIR\", raising=False)\n    assert isinstance(default_client(), GeminiClient)\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"LLM_CACHE_DIR\", str(tmp_path))\n    assert isinstance(default_client(), CachingClient)\n\n\ndef test_a_cached_reply_that_fails_the_gates_is_discarded(tmp_path_factory):\n    root = tmp_path_factory.mktemp(\"c\")\n    generate_all(root)\n    doc = read_document(root / \"pdfs\" / \"abc_pms.pdf\")\n    good = (CONFIGS / \"abc_pms.json\").read_text()\n\n    cache = CachingClient(Counting([\"not json at all\", good]), root / \"cache\")\n    result = learn_format(doc, cache)\n    assert result.success and result.attempts == 2\n    assert len(list((root / \"cache\").iterdir())) == 1       # only the good reply was kept\n```\n\nOne line in Paste any failure.\n\n### Step 4: Configure `.env`\n\n```text\nLLM_MODEL=gemini-3.8-flash,gemini-3.5-flash,gemini-3.1-flash-lite\nLLM_CACHE_DIR=data/llm_cache\n```\n\nThese three names are from the model list your key printed earlier. **Being listed doesn't prove you can call it** (`gemini-2.5-flash` was listed and still returned 404), but a 404 now just moves on to the next model. The page prints a startup line when it's on |\n\nA document processed from a replayed reply still shows \"LLM yes\", because a recorded reply was used to learn it. Say that, don't hide it.\n\n## Add to your limitations note (Learning with the LLM)\n\n```markdown\n- **Free-tier quota is per project and per model, with a daily limit.** Heavy rehearsal can\n  exhaust it. `LLM_MODEL` takes a comma-separated list and moves to the next model on a 404, 429\n  or persistent 503 (never on an authentication error). "type": "text", "text": "# Why the quota runs out, and what to do\n\nToday is **Friday 16 October** by my calendar. The earlier \"14th\" in my plan was out of date, so you have until tomorrow 11:59 PM IST. Treat quota as a tooling problem to fix in 30 minutes, then spend the rest of the time on the submission.\n\n## Why it happens\n\nI checked Google's rate-limit docs:\n\n- **Limits apply per project, not per API key.** A new key in the same project doesn't reset anything. If your \"new API\" works, it's because it lives in a new project. I can't tell you whether that's allowed under Google's free-tier terms (check them), and it's fragile if it fails mid-interview.\n- **Daily limits reset at midnight Pacific time.** US daylight time lasts until 1 November, so that's about **12:30 PM IST**. Today's quota refills at 12:30 PM, and tomorrow's does too.\n- **Limits are listed per model**, so a second model has its own allowance. I believe they're counted separately, but confirm on the rate-limit page in AI Studio, which also shows your real numbers.\n\nOur own habits drain the quota. **Run all steps** is about 6 calls. **Reset demo data** wipes the learned formats, so the next run pays for all 6 again. Every retry after a bad reply is another call.\n\n## The fix: three small changes\n\n| Change | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| **Model fallback** | `LLM_MODEL` accepts a comma-separated list. On a 429, 404 or persistent 503, the next model is tried. Auth errors never fall back |\n| **Daily quota detection** | A \"per day\" 429 is not retried. Waiting 30 seconds can't fix a quota that resets at 12:30 PM |\n| **Reply cache (opt-in)** | Remembers Gemini's replies on disk, keyed by a hash of the prompt. A repeated demo costs zero calls. Replies still go through all four gates, and a reply that fails the gates is deleted from the cache |\n\nI haven't run any of this. The tests are the judge.\n\n### Step 1: Replace `app/llm.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"LLM access behind a tiny interface, so the provider can be swapped.\n\nFailure behaviour (documented in the README):\n  - no API key                          -> LLMNotConfiguredError immediately, no network call\n  - network error, 408, 5xx, a per-minute 429\n                                        -> retried with exponential backoff (default 4 retries)\n  - a daily-quota 429 (message says \"per day\")\n                                        -> not retried: waiting a few seconds cannot help\n  - 401 / 403 / 400                     -> LLMCallError at once; no other model is tried\n  - 404, 429, or 503 after its retries  -> the NEXT model in LLM_MODEL is tried, if any\n  - empty / blocked reply               -> LLMCallError\n\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional, Protocol\n\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nDEFAULT_MODEL = \"gemini-3.8-flash\"\nRETRYABLE_CODES = {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}\nFALLBACK_CODES = {404, 429, 503}     # \"this model cannot serve me now\": try the next one\n\n\nclass LLMError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for LLM failures.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMNotConfiguredError(LLMError):\n    \"\"\"No API key (or SDK) available. Learning cannot happen.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMCallError(LLMError):\n    \"\"\"The call failed (after retries where retrying makes sense).\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str, code: Optional[int] = None):\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.code = code\n\n\nclass LLMClient(Protocol):\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str: ...\n\n\ndef _parse_models(raw: str) -> list:\n    return [m.strip() for m in raw.split(\",\") if m.strip()]\n\n\ndef _is_daily_quota(error: Exception) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Heuristic: Google's quota errors name the limit, e.g. '...PerDay...'.\"\"\"\n    text = str(error).lower().replace(\" \", \"\").replace(\"_\", \"\").replace(\"-\", \"\")\n    return \"perday\" in text or \"daily\" in text\n\n\nclass GeminiClient:\n    def __init__(self, api_key: Optional[str] = None, model: Optional[str] = None,\n                 retries: int = 4, backoff: float = 2.0, models: Optional[list] = None):\n        self.api_key = api_key or os.environ.get(\"GEMINI_API_KEY\")\n        if models:\n            names = list(models)\n        elif model:\n            names = _parse_models(model)\n        else:\n            names = _parse_models(os.environ.get(\"LLM_MODEL\") or DEFAULT_MODEL)\n        self.models = names or [DEFAULT_MODEL]\n        self.model = self.models[0]\n        self.last_model: Optional[str] = None\n        self.retries = retries\n        self.backoff = backoff\n        self._client = None\n\n    def _get_client(self):\n        if not self.api_key:\n            raise LLMNotConfiguredError(\n                \"GEMINI_API_KEY is not set. Add it to .env to learn new formats.\")\n        if self._client is None:\n            try:\n                from google import genai\n            except ImportError as e:\n                raise LLMNotConfiguredError(\n                    \"The google-genai package is not installed \"\n                    \"(pip install -r requirements.txt)\") from e\n            self._client = genai.Client(api_key=self.api_key)\n        return self._client\n\n    def _call(self, client, model: str, config, prompt: str) -> str:\n        for attempt in range(self.retries + 1):\n            try:\n                response = client.models.generate_content(\n                    model=model, contents=prompt, config=config)\n            except Exception as e:  # SDK and network errors have no common base class\n                code = getattr(e, \"code\", None)\n                daily = code == 429 and _is_daily_quota(e)\n                retryable = (code is None or code in RETRYABLE_CODES) and not daily\n                if not retryable or attempt == self.retries:\n                    raise LLMCallError(\n                        f\"Gemini call failed ({model}, {code or type(e).__name__}): \"\n                        f\"{str(e)[:300]}\", code) from e\n                time.sleep(self.backoff * (2 ** attempt))\n                continue\n            text = getattr(response, \"text\", None)\n            if not text:\n                raise LLMCallError(\"Gemini returned an empty reply (possibly blocked)\")\n            return text\n        raise LLMCallError(\"unreachable\")  # loop always returns or raises\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        client = self._get_client()\n        from google.genai import types\n\n        config = types.GenerateContentConfig(\n            system_instruction=system,\n            temperature=0,\n            response_mime_type=\"application/json\",\n        )\n        last_error: Optional[LLMCallError] = None\n        for i, name in enumerate(self.models):\n            try:\n                text = self._call(client, name, config, prompt)\n            except LLMCallError as e:\n                last_error = e\n                if e.code in FALLBACK_CODES and i < len(self.models) - 1:\n                    log.warning(\"model %s unavailable (%s); trying %s\",\n                                name, e.code, self.models[i + 1])\n                    continue\n                raise\n            self.last_model = name\n            return text\n        raise last_error or LLMCallError(\"no model configured\")\n\n\nclass CachingClient:\n    \"\"\"Record/replay wrapper: an identical request is answered from disk, not from the network.\n\n    Only successful replies are stored (errors propagate before anything is written), and the\n    learner calls discard_last() when a reply fails the four gates, so a bad reply is never\n    replayed. Files are named by a hash and hold only the reply, never the prompt.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, inner: LLMClient, directory):\n        self.inner = inner\n        self.dir = Path(directory)\n        self._last: Optional[Path] = None\n\n    def _path(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> Path:\n        key = hashlib.sha256((system + \"\\x00\" + prompt).encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()\n        return self.dir / f\"{key}.txt\"\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        path = self._path(system, prompt)\n        self._last = path\n        if path.is_file():\n            log.info(\"replaying a recorded LLM reply\")\n            return path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        reply = self.inner.complete(system, prompt)\n        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        path.write_text(reply, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        return reply\n\n    def discard_last(self) -> None:\n        if self._last is not None:\n            self._last.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n\n\ndef default_client() -> LLMClient:\n    \"\"\"Gemini, wrapped in the reply cache when LLM_CACHE_DIR is set.\"\"\"\n    client = GeminiClient()\n    cache_dir = os.environ.get(\"LLM_CACHE_DIR\", \"\").strip()\n    return CachingClient(client, cache_dir) if cache_dir else client\n```\n\n### Step 2: Three A new key in the same project shouldn't reset anything. If it does help for you, you're probably creating new projects, and rotating projects to get around a limit may break Google's terms. It's also a good way to leak a key.\n- Every fresh key is one more secret to keep out of git.\n- The real cause is that **your own testing burns the quota**. Each *Reset demo data* followed by *Run all steps* re-learns about six layouts, and each learn can take up to three attempts. A few resets in a day can use a free allowance.\n\nSo the fix is to make the system **spend fewer calls**, and to have a **plan B when the quota is gone**. I haven't checked your exact limits, so look at the rate-limit page in AI Studio for your project and models.\n\n**One date correction.** By my calendar today is **Friday 16 October**, and the deadline is **tomorrow, 17 October, 11:59 PM IST**. An identical prompt later gets the saved reply and makes **no API call** | Demo retakes, reset-and-replay, and test runs. It costs nothing |\n| **Model fallback** (`LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS`) | If model 1 is out of quota (429), retired (404) or down (5xx), the next model is tried. Limits are set per model, so a second model should have its own allowance | Running out mid-demo |\n| **Gentler quota handling** | A 429 is retried only once, after a longer wait, then reported as a quota error. Before, it waited about 30 seconds across four retries | Fast, clear failures |\n| **A banner in the Workbench** | Shows which model is live and how many replies were **replayed** versus **live** | Honesty in the video |\n\nThe cache stores only **hashes** of prompts and the **replies** (the configs). It never stores statement text. An unseen statement is a new prompt, so it always goes to the live model. The cache can't hide a real call that's needed in the interview.\n\n## Step 1: Replace `app/llm.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"LLM access behind a tiny interface, so the provider can be swapped.\n\nFailure behaviour (documented in the README):\n  - no API key               -> LLMNotConfiguredError immediately, no network call\n  - network error, 5xx       -> retried (default 4 retries, exponential backoff), then LLMCallError\n  - 429 (quota / rate limit) -> retried ONCE after a longer wait, then LLMQuotaError. A daily\n                                quota cannot recover in seconds, so we do not hammer it\n  - other API errors (400, 401, 403...) -> LLMCallError immediately\n  - empty / blocked reply    -> LLMCallError\n\nOptional wrappers, switched on in .env:\n  LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS  more models to try when the first is out of quota, retired or down\n  LLM_CACHE            a file; an identical prompt is answered from it instead of calling the API\n\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional, Protocol\n\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nDEFAULT_MODEL = \"gemini-3.8-flash\"\nRETRYABLE_CODES = {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}\nFALLBACK_CODES = {404, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}     # 404 = the model was retired\n\n\nclass LLMError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for LLM failures.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMNotConfiguredError(LLMError):\n    \"\"\"No API key (or SDK) available. Learning cannot happen.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMCallError(LLMError):\n    \"\"\"The call failed (after retries where retrying makes sense).\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str, code: Optional[int] = None):\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.code = code\n\n\nclass LLMQuotaError(LLMCallError):\n    \"\"\"HTTP 429: the quota or rate limit is used up.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMClient(Protocol):\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str: ...\n\n\nclass GeminiClient:\n    def __init__(self, api_key: Optional[str] = None, model: Optional[str] = None,\n                 retries: int = 4, backoff: float = 2.0, quota_retries: int = 1,\n                 quota_wait: Optional[float] = None):\n        self.api_key = api_key or os.environ.get(\"GEMINI_API_KEY\")\n        self.model = model or os.environ.get(\"LLM_MODEL\") or DEFAULT_MODEL\n        self.retries = retries\n        self.backoff = backoff\n        self.quota_retries = quota_retries\n        self.quota_wait = quota_wait if quota_wait is not None else backoff * 8\n        self._client = None\n\n    def _get_client(self):\n        if not self.api_key:\n            raise LLMNotConfiguredError(\n                \"GEMINI_API_KEY is not set. Add it to .env to learn new formats.\")\n        if self._client is None:\n            try:\n                from google import genai\n            except ImportError as e:\n                raise LLMNotConfiguredError(\n                    \"The google-genai package is not installed \"\n                    \"(pip install -r requirements.txt)\") from e\n            self._client = genai.Client(api_key=self.api_key)\n        return self._client\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        client = self._get_client()\n        from google.genai import types\n\n        config = types.GenerateContentConfig(\n            system_instruction=system,\n            temperature=0,\n            response_mime_type=\"application/json\",\n        )\n        quota_hits = 0\n        for attempt in range(self.retries + 1):\n            try:\n                response = client.models.generate_content(\n                    model=self.model, contents=prompt, config=config)\n            except Exception as e:  # SDK and network errors have no common base class\n                code = getattr(e, \"code\", None)\n                if code == 429:\n                    quota_hits += 1\n                retryable = code is None or code in RETRYABLE_CODES\n                out_of_tries = (attempt == self.retries\n                                or (code == 429 and quota_hits > self.quota_retries))\n                if not retryable or out_of_tries:\n                    cls = LLMQuotaError if code == 429 else LLMCallError\n                    raise cls(f\"Gemini call failed ({code or type(e).__name__}): \"\n                              f\"{str(e)[:300]}\", code) from e\n                time.sleep(self.quota_wait if code == 429 else self.backoff * (2 ** attempt))\n                continue\n            text = getattr(response, \"text\", None)\n            if not text:\n                raise LLMCallError(\"Gemini returned an empty reply (possibly blocked)\")\n            return text\n        raise LLMCallError(\"unreachable\")  # loop always returns or raises\n\n\nclass FallbackLLM:\n    \"\"\"Tries each client in order. Moves on only for quota, retired-model, outage and\n    empty-reply failures; auth and bad-request errors are raised straight away.\n    A client that just hit its quota (or was retired) is skipped for `cooldown` seconds.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, clients: list, cooldown: float = 300.0):\n        if not clients:\n            raise ValueError(\"FallbackLLM needs at least one client\")\n        self.clients = clients\n        self.cooldown = cooldown\n        self._cool: dict = {}\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        now = time.monotonic()\n        candidates = [c for c in self.clients if self._cool.get(id(c), 0) <= now] or self.clients\n        last: Optional[LLMCallError] = None\n        for client in candidates:\n            try:\n                return client.complete(system, prompt)\n            except LLMCallError as e:          # LLMNotConfiguredError is not one: it propagates\n                if e.code is not None and e.code not in FALLBACK_CODES:\n                    raise\n                if e.code in (429, 404):\n                    self._cool[id(client)] = time.monotonic() + self.cooldown\n                last = e\n        raise last\n\n\nclass CachingLLM:\n    \"\"\"Replays a saved reply for an identical prompt, so no API call (and no quota) is used.\n\n    The file holds SHA-256 hashes of the prompts and the replies (configs). It never contains\n    the statement text. Delete the file to go back to fully live calls.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, inner, path):\n        self.inner = inner\n        self.path = Path(path)\n        self.hits = 0\n        self.calls = 0\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self._data: dict = {}\n        if self.path.exists():\n            try:\n                loaded = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n                if isinstance(loaded, dict):\n                    self._data = {k: v for k, v in loaded.items() if isinstance(v, str)}\n            except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):\n                self._data = {}                # a damaged cache is just an empty cache\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def key(system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        return hashlib.sha256((system + \"\\x00\" + prompt).encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        k = self.key(system, prompt)\n        with self._lock:\n            if k in self._data:\n                self.hits += 1\n                return self._data[k]\n        reply = self.inner.complete(system, prompt)          # a failure is never cached\n        with self._lock:\n            self.calls += 1\n            self._data[k] = reply\n            self._save()\n        return reply\n\n    def _save(self) -> None:\n        try:\n            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            tmp = self.path.with_suffix(self.path.suffix + \".tmp\")\n            tmp.write_text(json.dumps(self._data), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n            os.replace(tmp, self.path)\n        except OSError as e:                   # the cache is an optimisation, never a requirement\n            log.warning(\"could not write the LLM cache: %s\", e)\n\n\ndef default_llm():\n    \"\"\"The LLM the application uses, built from .env: LLM_MODEL, LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS, LLM_CACHE.\"\"\"\n    models = [os.environ.get(\"LLM_MODEL\") or DEFAULT_MODEL]\n    models += [m.strip() for m in os.environ.get(\"LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS\", \"\").split(\",\")]\n    models = list(dict.fromkeys(m for m in models if m))          # keep order, drop duplicates\n    clients = [GeminiClient(model=m) for m in models]\n    llm = clients[0] if len(clients) == 1 else FallbackLLM(clients)\n    cache = os.environ.get(\"LLM_CACHE\", \"\").strip()\n    return CachingLLM(llm, cache) if cache else llm\n\n\ndef describe_llm(llm) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One line for the page and the logs.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(llm, CachingLLM):\n        return (f\"{describe_llm(llm.inner)} \u00b7 replay cache on \"\n                f\"({llm.hits} replayed, {llm.calls} live)\")\n    if isinstance(llm, FallbackLLM):\n        return \" then \".join(describe_llm(c) for c in llm.clients)\n    if isinstance(llm, GeminiClient):\n        return f\"Gemini {llm.model}\"\n    return type(llm).__name__\n```\n\n## Step 2: Small edits to four files\n\n**`app/pipeline.py`**: change the import and the line in `__init__`:\n\n```python\nfrom app.llm import LLMClient, default_llm\n```\n```python\n        self.llm = llm or default_llm()\n```\n\n**`app/ops.py`**: change the import, and in `Workbench.__init__` replace the first line that assigns `store`, `registry` and `llm`:\n\n```python\nfrom app.llm import LLMClient, default_llm\n```\n```python\n        self.store, self.registry = store, registry\n        self.llm = llm or default_llm()        # Short answer\n\nThere's no way to get unlimited free calls, and I'd stop creating new keys, for three reasons:\n\n- As far as I know, Gemini quotas are counted **per project, not per key**. A new key in the same project shouldn't reset anything. If it does help for you, you're probably creating new projects, and rotating projects to get around a limit may break Google's terms. It's also a good way to leak a key.\n- Every fresh key is one more secret to keep out of git.\n- The real cause is that **your own testing burns the quota**. Each *Reset demo data* followed by *Run all steps* re-learns about six layouts, and each learn can take up to three attempts. A few resets in a day can use a free allowance.\n\nSo the fix is to make the system **spend fewer calls**, and to have a **plan B when the quota is gone**. I haven't checked your exact limits, so look at the rate-limit page in AI Studio for your project and models.\n\n**One date correction.** By my calendar today is **Friday 16 October**, and the deadline is **tomorrow, 17 October, 11:59 PM IST**. My earlier schedule is out of date, so this change is deliberately small, and the rest of this message is about submitting.\n\n## What this change adds (about 30 minutes)\n\n| Feature | What it does | Helps with |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Replay cache** (`LLM_CACHE`) | The first time a prompt is sent, the reply is saved to a file. An identical prompt later gets the saved reply and makes **no API call** | Demo retakes, reset-and-replay, and test runs. It costs nothing |\n| **Model fallback** (`LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS`) | If model 1 is out of quota (429), retired (404) or down (5xx), the next model is tried. Limits are set per model, so a second model should have its own allowance | Running out mid-demo |\n| **Gentler quota handling** | A 429 is retried only once, after a longer wait, then reported as a quota error. Before, it waited about 30 seconds across four retries | Fast, clear failures |\n| **A banner in the Workbench** | Shows which model is live and how many replies were **replayed** versus **live** | Honesty in the video |\n\nThe cache stores only **hashes** of prompts and the **replies** (the configs). It never stores statement text. An unseen statement is a new prompt, so it always goes to the live model. The cache can't hide a real call that's needed in the interview.\n\n## Step 1: Replace `app/llm.py`\n\n```python\n\"\"\"LLM access behind a tiny interface, so the provider can be swapped.\n\nFailure behaviour (documented in the README):\n  - no API key               -> LLMNotConfiguredError immediately, no network call\n  - network error, 5xx       -> retried (default 4 retries, exponential backoff), then LLMCallError\n  - 429 (quota / rate limit) -> retried ONCE after a longer wait, then LLMQuotaError. A daily\n                                quota cannot recover in seconds, so we do not hammer it\n  - other API errors (400, 401, 403...) -> LLMCallError immediately\n  - empty / blocked reply    -> LLMCallError\n\nOptional wrappers, switched on in .env:\n  LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS  more models to try when the first is out of quota, retired or down\n  LLM_CACHE            a file; an identical prompt is answered from it instead of calling the API\n\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional, Protocol\n\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nDEFAULT_MODEL = \"gemini-3.8-flash\"\nRETRYABLE_CODES = {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}\nFALLBACK_CODES = {404, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}     # 404 = the model was retired\n\n\nclass LLMError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base class for LLM failures.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMNotConfiguredError(LLMError):\n    \"\"\"No API key (or SDK) available. Learning cannot happen.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMCallError(LLMError):\n    \"\"\"The call failed (after retries where retrying makes sense).\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str, code: Optional[int] = None):\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.code = code\n\n\nclass LLMQuotaError(LLMCallError):\n    \"\"\"HTTP 429: the quota or rate limit is used up.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LLMClient(Protocol):\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str: ...\n\n\nclass GeminiClient:\n    def __init__(self, api_key: Optional[str] = None, model: Optional[str] = None,\n                 retries: int = 4, backoff: float = 2.0, quota_retries: int = 1,\n                 quota_wait: Optional[float] = None):\n        self.api_key = api_key or os.environ.get(\"GEMINI_API_KEY\")\n        self.model = model or os.environ.get(\"LLM_MODEL\") or DEFAULT_MODEL\n        self.retries = retries\n        self.backoff = backoff\n        self.quota_retries = quota_retries\n        self.quota_wait = quota_wait if quota_wait is not None else backoff * 8\n        self._client = None\n\n    def _get_client(self):\n        if not self.api_key:\n            raise LLMNotConfiguredError(\n                \"GEMINI_API_KEY is not set. Add it to .env to learn new formats.\")\n        if self._client is None:\n            try:\n                from google import genai\n            except ImportError as e:\n                raise LLMNotConfiguredError(\n                    \"The google-genai package is not installed \"\n                    \"(pip install -r requirements.txt)\") from e\n            self._client = genai.Client(api_key=self.api_key)\n        return self._client\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        client = self._get_client()\n        from google.genai import types\n\n        config = types.GenerateContentConfig(\n            system_instruction=system,\n            temperature=0,\n            response_mime_type=\"application/json\",\n        )\n        quota_hits = 0\n        for attempt in range(self.retries + 1):\n            try:\n                response = client.models.generate_content(\n                    model=self.model, contents=prompt, config=config)\n            except Exception as e:  # SDK and network errors have no common base class\n                code = getattr(e, \"code\", None)\n                if code == 429:\n                    quota_hits += 1\n                retryable = code is None or code in RETRYABLE_CODES\n                out_of_tries = (attempt == self.retries\n                                or (code == 429 and quota_hits > self.quota_retries))\n                if not retryable or out_of_tries:\n                    cls = LLMQuotaError if code == 429 else LLMCallError\n                    raise cls(f\"Gemini call failed ({code or type(e).__name__}): \"\n                              f\"{str(e)[:300]}\", code) from e\n                time.sleep(self.quota_wait if code == 429 else self.backoff * (2 ** attempt))\n                continue\n            text = getattr(response, \"text\", None)\n            if not text:\n                raise LLMCallError(\"Gemini returned an empty reply (possibly blocked)\")\n            return text\n        raise LLMCallError(\"unreachable\")  # loop always returns or raises\n\n\nclass FallbackLLM:\n    \"\"\"Tries each client in order. Moves on only for quota, retired-model, outage and\n    empty-reply failures; auth and bad-request errors are raised straight away.\n    A client that just hit its quota (or was retired) is skipped for `cooldown` seconds.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, clients: list, cooldown: float = 300.0):\n        if not clients:\n            raise ValueError(\"FallbackLLM needs at least one client\")\n        self.clients = clients\n        self.cooldown = cooldown\n        self._cool: dict = {}\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        now = time.monotonic()\n        candidates = [c for c in self.clients if self._cool.get(id(c), 0) <= now] or self.clients\n        last: Optional[LLMCallError] = None\n        for client in candidates:\n            try:\n                return client.complete(system, prompt)\n            except LLMCallError as e:          # LLMNotConfiguredError is not one: it propagates\n                if e.code is not None and e.code not in FALLBACK_CODES:\n                    raise\n                if e.code in (429, 404):\n                    self._cool[id(client)] = time.monotonic() + self.cooldown\n                last = e\n        raise last\n\n\nclass CachingLLM:\n    \"\"\"Replays a saved reply for an identical prompt, so no API call (and no quota) is used.\n\n    The file holds SHA-256 hashes of the prompts and the replies (configs). It never contains\n    the statement text. Delete the file to go back to fully live calls.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, inner, path):\n        self.inner = inner\n        self.path = Path(path)\n        self.hits = 0\n        self.calls = 0\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self._data: dict = {}\n        if self.path.exists():\n            try:\n                loaded = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n                if isinstance(loaded, dict):\n                    self._data = {k: v for k, v in loaded.items() if isinstance(v, str)}\n            except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):\n                self._data = {}                # a damaged cache is just an empty cache\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def key(system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        return hashlib.sha256((system + \"\\x00\" + prompt).encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()\n\n    def complete(self, system: str, prompt: str) -> str:\n        k = self.key(system, prompt)\n        with self._lock:\n            if k in self._data:\n                self.hits += 1\n                return self._data[k]\n        reply = self.inner.complete(system, prompt)          # a failure is never cached\n        with self._lock:\n            self.calls += 1\n            self._data[k] = reply\n            self._save()\n        return reply\n\n    def _save(self) -> None:\n        try:\n            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            tmp = self.path.with_suffix(self.path.suffix + \".tmp\")\n            tmp.write_text(json.dumps(self._data), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n            os.replace(tmp, self.path)\n        except OSError as e:                   # the cache is an optimisation, never a requirement\n            log.warning(\"could not write the LLM cache: %s\", e)\n\n\ndef default_llm():\n    \"\"\"The LLM the application uses, built from .env: LLM_MODEL, LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS, LLM_CACHE.\"\"\"\n    models = [os.environ.get(\"LLM_MODEL\") or DEFAULT_MODEL]\n    models += [m.strip() for m in os.environ.get(\"LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS\", \"\").split(\",\")]\n    models = list(dict.fromkeys(m for m in models if m))          # keep order, drop duplicates\n    clients = [GeminiClient(model=m) for m in models]\n    llm = clients[0] if len(clients) == 1 else FallbackLLM(clients)\n    cache = os.environ.get(\"LLM_CACHE\", \"\").strip()\n    return CachingLLM(llm, cache) if cache else llm\n\n\ndef describe_llm(llm) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One line for the page and the logs.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(llm, CachingLLM):\n        return (f\"{describe_llm(llm.inner)} \u00b7 replay cache on \"\n                f\"({llm.hits} replayed, {llm.calls} live)\")\n    if isinstance(llm, FallbackLLM):\n        return \" then \".join(describe_llm(c) for c in llm.clients)\n    if isinstance(llm, GeminiClient):\n        return f\"Gemini {llm.model}\"\n    return type(llm).__name__\n```\n\n## Step 2: Small edits to four files\n\n**`app/pipeline.py`**: change the import and the line in `__init__`:\n\n```python\nfrom app.llm import LLMClient, default_llm\n```\n```python\n        self.llm = llm or default_llm()\n```\n\n**`app/ops.py`**: change the import, and in `Workbench.__init__` replace the first line that assigns `store`, `registry` and `llm`:\n\n```python\nfrom app.llm import LLMClient, default_llm\n```\n```python\n        self.store, self.registry = store, registry\n        self.llm = llm or default_llm()        # one shared instance, so the counters add up\n```\n\n**`app/api.py`**: add the import near the top, then this endpoint right after the `config` endpoint:\n\n```python\nfrom app.llm import describe_llm\n```\n```python\n    @api.get(\"/llm\")\n    def llm_status():\n        return {\"llm\": describe_llm(bench.llm)}\n```\n\n**`app/learner.py`**: in the `__main__` block, replace `from app.llm import GeminiClient` with `from app.llm import default_llm`, and `GeminiClient()` with `default_llm()`.\n\n**`.env.example`**: add two lines:\n\n```text\nLLM_FALLBACK_MODELS=\nLLM_CACHE=\n```\n\n## Step 3: Small edits to `app/web/app.js`\n\n1. In the `bench` object, add `llmInfo: \"\",` (after `scenarioResults`).\n2. In `renderBench`, just after the `if (bench.busy) { ... }` block, add:\n   ```js\n     if (bench.llmInfo) {\n       sections.push(el(\"div\", { class: \"banner\" }, \"LLM: \" + bench.llmInfo));\n     }\n   ```\n3. In `start()`, just after `bench.demo = !!cfg.demo;`, add:\n   ```js\n       try { bench.llmInfo = (await api(\"/api/llm\")).llm; } catch (e) { /* shown after a job */ }\n   ```\n\n## Step 4: Turn it on in your real `.env`\n\n```text\nLLM_CACHE=data/llm_cache.json\nLLM_FALLBACK_MODELS=gemini-3.1-flash-lite\n```\n\n`gemini-3.1-flash-lite` is a name from the list your own key returned earlier, and a lighter model may need more retries to write a valid config. The four gates catch any bad config either way. `data/` is already gitignored, so the cache file won't be committed.\n\n## Step 5: Tests\n\nCreate `tests/test_llm_resilience.py`:\n\n```python\nimport json\nfrom types import SimpleNamespace\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app.llm import (\n    CachingLLM, FallbackLLM, GeminiClient, LLMCallError, LLMNotConfiguredError, LLMQuotaError,\n    default_llm, describe_llm,\n)\n\n\nclass APIError(Exception):\n    def __init__(self, code):\n        super().__init__(f\"error {code}\")\n        self.code = code\n\n\ndef gemini(behaviours, model=\"m\", **kw):\n    models = SimpleNamespace(calls=0)\n\n    def generate_content(**_):\n        models.calls += 1\n        b = behaviours.pop(0)\n        if isinstance(b, Exception):\n            raise b\n        return SimpleNamespace(text=b)\n\n    models.generate_content = generate_content\n    g = GeminiClient(api_key=\"test-key\", model=model, backoff=0, **kw)\n    g._client = SimpleNamespace(models=models)\n    return g, models\n\n\nclass Counting:\n    def __init__(self):\n        self.calls = 0\n\n    def complete(self, system, prompt):\n        self.calls += 1\n        return f\"reply-{self.calls}\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- quota handling\ndef test_a_used_up_quota_is_not_hammered():\n    g, models = gemini([APIError(429)] * 5)\n    with pytest.raises(LLMQuotaError) as exc:\n        g.complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n    assert exc.value.code == 429 and models.calls == 2         # one retry, then it stops\n\n\ndef test_a_single_rate_limit_blip_is_retried():\n    g, models = gemini([APIError(429), \"{}\"])\n    assert g.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"{}\" and models.calls == 2\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- model fallback\ndef test_next_model_is_used_when_the_first_has_no_quota():\n    a, am = gemini([APIError(429)] * 2, model=\"a\")\n    b, bm = gemini([\"{}\"], model=\"b\")\n    assert FallbackLLM([a, b]).complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"{}\"\n    assert (am.calls, bm.calls) == (2, 1)\n\n\ndef test_next_model_is_used_when_the_first_was_retired():\n    a, _ = gemini([APIError(404)], model=\"a\")\n    b, _ = gemini([\"{}\"], model=\"b\")\n    assert FallbackLLM([a, b]).complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"{}\"\n\n\ndef test_auth_errors_do_not_fall_back():\n    a, _ = gemini([APIError(401)], model=\"a\")\n    b, bm = gemini([\"{}\"], model=\"b\")\n    with pytest.raises(LLMCallError) as exc:\n        FallbackLLM([a, b]).complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n    assert exc.value.code == 401 and bm.calls == 0\n\n\ndef test_the_last_error_is_raised_when_every_model_fails():\n    a, _ = gemini([APIError(429)] * 2, model=\"a\")\n    b, _ = gemini([APIError(503)] * 5, model=\"b\")\n    with pytest.raises(LLMCallError):\n        FallbackLLM([a, b]).complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n\n\ndef test_a_model_without_quota_is_skipped_for_a_while():\n    a, am = gemini([APIError(429)] * 2, model=\"a\")\n    b, bm = gemini([\"one\", \"two\"], model=\"b\")\n    llm = FallbackLLM([a, b])\n    assert llm.complete(\"s\", \"p1\") == \"one\"\n    assert llm.complete(\"s\", \"p2\") == \"two\"\n    assert am.calls == 2                                        # not tried again during cooldown\n\n\ndef test_missing_key_is_reported_not_swallowed(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"GEMINI_API_KEY\", raising=False)\n    with pytest.raises(LLMNotConfiguredError):\n        FallbackLLM([GeminiClient(api_key=None)]).complete(\"s\", \"p\")\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- replay cache\ndef test_identical_prompt_is_answered_from_the_cache(tmp_path):\n    inner = Counting()\n    llm = CachingLLM(inner, tmp_path / \"c.json\")\n    assert llm.complete(\"s\", \"p\") == \"reply-1\"\n This time it shows `(6 replayed, 6 live)`, with **no API calls**. The cards still say *LLM yes*, because the pipeline did ask the learner. The banner is where you see that the replies were replayed.\n\n## How to use this in practice\n\n| Moment | What to do |\n|---|---|\n| **Practising or testing** | Cache on. Reset as often as you like, at no quota cost |\n| **Recording the video** | Do one live run first so the cache is filled. Then record with the cache on, and **say so**: \"this replays the reply the LLM wrote earlier, so I don't spend quota on retakes\". The banner shows it on screen |\n| **The interview** | Keep a key with full quota, and **don't spend it on practice**. Unseen statements are new prompts, so they always go live. The fallback model covers a mid-demo 429. If both fail, known layouts still parse with no LLM, and the video covers the learning step |\n| **The day before / morning of** | `python -m app.preflight --llm`: it makes one real call and shows whether quota is available |\n\nIf you still need billing: enabling pay-as-you-go on the project raises limits a lot. For this workload the cost should be very small, but I haven't verified current prices, so check before relying on that. It's optional, and the cache plus fallback should be enough.\n\n## Honest notes for your documents\n\nAdd these to `docs/limitations.md` under *Learning with the LLM*:\n\n```markdown\n- **Quota:** the free tier allows a limited number of calls per model per day. The system\n  retries a 429 once, then fails clearly (`learning_failed`). An optional fallback model gives a\n  second allowance. A first-time layout cannot be learned when every configured model is\n  out of quota.\n- **The replay cache returns the stored reply for an identical prompt**, including a bad first\n  reply (its corrected retry is stored under a different key, so a replay is deterministic).\n  Delete `data/llm_cache.json` to go fully live again. The page shows how many replies were\n  replayed.\n```\n\nAnd in the README configuration table:\n\n| Variable | Needed for | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `LLM_FALLBACK_MODELS` | learning (optional) | Comma-separated models tried when the first is out of quota, retired or down |\n| `LLM_CACHE` | learning (optional) | A file path. Identical prompts are replayed from it, so no API call is made |\n\n## What's next\n\nCommit this, and then **stop adding features**. Use **Run all steps** only as a rehearsal, because it goes too fast to narrate.\n\n## Before you record\n\n1. **Check everything works:**\n   ```bash\n   python -m app.preflight --llm\n   ```\n2. **Rehearse once.** Start the server, click **Prepare demo files**, then **Run all steps**. Every card should show a green tick.\n   ```bash\n   rm -f demo.db\n   python -m app.api --db demo.db --demo\n   ```\n3. **Click Reset demo data**, so the recording starts from an empty database.\n4. **Tidy the screen.** Close other tabs, turn on Do Not Disturb (no notification pop-ups), zoom the browser to about 110%, and hide the bookmarks bar.\n5. **Sign in before you start recording**, or trim that part out. The access token must never be on screen.\n6. **Record with Cmd+Shift+5** (the \"Record Selected Portion\" option works well for just the browser), with the microphone on.\n\n## The recording plan (5 to 7 minutes)\n\n| Time | What you do | What you say |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0:00 | Show the README diagram | \"Investors get statements in many layouts. The LLM is used only the first time a layout is seen. After that, plain code parses it.\" |\n| 0:30 | Workbench: **Prepare demo files**, then step 1 (new provider) | \"ABC is new, so the LLM writes a config once. Four checks have to pass before it's stored.\" Fill the wait by describing those four checks |\n| 1:30 | Step 2 (next month) | Point at **LLM no**: \"Same layout, different numbers. No LLM call. This is the core rule.\" |\n| 2:00 | Step 3 (bad numbers) | \"One value is 10,000 too high. No LLM is involved: validation noticed the figures don't add up.\" |\n| 2:30 | Step 4 (renamed column) | \"The provider renamed Qty to Units. The stored config can't read it, so a new version is learned and a person is asked to confirm.\" |\n| 3:15 | Steps 5 and 6 (locked, then unlock) | \"The system never guesses a password and never sends a locked file to the LLM.\" |\n| 3:45 | Step 7 (messy 3-page statement) | \"Repeated headers, page footers and wrapped names. Still parsed by the stored config.\" |\n| 4:15 | Step 8 (three more providers) | \"Two of these are AIFs: no holdings, with units and NAV.\" |\n| 4:45 | Documents tab, **Needs attention**: open the bad-numbers file, then **Approve** it with a note | \"Errors in red, checks that passed in green. The machine's verdict is never edited; approvals are stored separately.\" |\n| 5:30 | Learned formats tab | \"This is exactly what the LLM wrote. It's data, never code.\" |\n| 5:50 | Drop a PDF onto the Workbench, then **Deliver April mail** | \"The brochure is skipped, with its reasons recorded.\" |\n| 6:30 | Open `docs/limitations.md` | Read two or three honest limits. Close with what isn't built: Excel and the consolidated view |\n\n## Practical advice\n\n- **Waiting on the LLM.** A new layout can take 30 to 60 seconds. Don't edit it out silently. The brief rewards a system that knows when it's wrong.\n- **Use the inbox simulator, not your real Gmail.** Your real inbox has dozens of unrelated emails, and the page can show subjects and senders. If you want to prove the real mailbox works, say so in one sentence and show only the dry-run result from the dedicated test account.\n- **Keep your voice steady and slow.** The cards have the wording. Read them, then add one sentence of your own.\n- **Edit lightly.** iMovie or QuickTime's trim is enough. Cut only dead air and mistakes.\n\n## When you're done\n\n1. Watch the whole video once to check for the token, your Gmail address, file paths with your username, and the `.env` file.\n2. Upload it as **unlisted** on YouTube, or share a Drive link with \"anyone with the link\".\n3. Open the link in a private window to confirm it plays.\n\n## One backup\n\nRecord a second take if the first has a long failure in the middle. A pre-recorded fake would weaken that. Your preflight output also shows that everything else is healthy: the key, the database, the sample files, and the Gmail login all pass. The one failure is a 503 from Google saying the model is under high demand. It's the same transient spike we saw earlier, and the client already retries four times with waits of 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds.\n\n## Step 1: Try another model\n\n`gemini-3.8-flash` is the newest model, so it's probably the busiest. Your list also had older Flash models. Test each one. A model set on the command line overrides `.env`, so nothing needs editing:\n\n```bash\nfor m in gemini-3.7-flash gemini-3.5-flash gemini-flash-latest gemini-3.1-flash-lite; do\n  echo \"== $m\"; LLM_MODEL=$m python -m app.preflight --llm | grep \"LLM call\"\ndone\n```\n\nPick one that says `OK`, then **run the whole rehearsal** with it (Prepare, Run all steps) to confirm the eight steps still go green. A different model can write configs slightly differently, and the four gates will catch a bad one, but check anyway. If it works, set `LLM_MODEL=<that model>` in `.env`. Update the README's configuration table to match, because it currently says the default is `gemini-3.8-flash`.\n\n## Step 2: Decide on a plan for the video\n\nYou need about six LLM calls in the whole video, and a few seconds to a minute each. That's manageable without faking anything:\n\n| Situation | What to do |\n|---|---|\n| A call is slow but works | Keep talking while it runs: describe the prompt and the four gates. Trim the dead air afterwards if it's long |\n| A step shows a 503 or 429 | Press **Run** again. It's a transient error, and finished steps aren't repeated |\n| It fails on every try | Record that step again later, or use the fallback below |\n\nA 503 on camera isn't a disaster either. It shows the system handling failure: retries, a clear status (`learning_failed`), and the **Retry processing** button. If it happens, say that out loud and press the button. The brief rewards that.\n\n## Step 3: A fallback only if 503s keep happening\n\nIf rehearsal shows constant failures, I can add a **replay mode**: a stand-in for the LLM that returns the configs real Gemini already wrote during development (they're saved in `configs/learned/`), so the demo runs instantly. I'd only add it if you need it, for three reasons:\n\n- It's more code on the last day, and it needs its own tests.\n- You'd have to **say clearly in the video** that this is a replay of earlier real output, and mark it in the README. Presenting it as a live call would be dishonest, and interviewers will check.\n- It can't show the one thing a real call shows: that the system copes with a fresh, unpredictable LLM reply.\n\nTell me if you want it, and I'll write it with its disclosure built in (a visible \"replay\" banner on the page).\n\n## Another idea, for the interview\n\nThe interview will probably show a spike like this one on a real call. Prepare for it:\n\n- Run **Run all steps** once before they arrive, so your five layouts are already learned (a warm database, with no reset).\n- Their unseen statement will need one live call. If it returns a 503, press **Retry processing** in the document drawer. That button was built for it.\n- Keep the demo video as the backup.\n\n## Timing\n\nBy my calendar today is the 16th, so the deadline is **tomorrow night**. I'd settle the model question in the next 15 minutes, record this evening, and submit tomorrow morning, leaving the evening as buffer. Remove the waiting afterwards, which is what almost every screen demo does. You'll end up with a short video and nothing fake in it.\n\n## How much time is really at stake\n\nOnly some steps call the LLM:\n\n| Step | LLM call? |\n|---|---|\n| 1 New provider (ABC) | yes |\n| 2 Next month | no, instant |\n| 3 Bad numbers | no, instant |\n| 4 Renamed column | yes |\n| 5 Locked, no password | no, instant |\n| 6 Unlock (XYZ) | yes |\n| 7 Messy 3-page | no, instant |\n| 8 Three more providers | yes, three calls |\n| Inbox simulator (after reset) | yes, two calls |\n\nThat's about 8 calls. At 10 to 40 seconds each, you'd have 2 to 5 minutes of waiting. Time each one in your rehearsal, so you know your real numbers.\n\n## Plan\n\n1. **Pick the fastest model.** Run the model loop from my last message and note the time each takes. A \"flash-lite\" model is often much quicker, and the four gates still check its output. Whichever model you choose, rehearse the full sequence with it first.\n2. **Record everything in one pass**, narrating what the step *will* do just before you press **Run** (\"this calls the LLM, which takes about half a minute; it writes the config, and four checks must pass before it's stored\").\n3. **Trim in the editor.** In iMovie or QuickTime:\n   - **Speed up the wait** (about 8x), and add a text caption such as \"sped up\", so it's clear. This is honest and common.\n   - Or **cut the wait** after the spinner starts and resume when the result appears, if the narration works without it.\n4. **Drop one expensive segment.** The most expensive is step 8, three calls for providers whose behaviour you've already shown. Two options:\n   - Speed it up to about 10 seconds, with the caption.\n   - Skip it and say \"three more providers, including two AIFs, are in the sample outputs\", then show `samples/outputs/` in the file browser.\n\n   I'd keep it, sped up, because it's the only place where the AIF layouts appear.\n5. **Keep the inbox segment short.** After the reset it needs two LLM calls (ABC and XYZ). Speed those up as well, then spend your real time on the interesting bit: the brochure skipped, and the May email giving **LLM no**.\n\n## Target length\n\n| Segment | After editing |\n|---|---|\n| Opening and README diagram | 0:30 |\n| Steps 1 to 8 | about 3:00 |\n| Review, approve, learned formats | 0:50 |\n| Drag and drop | 0:40 |\n| Inbox simulator | 1:00 |\n| Close: limitations | 0:40 |\n| **Total** | **about 6:40** |\n\nIf it's still over 7 minutes, cut in this order: the optional `.txt` rejection, the \"deliver April again\" step, then the learned-formats tab.\n\n## If you want a shorter live flow\n\nSkip *Run all steps* entirely, and rehearse the steps in your own order. Record steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 live, and mention steps 5, 7 and 8 in a sentence each. That keeps four LLM calls instead of six or more.\n\n## What I'd avoid\n\n- **Faking the LLM output** (the replay idea). Your video's selling point is real behaviour, and a replay hides the only part that's unpredictable. If you ever use one, label it clearly.\n- **Hiding the waiting silently.** A speed-up with a caption is honest. A jump cut that makes a 40-second call look instant isn't, and an interviewer who watches you run it live will notice.\n\nRecord the first take, trim it, and tell me how long it ends up, or send me your segment list and I'll check it.", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-15T19:35:06.715857Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-15T19:35:20.482563Z", "flags": null, "type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "summaries": [{"summary": "Shortening a demo video without losing its live feel."}, {"summary": "Weighing ways to cut live LLM calls and waits."}], "cut_off": false, "truncated": true, "hidden": false, "thinking_hidden": true, "alternative_display_type": null, "signature": null}, {"start_timestamp": "2026-10-15T19:35:20.482610Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-15T19:35:30.760992Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "# Cut the waiting in editing, not in the demo\n\nEverything should stay real and live while you record. Whichever model you choose, rehearse the full sequence with it first.\n2. **Record everything in one pass**, narrating what the step *will* do just before you press **Run** (\"this calls the LLM, which takes about half a minute; it writes the config, and four checks must pass before it's stored\").\n3. **Trim in the editor.** In iMovie or QuickTime:\n   - **Speed up the wait** (about 8x), and add a text caption such as \"sped up\", so it's clear. This is honest and common.\n   - Or **cut the wait** after the spinner starts and resume when the result appears, if the narration works without it.\n4. **Drop one expensive segment.** The most expensive is step 8, three calls for providers whose behaviour you've already shown. Two options:\n   - Speed it up to about 10 seconds, with the caption.\n   - Skip it and say \"three more providers, including two AIFs, are in the sample outputs\", then show `samples/outputs/` in the file browser.\n\n   I'd keep it, sped up, because it's the only place where the AIF layouts appear.\n5. **Keep the inbox segment short.** After the reset it needs two LLM calls (ABC and XYZ). Speed those up as well, then spend your real time on the interesting bit: the brochure skipped, and the May email giving **LLM no**.\n\n## Target length\n\n| Segment | After editing |\n|---|---|\n| Opening and README diagram | 0:30 |\n| Steps 1 to 8 | about 3:00 |\n| Review, approve, learned formats | 0:50 |\n| Drag and drop | 0:40 |\n| Inbox simulator | 1:00 |\n| Close: limitations | 0:40 |\n| **Total** | **about 6:40** |\n\nIf it's still over 7 minutes, cut in this order: the optional `.txt` rejection, the \"deliver April again\" step, then the learned-formats tab.\n\n## If you want a shorter live flow\n\nSkip *Run all steps* entirely, and rehearse the steps in your own order. Record steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 live, and mention steps 5, 7 and 8 in a sentence each. That keeps four LLM calls instead of six or more.\n\n## What I'd avoid\n\n- **Faking the LLM output** (the replay idea). Your video's selling point is real behaviour, and a replay hides the only part that's unpredictable. If you ever use one, label it clearly.\n- **Hiding the waiting silently.** A speed-up with a caption is honest. A jump cut that makes a 40-second call look instant isn't, and an interviewer who watches you run it live will notice.\n\nRecord the first take, trim it, and tell me how long it ends up, or send me your segment list and I'll check it.", "citations": []}], "sender": "assistant", "created_at": "2026-10-15T19:35:30.847253Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-15T19:35:30.847253Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a1410f-a1e0-71bb-8842-f576daa9e81b"}, {"uuid": "01a14568-e53f-7293-bad8-5e4ea86c5c86", "text": "i wanted to know that is calling the llm and getting the output i staking so much time is it because of the hybrid artifact that we have choosen or is it something else and i also want to know weather the project can handle multple page pdf example there is table somewhere betwwn the pdf and tht pdf is not a single page treansaction file", "content": [{"start_timestamp": "2026-10-16T15:51:06.964918Z", "stop_timestamp": "2026-10-16T15:51:06.964918Z", "flags": null, "type": "text", "text": "i wanted to know that is calling the llm and getting the output i staking so much time is it because of the hybrid artifact that we have choosen or is it something else and i also want to know weather the project can handle multple page pdf example there is table somewhere betwwn the pdf and tht pdf is not a single page treansaction file", "citations": []}], "sender": "human", "created_at": "2026-10-16T15:51:06.965158Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-16T15:51:06.965158Z", "attachments": [], "files": [], "parent_message_uuid": "01a1410f-a1e0-7c0d-b701-7bea55d9d988"}, {"uuid": "01a14568-e53f-7533-b8f0-9f5d0c5beaae", "text": "# Two separate questions, two separate answers\n\n## 1. Is the slowness caused by the hybrid config?\n\nNo. I'd say the hybrid choice makes the LLM step **cheaper**, not slower. Where the time goes, from most to least likely:\n\n| Cause | Why it adds time |\n|---|---|\n| **Retries on 503/429** | On an overloaded model, one failing call waits 2+4+8+16 = 30 seconds before reporting failure. Your preflight 503 is this case |\n| **Extra attempts** | If a gate rejects the reply, the learner calls again (up to 3 calls). Each is a full round trip |\n| **The model itself** | Newer models can spend time \"thinking\" before they answer. I haven't checked whether `gemini-3.8-flash` does, or how to turn it down |\n| **Free-tier queueing** | Demand spikes are slower on shared capacity |\n\nWhy the config isn't the culprit: the LLM's **output** is one JSON config, probably a few hundred tokens, and it stays the same size whether the statement has 5 rows or 500. Compare the alternatives:\n\n| Approach | What the LLM must write | Cost grows with statement size? |\n|---|---|---|\n| Extract the data itself, every time | Every holding and transaction | **Yes**, and on every statement |\n| Generate a Python parser | A whole program | No, but longer, plus the security risks |\n| **Our config** | A small JSON | **No, and only once per layout** |\n\nThe delay is paid once per new layout, not per statement. After that, parsing takes milliseconds.\n\n### Measure it, so we're not guessing\n\nThis makes one real call with **no retries**, so it shows the model's own latency:\n\n```bash\npython - <<'EOF'\nimport time\nfrom app.llm import GeminiClient\nfrom app.learner import SYSTEM_PROMPT, build_prompt\nfrom app.reader import read_document\n\ndoc = read_document('samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf')\nprompt = build_prompt(doc)\nprint('prompt chars:', len(prompt))\ng = GeminiClient(retries=0)\nstart = time.time()\ntry:\n    out = g.complete(SYSTEM_PROMPT, prompt)\n    print('reply chars:', len(out), '| seconds:', round(time.time() - start, 1))\nexcept Exception as e:\n    print('failed after', round(time.time() - start, 1), 's:', str(e)[:120])\nEOF\n```\n\nRun it two or three times, and once with each model (`LLM_MODEL=<name> python - <<'EOF' ...`). Also run `python -m app.learner samples/pdfs/abc_pms.pdf` and read `LEARNED in N attempt(s)`. N above 1 means a gate rejected a reply.\n\n| What you see | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| Clean call takes 5 to 15 s | Normal. Long waits in the demo came from 503 retries or extra attempts |\n| Clean call takes 30 s or more | Model latency. Try another model. If it still hurts, I can add a setting to reduce the model's thinking, but I haven't verified how that works for this model, so I'd test it before promising anything |\n| It fails quickly with a 503 | Google's capacity, not our code |\n\n## 2. Does it handle a multi-page PDF with the table somewhere in the middle?\n\n**Yes for tables that span pages, and it's tested.** `stress_long_abc.pdf` has 3 or more pages, 80 holdings, a repeated table header, running headers and page footers, and wrapped names. The holdings table starts partway down page 1 and continues across pages. It parsed to exactly the expected answer, with `llm=no`.\n\nHow it copes:\n\n- **Position doesn't matter.** The engine looks for the table's header line anywhere in the document, so the table can be on page 2 or page 10. Summary labels and header fields are also searched across all pages.\n- **Table continuing on the next page:** it keeps reading rows. A repeated header is skipped, and so are a \"(continued)\" line and page headers and footers.\n- **Table ending:** at a `Total` line, a section heading, or the end of the document.\n\n### What I haven't tested, or know is weak\n\nThese are the realistic risks for a long, mixed document:\n\n1. **Long prose pages may break the fingerprint.** This is my main worry, and I found it by reading the code, not by running a test. The fingerprint keeps pure-text lines. A page of market commentary or a changing disclaimer, without digits in a line, would become \"labels\", and it can change every month. Similarity would then drop, the layout would look unknown, and the LLM would be called every month for that provider. A narrative-heavy statement is the likeliest way to break the core constraint. The fix is small: ignore long lines (more than about 8 words), because prose isn't layout. I'd write it with a test if you want it.\n2. **Column positions come from the first header.** Later pages are placed using the first page's x-positions. If a later page uses different margins or a different scale, cells could land in the wrong column. A two-cells-in-one-column case is caught, but one cell in the wrong column isn't.\n3. **The LLM sees only the first 400 lines or 40,000 characters.** In a 15-page transaction list, the model may never see the table's end or total row. Gate 3 runs on the full document, so a missing `Total` stop usually shows up as a row error that is fed back, but that costs an extra call or two.\n4. **Two tables with the same header** (say, \"Date | Amount\" under two sections) are refused as ambiguous, which fails loudly.\n5. **A section heading with several cells** after the table might be read as a data row. It produces a visible error, not a wrong number.\n6. **Only text PDFs.** A scan fails as before.\n\nItems 2 to 5 are already in your limitations note or close to it. Item 1 isn't, and it's the only one I'd call a real gap. A quick check you can run yourself: look at what the fingerprint contains for a long statement with `python -m app.reader <file>`, and see whether sentences end up among the labels printed by the fingerprint snippet we used earlier.\n\n## What I'd do with the time you have\n\nToday is the 16th, so keep this small:\n\n1. Run the timing script above and choose the model.\n2. Decide whether to fix the prose issue. It's about 10 lines plus a test, and it makes your answer to \"what about a long PDF?\" honest and strong. If you'd rather not touch the code the night before submitting, add it to `docs/limitations.md` under *Fingerprint*: *\"Long pure-text lines (commentary, disclaimers) are included in the fingerprint, so a provider whose statements contain changing prose may be re-learned every month.\"*\n\nTell me which you prefer.
